facts.sourceQuote: De moderne geschiedenis van de brug begint in 1866; er werd een aanbesteding uitgeschreven voor de vervanging van de houten brug alhier.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The modern history of the bridge begins in 1866; a tender was issued for the replacement of the wooden bridge here.

features.name: M.S. Vaz Diasbrug
features.opening: The M.S. Vaz Diasbrug (bridge 238), is a bascule bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum.

facts.text: A bicycle tunnel runs beneath the approach slope to let slow traffic pass under Weesperstraat.
facts.sourceQuote: Onder de aanloophelling van de brug bevindt zich ook een fietstunnel, zodat langzaam verkeer onder de Weesperstraat door kan.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Under the approach slope of the bridge there is also a bicycle tunnel, so that slow traffic can pass under the Weesperstraat.

facts.text: Constant renovations and adjustments were made as the city expanded and traffic grew.
facts.sourceQuote: De bruggen waren constant aan vernieuwingen en aanpassingen onderhevig als gevolg van de uitdijende stad en het daarmee gepaard gaande groeiende verkeersaanbod.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The bridges were constantly subject to renovations and adjustments due to the expanding city and the accompanying growing traffic supply.

features.name: Oude Haagsebrug
features.opening: The Oude Haagsebrug (bridge no. 1864) was a bridge over the Ringvaart of the Haarlemmermeer on the route between Amsterdam, via the hamlet of Nieuwe Meer, and…

facts.text: Highway traffic moved to a new viaduct in 1966, leaving this span as a quiet remnant.
facts.sourceQuote: In het kader van de bouw van het nieuwe Schiphol-Centrum in de jaren zestig is de autosnelweg in 1966 een paar honderd meter naar het noordwesten verlegd, en werd deze over een nieuw Ringvaartviaduct geleid.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: As part of the construction of the new Schiphol Center in the 1960s, the highway was relocated a few hundred meters northwest in 1966, and was led over a new Ringvaartviaduct.

features.name: Joep Langebrug
features.opening: Joep Langebrug (bridge 417) is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Zuid.

facts.text: The namesake Joep Lange died in the 2014 MH17 crash while living near this location.
facts.sourceQuote: In september 2021 werd de brug omgedoopt tot de Joep Langebrug naar de in 2014 bij de MH17-ramp omgekomen arts en aids-deskundige Joep Lange die vlak bij deze brug woonde; geëffectueerd in juli 2022.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In September 2021, the bridge was renamed the Joep Langebrug after the doctor and AIDS expert Joep Lange, who died in the 2014 MH17 crash, who lived near this bridge; carried out in July 2022.

facts.text: Before 2016, this structure was officially known as the Beethoven Bridge.
facts.sourceQuote: Tot 2016 stond de brug officieus te boek als de 'Beethovenbrug', net als de straat vernoemd naar Ludwig van Beethoven.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Until 2016, the bridge was officially listed as the 'Beethoven Bridge', just like the street named after Ludwig van Beethoven.

facts.text: Hildo Kropp carved Norwegian granite images while the bridge was being finished.
facts.sourceQuote: Tegelijkertijd was Hildo krop nog bezig te beelden uit te beitelen uit Noors graniet.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: At the same time, Hildo Kropp was still busy carving images out of Norwegian granite.

features.name: Theo Fransmanbrug
features.opening: The Theo Fransmanbrug (bridge number 1788) is a structural work of art in Amsterdam-North.

facts.text: Construction spans were hoisted into place by crane in May or June 2013 before the bridge opened to traffic later that year.
facts.sourceQuote: De overspanningen werden in mei/juni 2013 door een hijskraan op hun plaats gehesen. De brug werd op 30 augustus 2013, inclusief naamplaat, in gebruik genomen.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The spans were hoisted back into place by a crane in May/June 2013. The bridge was put into use on August 30, 2013, including nameplate.

features.name: Oude Lijn
features.opening: The railway from Amsterdam through Haarlem to Rotterdam (also: Oude Lijn, Dutch for "old line") runs from Amsterdam Centraal to Rotterdam Centraal through…

facts.text: The oldest section connecting Amsterdam and Haarlem opened in 1839.
facts.sourceQuote: The oldest section, opened in 1839, ran from Amsterdam to Haarlem.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The oldest section, opened in 1839, ran from Amsterdam to Haarlem.

facts.text: Track doubling was finally completed on August 2, 2024 after a long delay.
facts.sourceQuote: On 2 August 2024 the doubling of the tracks was completed after a long delay.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: On 2 August 2024 the doubling of the tracks was completed after a long delay.

facts.text: A new tunnel and station in Delft opened in March 2015 to pass under the old viaduct.
facts.sourceQuote: In March 2015 a new tunnel and station were opened in Delft, underpassing the former railway station and viaduct.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In March 2015 a new tunnel and station were opened in Delft, underpassing the former railway station and viaduct.

facts.text: Since December 2011, the line has carried all direct trains from Amsterdam to The Hague.
facts.sourceQuote: From December 2011 it is used by all direct trains from Amsterdam to The Hague, and all direct supplement-free trains from Amsterdam to Rotterdam except those through Woerden.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: From December 2011 it is used by all direct trains from Amsterdam to The Hague, and all direct supplement-free trains from Amsterdam to Rotterdam except those through Woerden.

features.name: Gooilijn
features.opening: The Amsterdam–Zutphen railway is a railway line in the Netherlands running from Amsterdam, North Holland to Zutphen, Gelderland via the province of Utrecht.

facts.text: The Gooilijn is an informal name derived from the scenic Gooi region it traverses between Amsterdam and Amersfoort.
facts.sourceQuote: It is also informally called the Oosterspoorweg (English: Eastern railway), with the part between Amsterdam and Amersfoort sometimes being called the Gooilijn (Gooi line) because of the region it runs through.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: It is also informally called the Oosterspoorweg (English: Eastern railway), with the part between Amsterdam and Amersfoort sometimes being called the Gooilijn (Gooi line) because of the region it runs through.

features.name: M. Justbrug
features.opening: The M. Justbrug (bridge 803) is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Zuid.

facts.text: M. Justbrug honors Chief Rabbi Meir Just, who died in 2010 and lived near a local synagogue.
facts.sourceQuote: De brug werd in april 2013 vernoemd naar de in 2010 overleden opperrabbijn Meir Just, die een standplaats had in de synagoge aan het Jacob Obrechtplein.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The bridge was named after the late Chief Rabbi Meir Just, who died in 2010 and had a place of residence in the synagogue on Jacob Obrechtplein.

facts.text: Meir Just frequently walked across this bridge between his home and the Jewish Cultural Center.
facts.sourceQuote: Meir Just wandelde vaak over de brug tussen zijn huis aan Soetendaal en Van der Boechorststraat 26, alwaar sinds de jaren zeventig een Joods Cultuteel Centrum gevestigd was.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Meir Just often walked across the bridge between his house in Soetendaal and Van der Boechorststraat 26, where a Jewish Cultural Center had been located since the 1970s.

features.name: Singelgrachtbrug
features.opening: The Houtmanspoorbrug, colloquially known as the Singelgrachtbrug, is a system of lift bridges in Amsterdam-Centrum, near the Spaarndammerbuurt district.

facts.text: A new lift bridge opened on July 2, 1923 next to the existing swing bridge.
facts.sourceQuote: Om voldoende capaciteit op het spoor te krijgen werd er eerst op 2 juli 1923 naast de bestaande draaibrug een nieuwe grotere, hogere ophaalbrug in gebruikgenomen (inclusief een nieuw spoorwegviaduct tussen deze brug en Amsterdam Centraal) (de onderdelen van deze brug waren in Duitsland gefabriceerd).
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In order to obtain sufficient capacity on the tracks, a new larger, higher hoist bridge was first put into use on July 2, 1923 next to the existing swing bridge (including a new railway viaduct between this bridge and Amsterdam Central) (the parts of this bridge were manufactured in Germany).

facts.text: Engineers David Adriaan van Heijst and Pieter Joosting designed these large bridges.
facts.sourceQuote: Het ontwerp van die relatief grote bruggen kwam van Rijkswaterstaat uit de pen van ingenieurs David Adriaan van Heijst (1879-1966, zoon van schrijver David François van Heijst) en Pieter Joosting (bekend van De Hef).
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The design of those relatively large bridges came from Rijkswaterstaat from the pen of engineers David Adriaan van Heijst (1879-1966, son of writer David François van Heijst) and Pieter Joosting (known from De Hef).

facts.text: Three distinct railway lines between Central Station and Sloterdijk cross here.
facts.sourceQuote: De brug ligt in de drie spoorlijnen tussen de stations Amsterdam Centraal Station en Station Amsterdam Sloterdijk, de lijnen: Amsterdam - Haarlem; Amsterdam - Zaandam; Amsterdam Centraal - Schiphol.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The bridge is located in the three railway lines between the stations Amsterdam Central Station and Amsterdam Sloterdijk, the lines: Amsterdam - Haarlem; Amsterdam - Zaandam; Amsterdam Central - Schiphol.

features.name: Zeilbrug
features.opening: The Zeilbrug or Zeilstraatbrug (bridge no. 348) is a bridge over the Schinkel in Amsterdam.

facts.text: Municipal documents once listed it only as bridge 348, ignoring the name Zeilbrug.
facts.sourceQuote: Diverse documenten van de gemeente Amsterdam vermeldden alleen brug 348; Zeilbrug was kennelijk geen officiële benaming.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Various documents from the municipality of Amsterdam only mentioned bridge 348; Zeilbrug was apparently not an official name.

facts.text: The Amsterdam Street Names Book 2010 officially adopted the name Zeilbrug for bridge 348.
facts.sourceQuote: Echter, in het Amsterdamse Straatnamenboek 2010 staat brug 348 nu als Zeilbrug vermeld.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: However, in the Amsterdam Street Names Book 2010, bridge 348 is now listed as Zeilbrug.

facts.text: Amsterdam School architect Piet Kramer designed the bridge alongside engineer Wichert Arend de Graaf.
facts.sourceQuote: De brug werd ontworpen in de Amsterdamse Schoolstijl door de architect Piet Kramer en de ingenieur Wichert Arend de Graaf van de Dienst der Publieke Werken van de gemeente Amsterdam.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The bridge was designed in the Amsterdam School style by the architect Piet Kramer and the engineer Wichert Arend de Graaf of the Department of Public Works of the municipality of Amsterdam.

facts.text: Granite sculptures by Hildo Krop depicting fishermen, ships, and seal heads adorn the structure.
facts.sourceQuote: Ook granieten beeldhouwwerken aan de brug, met vissers, schepen en koppen van zeerobben, in ontwerpen van Hildo Krop ontbreken hier niet.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Granite sculptures on the bridge, with fishermen, ships and heads of seals, in designs by Hildo Krop are also not missing here.

facts.text: Tram line 1 crossed this bridge starting in 1929 before line 2 took over in 1948.
facts.sourceQuote: Sinds 1929 reed tramlijn 1 over de brug. In 1948 kwam lijn 2 daarvoor in de plaats.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Since 1929, tram line 1 has been running over the bridge. In 1948, line 2 took its place for this purpose.

features.name: Armand Sunierbrug
features.opening: Armand Sunierbrug (bridge 327) is the name of a swing bridge in Amsterdam.

facts.text: Original bridges vanished during the 1932-1933 construction of a new cable-stayed bridge.
facts.sourceQuote: De bruggen verdwenen weer, bij de bouw van de beltbrug in de 1932/1933 waren de bruggen al verdwenen.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The bridges disappeared again, during the construction of the cable-stayed bridge in 1932/1933 the bridges had already disappeared.

facts.text: Administrators once listed it as P-83 because it was not under municipal control.
facts.sourceQuote: De brug was in de administratie bekend als P-83 hetgeen inhield dat de brug weliswaar in Amsterdam lag, maar niet in beheer was bij de gemeente.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The bridge was known in the administration as P-83, which meant that while the bridge was located in Amsterdam, it was not under the management of the municipality.

features.name: Entrepotdok
features.opening: The Entrepotdok (Warehouse Dock), formerly Nieuwe Rapenburgergracht, is a canal in Amsterdam, and a street and row of former warehouses with the same name…

facts.text: The Entrepotdok (Warehouse Dock) was formerly known as Nieuwe Rapenburgergracht.
facts.sourceQuote: The Entrepotdok (Warehouse Dock), formerly Nieuwe Rapenburgergracht, is a canal in Amsterdam, and a street and row of former warehouses with the same name along the northeast side of the canal.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Entrepotdok (Warehouse Dock), formerly Nieuwe Rapenburgergracht, is a canal in Amsterdam, and a street and row of former warehouses with the same name along the northeast side of the canal.

facts.text: Construction of these warehouses spanned from 1708 until 1829.
facts.sourceQuote: They were constructed between 1708 and 1829, used for storage, squatted in the 1990s and are now converted into apartments.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: They were constructed between 1708 and 1829, used for storage, squatted in the 1990s and are now converted into apartments.

facts.text: Squatters occupied the complex during the 1990s before conversion to apartments.
facts.sourceQuote: They were constructed between 1708 and 1829, used for storage, squatted in the 1990s and are now converted into apartments.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: They were constructed between 1708 and 1829, used for storage, squatted in the 1990s and are now converted into apartments.

features.name: Grimnessesluis
features.opening: The Grimnessesluis (bridge 202) is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum.

facts.text: The current structure replaced an older vaulted bridge around 1868 after the waterway was dammed.
facts.sourceQuote: Toen dat water een paar jaar later werd gedempt, was het Rokin versmald en werd de oude brug overbodig. Rond 1868 verdween de oude brug, zodat in praktijk de brug 10 meter opgeschoven was.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: When that water was dammed a few years later, the Rokin narrowed and the old bridge became unnecessary. Around 1868, the old bridge disappeared, so in practice the bridge was moved 10 meters forward.

facts.text: Grimnessesluis was also the name of a former street that crossed the Nes at this location.
facts.sourceQuote: Grimnessesluis was in vroeger tijden ook de aanduiding van de straat, die hier de Nes kruiste.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Grimnessesluis was also the name of the street that crossed the Nes here in the past.

features.name: Planciusspoorbrug
features.opening: The Planciusspoorbrug is a railway viaduct in Amsterdam-Centrum in the Netherlands.

facts.text: A steel bridge replaced the old arch structure around 1957 after road widening.
facts.sourceQuote: In 1955 werd er via foto vastgelegd dat er twee parallelle bruggen lagen, de oude en een geheel stalen brug in één overspanning over zowel trambaan als rijweg. Rond 1957 werd de weg verbreed en sneuvelde de oude combinatie om plaats te maken voor een tweede stalen brug met een overspanning.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 1955, a photo captured that there were two parallel bridges, the old one and a completely steel bridge in one span over both tramway and road. Around 1957, the road was widened and the old combination collapsed to make way for a second steel bridge with a span.

facts.text: Tram overhead wires were frequently damaged by trucks that were too tall.
facts.sourceQuote: Regelmatig werd de bovenleiding van de tram door te hoge vrachtwagens vernield.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The overhead wires of the tram were regularly damaged by too high trucks.

features.name: Rozenoordspoorbrug
features.opening: The Rozenoord Bridge (bridge no. 174P (A10)) consists of two traffic bridges over the Amstel River in Amsterdam.

facts.text: Over 100 resistance fighters were executed at this spot by the end of World War II.
facts.sourceQuote: Tegen het einde van de Tweede Wereldoorlog werden op deze plaats meer dan 100 verzetsstrijders gefusilleerd.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: By the end of World War II, more than 100 resistance fighters were executed at this location.

facts.text: The southern bridge opened in 1981, while the northern one arrived in 1989 to complete the road's width.
facts.sourceQuote: De eerste (zuidelijke) brug werd geopend in 1981. In 1989 kwam de tweede (noordelijke) brug in gebruik, waarmee de weg zijn uiteindelijke breedte kreeg.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The first (southern) bridge was opened in 1981. In 1989, the second (northern) bridge came into use, with which the road gained its final width.

features.name: Jan Evertsenbrug
features.opening: The Jan Evertsenbrug (145p) is a work of art in Amsterdam Nieuw-West.

facts.text: Amsterdam officially assigned this name to the viaduct on December 8, 2017.
facts.sourceQuote: Amsterdam vernoemde op 8 december 2017 (bijna) alle viaducten in de ringweg, om een betere plaatsaanduiding te krijgen. Op die datum werd de nieuwe naam Jan Evertsenbrug opgenomen in de Basisadministratie Adressen en Gebouwen (BAG).
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Amsterdam renamed almost all the overpasses in the ring road on December 8, 2017, to get a better place name. On that date, the new name Jan Evertsenbrug was included in the Basic Addresses and Buildings Administration (BAG).

facts.text: The entire concrete system spans the Jan Evertsen waterway and a parallel channel.
facts.sourceQuote: Het viaducten- en bruggenstelsel, geheel van beton, is gelegen in de Ringweg Amsterdam en overspant de Jan Evertsen en een parallel liggende waterweg.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The viaduct and bridge system, entirely made of concrete, is located in the Ringweg Amsterdam and spans the Jan Evertsen and a parallel waterway.

facts.text: Construction began in May 1969 with a large sand dune visible just days later.
facts.sourceQuote: De bouw van het complex ging van start op 1 mei 1969 Op 9 mei was er een grote zandvlakte te zien..
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Construction of the complex began on May 1, 1969 On May 9, there was a large sand dune visible..

features.name: Lucas Jansz Sinckbrug
features.opening: The Lucas Jansz Sinckbrug (bridge no. 36) is a bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum in the canal belt.

facts.text: The current stone structure dates to 1769, confirmed by an inscribed stone on the northern wall.
facts.sourceQuote: De huidige brug dateert uit 1769, aldus een ingemetselde steen in de noordelijke kademuur aan de Amstel.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The current bridge dates back to 1769, according to an inscribed stone in the northern embankment wall on the Amstel.

features.name: Henriëtte van Heukelom-van den Brandelerbrug
features.opening: Henriëtte van Heukelom-van den Brandelerbrug is a permanent bridge in Amsterdam-Zuid.

facts.text: Before its 2016 naming, the structure existed simply as unnamed bridge number 496.
facts.sourceQuote: De brug ging tot najaar 2016 naamloos als brug 496 door het leven.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The bridge continued to exist as bridge 496 without a name until autumn 2016.

facts.text: Dark brown armrests made of tropical hardwood sit atop wooden platforms with planks.
facts.sourceQuote: Daarover liggen houten liggers met daarop gemonteerd planken en donkerbruine leuningen uitgevoerd in tropisch hardhout.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: There are wooden platforms with planks mounted on them and dark brown armrests made of tropical hardwood.

features.name: Abdellah Zakibrug
features.opening: The Abdellah Zakibrug (bridge 180) is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam Oud-West.

facts.text: A British stray bullet hit a building on the northeastern slope during World War II in 1940.
facts.sourceQuote: In 1940, tijdens de begindagen van de Tweede Wereldoorlog werd het gebouw op de noordoostelijke helling getroffen door een Britse blindganger, waardoor het gebouw ontruimd werd.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 1940, during the early days of World War II, the building on the northeastern slope was hit by a British stray bullet, causing the building to be evacuated.

facts.text: Mayors Femke Halsema and Nabila Rmili unveiled the nameplate and information board in April 2024.
facts.sourceQuote: De tenaamstelling werd in april 2024 aan de brug bevestigd; tevens werd er een infobord geplaatst. Deze werden door burgemeesters Femke Halsema van Amsterdam en Nabila Rmili van Casablanca onthuld.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The name was confirmed on the bridge in April 2024; an information board was also placed there. These were unveiled by mayors Femke Halsema of Amsterdam and Nabila Rmili of Casablanca.

features.name: Berlagebrug
features.opening: The Berlagebrug (Dutch pronunciation: [ˈbɛrlaːɣəˌbrʏx]; English: Berlage Bridge) is a bascule bridge over the river Amstel in Amsterdam, Netherlands.

facts.text: The road it serves was renamed Stalinlaan before becoming Vrijheidslaan in 1956.
facts.sourceQuote: In 1925, the main thoroughfare of the new Rivierenbuurt district, the Amstellaan (later renamed Stalinlaan, then renamed again to Vrijheidslaan, in 1956), was completed.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 1925, the main thoroughfare of the new Rivierenbuurt district, the Amstellaan (later renamed Stalinlaan, then renamed again to Vrijheidslaan, in 1956), was completed.

facts.text: Although originally planned as round buildings, the control tower and bridgekeeper's house were ultimately constructed with rectangular shapes.
facts.sourceQuote: The control tower (placed eccentrically) and the bridgekeeper's house had been designed as round buildings, but this was changed to rectangular.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The control tower (placed eccentrically) and the bridgekeeper's house had been designed as round buildings, but this was changed to rectangular.

features.name: Leidsebrug
features.opening: The Leidsebrug or Leidsepleinbrug, bridge no. 174, is a fixed plate bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum and crosses the Singelgracht.

facts.text: Amsterdam School architect Piet Kramer designed the structure in 1917.
facts.sourceQuote: De brug werd in 1917 ontworpen door Piet Kramer in de stijl van de Amsterdamse school, maar werd pas tussen 1923 en 1925 gebouwd, ter vervanging van een oude stenen boogbrug die daar tot dan toe lag en ook wel de "Leidse Barrière" werd genoemd.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The bridge was designed in 1917 by Piet Kramer in the style of the Amsterdam School, but was not built until between 1923 and 1925, to replace an old stone arch bridge that had been there until then and was also known as the "Leidse Barrier".

facts.text: Construction occurred between 1923 and 1925 to replace an older stone arch.
facts.sourceQuote: De brug werd in 1917 ontworpen door Piet Kramer in de stijl van de Amsterdamse school, maar werd pas tussen 1923 en 1925 gebouwd, ter vervanging van een oude stenen boogbrug die daar tot dan toe lag en ook wel de "Leidse Barrière" werd genoemd.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The bridge was designed in 1917 by Piet Kramer in the style of the Amsterdam School, but was not built until between 1923 and 1925, to replace an old stone arch bridge that had been there until then and was also known as the "Leidse Barrier".

facts.text: Since 2015, this national monument underwent complete renovation while temporarily closing to all traffic except trams.
facts.sourceQuote: Sinds 2015 werd de brug, een rijksmonument, volledig gerenoveerd en behalve voor de trams voor al het verkeer tijdelijk gesloten en het verkeer werd omgeleid.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Since 2015, the bridge, a national monument, has been completely renovated and, except for the trams, temporarily closed to all traffic and traffic was diverted.

facts.text: After renovation, numerous night buses from both GVB and Connexxion ceased stopping directly on the structure.
facts.sourceQuote: Daarnaast halteerde een groot aantal nachtbussen zowel van het GVB als van Connexxion op de brug. Na de renovatie keerde de buslijnen niet terug op de brug.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In addition, a large number of night buses from both GVB and Connexxion stopped on the bridge. After the renovation, the bus lines did not return to the bridge.

facts.text: During construction, a temporary emergency bridge for pedestrians and cyclists was installed alongside the main span.
facts.sourceQuote: Voor voetgangers en fietsers was er tijdens de renovatie een tijdelijke noodbrug naast de te renoveren brug geplaatst.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: For pedestrians and cyclists, a temporary emergency bridge was placed next to the bridge to be renovated during the renovation.

features.name: Hendrick Jacobsz Staetsbrug
features.opening: The Hendrick Jacobsz.

facts.text: Stone markers on the Amstel side date the current structure to the year 1728.
facts.sourceQuote: De huidige brug heeft aan de Amstelzijde nog steeds twee stenen met de aanduiding "Anno" en "1728" aan weerszijden van de middelste doorvaart.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The current bridge still has two stones on the Amstel side with the indication "Anno" and "1728" on both sides of the central passage.

features.name: Entrepotdoksluis
features.opening: The Entrepotdoksluis (bridge no. 80) is a bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum that crosses a lock by the same name.

facts.text: The municipality selected an iron and steel drawbridge design around the year 1902.
facts.sourceQuote: Around 1902, the municipality opted for an iron/steel drawbridge.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Around 1902, the municipality opted for an iron/steel drawbridge.

facts.text: Designer Arend de Graaf created this bridge as part of his first generation of drawbridges.
facts.sourceQuote: According to Smit van Wichert, the designer was Arend de Graaf and belongs to his first generation of drawbridges.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: According to Smit van Wichert, the designer was Arend de Graaf and belongs to his first generation of drawbridges.

facts.text: Electric power controls were installed in 1911 by the NB Haarlemsche Machinefabriek.
facts.sourceQuote: In 1911, the controls were given electric power with a drive from the NB Haarlemsche Machinefabriek v / h / Gebr.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 1911, the controls were given electric power with a drive from the NB Haarlemsche Machinefabriek v / h / Gebr.

features.name: Wim Sonneveldbrug
features.opening: The Wim Sonneveldbrug (bridge 175) is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum.

facts.text: André van Duin unveiled the official nameplate on June 28, 2017 to mark Wim Sonneveld's centenary.
facts.sourceQuote: In 2017 is de 100e geboortedag van Sonneveld herdacht. Op 28 juni 2017 onthulde onder meer André van Duin de nieuwe naamplaat van de brug.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 2017, Sonneveld's 100th birthday was commemorated. On June 28, 2017, among other things, André van Duin unveiled the new nameplate of the bridge.

facts.text: Architect Piet Kramer created a simple design without any decorations or sculptures.
facts.sourceQuote: De brug is in 1935/1936 geplaatst naar een eenvoudig ontwerp van Piet Kramer, er zijn geen versieringen of beeldhouwwerken toegepast.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The bridge was built in 1935/1936 according to a simple design by Piet Kramer, no decorations or sculptures were applied.

facts.text: Construction of this structure took place during the years 1935 and 1936.
facts.sourceQuote: De brug is in 1935/1936 geplaatst naar een eenvoudig ontwerp van Piet Kramer, er zijn geen versieringen of beeldhouwwerken toegepast.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The bridge was built in 1935/1936 according to a simple design by Piet Kramer, no decorations or sculptures were applied.

features.name: Bullebaksluis
features.opening: The Bullebakssluis (bridge number 160) is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum.

facts.text: Piet Kramer, the city's bridge architect, designed this structure around 1930.
facts.sourceQuote: De brug die stamt uit ongeveer 1930 is ontworpen door Piet Kramer, de bruggenarchitect van de Dienst der Publieke Werken van Amsterdam.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The bridge dating back to around 1930 was designed by Piet Kramer, the bridge architect of the Amsterdam Public Works Department.

facts.text: Freight and bus traffic were banned in March 2019 due to poor structural condition.
facts.sourceQuote: Vanwege de slechte conditie van de brug besloot wethouder Sharon Dijksma in maart 2019 dat de brug per direct verboden terrein voor vracht- en busverkeer zou zijn.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Due to the poor condition of the bridge, alderman Sharon Dijksma decided in March 2019 that the bridge would immediately be prohibited territory for freight and bus traffic.

facts.text: The nearby square features a 1975 bronze sculpture of a female figure named Nieuwe Naatje.
facts.sourceQuote: Rondom de brug is op een pleintje (dat in 2005 na herinrichting officieus de naam Bullebakssluis kreeg) te vinden “Nieuwe Naatje”, een bronzen plastiek uit 1975 in de vorm van een vrouwenfiguur, van beeldhouwster Hanna Mobach.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Around the bridge, on a square (which officially took the name Bullebakssluis in 2005 after renovation) you can find "Nieuwe Naatje", a bronze sculpture from 1975 in the shape of a female figure, by sculptor Hanna Mobach.

features.name: Vier Heemskinderenbrug
features.opening: The Vier Heemskinderenbrug, also known as Vier Heemskinderensluis, is a permanent bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum.

facts.text: A striking design quirk is the abrupt transition where the bridge meets the quay on both sides without a gradual slope.
facts.sourceQuote: Opvallend aan de brug is de overgang of juist het ontbreken daarvan van de beide walkanten naar de brug zelf.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Remarkable about the bridge is the transition or rather the lack thereof from the two sides to the bridge itself.

features.name: Jan Wilsbrug
features.opening: The Jan Wils Bridge is a permanent bridge for pedestrians and cyclists in Amsterdam-Zuid.

facts.text: Jan Wilsbrug honors architect Jan Wils, who designed the nearby Olympic Stadium and two famous Citroën buildings.
facts.sourceQuote: The bridge is named after architect Jan Wils who provided the design of the nearby Olympic Stadium and the two buildings in Amsterdam famous for Citroën on Stadionplein.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The bridge is named after architect Jan Wils who provided the design of the nearby Olympic Stadium and the two buildings in Amsterdam famous for Citroën on Stadionplein.

features.name: Pathé Arena
features.opening: Cinema in Amsterdam, Netherlands.

facts.text: The largest room features a 200-square-meter screen for IMAX presentations.
facts.sourceQuote: De grootste zaal (14) heeft 480 stoelen en wordt gebruikt voor IMAX-voorstellingen; het scherm in deze zaal heeft een grootte van 200 m².
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The largest room (14) has 480 seats and is used for IMAX presentations; the screen in this room has a size of 200 m².

facts.text: Illuminated stairs flank the escalators, creating a distinctive visual feature.
facts.sourceQuote: Kenmerkend aan de bioscoop zijn de lichtgevende trappen aan weerszijden van de roltrap.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Characteristic of the cinema are the illuminated stairs on either side of the escalator.

facts.text: A specialized 4DX room offers seating for exactly 70 moviegoers.
facts.sourceQuote: Daarnaast beschikt de bioscoop over een 4DX-zaal met een capaciteit van 70 stoelen.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In addition, the cinema has a 4DX room with a capacity of 70 seats.

facts.text: The venue welcomed 1.4 million visitors in 2019 alone.
facts.sourceQuote: In 2019 trok de bioscoop 1,4 miljoen bezoekers.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 2019, the cinema attracted 1.4 million visitors.

features.name: Montelbaanstoren
features.opening: The Montelbaanstoren is a tower on the bank of the Oudeschans – a canal in Amsterdam.

facts.text: The name Montelbaanstoren evolved from the Duke of Alba's unrealized castle plan, Monte Albano.
facts.sourceQuote: Because the 3rd Duke of Alba proposed incorporating the tower into a castle (the Monte Albano) the tower became known in Dutch as the Monte Albano Toren. Over the years this became garbled to "Montelbaanstoren." The castle was never built.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Because the 3rd Duke of Alba proposed incorporating the tower into a castle (the Monte Albano) the tower became known in Dutch as the Monte Albano Toren. Over the years this became garbled to "Montelbaanstoren." The castle was never built.

facts.text: Built in 1516 as part of the city walls, the tower originally defended Amsterdam and its harbor.
facts.sourceQuote: The original tower was built in 1516 as part of the Walls of Amsterdam for the purpose of defending the city and the harbour.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The original tower was built in 1516 as part of the Walls of Amsterdam for the purpose of defending the city and the harbour.

features.name: ASC SDW
features.opening: ASC SDW (Amsterdam Sports Club Strong Through Willpower) is an amateur football club from Amsterdam, North Holland, Netherlands.

facts.text: A small athletics department once counted Giel Koolemans and Guus Dräger among its athletes.
facts.sourceQuote: Tussen 1920 en 1955 was er een kleine atletiek-afdeling met bekende atleten als Giel Koolemans en Guus Dräger.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Between 1920 and 1955 there was a small athletics department with well-known athletes such as Giel Koolemans and Guus Dräger.

facts.text: Between 1959 and 2005 the club maintained a handball department with women's, men's, and youth teams.
facts.sourceQuote: Van 1959 tot 2005 was er een handbal-afdeling met dames, heren en jeugd onder de bezielende leiding van o.a.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: From 1959 to 2005, there was a handball department with women's, men's and youth teams under the inspiring leadership of, among others.

features.name: De Duif
features.opening: De Duif is a church on the Prinsengracht in Amsterdam.

facts.text: The current church replaced a smaller predecessor built on the site of an 18th-century burnt sugar factory.
facts.sourceQuote: It was a modern replacement for the old St. Willibrordus church which had become too small. That had been the first Catholic church to be built in the Netherlands that was not a hidden church and which had been built on the former location of a sugar factory called "Het Fortuyn", which had burnt down at the close of the 18th century.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: It was a modern replacement for the old St. Willibrordus church which had become too small. That had been the first Catholic church to be built in the Netherlands that was not a hidden church and which had been built on the former location of a sugar factory called "Het Fortuyn", which had burnt down at the close of the 18th century.

facts.text: A massive organ by Franciscus Cornelius Smits and his son stands inside as a protected national monument.
facts.sourceQuote: It is a rijksmonument and inside there is a large Smits-orgel, which is a rijksmonument because it was built by Franciscus Cornelius Smits and his son. This organ was the largest built north of the big Dutch rivers and was taken into service on 25 September 2006, after a restoration.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: It is a rijksmonument and inside there is a large Smits-orgel, which is a rijksmonument because it was built by Franciscus Cornelius Smits and his son. This organ was the largest built north of the big Dutch rivers and was taken into service on 25 September 2006, after a restoration.

facts.text: De Duif hosts annual festivals like Tangomagia and the Tribal Art Fair.
facts.sourceQuote: It hosts yearly events like the Tangomagia and the Tribal Art Fair.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: It hosts yearly events like the Tangomagia and the Tribal Art Fair.

facts.text: The venue served as a location for the Holland Festival in summer 2006.
facts.sourceQuote: In the summer of 2006 it was one of the locations of the Holland Festival.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In the summer of 2006 it was one of the locations of the Holland Festival.

features.name: Muiderkerk
features.opening: The Muiderkerk is a Protestant church on Linnaeusstraat in Amsterdam-Oost, on the edge of Oosterpark.

facts.text: The original church partially burned down in 1989, though its distinctive tower survived unscathed.
facts.sourceQuote: De oude Muiderkerk, gebouwd in 1892, brandde deels af in 1989 maar de markante toren bleef gespaard.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The old Muiderkerk, built in 1892, partially burned down in 1989 but the distinctive tower remained unscathed.

facts.text: A modern structure built against the old tower in 1997 lacks the exterior appearance of a traditional church.
facts.sourceQuote: De huidige Muiderkerk is tegen de oude toren aan gebouwd en is onderdeel van een bouwcomplex uit 1997 dat ontworpen werd door architect Van Hoogevest. Het nieuwe gedeelte heeft niet het karakteristiek exterieur dat men van een kerk verwacht.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The current Muiderkerk is built against the old tower and is part of a 1997 construction complex designed by architect Van Hoogevest. The new part does not have the characteristic exterior that one expects of a church.

facts.text: A city square featuring an art object named Wensplein voor vrede opened south of the tower in 2008.
facts.sourceQuote: Ten zuiden van de toren werd in 2008 een stadspleintje met kunstobject geopend onder de titel Wensplein voor vrede.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: South of the tower, a city square with an art object was opened in 2008 under the title Wensplein voor vrede (Wishing Square for Peace).

facts.text: The complex houses part of the Royal Institute for the Tropics.
facts.sourceQuote: Het complex huisvest ook een deel van het Koninklijk Instituut voor de Tropen.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The complex also houses part of the Royal Institute for the Tropics.

features.name: Andrieskerk
features.opening: The Andrieskerk is the church building of the Christian Community at Arent Janszoon Ernststraat 869 in the Buitenveldert district of Amsterdam.

facts.text: Copper plates on the roof will eventually turn green with age.
facts.sourceQuote: Het dak werd afgewerkt met koperen platen, zodat het na verloop van tijd groen zou uitslaan.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The roof was finished with copper plates, so that it would turn green over time.

features.name: Nassaukerk
features.opening: The Nassaukerk is a Protestant church of 1926 on the De Wittenkade in the Staatsliedenbuurt in Amsterdam-West.

facts.text: Valckx & Van Kouteren constructed the pneumatic instrument in 1931.
facts.sourceQuote: Het orgel is gebouwd door Valckx & Van Kouteren in 1931. Het is een pneumatisch orgel met 21 registers.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The organ was built by Valckx & Van Kouteren in 1931. It is a pneumatic organ with 21 registers.

facts.text: A 1940 sale plan was abandoned after the Haarlemmerpoortkerk was sold instead.
facts.sourceQuote: In 1940 leek het doek te vallen voor de kerk; een besluit tot verkoop werd echter ingetrokken, in plaats van de Nassaukerk werd de Haarlemmerpoortkerk van Tjeerd Kuipers verkocht.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 1940, it seemed that the curtain was falling for the church; however, a decision to sell was withdrawn, instead of the Nassaukerk, the Haarlemmerpoortkerk by Tjeerd Kuipers was sold.

features.name: Berlage's Stock Market
features.opening: The Beurs van Berlage (literally Berlage's stock market) is a building on the Damrak, in the centre of Amsterdam.

facts.text: Berlage's Stock Market uses massive brick walls to symbolize a democratic society where individuals are small but the mass is powerful.
facts.sourceQuote: The enormous brick walls found in the Exchange embodied, in Berlage’s view, democratic society: “as individuals insignificant, as a mass a power.” The clock tower containing the “Beursbengel” may have been inspired by the thirteenth-century Torre del Popolo in the northern Italian city of Brescia.[1] More broadly, Romanesque and Renaissance architecture in northern Italy formed an important source of inspiration for Berlage’s Exchange, as can be seen, for example, in the Basilica of Saint Ambrose in Milan.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The enormous brick walls found in the Exchange embodied, in Berlage’s view, democratic society: “as individuals insignificant, as a mass a power.” The clock tower containing the “Beursbengel” may have been inspired by the thirteenth-century Torre del Popolo in the northern Italian city of Brescia.[1] More broadly, Romanesque and Renaissance architecture in northern Italy formed an important source of inspiration for Berlage’s Exchange, as can be seen, for example, in the Basilica of Saint Ambrose in Milan.

facts.text: Berlage's Stock Market draws inspiration from Romanesque and Renaissance architecture found in northern Italian cities like Milan.
facts.sourceQuote: The enormous brick walls found in the Exchange embodied, in Berlage’s view, democratic society: “as individuals insignificant, as a mass a power.” The clock tower containing the “Beursbengel” may have been inspired by the thirteenth-century Torre del Popolo in the northern Italian city of Brescia.[1] More broadly, Romanesque and Renaissance architecture in northern Italy formed an important source of inspiration for Berlage’s Exchange, as can be seen, for example, in the Basilica of Saint Ambrose in Milan.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The enormous brick walls found in the Exchange embodied, in Berlage’s view, democratic society: “as individuals insignificant, as a mass a power.” The clock tower containing the “Beursbengel” may have been inspired by the thirteenth-century Torre del Popolo in the northern Italian city of Brescia.[1] More broadly, Romanesque and Renaissance architecture in northern Italy formed an important source of inspiration for Berlage’s Exchange, as can be seen, for example, in the Basilica of Saint Ambrose in Milan.

facts.text: A massive restoration occurred between 1998 and 2004 to prepare the building for new metro construction.
facts.sourceQuote: Between 1998 and 2004, the Beurs van Berlage underwent a large-scale restoration. The primary impetus for this restoration was the decision to construct the North/South Line of the Amsterdam metro.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Between 1998 and 2004, the Beurs van Berlage underwent a large-scale restoration. The primary impetus for this restoration was the decision to construct the North/South Line of the Amsterdam metro.

facts.text: Engineers installed screw piles reaching twenty meters deep to stabilize the structure on a new concrete slab.
facts.sourceQuote: The solution involved installing screw injection piles throughout the entire basement. These piles were driven down to the so-called second sand layer, approximately 20 meters below Amsterdam Ordnance Datum (NAP). Across the full surface of the basement, a concrete foundation slab was constructed, which—through recesses in the masonry—was designed to support the superstructure.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The solution involved installing screw injection piles throughout the entire basement. These piles were driven down to the so-called second sand layer, approximately 20 meters below Amsterdam Ordnance Datum (NAP). Across the full surface of the basement, a concrete foundation slab was constructed, which—through recesses in the masonry—was designed to support the superstructure.

facts.text: The exterior color scheme was restored based on original hues discovered through meticulous historical research.
facts.sourceQuote: Special points of attention during the restoration included the complete reconstruction of the former Safe Deposit (vaults) in the basement beneath the Café, and the striking “new” exterior color scheme, which was based on original colors identified through meticulous research.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Special points of attention during the restoration included the complete reconstruction of the former Safe Deposit (vaults) in the basement beneath the Café, and the striking “new” exterior color scheme, which was based on original colors identified through meticulous research.

features.name: Canal Ring Area of Amsterdam
features.opening: The Grachtengordel (Dutch pronunciation: [ˌɣrɑxtə(ŋ)ˈɣɔrdəl] , lit.

facts.text: The city expanded in four distinct stages between 1585 and 1665.
facts.sourceQuote: This led to Amsterdam's expansion in four stages between 1585 and 1665.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: This led to Amsterdam's expansion in four stages between 1585 and 1665.

facts.text: Canals were extended to the Amstel around 1660 with new names added.
facts.sourceQuote: From about 1660, the canals were extended to the Amstel; these extensions bear the names: Nieuwe Herengracht, Nieuwe Keizersgracht and Nieuwe Prinsengracht.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: From about 1660, the canals were extended to the Amstel; these extensions bear the names: Nieuwe Herengracht, Nieuwe Keizersgracht and Nieuwe Prinsengracht.

facts.text: The Dutch name Grachtengordel literally translates to 'canal belt' or 'girdle'.
facts.sourceQuote: The Grachtengordel (Dutch pronunciation: [ˌɣrɑxtə(ŋ)ˈɣɔrdəl] , lit. 'canal belt/girdle'), known in English as the Canal District, is a neighborhood in Amsterdam, Netherlands located in the Centrum district.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Grachtengordel (Dutch pronunciation: [ˌɣrɑxtə(ŋ)ˈɣɔrdəl] , lit. 'canal belt/girdle'), known in English as the Canal District, is a neighborhood in Amsterdam, Netherlands located in the Centrum district.

facts.text: Though built in the Dutch Golden Age, many facades show styles from later restorations.
facts.sourceQuote: Many of the canal houses in the Amsterdam Canal District are from the Dutch Golden Age, 17th century. Many of these buildings, however, underwent restoration or reconstruction in various centuries, meaning that the buildings display many different architectural styles and facades.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Many of the canal houses in the Amsterdam Canal District are from the Dutch Golden Age, 17th century. Many of these buildings, however, underwent restoration or reconstruction in various centuries, meaning that the buildings display many different architectural styles and facades.

features.name: Westergasfabriek
features.opening: The Westergasfabriek is a former gasworks in Amsterdam, the Netherlands, now used as a cultural venue.

facts.text: A massive big Gasholder structure was added to the site in 1902 to store the produced fuel.
facts.sourceQuote: The big Gasholder was built in 1902.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The big Gasholder was built in 1902.

facts.text: Coal gas production ceased permanently in 1967 after natural gas was discovered in Slochteren.
facts.sourceQuote: In the sixties natural gas was found in Slochteren in the North of the Netherlands. This is why in 1967 the production of gas from the factory stopped permanently.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In the sixties natural gas was found in Slochteren in the North of the Netherlands. This is why in 1967 the production of gas from the factory stopped permanently.

facts.text: Following closure, the owner destroyed key structures including the original water tower and main plant.
facts.sourceQuote: After the Western Gas Factory closed, the Amsterdam Electricity and Gas Company (GEB) destroyed some of the buildings, among them the gas plant itself and the water tower.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: After the Western Gas Factory closed, the Amsterdam Electricity and Gas Company (GEB) destroyed some of the buildings, among them the gas plant itself and the water tower.

facts.text: Six festivals are organized annually on the park's main grass field.
facts.sourceQuote: The main grass field of the park allows for six festivals to be organized annually.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The main grass field of the park allows for six festivals to be organized annually.

features.name: Oudemanhuispoort
features.opening: Oudemanhuispoort (often abbreviated as: OMHP) is a complex of buildings in Amsterdam, between the Spui and the Waterlooplein.

facts.text: Carpenter Hendrik Gerrit van Raan submitted six rejected design drawings before the final gate was commissioned.
facts.sourceQuote: De Amsterdamse timmerman Hendrik Gerrit van Raan die veel bij het Gasthuis werkte, had daarvoor in 1783 al zes ontwerptekeningen gemaakt die allen werden afgekeurd.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Amsterdam carpenter Hendrik Gerrit van Raan, who worked at the Gasthuis a lot, had already made six design drawings for it in 1783, all of which were rejected.

facts.text: Built in the seventeenth century, this square structure originally served as a hospital for the elderly.
facts.sourceQuote: Het is in de 17e eeuw gebouwd in carrévorm en werd oorspronkelijk gebruikt als Oude mannen en vrouwen gasthuis, het is beschermd als rijksmonument.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: It was built in the 17th century in a square shape and was originally used as an Old Men and Women's Hospital, it is protected as a national monument.

features.name: Artis Bibliotheek
features.opening: The Artis Library (Dutch: Artis Bibliotheek) is a nineteenth-century library located at Plantage Middenlaan 45 in Amsterdam.

facts.text: The library joined the University of Amsterdam's Special Collections in 2005.
facts.sourceQuote: Since 2005, the Artis Bibliotheek has been part of the Special Collections at the University of Amsterdam, which in turn has been part of the Allard Pierson Museum since 2019.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Since 2005, the Artis Bibliotheek has been part of the Special Collections at the University of Amsterdam, which in turn has been part of the Allard Pierson Museum since 2019.

facts.text: Since 2019, it has been part of the Allard Pierson Museum.
facts.sourceQuote: Since 2005, the Artis Bibliotheek has been part of the Special Collections at the University of Amsterdam, which in turn has been part of the Allard Pierson Museum since 2019.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Since 2005, the Artis Bibliotheek has been part of the Special Collections at the University of Amsterdam, which in turn has been part of the Allard Pierson Museum since 2019.

features.name: Royal Theater Carré
features.opening: The Royal Theater Carré (Dutch: Koninklijk Theater Carré) is a Neo-Renaissance theatre in Amsterdam, located near the river Amstel.

facts.text: The venue opened on December 3, 1887 as a wooden structure with a stone façade.
facts.sourceQuote: On 3 December 1887 this building was officially opened. In the beginning, it was just a wooden building with a stone façade.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: On 3 December 1887 this building was officially opened. In the beginning, it was just a wooden building with a stone façade.

facts.text: Oscar Carré was the German circus director who built this first stone theatre in 1866.
facts.sourceQuote: In 1866 the German circus director Oscar Carré finally got permission to build his first stone theatre, replacing the Rooseboom windmill at the city locks of the river Amstel.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 1866 the German circus director Oscar Carré finally got permission to build his first stone theatre, replacing the Rooseboom windmill at the city locks of the river Amstel.

facts.text: Doors remained closed from 1944 to 1945 due to police raids during World War II.
facts.sourceQuote: During the Second World War, Carré attracted more custom, because people were searching for distraction. however, owing to the razias (police raids) in 1944, people started to stay away; the doors were closed from 1944 till 1945.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: During the Second World War, Carré attracted more custom, because people were searching for distraction. however, owing to the razias (police raids) in 1944, people started to stay away; the doors were closed from 1944 till 1945.

facts.text: Founded in 1887, the venue was originally designed as a permanent circus building.
facts.sourceQuote: When the theatre was founded in 1887, it was originally meant as a permanent circus building.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: When the theatre was founded in 1887, it was originally meant as a permanent circus building.

features.name: Max Euwe Centrum
features.opening: The Max Euwe Centrum is a chess centre on the Max Euweplein in Amsterdam.

facts.text: Amsterdam mayor Ed van Thijn, a chess enthusiast, helped secure the venue for the new center.
facts.sourceQuote: Met steun van de Koninklijke Nederlandse Schaakbond (KNSB), sponsoren, donateurs en de Amsterdamse burgemeester Ed van Thijn, zelf een schaakliefhebber, kreeg het Max Euwe Centrum een eigen ruimte aan de Paleisstraat – nabij de Dam – waar ook het Bondsbureau van de KNSB was gevestigd.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: With support from the Royal Dutch Chess Federation (KNSB), sponsors, donors and the Amsterdam mayor Ed van Thijn, himself a chess enthusiast, the Max Euwe Centrum was given its own space on Paleisstraat - near the Dam - where the KNSB Federal Bureau was also located.

facts.text: The current building previously served as a penitentiary facility before becoming a chess hub.
facts.sourceQuote: In dit gebouw hebben zich sinds de sluiting van de penitentiaire inrichting in 1979 diverse startende bedrijven en non-profitorganisaties gevestigd, waaronder het Max Euwe Centrum.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Since the closure of the penitentiary facility in 1979, various start-up companies and non-profit organizations have settled in this building, including Max Euwe Centrum.

facts.text: The center honors Max Euwe, a Dutch world chess champion who lived from 1901 to 1981.
facts.sourceQuote: Het bestaat uit een klein museum over de schaakcarrière en het leven van de Nederlandse wereldkampioen Max Euwe (1901-1981) en een ontmoetingscentrum annex bibliotheek met circa elfduizend boeken en tijdschriften.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: It consists of a small museum about the chess career and the life of the Dutch world champion Max Euwe (1901-1981) and a meeting center annex library with about eleven thousand books and magazines.

features.name: Nederlandse Film en Televisie Academie
features.opening: The Netherlands Film Academy (Dutch: Nederlandse Filmacademie) (NFA) was founded in 1958.

facts.text: The institution was established in 1958 as the Netherlands Film Academy.
facts.sourceQuote: The Netherlands Film Academy (Dutch: Nederlandse Filmacademie) (NFA) was founded in 1958.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Netherlands Film Academy (Dutch: Nederlandse Filmacademie) (NFA) was founded in 1958.

facts.text: Students can specialize in areas ranging from sound design to interactive multimedia effects.
facts.sourceQuote: Specialisation is possible in fiction directing, documentary directing, screenwriting, editing, producing, sounddesign, cinematography, production design, and interactive multimedia/visual effects.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Specialisation is possible in fiction directing, documentary directing, screenwriting, editing, producing, sounddesign, cinematography, production design, and interactive multimedia/visual effects.

facts.text: Alumni include director Paul Verhoeven, known for Total Recall and Basic Instinct.
facts.sourceQuote: Mike van Diem, director of Character Gied Jaspars, television and radio director Frank Ketelaar, screenwriter, film and television director Martin Koolhoven, director Nanouk Leopold, director Dick Maas, director Pim de la Parra, director Diederik van Rooijen, director Theo van de Sande, cinematographer of Blade and Grown Ups Carel Struycken, actor in The Addams Family and Twin Peaks Paul Verhoeven, director of Total Recall and Basic Instinct Leon de Winter, writer and film producer
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Mike van Diem, director of Character Gied Jaspars, television and radio director Frank Ketelaar, screenwriter, film and television director Martin Koolhoven, director Nanouk Leopold, director Dick Maas, director Pim de la Parra, director Diederik van Rooijen, director Theo van de Sande, cinematographer of Blade and Grown Ups Carel Struycken, actor in The Addams Family and Twin Peaks Paul Verhoeven, director of Total Recall and Basic Instinct Leon de Winter, writer and film producer

facts.text: Cinematographer Jan de Bont directed the blockbusters Twister and Speed.
facts.sourceQuote: Jan de Bont, cinematographer of Die Hard and director of Twister and Speed Stephan Brenninkmeijer, director and film producer Pieter Jan Brugge, producer of Heat and Defiance Danniel Danniel, director and editor of Ei 1987.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Jan de Bont, cinematographer of Die Hard and director of Twister and Speed Stephan Brenninkmeijer, director and film producer Pieter Jan Brugge, producer of Heat and Defiance Danniel Danniel, director and editor of Ei 1987.

facts.text: Actor Carel Struycken appeared in The Addams Family and Twin Peaks.
facts.sourceQuote: Mike van Diem, director of Character Gied Jaspars, television and radio director Frank Ketelaar, screenwriter, film and television director Martin Koolhoven, director Nanouk Leopold, director Dick Maas, director Pim de la Parra, director Diederik van Rooijen, director Theo van de Sande, cinematographer of Blade and Grown Ups Carel Struycken, actor in The Addams Family and Twin Peaks Paul Verhoeven, director of Total Recall and Basic Instinct Leon de Winter, writer and film producer
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Mike van Diem, director of Character Gied Jaspars, television and radio director Frank Ketelaar, screenwriter, film and television director Martin Koolhoven, director Nanouk Leopold, director Dick Maas, director Pim de la Parra, director Diederik van Rooijen, director Theo van de Sande, cinematographer of Blade and Grown Ups Carel Struycken, actor in The Addams Family and Twin Peaks Paul Verhoeven, director of Total Recall and Basic Instinct Leon de Winter, writer and film producer

features.name: Vondelmonument
features.opening: The Vondel monument, also known as the Vondelbeeld, is a large statue of the 17th-century Dutch poet and playwright Joost van den Vondel in the Vondelpark in…

facts.text: The municipality of Amsterdam acquired the full park in 1953, though it held only the statue's square meters since 1868.
facts.sourceQuote: Hoewel het park pas in 1953 in handen van de gemeente Amsterdam overging, had die al sinds 1868 een heel klein stukje van het park in handen, namelijk 'de paar vierkante meter waarop het beeld van Vondel staat.'
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Although the park only came into the hands of the municipality of Amsterdam in 1953, it had already had a very small part of the park in its hands since 1868, namely 'the few square meters on which the statue of Vondel stands.'

facts.text: In 1942, the monument celebrated its 75th anniversary during the Occupation.
facts.sourceQuote: In 1942, tijdens de Bezetting, beleefde het monument zijn 75-jarig jubileum.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 1942, during the Occupation, the monument celebrated its 75th anniversary.

facts.text: Napoleon III is specifically mentioned as one of the crowned heads who contributed to the statue.
facts.sourceQuote: De ondertitel luidde 'Geestdriftige poëzie achter prikkeldraad' en er wordt aan herinnerd dat destijds 'meer dan één gekroond hoofd in Europa' aan het standbeeld heeft bijgedragen, waarvan Napoleon III met name wordt genoemd.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The subtitle was 'Spirituous poetry behind barbed wire' and it is recalled that at the time 'more than one crowned head in Europe' contributed to the statue, of which Napoleon III is particularly mentioned.

features.name: Cat Cabinet
features.opening: The KattenKabinet ("Cat Cabinet") is an art museum in Amsterdam devoted to works depicting cats.

facts.text: Founder Bob Meijer named the museum after his red tomcat, John Pierpont Morgan.
facts.sourceQuote: In 1985, the building was restored, and in 1990 the museum was founded by Bob Meijer in memory of his red tomcat John Pierpont Morgan (named after the American banker J. P. Morgan).
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 1985, the building was restored, and in 1990 the museum was founded by Bob Meijer in memory of his red tomcat John Pierpont Morgan (named after the American banker J. P. Morgan).

facts.text: The owner lives on the second floor of the building with his family.
facts.sourceQuote: The owner lives on the second floor of the building with his family.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The owner lives on the second floor of the building with his family.

features.name: LJG
features.opening: The Liberal Jewish Community of Amsterdam (LJG) is the local community of the liberal Jews in the Dutch city of Amsterdam and its surroundings, with (since…

facts.text: Menno ten Brink has served as a rabbi for the community since 1995.
facts.sourceQuote: Rabbijn voor de LJG zijn (anno 2025): Menno ten Brink (sinds 1995) en Joram Rookmaker.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Rabbins for the LJG are (as of 2025): Menno ten Brink (since 1995) and Joram Rookmaker.

facts.text: The group manages the Gan Hasjalom cemetery located in Hoofddorp and Amstelveen.
facts.sourceQuote: Ook de begraafplaats Gan Hasjalom, in Hoofddorp en Amstelveen, valt onder de Amsterdamse LJG.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Gan Hasjalom cemetery, in Hoofddorp and Amstelveen, is also under the Amsterdam LJG.

features.name: HvA
features.opening: The University of Applied Sciences for Economic Studies (HES) in Amsterdam was an HBO educational institution with programs in the field of economics and was a…

facts.text: The HES merged with the Hogeschool of Amsterdam, making all former HES courses part of the new institution.
facts.section: Fusie en de huidige stand van zaken
facts.sourceQuote: Later in hetzelfde jaar zijn de HES en de Hogeschool van Amsterdam gefuseerd. Alle opleidingen die voorheen zelf door de HES werden gegeven werden vallen nu onder de Hogeschool van Amsterdam.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Later in the same year, the HES and the Hogeschool of Amsterdam merged. All courses that were previously taught by the HES themselves are now under the Hogeschool of Amsterdam.

facts.text: Economic courses are split between two locations: Leeuwenburg near Amstel station and Fraijlemaborg.
facts.section: Fusie en de huidige stand van zaken
facts.sourceQuote: Door de fusie en dit nieuwe pand heeft de Hogeschool van Amsterdam nu twee locaties gekregen waar de economische opleidingen worden gegeven. De eerste is de locatie Leeuwenburg nabij het Amstelstation. Met de nieuwe domeinvorming van Economie en Management, is de naam "Hogeschool voor Economische Studies" nu overbodig geworden en is ook de vestiging aan de Fraijlemaborg een integraal onderdeel geworden binnen de hogeschool.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Due to the merger and this new building, the Hogeschool van Amsterdam now has two locations where the economic courses are taught. The first is the location Leeuwenburg near Amstel station. With the new domain formation of Economics and Management, the name "Hogeschool for Economische Studies" has now become redundant and the branch at Fraijlemaborg has also become an integral part of the university.

features.name: AFC
features.opening: Amsterdamsche Football Club, commonly known as AFC is a football club based in Amsterdam.

facts.text: The club was officially established on January 18, 1895.
facts.sourceQuote: On 18 January 1895 the founding meeting took place in the basement of a house on the Koninginneweg where after a long discussion the name "Amsterdamsche Football Club (AFC)" was chosen.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: On 18 January 1895 the founding meeting took place in the basement of a house on the Koninginneweg where after a long discussion the name "Amsterdamsche Football Club (AFC)" was chosen.

facts.text: Members chose the name Amsterdamsche Football Club (AFC) after lengthy debate.
facts.sourceQuote: On 18 January 1895 the founding meeting took place in the basement of a house on the Koninginneweg where after a long discussion the name "Amsterdamsche Football Club (AFC)" was chosen.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: On 18 January 1895 the founding meeting took place in the basement of a house on the Koninginneweg where after a long discussion the name "Amsterdamsche Football Club (AFC)" was chosen.

facts.text: AFC won its first championship in 1906 and has claimed the title fourteen times since.
facts.sourceQuote: AFC-1 were crowned champions 14 times; 1906, 1909, 1917, 1918, 1919, 1946, 1961, 1963, 1967, 1969, 2001, 2010, 2014 and 2019, while also having been relegated three times; 1921, 1922 and 1998.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: AFC-1 were crowned champions 14 times; 1906, 1909, 1917, 1918, 1919, 1946, 1961, 1963, 1967, 1969, 2001, 2010, 2014 and 2019, while also having been relegated three times; 1921, 1922 and 1998.

features.name: Bijzondere Collecties
features.opening: The Bijzondere Collecties of the University of Amsterdam is part of the University Library of Amsterdam.

facts.text: Monastery libraries annexed in 1578 formed the basis for the new City Library.
facts.sourceQuote: Tijdens de alteratie van 1578 werden de kloosterbibliotheken van Amsterdam door de stad geannexeerd. Zij vormden de basis voor de nieuwe Stadsbibliotheek.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: During the alteration of 1578, the monastery libraries of Amsterdam were annexed by the city. They formed the basis for the new City Library.

facts.text: The library served the Athenaeum Illustre, founded in 1632 as a university precursor.
facts.sourceQuote: Naast de stad faciliteerde de bibliotheek het in 1632 opgerichte Athenaeum Illustre, de voorloper van de Universiteit van Amsterdam.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In addition to the city, the library facilitated the Athenaeum Illustre, founded in 1632, the precursor to the Universiteit of Amsterdam.

facts.text: In 1877, the institution was elevated to become a municipal university library.
facts.sourceQuote: In 1877 werd het Athenaeum Illustre verheven tot gemeentelijke universiteit en de Stadsbibliotheek daarmee tot universiteitsbibliotheek.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 1877, the Athenaeum Illustre was elevated to municipal university and the City Library was thus elevated to university library.

facts.text: A medical society's library was already housed there by 1855, decades before major expansions.
facts.sourceQuote: Maar de meeste grote collecties werden verworven na 1850. De bibliotheek van de Nederlandsche Maatschappij tot Bevordering der Geneeskunst werd bijvoorbeeld al in 1855 ondergebracht in de Stadsbibliotheek.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: But most of the large collections were acquired after 1850. For example, the library of the Nederlandsche Maatschappij tot Bevordering der Geneeskunst was already housed in the Stadsbibliotheek in 1855.

facts.text: The Bibliotheca Rosenthaliana was established in 1880 after Leeser Rosenthal donated Jewish and Hebrew works.
facts.sourceQuote: De schenking van een belangrijke collectie Joodse en Hebreeuwse werken van Leeser Rosenthal in 1880 leidde tot de oprichting van de eerste afdeling binnen de Universiteitsbibliotheek, de Bibliotheca Rosenthaliana, met een eigen conservator en gehuisvest in een eigen zaal.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The donation of an important collection of Jewish and Hebrew works by Leeser Rosenthal in 1880 led to the establishment of the first department within the University Library, the Bibliotheca Rosenthaliana, with its own curator and housed in its own room.

features.name: Dam Square Victims 7 mei 1945
features.opening: A plaque and thirty-two street stones on the Dam in Amsterdam-Centrum commemorate the victims of the Shooting on the Dam on May 7, 1945.

facts.text: A plaque honoring the fallen was unveiled on May 7, 1947 by Mayor Arnold d'Ailly.
facts.sourceQuote: Op 7 mei 1947 werd er door burgemeester Arnold d'Ailly op het gebouw van de voormalige De Groote Club op de hoek van de Paleisstraat en Kalverstraat een plaquette onthuld ter nagedachtenis van de schietpartij.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: On May 7, 1947, by Mayor Arnold d'Ailly, a plaque was unveiled on the building of the former De Groote Club at the corner of Paleisstraat and Kalverstraat in memory of the shooting.

facts.text: Contemporary reports from the Algemeen Handelsblad listed nineteen victims of the shooting.
facts.sourceQuote: Het Algemeen Handelsblad maakte toen melding van negentien slachtoffers.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Algemeen Handelsblad then reported nineteen victims.

facts.text: The memorial text generally reads: In memory of the citizens who fell on the Dam on May 7, 1945.
facts.sourceQuote: De tekst van die plaquette is algemeen gesteld: Ter herdenkingvan de burgersdie 7 mei 1945op de Dam gevallen zijn.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The text of that plaque is generally stated: In memory of the citizens who fell on the Dam on May 7, 1945.

facts.text: Investigation revealed thirty-one fatal casualties, not the assumed twenty deaths.
facts.sourceQuote: Men ging daarbij uit van een twintigtal doden; het bleek na onderzoek om eenendertig dodelijke slachtoffers te gaan.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: It was assumed that there were twenty deaths; it turned out after investigation that there were thirty-one fatal casualties.

features.name: Plaquette Chet Baker
features.opening: The Plaquette Chet Baker is an artistic work of art in Amsterdam-Centrum.

facts.text: Chet Baker died in 1988 after falling from a hotel window near the canal.
facts.sourceQuote: Die overleed in de nacht van 12 op 13 mei 1988, vermoedelijk onder invloed, uit het raam viel van Hotel Prins Hendrik, gevestigd aan de Prins Hendrikkade 52-58.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: He died in the night of May 12 to 13, 1988, presumably under the influence, falling from the window of Hotel Prins Hendrik, located at Prins Hendrikkade 52-58.

features.name: Buiksloterkerk
features.opening: The Buiksloterkerk is the (former) village church of the dike village Buiksloot in Amsterdam-Noord.

facts.text: Although named for Buiksloot, the building sits slightly lower on Buiksloterkerkpad rather than along the main dike.
facts.sourceQuote: Het kerkgebouw staat niet langs de Buiksloterdijk, maar iets lager aan het Buiksloterkerkpad.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The church building is not located along the Buiksloterdijk, but slightly lower on the Buiksloterkerkpad.

facts.text: Construction in 1710 reused older parts including beautifully carved seventeenth-century corbels.
facts.sourceQuote: De eenbeukige, vijfzijdig gesloten kerk kwam in 1710 tot stand met gebruikmaking van oudere onderdelen waaronder fraai gesneden zeventiende-eeuwse korbelen.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The single-aisled, five-sided closed church was built in 1710 using older parts including beautifully carved seventeenth-century corbels.

features.name: The Amsterdam Dungeon
features.opening: The Amsterdam Dungeon is a haunted attraction in central Amsterdam, Netherlands.

facts.text: A prop grave for Rembrandt van Rijn appears in the show, though he is actually buried elsewhere.
facts.sourceQuote: The Amsterdam Dungeon features a prop grave belonging to the painter Rembrandt van Rijn (who is mentioned in one of the shows). While it is very convincing, Rembrandt van Rijn is actually buried in the Westerkerk, a different church in Amsterdam.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Amsterdam Dungeon features a prop grave belonging to the painter Rembrandt van Rijn (who is mentioned in one of the shows). While it is very convincing, Rembrandt van Rijn is actually buried in the Westerkerk, a different church in Amsterdam.

facts.text: The Nieuwezijdse Kapel sits atop several real graves that remain invisible to visitors inside.
facts.sourceQuote: However, the Nieuwezijdse Kapel is built on top of several real graves, none of which are visible to the Dungeon's visitors.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: However, the Nieuwezijdse Kapel is built on top of several real graves, none of which are visible to the Dungeon's visitors.

facts.text: The attraction opened its doors in September 2005.
facts.sourceQuote: It opened in September 2005.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: It opened in September 2005.

facts.text: Merlin Entertainments, a British company, owns and operates the site.
facts.sourceQuote: The attraction is owned and operated by British company Merlin Entertainments, and is similar to Merlin's other properties, the London Dungeon, York Dungeon, Berlin Dungeon and Hamburg Dungeon.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The attraction is owned and operated by British company Merlin Entertainments, and is similar to Merlin's other properties, the London Dungeon, York Dungeon, Berlin Dungeon and Hamburg Dungeon.

facts.text: Visitors experience history through live actors, rides, shows, and special effects.
facts.sourceQuote: It depicts history through an interactive adventure, using live actors, a ride, shows and special effects to simulate historical dark and bleak times.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: It depicts history through an interactive adventure, using live actors, a ride, shows and special effects to simulate historical dark and bleak times.

features.name: The Movies
features.opening: The Movies is a cinema in Amsterdam.

facts.text: Founded in 1912 as Bioscoop Tavenu, the venue was renamed Cinema Hollandia just two years later.
facts.sourceQuote: The Movies is opgericht in 1912 onder de naam Bioscoop Tavenu. Reeds twee jaar later werd de naam gewijzigd in Cinema Hollandia.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Movies was founded in 1912 under the name Bioscoop Tavenu. Two years later, the name was changed to Cinema Hollandia.

facts.text: While many local cinemas closed during the 1960s, this specific theater managed to survive the era.
facts.sourceQuote: In de jaren zestig, waar vele buurtbioscopen ten onder gingen, wist de bioscoop te overleven.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In the 1960s, when many neighborhood cinemas went under, the cinema managed to survive.

facts.text: Owner Pieter Goedings originally planned to call the cinema Piccadilly before settling on The Movies.
facts.sourceQuote: Hij wilde de cinema aanvankelijk van naam laten veranderen in "Piccadilly", maar koos uiteindelijk voor de naam The Movies.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: He initially wanted to change the cinema's name to "Piccadilly", but eventually chose the name The Movies.

facts.text: The preserved art deco interior earned the venue the nickname Klein Tuschinski.
facts.sourceQuote: Het art-deco-interieur bleef echter behouden waardoor het de bijnaam "Klein Tuschinski" kreeg.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: However, the art deco interior was preserved, which is why it got the nickname "Klein Tuschinski".

facts.text: A Clockwork Orange screened regularly as a night film for eight years until it became legal in England.
facts.sourceQuote: De bioscoop heeft jarenlang op vrijdag en zaterdagnacht nachtfilms gedraaid; in een van de zalen heeft ongeveer acht jaar lang A Clockwork Orange als vaste nachtfilm gedraaid. De traditie hield op nadat die film in Engeland legaal vertoond mocht worden.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The cinema has shown night films on Friday and Saturday nights for many years; in one of the rooms, A Clockwork Orange has been shown as a regular night film for about eight years. The tradition stopped after that film was allowed to be legally shown in England.

facts.text: After buying out partners in 1989, Roeland Kerbosch expanded the theater with a fourth room and restaurant.
facts.sourceQuote: In 1989 verkocht Goedings de bioscoop aan enkele beleggers onder wie Roeland Kerbosch. De laatste kocht enkele maanden later de anderen uit en haalde Matthijs van Heijningen binnen als mede-eigenaar. The Movies werd uitgebreid met een vierde zaal en een restaurant.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 1989, Goedings sold the cinema to several investors including Roeland Kerbosch. The latter bought out the others a few months later and brought Matthijs van Heijningen on board as a co-owner. The Movies was expanded with a fourth room and a restaurant.

features.name: The Shipping House
features.opening: The Shipping House (Dutch: Scheepvaarthuis) is a building on the western tip of the Waalseiland near Amsterdam harbour that is one of the top 100 Dutch…

facts.text: The concrete frame was engineered by the van Gendt brothers, while architect Johan van der Mey handled the overall design.
facts.sourceQuote: The building's design and execution were entrusted to the brothers Johan Godart and Adolf Daniel Nicholas van Gendt. The van Gendt brothers were responsible for the technical implementation and the design of the concrete frame. The architectural design was left to the then relatively unknown architect Johan van der Mey.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The building's design and execution were entrusted to the brothers Johan Godart and Adolf Daniel Nicholas van Gendt. The van Gendt brothers were responsible for the technical implementation and the design of the concrete frame. The architectural design was left to the then relatively unknown architect Johan van der Mey.

facts.text: Exterior carvings depict the Dutch colonial empire and feature exotic women personifying the oceans at the main entrance.
facts.sourceQuote: For example, the outside of the building is covered in carving and relief sculptures that reflect the Dutch colonial empire, with the sculpted personifications of the oceans around the main entrance presented as "exotic mysterious women".
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: For example, the outside of the building is covered in carving and relief sculptures that reflect the Dutch colonial empire, with the sculpted personifications of the oceans around the main entrance presented as "exotic mysterious women".

facts.text: Bricks for both construction phases were baked simultaneously to ensure there was no color variation.
facts.sourceQuote: In order to avoid colour variation, the bricks were baked at the same time for both construction phases.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In order to avoid colour variation, the bricks were baked at the same time for both construction phases.

features.name: Kraan 2868
features.opening: Kraan 2868, also called the Figeekraan, is a former harbour crane on KNSM-eiland in Amsterdam-Oost.

facts.text: Kraan 2868 was manufactured in 1957 by the Figee factory after all cranes were destroyed in 1944.
facts.sourceQuote: In 1944, tijdens de Tweede Wereldoorlog, werden de hijskranen door de Duitse bezetter vernield, waardoor na de oorlog alle kranen vernieuwd moesten worden. In 1957 kwam hijskraan 2868 uit de fabrieken van Figee (NV Haarlemsche Machinefabriek van de Gebroeders Figee).
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 1944, during World War II, the cranes were destroyed by the German occupiers, so after the war all the cranes had to be replaced. In 1957, the crane 2868 came out of the factories of Figee (NV Haarlemsche Machinefabriek van de Gebroeders Figee).

facts.text: The crane officially became a municipal monument in late November 2011.
facts.sourceQuote: Het object is van het type wipkraan (geen vaste arm, maar een die in hoogte verstelbaar is) en is sinds 29 november 2011 een gemeentelijk monument.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The object is of the type of gantry crane (no fixed arm, but one that can be adjusted in height) and has been a municipal monument since November 29, 2011.
