facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The free facades on the corner are slightly behind the roofline, so that a small 'courtyard' is created between the wrought iron fences and the building.

features.name: Herepoort
features.opening: The Herepoort was originally one of the city gates of the city of Groningen.

facts.text: Four distinct versions of the gate were constructed between the 11th and early 17th centuries.
facts.sourceQuote: De eerste Herepoort werd vermoedelijk nog in de 11e eeuw gebouwd, de tweede in de 13e eeuw, de derde in de 15e eeuw en de vierde begin 17e eeuw.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The first Herepoort was probably built in the 11th century, the second in the 13th century, the third in the 15th century and the fourth at the beginning of the 17th century.

facts.text: City archaeologist Kortekaas dates the first Herepoort to around the year 1100.
facts.sourceQuote: Stadsarcheoloog Kortekaas dateert de eerste Herepoort rond het jaar 1100.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: City archaeologist Kortekaas dates the first Herepoort around the year 1100.

features.name: Huis aan 3 grachten
features.opening: The Huis aan de Drie Grachten or Huis op de Drie Grachten ("House on Three Canals") is a 17th-century canal house in Amsterdam, at the southeastern end of the…

facts.text: The name Huis aan 3 grachten refers to the building facing three distinct canals.
facts.sourceQuote: The name is a reference to the fact that the building faces three different Amsterdam canals.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The name is a reference to the fact that the building faces three different Amsterdam canals.

facts.text: A bookstore opened here in 1936 and later clandestinely printed literature during World War II.
facts.sourceQuote: August Aimé Balkema opened a bookstore in the building in 1936. During the Second World War, the bookstore was used to clandestinely print and publish works of poetry and other literature.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: August Aimé Balkema opened a bookstore in the building in 1936. During the Second World War, the bookstore was used to clandestinely print and publish works of poetry and other literature.

facts.text: A hidden compartment over a mantelpiece held wartime documents and may have sheltered Jewish refugees.
facts.sourceQuote: A hidden compartment over one of the mantelpieces was uncovered during the renovations in 2005. This compartment was found to contain an archive of wartime documents, including manuscripts and correspondence. The compartment may also have served as a hiding place for (Jewish) onderduikers (people hiding from the Germans).
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: A hidden compartment over one of the mantelpieces was uncovered during the renovations in 2005. This compartment was found to contain an archive of wartime documents, including manuscripts and correspondence. The compartment may also have served as a hiding place for (Jewish) onderduikers (people hiding from the Germans).

features.name: Universiteit van Amsterdam
features.opening: The University of Amsterdam (abbreviated as UvA; Dutch: Universiteit van Amsterdam) is a public research university located in Amsterdam, Netherlands.

facts.text: The university counts six Nobel laureates among its former professors, including Tobias Asser.
facts.sourceQuote: Notable former professors include winner of the Nobel Peace Prize in 1911 Tobias Asser, mathematician Luitzen Egbertus Jan Brouwer, winner of the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1901 Jacobus Henricus van 't Hoff, winner of the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1910 Johannes Diderik van der Waals, winner of the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1902 Pieter Zeeman, winner of the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1953 Frits Zernike, and scholar of religion, C.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Notable former professors include winner of the Nobel Peace Prize in 1911 Tobias Asser, mathematician Luitzen Egbertus Jan Brouwer, winner of the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1901 Jacobus Henricus van 't Hoff, winner of the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1910 Johannes Diderik van der Waals, winner of the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1902 Pieter Zeeman, winner of the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1953 Frits Zernike, and scholar of religion, C.

facts.text: Mathematician Luitzen Egbertus Jan Brouwer once taught at this institution.
facts.sourceQuote: Notable former professors include winner of the Nobel Peace Prize in 1911 Tobias Asser, mathematician Luitzen Egbertus Jan Brouwer, winner of the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1901 Jacobus Henricus van 't Hoff, winner of the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1910 Johannes Diderik van der Waals, winner of the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1902 Pieter Zeeman, winner of the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1953 Frits Zernike, and scholar of religion, C.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Notable former professors include winner of the Nobel Peace Prize in 1911 Tobias Asser, mathematician Luitzen Egbertus Jan Brouwer, winner of the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1901 Jacobus Henricus van 't Hoff, winner of the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1910 Johannes Diderik van der Waals, winner of the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1902 Pieter Zeeman, winner of the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1953 Frits Zernike, and scholar of religion, C.

facts.text: Municipal authorities established Universiteit van Amsterdam in 1632.
facts.sourceQuote: Established in 1632 by municipal authorities, it is the fourth-oldest academic institution in the Netherlands still in operation.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Established in 1632 by municipal authorities, it is the fourth-oldest academic institution in the Netherlands still in operation.

features.name: Warmoesstraat
features.opening: Warmoesstraat ('Chard Street') is one of the oldest streets in Amsterdam, running parallel to Damrak from Nieuwebrugsteeg to Dam Square.

facts.text: Joost van den Vondel's father ran a silk business here during the Dutch Golden Age.
facts.sourceQuote: During the Dutch Golden Age, the father of legendary poet and playwright Joost van den Vondel ran a business as a silk merchant there.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: During the Dutch Golden Age, the father of legendary poet and playwright Joost van den Vondel ran a business as a silk merchant there.

facts.text: The first leather bar in the Netherlands opened on this street around 1955.
facts.sourceQuote: On Warmoesstraat street the first leather bar in the country opened around 1955.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: On Warmoesstraat street the first leather bar in the country opened around 1955.

features.name: Westermoskee
features.opening: Westermoskee (Dutch: [ˌʋɛstərmɔsˈkeː], transl.

facts.text: French architects Marc and Nada Breitman designed the structure.
facts.sourceQuote: The building was designed by French traditional architects Marc and Nada Breitman, winners of the 2018 Driehaus Prize and part of the New Classical movement.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The building was designed by French traditional architects Marc and Nada Breitman, winners of the 2018 Driehaus Prize and part of the New Classical movement.

facts.text: Construction began in 2013 and finished two years later in 2015.
facts.sourceQuote: Construction started in 2013 and the building was completed in 2015.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Construction started in 2013 and the building was completed in 2015.

facts.text: The mosque held its unofficial opening ceremony on April 1, 2016.
facts.sourceQuote: The mosque was unofficially opened on 1 April 2016.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The mosque was unofficially opened on 1 April 2016.

features.name: De Krakeling
features.opening: De Krakeling is a theater hall in Amsterdam focused on youth theater.

facts.text: The name De Krakeling references the nearby Koekjesbrug bridge in the Nieuwe Passeerdersstraat.
facts.sourceQuote: De naam "De Krakeling" was een verwijzing naar de naastgelegen Koekjesbrug in de Nieuwe Passeerdersstraat.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The name "De Krakeling" was a reference to the adjacent Koekjesbrug in the Nieuwe Passeerdersstraat.

facts.text: After forty-two years, the theater moved to the Westergasfabriek grounds in July 2020.
facts.sourceQuote: Het theater is vanaf juli 2020 gevestigd in het Westergastheater op de terreinen van de voormalige Westergasfabriek aan de Pazzanistraat. Daarvoor was het 42 jaar lang gevestigd in het gebouw en rijksmonument Nieuwe Passeerdersstraat 1.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The theater has been located in the Westergastheater on the grounds of the former Westergasfabriek on Pazzanistraat since July 2020. Before that, it was located in the building and national monument Nieuwe Passeerdersstraat 1 for 42 years.

facts.text: A damaged foundation caused the original building's floor to sink during the 1910s.
facts.sourceQuote: Dat gebouw kreeg in de jaren tien te maken met ernstige verzakkingen als gevolg van een aangetaste fundering. De theatervloer verzakte mee zodat ingrijpen noodzakelijk werd.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: That building had to deal with serious subsidence in the 1910s as a result of a damaged foundation. The theater floor sank with it so that intervention became necessary.

features.name: Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam
features.opening: The Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam (abbreviated as VU Amsterdam or simply VU when in context) is a public research university in Amsterdam, Netherlands, founded…

facts.text: Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam means 'Free University' to show independence from government and church.
facts.sourceQuote: As a reflection of his beliefs, Vrije Universiteit literally means 'Free University' (or 'Liberated University') to signify independence from both government and church.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: As a reflection of his beliefs, Vrije Universiteit literally means 'Free University' (or 'Liberated University') to signify independence from both government and church.

facts.text: Teaching began in 1880 inside rented rooms at the Scottish Missionary Church along the Amstel river.
facts.sourceQuote: Teaching at the Vrije Universiteit started in 1880 in a few rooms rented at the Scottish Missionary Church (now the Kleine Komedie theatre), along the Amstel river in Amsterdam's city centre.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Teaching at the Vrije Universiteit started in 1880 in a few rooms rented at the Scottish Missionary Church (now the Kleine Komedie theatre), along the Amstel river in Amsterdam's city centre.

facts.text: Professor Andrew S. Tanenbaum created MINIX, the operating system that inspired Linux.
facts.sourceQuote: Tanenbaum, professor of Computer Science who wrote the MINIX operating system, the inspiration and precursor to Linux.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Tanenbaum, professor of Computer Science who wrote the MINIX operating system, the inspiration and precursor to Linux.

facts.text: Computer scientist Henri Bal and student John Romein wrote a program that solves the ancient game of Oware.
facts.sourceQuote: Henri Bal, professor of Computer Science and author of several books, who together with his student John Romein wrote a program that broke the ancient game of Oware (Awari) and gives the best move in any situation, usually leading to a forced win.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Henri Bal, professor of Computer Science and author of several books, who together with his student John Romein wrote a program that broke the ancient game of Oware (Awari) and gives the best move in any situation, usually leading to a forced win.

facts.text: Visiting professor Brad Bushman is a leading expert on the causes and consequences of human aggression.
facts.sourceQuote: Brad Bushman, since 2005 a visiting professor from Ohio State University in United States who is a foremost expert on the causes and consequences of human aggression.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Brad Bushman, since 2005 a visiting professor from Ohio State University in United States who is a foremost expert on the causes and consequences of human aggression.

features.name: Muiderpoort
features.opening: The Muiderpoort in Amsterdam is a city gate on Alexanderplein, at the intersection of Plantage Middenlaan and Sarphatistraat.

facts.text: The original gate sank sixteen feet after slipping from its foundation in January 1769.
facts.sourceQuote: In de nacht van 29 op 30 januari 1769 gleed de poort van zijn fundering en zakte zestien voet.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: On the night of January 29 to 30, 1769, the gate slipped from its foundation and sank sixteen feet.

facts.text: The exterior side features columns interrupted by bands, while the interior uses rustic-style pilasters.
facts.sourceQuote: De achtergrond van de pilasters is in rustica uitgevoerd. Aan de land- of buitenzijde zijn zuilen toegepast die door banden onderbroken worden.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The background of the pilasters is executed in rustic style. Columns have been applied to the land or exterior side, which are interrupted by bands.

facts.text: The city side displays the old coat of arms with a medieval ship hull rather than the assumed cannonball.
facts.sourceQuote: Aan de landzijde is het nieuwe Amsterdamse stadswapen met de drie Andreaskruisen in het fronton aangebracht, aan de stadskant het oude stadswapen met een middeleeuws schip (een hulk en niet een kogge, zoals vaak wordt aangenomen).
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: On the land side, the new Amsterdam city coat of arms with the three Andrew crosses is attached to the pediment, on the city side the old city coat of arms with a medieval ship (a hull and not a cannonball, as is often assumed).

features.name: Bimhuis
features.opening: The Bimhuis is a concert hall for jazz and improvised music in Amsterdam.

facts.text: The venue opened its doors on October 1, 1974 after being founded the previous year.
facts.sourceQuote: The Bimhuis was founded in 1973 and opened on October 1, 1974.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Bimhuis was founded in 1973 and opened on October 1, 1974.

facts.text: In 2017, the hall hosted the seventeenth edition of the Sonic Acts Festival.
facts.sourceQuote: In 2017 it was also a host for the 17th edition of the Sonic Acts Festival.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 2017 it was also a host for the 17th edition of the Sonic Acts Festival.

features.name: Zigeunermonument - Hel en Vuur
features.opening: War memorial in Amsterdam, Netherlands.

facts.text: Roma and Sinti gather annually at the site on August 1st to commemorate the Auschwitz gassings.
facts.sourceQuote: Sinti en Roma houden jaarlijks op 1 augustus een herdenkingsbijeenkomst bij het monument. In de nacht van 31 juli op 1 augustus 1944 zijn vijfduizend Roma en Sinti (mannen, vrouwen en kinderen) in Auschwitz vergast.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Sinti and Roma hold an annual commemoration meeting at the monument on August 1st. On the night of July 31 to August 1, 1944, five thousand Roma and Sinti (men, women and children) were gassed in Auschwitz.

features.name: De Balie
features.opening: De Balie is a Dutch organization that produces independent journalistic programs about art, culture and politics.

facts.text: A 1970s campaign saved the former courthouse from demolition to become an art center in 1982.
facts.sourceQuote: When the 19th-century building of the Amsterdam Cantonal Court was threatened to be demolished in order to build an eight-storey Bouweshotel in the late 1970s, Amsterdammers, including politician Hedy d'Ancona and artist Wim T. Schippers, launched the campaign "Bouw es wat anders" to prevent this from happening. The city council was persuaded, and a good destination for the building was found in art center De Balie in 1982.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: When the 19th-century building of the Amsterdam Cantonal Court was threatened to be demolished in order to build an eight-storey Bouweshotel in the late 1970s, Amsterdammers, including politician Hedy d'Ancona and artist Wim T. Schippers, launched the campaign "Bouw es wat anders" to prevent this from happening. The city council was persuaded, and a good destination for the building was found in art center De Balie in 1982.

facts.text: Editors produce about 400 live events annually under artistic director Yoeri Albrecht.
facts.sourceQuote: The editors of De Balie are a group of program makers that produce about 400 live events a year under the leadership of Yoeri Albrecht.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The editors of De Balie are a group of program makers that produce about 400 live events a year under the leadership of Yoeri Albrecht.

facts.text: De Balie belongs to the international Time to Talk network of debate centers.
facts.sourceQuote: De Balie is part of the international network for debate centers Time to Talk.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: De Balie is part of the international network for debate centers Time to Talk.

features.name: De Knoop
features.opening: Sculpture by André Volten in Amsterdam, the Netherlands.

facts.text: André Volten lived in Amsterdam-Noord since 1950 but felt the district lacked his own artwork.
facts.sourceQuote: Het idee kwam mede tot stand omdat Volten al sinds 1950 in Amsterdam-Noord woonde en werkte (terrein Asterdorp) maar zag dat dat stadsdeel nog geen kunstwerk van hem had.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The idea came about partly because Volten had lived and worked in Amsterdam-Noord since 1950 (on the Asterdorp site) but saw that the district did not yet have a work of art by him.

facts.text: Stainless steel links were welded together locally after a German factory struggled to shape the stiff metal.
facts.sourceQuote: Daarbij bleek dat geen Nederlandse firma zich aan die roestvaste stalen constructie wilde wagen; Volten moest uitwijken naar Duitsland. Ook die firma had moeite het stugge staal in ronde vormen te krijgen. Toen dat allemaal klaar was moesten in Amsterdam die schakelsegmenten aan elkaar gelast worden; dit gebeurde bij de Noord-Amsterdamse Machinefabriek, waarmee Volten vaker samenwerkte.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: It turned out that no Dutch company wanted to take a chance on that stainless steel construction; Volten had to move to Germany. That company also had trouble getting the stiff steel into round shapes. When all that was done, those switching segments had to be welded together in Amsterdam; this happened at the North Amsterdam Machinefabriek, with which Volten worked together more often.

features.name: Westerkerk
features.opening: The Westerkerk (Dutch pronunciation: [ˈʋɛstərˌkɛr(ə)k]; English: Western Church) is a Reformed church within Dutch Protestant Calvinism in central Amsterdam,…

facts.text: Hendrick de Keyser designed the church, but his son Pieter finished its construction.
facts.sourceQuote: The Westerkerk was built between 1620 and 1631 in Renaissance style according to designs by architect Hendrick de Keyser. The building of the Westerkerk was finished and completed by his son Pieter de Keyser and inaugurated on June 8, 1631.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Westerkerk was built between 1620 and 1631 in Renaissance style according to designs by architect Hendrick de Keyser. The building of the Westerkerk was finished and completed by his son Pieter de Keyser and inaugurated on June 8, 1631.

facts.text: Unlike older Amsterdam churches converted in 1578, this was built specifically for Protestant worship.
facts.sourceQuote: Several older churches in Amsterdam, such as the Oude Kerk and Nieuwe Kerk, were originally built before the Reformation and were converted to Protestantism during the Reformation in 1578. The Westerkerk was one of the first purpose-built Protestant churches.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Several older churches in Amsterdam, such as the Oude Kerk and Nieuwe Kerk, were originally built before the Reformation and were converted to Protestantism during the Reformation in 1578. The Westerkerk was one of the first purpose-built Protestant churches.

facts.text: A concert featuring music from Rembrandt's era is held annually on July 15th.
facts.sourceQuote: Every year on his birthday anniversary, the 15th of July, he is remembered in the Westerkerk with a lunchtime concert with music from the time of Rembrandt's life, and flowers are hung on his memorial marker.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Every year on his birthday anniversary, the 15th of July, he is remembered in the Westerkerk with a lunchtime concert with music from the time of Rembrandt's life, and flowers are hung on his memorial marker.

features.name: Westerwijk
features.opening: Westerwijk or Wester-wijk is a building in Amsterdam with houses, office space and two rooms.

facts.text: The Reformed Petrus Church in Sloterdijk commissioned this project as their client.
facts.sourceQuote: De opdrachtgever was de Nederlands Hervormde Petruskerk in Sloterdijk.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The client was the Reformed Petrus Church in Sloterdijk.

features.name: Onze Lieve Vrouwe Kapel
features.opening: The Onze Lieve Vrouwe Kapel is a chapel in Amsterdam-Oost.

facts.text: The chapel served the Onze Lieve Vrouwe Hospital complex from 1895 until 1986.
facts.sourceQuote: Van deze kerk zijn twee versies: Van 1895 tot 1986 maakte ze deel uit van het gebouwencomplex Onze Lieve Vrouwe Gasthuis waarvan de laatste gebouwen (Annapaviljoen en Mariapaviljoen) rond 2001 gesloopt werden.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: There are two versions of this church: From 1895 to 1986 it was part of the Onze Lieve Vrouwe Hospital complex, whose last buildings (Annapaviljoen and Mariapaviljoen) were demolished around 2001.

facts.text: Architect Adrianus Bleijs created the total design for the site bordering Oosterpark.
facts.sourceQuote: Het ontwerp van kapel, kerk en ziekenhuis kwam van de hand van Adrianus Bleijs, die een totaalontwerp maakte voor het terrein dat grensde aan het Oosterpark.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The design of the chapel, church and hospital was by Adrianus Bleijs, who made a total design for the site bordering the Oosterpark.

facts.text: Covered corridors allowed caregivers to reach the chapel without stepping outside into the weather.
facts.sourceQuote: Nieuw aan de opstelling van de kerk/kapel was, dat zij door overdekte gangen vanuit de paviljoens en het zusterhuis bereikbaar waren, zodat verpleegden en verplegers niet door de buitenlucht hoefden als zij dat niet wilden.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: New to the arrangement of the church/chapel was that they could be accessed through covered corridors from the pavilions and the sister house, so that nurses and caregivers did not have to go outside if they did not want to.

facts.text: Most of the church and chapel were leveled in June 1987 following a final celebration in November 1986.
facts.sourceQuote: Met een laatste eucharistieviering op 17 november 1986 viel het doek voor de kapel; in juni 1987 was het grootste deel van kerk en kapel met de grond gelijk gemaakt.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: With a final Eucharistic celebration on November 17, 1986, the curtain fell on the chapel; in June 1987, most of the church and chapel were leveled.

features.name: De Ateliers
features.opening: De Ateliers (formerly Ateliers '63) is an independent art school in located in Amsterdam.

facts.text: Students are not called students but are officially referred to as participants.
facts.sourceQuote: Students are called 'participants'.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Students are called 'participants'.

features.name: Pathé Tuschinski Cinema
features.opening: The Koninklijk Theater Tuschinski (English: Royal Theatre Tuschinski) also called Pathé Tuchinski, is a movie theatre in Amsterdam, Netherlands, near…

facts.text: Founder Abraham Tuschinski opened the venue with a theatre organ he personally sourced from Brussels.
facts.sourceQuote: Tuschinski wanted to open the theatre with the first theatre organ in the Netherlands; unfortunately Wurlitzer could not deliver in time; determined to open with an organ Tuschinski travelled to Brussels to acquire an existing one from another cinema.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Tuschinski wanted to open the theatre with the first theatre organ in the Netherlands; unfortunately Wurlitzer could not deliver in time; determined to open with an organ Tuschinski travelled to Brussels to acquire an existing one from another cinema.

facts.text: The architecture blends Art Deco, Art Nouveau, Jugendstil, and the Amsterdam School styles.
facts.sourceQuote: The facade blends several architectural styles: Art Deco, Art Nouveau, Jugendstil and the Amsterdam School.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The facade blends several architectural styles: Art Deco, Art Nouveau, Jugendstil and the Amsterdam School.

facts.text: The main auditorium hosts both films and live performances on a stage equipped with an organ.
facts.sourceQuote: The Tuschinski's main auditorium has served as both a movie theater and a live performance space since its opening. In addition to a film screen, it also contains a stage and an organ.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Tuschinski's main auditorium has served as both a movie theater and a live performance space since its opening. In addition to a film screen, it also contains a stage and an organ.

features.name: Het Veem Theater
features.opening: Veem House for Performance, called Het Veem Theater until 2014, is a production house, workshop, stage, laboratory and centre of expertise for contemporary…

facts.text: An open day for workspace seekers was held on November 7, 1981.
facts.sourceQuote: Met hun kraakactie en de oprichting van de stichting (later vereniging) Werkgebouw Het Veem werd op 7 november 1981 een open dag gehouden voor alle geïnteresseerden die werkruimte zochten.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: With their eviction campaign and the establishment of the foundation (later association) Werkgebouw Het Veem, an open day was held on November 7, 1981 for all interested parties looking for workspace.

features.name: Plein Theater
features.opening: The PleinTheater in Amsterdam-Oost is a stage for small-scale theatre, dance, contemporary classical music, youth theatre and neighbourhood activities.

facts.text: The venue was briefly renamed East Bloc in 2015 before reverting to Plein Theater in March 2019.
facts.sourceQuote: In 2015 werd Pleintheater omgedoopt tot Oostblok, maar kreeg in maart 2019 weer de originele naam terug.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 2015 Pleintheater was renamed East Bloc, but regained its original name in March 2019.

facts.text: Since June 2019, the venue has hosted monthly contemporary chamber music concerts.
facts.sourceQuote: De concertreeks Nieuwe Noten Amsterdam startte in 2016 en kreeg vanaf juni 2019 als vaste standplaats het Plein Theater. In de reeks wordt maandelijks hedendaags gecomponeerde kamermuziek gepresenteerd.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Nieuwe Noten Amsterdam concert series started in 2016 and has been based at the Plein Theater since June 2019. The series presents contemporary chamber music composed monthly.

facts.text: Bass clarinetist Fie Schouten and composer Aspasia Nasopoulou curate the series held here.
facts.sourceQuote: Curatoren zijn basklarinettist Fie Schouten en componist Aspasia Nasopoulou.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Curators are bass clarinetist Fie Schouten and composer Aspasia Nasopoulou.

features.name: Zuiderkerk Tower
features.opening: The Zuidertoren is the tower of the Zuiderkerk in Amsterdam.

facts.text: The tower was designed by Hendrick Cornelisz de Keyser, son of a Utrecht furniture maker.
facts.sourceQuote: Het ontwerp in renaissancestijl is van de Amsterdamse architect Hendrick Cornelisz de Keyser zoon van een meubelmaker uit Utrecht die rond 1591 samen met de stadsingenieur Cornelis Bloemaert naar Amsterdam was gekomen.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The design in Renaissance style was by the Amsterdam architect Hendrick Cornelisz de Keyser, son of a furniture maker from Utrecht who had come to Amsterdam around 1591 together with the city engineer Cornelis Bloemaert.

facts.text: Visitors can view a small exhibition of bell keyboards and hourglasses inside the tower.
facts.sourceQuote: In de toren is een kleine expositie van beiaardklavieren en uurwerken te zien.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In the tower you can see a small exhibition of bell keyboards and hourglasses.

facts.text: The tower offers views over the former Amsterdam Jewish Quarter and Nieuwmarkt Quarter.
facts.sourceQuote: Vanaf de toren is er een fraai uitzicht over de voormalige Amsterdamse Jodenbuurt en Nieuwmarktbuurt.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: From the tower there is a beautiful view over the former Amsterdam Jewish Quarter and Nieuwmarkt Quarter.

features.name: Stedelijk Museum Amsterdam
features.opening: The Stedelijk Museum Amsterdam (Dutch pronunciation: [ˈsteːdələk myˈzeːjʏm ˌɑmstərˈdɑm]; Municipal Museum Amsterdam), colloquially known as the Stedelijk, is a…

facts.text: The original 19th-century structure was designed by architect Adriaan Willem Weissman.
facts.sourceQuote: The 19th-century building was designed by Adriaan Willem Weissman.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The 19th-century building was designed by Adriaan Willem Weissman.

facts.text: A modern wing housing the current entrance was added in the 21st century by Benthem Crouwel Architects.
facts.sourceQuote: The connecting 21st-century wing, which houses the current entrance, was designed by Benthem Crouwel Architects.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The connecting 21st-century wing, which houses the current entrance, was designed by Benthem Crouwel Architects.

features.name: Van Eesteren Museum
features.opening: The Van Eesteren Museum is a museum in Amsterdam Nieuw-West devoted entirely to the architect and town planner Cornelis van Eesteren.

facts.text: Half a square kilometer was designated as a protected urban landscape in 2007.
facts.sourceQuote: In 2007 bestempelde het bestuur van Geuzenveld-Slotermeer daar een gebied van ongeveer een halve vierkante kilometer als een belangrijk cultuurhistorisch erfgoed tot beschermd stadsgezicht vanwege de architectuur en vooral de stedenbouwkundige opzet: het 'Van Eesteren Buitenmuseum'.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 2007, the board of directors of Geuzenveld-Slotermeer designated an area of about half a square kilometer as an important cultural historical heritage as a protected urban landscape due to the architecture and especially the urban planning layout: the 'Van Eesteren Outdoor Museum'.

features.name: NIOD Institute for War, Holocaust, and Genocide Studies
features.opening: The NIOD Institute for War, Holocaust and Genocide Studies (Dutch: NIOD Instituut voor Oorlogs-, Holocaust- en Genocidestudies) is an organisation in the…

facts.text: The name NIOD Institute for War, Holocaust, and Genocide Studies combines the Dutch acronym NIOD with its full English title.
facts.sourceQuote: The NIOD Institute for War, Holocaust and Genocide Studies (Dutch: NIOD Instituut voor Oorlogs-, Holocaust- en Genocidestudies) is an organisation in the Netherlands which maintains archives and carries out historical studies into the Second World War, the Holocaust and other genocides around the world, past and present.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The NIOD Institute for War, Holocaust and Genocide Studies (Dutch: NIOD Instituut voor Oorlogs-, Holocaust- en Genocidestudies) is an organisation in the Netherlands which maintains archives and carries out historical studies into the Second World War, the Holocaust and other genocides around the world, past and present.

facts.text: Since January 1, 1999, the organization has belonged to the Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences.
facts.sourceQuote: It has been part of the Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences since 1 January 1999.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: It has been part of the Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences since 1 January 1999.

facts.text: The institute administers archives of the Japanese occupation of the Dutch East Indies.
facts.sourceQuote: It administers the archives of the German occupation of the Netherlands and the Japanese occupation of the Dutch East Indies, as well as large collections of clandestine newspapers and pamphlets, photographs, books and articles.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: It administers the archives of the German occupation of the Netherlands and the Japanese occupation of the Dutch East Indies, as well as large collections of clandestine newspapers and pamphlets, photographs, books and articles.

features.name: Sarphatimonument
features.opening: The Sarphatimonument is a monument in honor of the 19th-century Jewish Amsterdam physician and benefactor Samuel Sarphati, in Sarphatipark in the Amsterdam…

facts.text: The round stone structure stands 12 meters high and is surrounded by a water basin with a diameter of 16 meters.
facts.sourceQuote: Het is een rond stenen tempelachtig bouwwerk, van 12 meter hoog, ontworpen door Jacobus Roeland de Kruijff, dat omringd wordt door water. De waterbak bevat fonteinen en heeft een diameter van 16 meter.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: It is a round stone temple-like structure, 12 meters high, designed by Jacobus Roeland de Kruijff, surrounded by water. The water basin contains fountains and has a diameter of 16 meters.

facts.text: During World War II the park was renamed Bollandpark and the bust was removed before being restored in 1945.
facts.sourceQuote: Tijdens de Duitse bezetting van Nederland in de Tweede Wereldoorlog kregen alle straten en dergelijke die vernoemd waren naar Joden een andere naam en zo werd het Sarphatipark omgedoopt tot Bollandpark. Uit het monument werd het borstbeeld van Sarphati verwijderd. Dit werd op 18 mei 1945 teruggedraaid.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: During the German occupation of the Netherlands during World War II, all streets and such that were named after Jews were given a different name and thus Sarphatipark was renamed Bollandpark. The bust of Sarphati was removed from the monument. This was reversed on May 18, 1945.

features.name: Sexmuseum
features.opening: The Sexmuseum or the Temple of Venus (Dutch: Venustempel) is a sex museum located in Amsterdam, Netherlands.

facts.text: Rooms honor figures like Mata Hari, Oscar Wilde, and the Marquis de Sade.
facts.sourceQuote: The museum's various rooms are named after famous figures, such as Mata Hari, Oscar Wilde, Marquis de Sade, Rudolf Valentino, and Marquise de Pompadour.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The museum's various rooms are named after famous figures, such as Mata Hari, Oscar Wilde, Marquis de Sade, Rudolf Valentino, and Marquise de Pompadour.

facts.text: In 2015 alone, nearly 675,000 people visited this unique museum.
facts.sourceQuote: It had 675,000 visitors in 2015, making it one of the most visited museums in the Netherlands.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: It had 675,000 visitors in 2015, making it one of the most visited museums in the Netherlands.

features.name: Faralda NDSM Crane Hotel Amsterdam
features.opening: The Crane Hotel Faralda (Kraanhotel Faralda) is a hotel located on top of a Rijksmonumentale crane on the NDSM site, a former shipyard on the banks of the IJ…

facts.text: The entire steel structure was moved on a pontoon to Franeker for restoration before returning in 2013.
facts.sourceQuote: De kraan werd op 26 juli 2013 op een 100 meter lang ponton vervoerd naar Franeker om te worden gerestaureerd. Op 22 oktober 2013 keerde de kraan gerestaureerd terug.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The crane was transported on July 26, 2013 on a 100-meter-long pontoon to Franeker to be restored. On October 22, 2013, the crane returned restored.

features.name: NACO-house
features.opening: The Office of Koppe's Shipping Agency, also known as the NACO cottage, is a former shipping office on the De Ruijterkade in Amsterdam-Centrum.

facts.text: The unofficial name NACO-house comes from the Nederlandsche Auto Car Onderneming office that occupied it from the mid-1960s.
facts.sourceQuote: Vanaf midden jaren zestig was het gebouw in gebruik als kantoor van de scheepvaartafdeling van de Nederlandsche Auto Car Onderneming (NACO), vandaar de officieuze naam NACO-huisje.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: From the mid-1960s, the building was used as an office for the shipping department of the Nederlandsche Auto Car Onderneming (NACO), hence the unofficial name NACO cottage.

facts.text: Since December 13, 2021, the building has stood over the Oostertoegang canal bridge.
facts.sourceQuote: Het gebouw staat sinds 13 december 2021 bij brug 2274 over de Oostertoegang.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The building has been located over the Oostertoegang at bridge 2274 since December 13, 2021.

features.name: Amsterdam Memorial to the Canadian Liberators
features.opening: Amsterdam dankt zijn Canadezen is a monument in the Canadezenplantsoen, called the Apollolaan before 2020, in Amsterdam, opposite the Apollohal between the…

facts.text: Thousands of Canadian troops entered the city in 1945 to liberate Amsterdam.
facts.sourceQuote: Via de Berlagebrug, de Apollolaan, de Van Baerlestraat, het Leidseplein en het Singel trokken in 1945 duizend Canadezen Amsterdam binnen en gingen naar de Dam.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 1945, thousands of Canadezen Amsterdam entered via the Berlage Bridge, the Apollolaan, the Van Baerlestraat, the Leidseplein and the Singel and went to the Dam.

facts.text: About half a million local residents cheered on the arriving soldiers.
facts.sourceQuote: Ongeveer een half miljoen Amsterdammers juichten hen toe.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: About half a million Amsterdamers cheered them on.

facts.text: On May 5, 1980, Canadians retraced their 1945 liberation route through the city.
facts.sourceQuote: Op 5 mei 1980 trokken Canadezen over dezelfde route als in 1945 opnieuw Amsterdam binnen.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: On May 5, 1980, Canadezen again entered Amsterdam along the same route as in 1945.

facts.text: Sculptor Jan de Baat created the steel flag that rises from a grassy field.
facts.sourceQuote: Het monument is gemaakt door Jan de Baat (1921-2010) en omvat een stalen wimpel die uit de grond rijst in een grasveld.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The monument was made by Jan de Baat (1921-2010) and includes a steel flag that rises from the ground in a grassy field.

facts.text: The waving flag symbolizes restored freedom of movement and the future.
facts.sourceQuote: Het uitwaaieren van de wimpel is een verwijzing naar de toekomst en de in 1945 herstelde bewegingsvrijheid.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The waving of the flag is a reference to the future and the restored freedom of movement in 1945.

features.name: Red Light District
features.opening: De Wallen (Dutch pronunciation: [də ˈʋɑlə(n)]) is the largest and best known red-light district in Amsterdam.

facts.text: In 1578, a Protestant city board banned fornication and forced sex workers underground.
facts.sourceQuote: In 1578, during the Dutch Revolt against Spanish rule, a Protestant city board was formed with fornication deemed punishable. Sex workers were banned and forced underground.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 1578, during the Dutch Revolt against Spanish rule, a Protestant city board was formed with fornication deemed punishable. Sex workers were banned and forced underground.

facts.text: During the Napoleonic era, French Imperial Naval Corps soldiers became the primary clients in the district.
facts.sourceQuote: In this Napoleonic era, men from the French Imperial Naval Corps were the main clients for prostitutes in De Wallen.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In this Napoleonic era, men from the French Imperial Naval Corps were the main clients for prostitutes in De Wallen.

features.name: Our Lord in the Attic
features.opening: Ons' Lieve Heer op Solder (OLHOS; English: Our Lord in the Attic) is a 17th-century canal house, house church, and museum in the city center of Amsterdam, The…

facts.text: Catholics built this church on the top three floors of the house during the 1660s.
facts.sourceQuote: The Catholic church was built on the top three floors of the canal house during the 1660s.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Catholic church was built on the top three floors of the canal house during the 1660s.

facts.text: Dissenters used this space as a clandestine church to worship when public services were banned.
facts.sourceQuote: It is an important example of a "schuilkerk", or "clandestine church" in which Catholics and other religious dissenters from the seventeenth-century Dutch Reformed Church, unable to worship in public, held services.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: It is an important example of a "schuilkerk", or "clandestine church" in which Catholics and other religious dissenters from the seventeenth-century Dutch Reformed Church, unable to worship in public, held services.

facts.text: The top three floors were converted into a house church between 1661 and 1663.
facts.sourceQuote: Between 1661 and 1663 the top three floors of the house were changed into a house church.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Between 1661 and 1663 the top three floors of the house were changed into a house church.

facts.text: Renovations to the structure took place during both the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries.
facts.sourceQuote: The building was renovated in the 18th and 19th centuries.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The building was renovated in the 18th and 19th centuries.

features.name: Dutch East Indian Company
features.opening: The Oost-Indisch Huis (Dutch for "East India House") is an early 17th-century building in the centre of Amsterdam.

facts.text: Architect Hendrick de Keyser likely designed the building's elegant Amsterdam Renaissance facades.
facts.sourceQuote: A gate with Tuscan-style pilasters and a small tunnel lead to an inner courtyard with elegant facades in Amsterdam Renaissance style, a style closely identified with the architect Hendrick de Keyser, who was most likely responsible for designing the building.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: A gate with Tuscan-style pilasters and a small tunnel lead to an inner courtyard with elegant facades in Amsterdam Renaissance style, a style closely identified with the architect Hendrick de Keyser, who was most likely responsible for designing the building.

facts.text: After the company dissolved in 1798, the site became the seat of the Batavian Republic's colonial government.
facts.sourceQuote: After the East India Company was dissolved in 1798, the building served until 1808 as the seat of the colonial government of the Batavian Republic.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: After the East India Company was dissolved in 1798, the building served until 1808 as the seat of the colonial government of the Batavian Republic.

features.name: Theo Thijssen Museum
features.opening: The Theo Thijssen Museum is a museum in Amsterdam devoted to the writer, teacher and politician Theo Thijssen.

facts.text: Visual artist Hans Bayens created the memorial stone and the statue on Lindengracht.
facts.sourceQuote: Deze steen was aangeboden door beeldend kunstenaar Hans Bayens, die ook het standbeeld van Thijssen maakte dat op de Lindengracht staat.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: This stone was offered by visual artist Hans Bayens, who also made the statue of Thijssen that stands on the Lindengracht.

features.name: Sint-Petrus-en-Pauluskerk
features.opening: The Sint-Petrus-en-Pauluskerk is a Dutch Old Catholic church building on Ruysdaelstraat in the Duivelseiland district of Amsterdam.

facts.text: A rare Dordrecht Rotating Tabernacle from 1789 is housed within this church.
facts.sourceQuote: Een bijzonder object in deze kerk is het veel oudere Dordts Draaitabernakel uit 1789, dat via een gift aan De Ooievaar in de Amsterdamse parochie terecht kwam.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: A particularly special object in this church is the much older Dordrecht Rotating Tabernacle from 1789, which came to De Ooievaar in the Amsterdam parish through a donation.

features.name: Blauwe Moskee
features.opening: The Blue Mosque (Dutch: Blauwe Moskee) is a mosque and cultural center in Amsterdam Nieuw-West, the Netherlands.

facts.text: Unlike many traditional mosques, it lacks loudspeakers for the call to prayer.
facts.sourceQuote: Unlike many traditional mosques, the Blue Mosque lacks a loudspeaker used to broadcast the call to prayer.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Unlike many traditional mosques, the Blue Mosque lacks a loudspeaker used to broadcast the call to prayer.

facts.text: The interior includes five Islamic education classrooms alongside the main prayer room.
facts.sourceQuote: The mosque consists of a room for prayer, five Islamic education class rooms, a room for lectures, and two meeting rooms.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The mosque consists of a room for prayer, five Islamic education class rooms, a room for lectures, and two meeting rooms.

facts.text: Construction began in 2008 thanks to funding from the Kuwaiti government.
facts.sourceQuote: Construction of the mosque was financed by the government of Kuwait through the offices of Europe Trust Netherlands and began in 2008.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Construction of the mosque was financed by the government of Kuwait through the offices of Europe Trust Netherlands and began in 2008.

features.name: De Ark
features.opening: De Ark is a church building in the Slotervaart district in Amsterdam Nieuw-West.

facts.text: Four scenes from Noah's story appear on the bronze doors, including the dove with a twig and the sacrifice.
facts.sourceQuote: Er zijn vier hoofdstukken uit het verhaal van Noach afgebeeld. Te zien zijn de bouw van de ark, de intocht in de ark, de duif met een takje en het dankoffer.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Four chapters from the story of Noah are depicted. The construction of the ark, the entry into the ark, the dove with a twig and the sacrifice are visible.

facts.text: A separate prayer chapel was added because the large hall lacked the right atmosphere for small-scale prayer.
facts.sourceQuote: Omdat de grote kerkruimte niet de juiste sfeer voor gebed op kleine schaal bood werd een aparte kleine bidkapel gemaakt, met een eigen sfeer.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Because the large church space did not offer the right atmosphere for small-scale prayer, a separate small chapel was made, with its own atmosphere.

features.name: This is Holland
features.opening: THIS IS HOLLAND is a tourist attraction with a panoramic flight simulator in Amsterdam.

facts.text: The project was originally scheduled for 2015 but opened later after the developer faced bankruptcy.
facts.sourceQuote: Het initiatief voor de attractie in Nederland werd genomen door het bedrijf Brand New Leisure met als werktitel Fly over Holland, en zou oorspronkelijk openen in 2015. Brand New Leisure kwam later in financiële problemen door het failliet gaan van het attractiepark Yumble.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The initiative for the attraction in the Netherlands was taken by the company Brand New Leisure with the working title Fly over Holland, and was originally scheduled to open in 2015. Brand New Leisure later fell into financial difficulties due to the bankruptcy of the amusement park Yumble.

facts.text: Engineers Vekoma and Brogent Technologies constructed the simulator that cost eighteen million euros.
facts.sourceQuote: De attractie kostte 18 miljoen euro en is daarmee een van de duurste attracties van Nederland. De simulator is gebouwd door de pretparkattractiebouwer Vekoma en Brogent Technologies.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The attraction cost 18 million euros and is therefore one of the most expensive attractions in the Netherlands. The simulator was built by the amusement park attraction builder Vekoma and Brogent Technologies.

features.name: Orgelpark
features.opening: The Orgelpark is an art center in Amsterdam where the organ is central.

facts.text: Pastor Johannes Geelkerken caused a stir in 1923 by calling the Genesis snake a metaphor.
facts.sourceQuote: De Parkkerk werd gebouwd in 1918 als Gereformeerde Kerk, waarin predikant Johannes Geelkerken in 1923 ophef veroorzaakte door te preken, dat de sprekende slang in Genesis 3 moest worden opgevat als een metafoor.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Park Church was built in 1918 as a Reformed Church, in which pastor Johannes Geelkerken caused a stir in 1923 by preaching that the talking snake in Genesis 3 should be understood as a metaphor.

facts.text: A 2005 restoration replaced roof leadwork and used English Ffestiniog slate.
facts.sourceQuote: De kerk is gebouwd in 1916-1918 en gerestaureerd in 2005 met onder meer Engelse Ffestiniog leisteen. Op het dak en de toren werd veel loodwerk vervangen.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The church was built in 1916-1918 and restored in 2005 with English Ffestiniog slate, among other things. A lot of leadwork was replaced on the roof and the tower.

facts.text: The venue officially opened its doors on January 20, 2007.
facts.sourceQuote: Het is op 20 januari 2007 geopend.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: It was opened on January 20, 2007.

facts.text: Businessman Loek Dijkman provided financial resources through his Utopa Foundation.
facts.sourceQuote: Financiële middelen voor het Orgelpark worden door de Stichting Utopa van de zakenman Loek Dijkman beschikbaar gesteld.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Financial resources for Orgelpark are made available by the Utopa Foundation of businessman Loek Dijkman.

features.name: El Tawheed
features.opening: The El Tawheed Mosque is a Sunni mosque in Amsterdam, Netherlands.

facts.text: Funding came in part from the Saudi NGO al-Haramain Foundation.
facts.sourceQuote: The mosque was in-part funded by the Saudi non-governmental organization al-Haramain Foundation.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The mosque was in-part funded by the Saudi non-governmental organization al-Haramain Foundation.

features.name: Kunstenaarsverzet
features.opening: Monument and work of art in Amsterdam, Netherlands.

facts.text: Gerrit van der Veen, the resistance fighter honored here, destroyed population registers in March 1943.
facts.sourceQuote: De Plantage Middenlaan werd gekozen als locatie omdat Gerrit van der Veen in de buurt een “vernielingsactie” in het bevolkingsregister (27 maart 1943) had gehouden.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Plantage Middenlaan was chosen as the location because Gerrit van der Veen had held a "destruction campaign" in the population register (March 27, 1943) in the vicinity.

facts.text: Artist Carel Kneulman originally envisioned an eight-meter-high statue for this monument.
facts.sourceQuote: Aan kunstenaar Carel Kneulman werd de opdracht verstrekt; hij had een beeld van acht meter hoog voor ogen.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The task was given to artist Carel Kneulman; he had an eight-meter-high statue in mind.

features.name: ACTA
features.opening: The Academic Center for Dentistry Amsterdam (ACTA) is the joint Faculty of Dentistry of the University of Amsterdam and the Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam.

facts.text: ACTA was founded in 1985 to merge two separate faculties due to a national oversupply of dentists.
facts.sourceQuote: ACTA is in 1985 opgericht. Destijds had Nederland een overschot aan tandartsen, zodat er voor twee afzonderlijke faculteiten geen plaats meer was.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: ACTA was founded in 1985. At that time, the Netherlands had an oversupply of dentists, so there was no room left for two separate faculties.

facts.text: By 2010, the site housed roughly nine hundred students alongside twenty-seven thousand patients.
facts.sourceQuote: In 2010 bediende dit gebouw circa negenhonderd studenten en 27 000 patiënten.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 2010, this building served approximately nine hundred students and 27,000 patients.

features.name: foam
features.opening: Foam or Fotografiemuseum Amsterdam is a photography museum located on Keizersgracht in Amsterdam, the Netherlands.

facts.text: Architects BenthemCrouwel converted three Keizersgracht buildings into the modern space.
facts.sourceQuote: Architects BenthemCrouwel turned three buildings at the Keizersgracht into a modern museum.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Architects BenthemCrouwel turned three buildings at the Keizersgracht into a modern museum.

facts.text: Foam presents short exhibitions for young photographers alongside major retrospectives.
facts.sourceQuote: Next to large exhibitions by well-known photographers, Foam also shows the work of young and upcoming photographers, in shorter running exhibitions.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Next to large exhibitions by well-known photographers, Foam also shows the work of young and upcoming photographers, in shorter running exhibitions.

facts.text: A major Helmut Newton retrospective was presented by the museum in summer 2016.
facts.sourceQuote: In summer 2016, Foam presented a major Helmut Newton retrospective exhibition.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In summer 2016, Foam presented a major Helmut Newton retrospective exhibition.

facts.text: The institution publishes a quarterly international photography magazine called Foam Magazine.
facts.sourceQuote: The museum also publishes a quarterly international photography magazine called Foam Magazine.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The museum also publishes a quarterly international photography magazine called Foam Magazine.

features.name: Nemo
features.opening: NEMO Science Museum (from Latin: Nemo, lit.

facts.text: The name Nemo comes from Latin, meaning 'Nobody'.
facts.sourceQuote: NEMO Science Museum (from Latin: Nemo, lit. 'Nobody') is a science centre in Amsterdam, Netherlands.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: NEMO Science Museum (from Latin: Nemo, lit. 'Nobody') is a science centre in Amsterdam, Netherlands.

facts.text: Renzo Piano designed the building that now houses the museum.
facts.sourceQuote: The museum has its origins in 1923, and is housed in a building designed by Renzo Piano since 1997.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The museum has its origins in 1923, and is housed in a building designed by Renzo Piano since 1997.

facts.text: The institution traces its origins back to the year 1923.
facts.sourceQuote: The museum has its origins in 1923, and is housed in a building designed by Renzo Piano since 1997.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The museum has its origins in 1923, and is housed in a building designed by Renzo Piano since 1997.

features.name: W139
features.opening: W139 is an artist-run space established in 1979 on the Warmoesstraat, Amsterdam, the Netherlands.

facts.text: Five young artists squatted the former theatre in October 1979 to protest commercial art.
facts.sourceQuote: The former theatre was squatted in October 1979 by five young artists as "a movement against the closed world of commercial art and museums".
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The former theatre was squatted in October 1979 by five young artists as "a movement against the closed world of commercial art and museums".

facts.text: In 2016, exhibitions included Gym of Absolute Technology and Shifting Spaces.
facts.sourceQuote: In 2016 the expositions 'Gym of Absolute Technology', 'Shifting Spaces' and 'UU&ME' were held.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 2016 the expositions 'Gym of Absolute Technology', 'Shifting Spaces' and 'UU&ME' were held.

features.name: Badhuistheater
features.opening: The Badhuistheater (Dutch: Bath house theatre) is a theater venue located in a former bath house on the east-side of Amsterdam.

facts.text: Renowned architect Arend Jan Westerman designed this unique building.
facts.sourceQuote: Designed by renowned architect Arend Jan Westerman, the building has a distinct circular shape around a central chimney.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Designed by renowned architect Arend Jan Westerman, the building has a distinct circular shape around a central chimney.

facts.text: The Dutch name Badhuistheater translates to "bath house theatre," reflecting its origin as a former bath house.
facts.sourceQuote: The Badhuistheater (Dutch: Bath house theatre) is a theater venue located in a former bath house on the east-side of Amsterdam.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Badhuistheater (Dutch: Bath house theatre) is a theater venue located in a former bath house on the east-side of Amsterdam.

facts.text: British actor and writer Michael Manicardi acquired the neglected building around 1985 to transform it into a theater.
facts.sourceQuote: The theater is run by British actor and writer Michael Manicardi who acquired the neglected bath house around 1985 and transformed it into a theater.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The theater is run by British actor and writer Michael Manicardi who acquired the neglected bath house around 1985 and transformed it into a theater.

facts.text: Seating capacity ranges from 50 to 120 people depending on the specific configuration chosen for each show.
facts.sourceQuote: As a theater it seats between 50 and 120 people, depending on the chosen configuration.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: As a theater it seats between 50 and 120 people, depending on the chosen configuration.

features.name: Buchenwald Memorial
features.opening: The Buchenwald monument is a monument placed on De Nieuwe Ooster cemetery.

facts.text: An urn containing ashes and earth from six European sites was buried there a week before the monument's 1955 unveiling.
facts.sourceQuote: Het monument, in de vorm van een grafsteen, werd op 26 oktober 1955 onthuld. Er werd toen een week eerder een urn begraven waarin as van slachtoffers en aarde opgeslagen werden uit Buchenwald, Putten (Razzia van Putten), Lidice (slachting), Dachau, Warschau, Auschwitz en Oradour-sur-Glane (Bloedbad van Oradour-sur-Glane).
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The monument, in the form of a gravestone, was unveiled on October 26, 1955. A week earlier, an urn was buried in which ashes of victims and earth were stored from Buchenwald, Putten (Razzia van Putten), Lidice (slaughter), Dachau, Warsaw, Auschwitz and Oradour-sur-Glane (Bloodbath of Oradour-sur-Glane).

facts.text: The sculptor Herman Schutte was a survivor of Camp Vught who designed the rising hands holding the urn.
facts.sourceQuote: De Zeeuwse kunstenaar Herman Schutte (1908-1964 en overlever van Kamp Vught) ontwierp een beeld bestaande uit twee handen die uit het graf omhoogsteken en een stenen urn vasthouden.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Zeelandish artist Herman Schutte (1908-1964 and survivor of Camp Vught) designed a sculpture consisting of two hands rising from the grave and holding a stone urn.

features.name: Anthony Winkler Prins
features.opening: A work of art in Amsterdam-Centrum is a reminder of Anthony Winkler Prins.

facts.text: Volten originally called the work 'the thing' because he found any formal title too heavy.
facts.sourceQuote: Volten noemde het zelf "het ding" (een ding tussen andere dingen op het plein), hij vond een titel met monument daarin te zwaar klinken.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Volten himself called it "the thing" (a thing among other things on the square), he found a title with a monument in it too heavy sounding.

features.name: Bevrijdingslinde
features.opening: Bevrijdingslinde van de Jordaankinderen is a war monument in Amsterdam-Centrum.

facts.text: In 1984, the monument nearly vanished when a utility company planned to build an electricity shed there.
facts.sourceQuote: In 1984 gingen boom en gedenksteen bijna verloren toen het Gemeentelijk Energie Bedrijf hier een elektriciteitshuisje wilde bouwen.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 1984, the tree and monument almost disappeared when the Municipal Energy Company wanted to build an electricity shed here.

features.name: Museum Vrolik
features.opening: Museum Vrolik is an anatomical museum renowned for its collection of medical heritage.

facts.text: Father and son professors Gerardus and Willem Vrolik assembled the original anatomical collection around 1800.
facts.sourceQuote: The museum's history begins around 1800 when Gerardus Vrolik (1775–1859) and his son Willem Vrolik (1801–1863) began assembling a collection of anatomical and medical specimens. Both were professors of anatomy at the Athenaeum Illustre, the predecessor of the University of Amsterdam.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The museum's history begins around 1800 when Gerardus Vrolik (1775–1859) and his son Willem Vrolik (1801–1863) began assembling a collection of anatomical and medical specimens. Both were professors of anatomy at the Athenaeum Illustre, the predecessor of the University of Amsterdam.

facts.text: Willem Vrolik specialized in teratology, publishing groundbreaking work on cyclopia and conjoined twins.
facts.sourceQuote: Willem Vrolik (1801–1863) was particularly interested in teratology (the study of congenital malformations) and made significant contributions to vertebrate teratology. He published extensively on conditions such as cyclopia, the pathogenesis of congenital anomalies, and conjoined twins.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Willem Vrolik (1801–1863) was particularly interested in teratology (the study of congenital malformations) and made significant contributions to vertebrate teratology. He published extensively on conditions such as cyclopia, the pathogenesis of congenital anomalies, and conjoined twins.

features.name: Albert
features.opening: Police dog Albert is a 1924 statue placed in Oosterpark in Amsterdam.

facts.text: Albert was a Tervuerense shepherd who helped police solve crimes before dying in 1923.
facts.sourceQuote: Het beeldje is neergezet ter nagedachtenis van politiehond Albert (roepnaam Ab of Appie), die leefde van 1916 tot en met maart 1923. De privéspeurhond was een Tervuerense herder van agent Water, die de Amsterdamse politie af en toe hielp bij het oplossen van misdrijven.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The small statue is placed in memory of police dog Albert (nickname Ab or Appie), who lived from 1916 to March 1923. The private search dog was a Tervuerense shepherd from agent Water, who occasionally helped the Amsterdam police solve crimes.

features.name: Muziekgebouw
features.opening: Muziekgebouw aan 't IJ (English: "Music Building on the IJ") is the main concert hall for contemporary classical music on the IJ in Amsterdam, Netherlands.

facts.text: The venue replaced the former Muziekcentrum de IJsbreker, which was shut down at Weesperzijde.
facts.sourceQuote: Before the Muziekgebouw there was Muziekcentrum de IJsbreker located at the Weesperzijde that got shut down and replaced by the Muziekgebouw.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Before the Muziekgebouw there was Muziekcentrum de IJsbreker located at the Weesperzijde that got shut down and replaced by the Muziekgebouw.

facts.text: The venue officially opened its doors to the public in 2005.
facts.sourceQuote: The building opened in 2005 and is located above the IJtunnel, a ten-minute walk from Amsterdam Centraal station.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The building opened in 2005 and is located above the IJtunnel, a ten-minute walk from Amsterdam Centraal station.

facts.text: Danish architects from the firm 3XN designed this concert hall.
facts.sourceQuote: The building was designed by Danish architects 3XN.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The building was designed by Danish architects 3XN.

features.name: Grenspaal
features.opening: Grenspaal, also known as the Column-bearing Turtle or Monument of Jacob Israël de Haan is a statue in Amsterdam-Centrum.

facts.text: Residents in the 1970s resisted the planned highway, causing clashes with police.
facts.sourceQuote: Buurtbewoners van de Nieuwmarktbuurt verzetten zich daar in de jaren zeventig hevig tegen. Onder meer schermutselingen met politie en Mobiele Eenheid leidden er toe dat de aanleg werd gestaakt.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Neighbors of the Nieuwmarkt neighborhood strongly resisted this in the 1970s. Among other things, clashes with the police and Mobile Unit led to the suspension of construction.

features.name: Obrechtkerk
features.opening: The Obrechtkerk (Dutch: Kerk van Onze Lieve Vrouw van de Allerheiligste Rozenkrans) (Church of Our Lady of the Most Holy Rosary) is the common name for the…

facts.text: Bishop Augustinus Callier consecrated the church in 1911.
facts.sourceQuote: The building was consecrated in 1911 by Mgr. A.J. Callier (Augustinus Callier), the bishop of Haarlem.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The building was consecrated in 1911 by Mgr. A.J. Callier (Augustinus Callier), the bishop of Haarlem.

facts.text: Artists including Jan Eloy Brom and Otto van Rees contributed to the church's decoration.
facts.sourceQuote: Many artists contributed to the decoration of the church, including Jan Eloy Brom, Joep Nicolas, Otto van Rees, John Rädecker, Matthieu Wiegman, Kees Dunselman, Nico Witteman and Mari Andriessen.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Many artists contributed to the decoration of the church, including Jan Eloy Brom, Joep Nicolas, Otto van Rees, John Rädecker, Matthieu Wiegman, Kees Dunselman, Nico Witteman and Mari Andriessen.

features.name: Dutch National Opera & Ballet
features.opening: National Opera & Ballet (formerly Het Muziektheater Amsterdam) is a theater in Amsterdam that was specially built for the performance of operas, ballets and…

facts.text: The complex earned the nickname Stopera, a blend of 'Stadhuis' (town hall) and 'opera'.
facts.sourceQuote: Het complex kreeg al snel de bijnaam Stopera (stadhuis + opera).
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The complex soon earned the nickname Stopera (town hall + opera house).

facts.text: The organization houses two distinct performing groups: De Nationale Opera and Het Nationale Ballet.
facts.sourceQuote: Het is tevens de naam van de organisatie die naast het theater ook de gezelschappen De Nationale Opera en Het Nationale Ballet omvat.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: It is also the name of the organization that, in addition to the theater, also includes the companies De Nationale Opera and Het Nationale Ballet.

features.name: Oosterkerk
features.opening: The Oosterkerk ("eastern church") is a 17th-Century Dutch Reformed church in Amsterdam, The Netherlands.

facts.text: After serving as a place of worship until 1962, the building fell into decay before a major restoration in the 1980s.
facts.sourceQuote: The church has not been used for church services since 1962, and fell into decay since then. It was restored in the 1980s.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The church has not been used for church services since 1962, and fell into decay since then. It was restored in the 1980s.

features.name: Internationaal Theater Amsterdam
features.opening: The Stadsschouwburg (Dutch pronunciation: [stɑtˈsxʌubʏr(ə)x]; Dutch: Municipal Theatre) of Amsterdam is a theatre building on the Leidseplein in Amsterdam,…

facts.text: Architects constructed this venue using a distinctive neo-Renaissance style.
facts.sourceQuote: The building was built in 1894 in the neo-Renaissance style, and was the home of the National Ballet and Opera.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The building was built in 1894 in the neo-Renaissance style, and was the home of the National Ballet and Opera.

facts.text: In the 16th century, precursors to modern theater organized into groups called 'rederijkerskamers'.
facts.sourceQuote: In the 16th century, these so-called precursors of modern theatre organized themselves into 'rederijkerskamers', which can be compared to theater companies.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In the 16th century, these so-called precursors of modern theatre organized themselves into 'rederijkerskamers', which can be compared to theater companies.

features.name: Muurschildering Johan Cruijff
features.opening: The Muurschildering Johan Cruijff is a mural in Amsterdam-Watergraafsmeer.

facts.text: Brazilian artist Paulo Consentino painted the mural with help from local youth over eleven days.
facts.sourceQuote: De Braziliaanse straat-kunstenaar Paulo Consentino, die ook elders in de wereld muurschilderingen gerelateerd aan de voetbalsport aanbracht, zag een wens in vervulling gaan om Johan Cruijff vast te leggen. De schildering die de kunstenaar met behulp van jongeren uit de buurt in elf dagen maakte werd gesponsord door Legacy of John Cruyff, Johan Cruyff Foundation en Akzo Nobel.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Brazilian street artist Paulo Consentino, who also painted murals related to the sport of football elsewhere in the world, saw a wish come true to capture Johan Cruijff. The painting that the artist made in eleven days with the help of young people from the neighborhood was sponsored by Legacy of John Cruyff, Johan Cruyff Foundation and Akzo Nobel.

facts.text: The flat overlooking the artwork faces Betondorp, the actual birthplace of Johan Cruijff.
facts.sourceQuote: De desbetreffende flat kijkt westwaarts uit over Betondorp, geboortegrond van de voetballer.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The relevant flat overlooks Betondorp to the west, the birthplace of the footballer.

features.name: Wine buyers' guildhall
features.opening: The Wijnkopersgildehuis ("Wine buyers' guildhall") is a former guildhall in Amsterdam.

facts.text: Master mason Pieter de Keyser designed an entrance gate that once depicted Bacchus riding a wine barrel.
facts.sourceQuote: The building was purchased in 1630 by the guild of wine buyers, who had it radically altered by the Amsterdam master mason Pieter de Keyser. In 1633 the right wing of the building (Koestraat number 10) began to be used as guildhall, with a meeting room for the guild directors at the front, a new back wing with a communal guild room (gildezaal), large cellars for storage, and an entrance gate designed by Pieter de Keyser. This gate originally depicted Bacchus astride a barrel of wine, but this was later replaced with an image of the saint Urban.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The building was purchased in 1630 by the guild of wine buyers, who had it radically altered by the Amsterdam master mason Pieter de Keyser. In 1633 the right wing of the building (Koestraat number 10) began to be used as guildhall, with a meeting room for the guild directors at the front, a new back wing with a communal guild room (gildezaal), large cellars for storage, and an entrance gate designed by Pieter de Keyser. This gate originally depicted Bacchus astride a barrel of wine, but this was later replaced with an image of the saint Urban.

features.name: Nationaal Holocaust Namenmonument
features.opening: The National Holocaust Names Memorial (Amsterdam) (Dutch: Holocaust Namenmonument) is since 2021 the Dutch national memorial for the Holocaust and the Porajmos…

facts.text: The Nederlands Auschwitz Comité founded this monument to commemorate the Dutch Holocaust victims.
facts.sourceQuote: The monument founded by the Nederlands Auschwitz Comité (Dutch Auschwitz Committee) is located in the former Jewish quarter (Dutch: Jodenbuurt) on a roughly north–south strip along the west side of the Weesperstraat, clockwise from the north between Nieuwe Herengracht, Weesperstraat, Nieuwe Keizersgracht, and Amstel river, east of the H'ART Museum Museum and the Hoftuin garden.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The monument founded by the Nederlands Auschwitz Comité (Dutch Auschwitz Committee) is located in the former Jewish quarter (Dutch: Jodenbuurt) on a roughly north–south strip along the west side of the Weesperstraat, clockwise from the north between Nieuwe Herengracht, Weesperstraat, Nieuwe Keizersgracht, and Amstel river, east of the H'ART Museum Museum and the Hoftuin garden.

facts.text: Alongside Jewish victims, the site also remembers 220 Roma and Sinti people murdered by the Nazi regime.
facts.sourceQuote: It commemorates the approximately 102,000 Jewish victims from the Netherlands who were arrested by the Nazi regime during the German occupation of the country (1940-1945), deported and mostly murdered in the Auschwitz and Sobibor death camps, as well as 220 Roma and Sinti victims.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: It commemorates the approximately 102,000 Jewish victims from the Netherlands who were arrested by the Nazi regime during the German occupation of the country (1940-1945), deported and mostly murdered in the Auschwitz and Sobibor death camps, as well as 220 Roma and Sinti victims.

features.name: Decembermoorden
features.opening: The December murders (Dutch: Decembermoorden) were the murders on 7, 8, and 9 December 1982, of fifteen prominent young Surinamese men who had criticized the…

facts.text: The dictator claimed on TV that all detainees died while attempting to flee.
facts.sourceQuote: On 10 December 1982, Bouterse claimed on national television that all of the detainees had been shot dead "in an attempt to flee".
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: On 10 December 1982, Bouterse claimed on national television that all of the detainees had been shot dead "in an attempt to flee".

facts.text: A former confidant later testified under oath that the dictator personally shot two men.
facts.sourceQuote: In March 2012, however, a former confidant of Bouterse testified under oath that Bouterse himself had shot two of the victims.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In March 2012, however, a former confidant of Bouterse testified under oath that Bouterse himself had shot two of the victims.

facts.text: Victims included lawyers, journalists, businessmen, soldiers, teachers and a union leader.
facts.sourceQuote: Among the victims were lawyers, journalists, businessmen, soldiers, university teachers and a union leader.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Among the victims were lawyers, journalists, businessmen, soldiers, university teachers and a union leader.

features.name: OT301
features.opening: OT301 is a self-managed social centre in a legalized squat in the Dutch city of Amsterdam, located on Overtoom 301.

facts.text: Artists squatted the former Dutch film academy in 1999 before the council sold it to a user association in 2006.
facts.sourceQuote: In 1999, a group of artists squatted the former Dutch film academy. After serving as a breeding ground for several years, the building was bought by the user association Eerste Hulp Bij Kunst (EHBK) from the council in 2006.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 1999, a group of artists squatted the former Dutch film academy. After serving as a breeding ground for several years, the building was bought by the user association Eerste Hulp Bij Kunst (EHBK) from the council in 2006.

facts.text: A vegan restaurant called De Peper closed in 2023 to become the lunch café Café Gilde.
facts.sourceQuote: OT301 is a venue for music and films, a non-profit print shop, artists' workspace and originally an 'organic cultural kitchen' (a vegan restaurant) called De Peper, which was closed in 2023 and has become a lunch café called Café Gilde.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: OT301 is a venue for music and films, a non-profit print shop, artists' workspace and originally an 'organic cultural kitchen' (a vegan restaurant) called De Peper, which was closed in 2023 and has become a lunch café called Café Gilde.

facts.text: Amsterdam Mayor Job Cohen awarded OT301 the Amsterdam Prize for the Arts in August 2007.
facts.sourceQuote: Amsterdam Mayor Job Cohen presented OT301 with the Amsterdamprijs voor de Kunsten (Amsterdam Prize for the Arts) from the Amsterdam Fonds voor de Kunst on 23 August 2007.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Amsterdam Mayor Job Cohen presented OT301 with the Amsterdamprijs voor de Kunsten (Amsterdam Prize for the Arts) from the Amsterdam Fonds voor de Kunst on 23 August 2007.

facts.text: The venue once housed offices for European Youth For Action and Green Pepper magazine.
facts.sourceQuote: Formerly, it housed the offices of European Youth For Action and Green Pepper magazine.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Formerly, it housed the offices of European Youth For Action and Green Pepper magazine.

features.name: OCCII
features.opening: The OCCII (Onafhankelijk Cultureel Centrum In It) is a venue for alternative and independent music at Amstelveenseweg 134, in Amsterdam, Netherlands.

facts.text: The original building was squatted in 1984 before being legalized five years later.
facts.sourceQuote: The original building was squatted in 1984 and "legalized" in 1989.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The original building was squatted in 1984 and "legalized" in 1989.

facts.text: Architect Abraham Salm designed the structure originally as a horse tram garage in 1883-84.
facts.sourceQuote: The building the OCCII resides in was built as a horse tram garage with stables in 1883-84 by architect Abraham Salm (1857–1915), who also designed (together with his father G.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The building the OCCII resides in was built as a horse tram garage with stables in 1883-84 by architect Abraham Salm (1857–1915), who also designed (together with his father G.

features.name: Mama Baranka (Moeder Rots)
features.opening: Mama Baranka is an artistic work of art in Vondelpark in Amsterdam-Zuid, in memory of the death of Kerwin Duinmeijer.

facts.text: The sculpture stands directly on the ground without a pedestal to symbolize the woman's power and connection to the earth.
facts.sourceQuote: De oerkracht wordt mede gesymboliseerd doordat de vrouw afgebeeld is met beide voeten in de grond, een sokkel ontbreekt.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The original power is also symbolized by the fact that the woman is depicted with both feet in the ground, a pedestal is missing.

features.name: Haarlemmermeerstation
features.opening: The Haarlemmermeer station, called Willemspark Station, was built in 1915 by architect H. van Emmerik, but originally designed by Karel de Bazel.

facts.text: The station was originally called Willemspark Station before adopting its current name.
facts.sourceQuote: The Haarlemmermeer station, called Willemspark Station, was built in 1915 by architect H. van Emmerik, but originally designed by Karel de Bazel.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Haarlemmermeer station, called Willemspark Station, was built in 1915 by architect H. van Emmerik, but originally designed by Karel de Bazel.

facts.text: Passenger service ended in 1950, leaving only coal freight until 1972.
facts.sourceQuote: Passenger traffic was discontinued in 1950, after which the traffic of goods (mainly coal transport) remained until 1972.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Passenger traffic was discontinued in 1950, after which the traffic of goods (mainly coal transport) remained until 1972.

facts.text: The station and its line became a tram museum route starting in 1975.
facts.sourceQuote: After the closure, the Haarlemmermeer station and the line to Amstelveen – Bovenkerk came to use from 1975 at the Electrische Museumtramlijn Amsterdam (EMA).
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: After the closure, the Haarlemmermeer station and the line to Amstelveen – Bovenkerk came to use from 1975 at the Electrische Museumtramlijn Amsterdam (EMA).

facts.text: Parts of the old track briefly supplied materials for Schiphol construction between 1976 and 1981.
facts.sourceQuote: During the construction of the Schiphol line, part of the route was again used from 1976 to 1981 for the supply of building materials and trainsets.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: During the construction of the Schiphol line, part of the route was again used from 1976 to 1981 for the supply of building materials and trainsets.

features.name: Fatih
features.opening: The Fatih mosque is a mosque on the Rozengracht in the Jordaan, Amsterdam-Centrum.

facts.text: Prayer attendees now face the former main entrance where a mihrab was installed.
facts.sourceQuote: Tijdens het gebed richten de aanwezigen zich tot de voormalige hoofdingang, waar een mihrab is aangebracht met daarboven een kalligrafie van 'Gods naam'.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: During prayer, the attendees turn to the former main entrance, where a mihrab has been installed with calligraphy of 'God's name' above it.

features.name: Artis
features.opening: Natura Artis Magistra (Latin for "Nature is the teacher of art"), commonly known just as Artis (Dutch pronunciation: [ˈɑrtɪs]), is a zoo and botanical garden…

facts.text: Visitors often called it Artis because only the middle gate, reading 'Artis', was usually open.
