facts.sourceQuote: Like many other "Torture Museums", it exhibits fake items, devices which were seldom or never used in real history, particularly in the "Middle Age", such as Scold's bridle, iron maidens (a literary invention of the 19th century) or "breast rippers" which may have been used only in the ancient Roman empire.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Like many other "Torture Museums", it exhibits fake items, devices which were seldom or never used in real history, particularly in the "Middle Age", such as Scold's bridle, iron maidens (a literary invention of the 19th century) or "breast rippers" which may have been used only in the ancient Roman empire.

facts.text: A separate Amsterdam institution called the Museum of Medieval Torture Instruments exists independently from this one.
facts.sourceQuote: The Torture Museum Amsterdam is not connected with another museum showcasing instruments of torture in Amsterdam: "the Museum of Medieval Torture Instruments".
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Torture Museum Amsterdam is not connected with another museum showcasing instruments of torture in Amsterdam: "the Museum of Medieval Torture Instruments".

facts.text: Narrow, dimly lit rooms house one or two torture devices each.
facts.sourceQuote: The museum consists of narrow and dimly lit rooms. Each room features one or two torture devices.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The museum consists of narrow and dimly lit rooms. Each room features one or two torture devices.

facts.text: Descriptions of device usage appear in six languages including English and Spanish.
facts.sourceQuote: The articles are translated into English, Dutch, French, German, Italian, and Spanish.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The articles are translated into English, Dutch, French, German, Italian, and Spanish.

features.name: Tobacco Theater
features.opening: The Tobacco Theater is a national monument, located on the "theaterstraat" Nes in Amsterdam (odd house numbers 75 to 87).

facts.text: Slanted window panes once flooded the space with light to help tobacco plants grow.
facts.sourceQuote: Door de scheef opgestelde raampartijen viel er veel licht in het gebouw wat de groei van de tabaksplanten bevorderde.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The slanted window panes allowed a lot of light into the building, which promoted the growth of the tobacco plants.

facts.text: Tobacco auctions were held in north-facing rooms so buyers could best judge leaf quality.
facts.sourceQuote: Ook was er in de panden in het begin van de twintigste eeuw de tabaksveiling gevestigd in een van de grote ruimtes waarvan de ramen op het noorden gericht zijn zodat de potentiële kopers de beste lichtval hadden om de kwaliteit van de tabaksbladeren te kunnen beoordelen.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: At the beginning of the twentieth century, there was also the tobacco auction held in one of the large rooms in the buildings, whose windows faced north so that potential buyers had the best lighting to assess the quality of the tobacco leaves.

features.name: Mor Sharbil
features.opening: The building Burgemeester Eliasstraat 72-74 in Amsterdam-Slotermeer Amsterdam has been a municipal monument since 2011.

facts.text: The original church on this site was demolished in 1939 before a new structure rose in 1954.
facts.sourceQuote: In 1954 verrees op deze plek een nieuwe Sint-Catharinakerk, nadat de oude kerk in 1939 was gesloopt.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 1954, a new St. Catherine's Church was built on this site, after the old church was demolished in 1939.

facts.text: Although dedicated to Saint Sharbel, locals still commonly call the building Catherine's Church.
facts.sourceQuote: Het gebouw is sindsdien in gebruik als Syrisch-orthodoxe kerk gewijd aan Sint-Sharbel (Mor Sharbil), maar in de volksmond wordt nog steeds "Catharinakerk" gebruikt
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Since then, the building has been used as a Syrian Orthodox church dedicated to Saint Sharbel (Mor Sharbil), but in popular parlance it is still commonly referred to as the "Catherine's Church"

features.name: Stadhuis
features.opening: The Weesp City Hall is the former city hall of Weesp, Netherlands.

facts.text: Architect Jacob Otten Husly designed the structure with his assistant Leendert Viervant the Younger.
facts.sourceQuote: The building was designed by the architects Jacob Otten Husly (1738-1796) and his assistant Leendert Viervant the Younger.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The building was designed by the architects Jacob Otten Husly (1738-1796) and his assistant Leendert Viervant the Younger.

facts.text: Construction of the building took place between the years 1772 and 1776.
facts.sourceQuote: They built it during the years 1772-1776.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: They built it during the years 1772-1776.

facts.text: The municipal council met in the Raadzaal until Weesp joined Amsterdam on March 24, 2022.
facts.sourceQuote: The main body of the municipality, the municipal council, convened in the Raadzaal (Council Hall) until 24 March 2022 when Weesp became part of the municipality of Amsterdam.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The main body of the municipality, the municipal council, convened in the Raadzaal (Council Hall) until 24 March 2022 when Weesp became part of the municipality of Amsterdam.

facts.text: Weddings and official proceedings still take place in the former Vierschaar and Burgerzaal halls.
facts.sourceQuote: The administrative offices have moved, but the former Vierschaar and Burgerzaal (Civic Hall) are still used for weddings and other official proceedings.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The administrative offices have moved, but the former Vierschaar and Burgerzaal (Civic Hall) are still used for weddings and other official proceedings.

features.name: Noorderkerk
features.opening: The Noorderkerk (Dutch for "northern church") is a 17th-century Protestant church in Amsterdam, The Netherlands.

facts.text: Illicit meetings for the 1941 February Strike were held on the square surrounding this church.
facts.sourceQuote: In 1941, organisers of the February Strike held illicit public meetings on Noordermarkt, the square around the church. This is commemorated by a plaque on the south face of the church.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 1941, organisers of the February Strike held illicit public meetings on Noordermarkt, the square around the church. This is commemorated by a plaque on the south face of the church.

features.name: Dutch Resistance Museum
features.opening: The Resistance Museum (Dutch: Verzetsmuseum) is a museum located in the Plantage neighbourhood in Amsterdam, the Netherlands.

facts.text: Permanent exhibits recreate Amsterdam streets using big photos, old posters, objects, films and sounds.
facts.sourceQuote: Permanent exhibits of the museum recreate the atmosphere of the streets of Amsterdam during the German occupation of World War II. Big photographs, old posters, objects, films and sounds from that time, help to recreate the scene.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Permanent exhibits of the museum recreate the atmosphere of the streets of Amsterdam during the German occupation of World War II. Big photographs, old posters, objects, films and sounds from that time, help to recreate the scene.

facts.text: A Jewish singing society named Oefening Baart Kunst constructed this building in 1876.
facts.sourceQuote: The building bearing the Star of David and the name of Petrus Plancius (1550-1622), the Renaissance Amsterdam clergyman and geographer, was built in 1876 by the Jewish singing society Oefening Baart Kunst (practice makes perfect).
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The building bearing the Star of David and the name of Petrus Plancius (1550-1622), the Renaissance Amsterdam clergyman and geographer, was built in 1876 by the Jewish singing society Oefening Baart Kunst (practice makes perfect).

features.name: Anton de Kom
features.opening: The Monument voor Anton de Kom is an artwork in Amsterdam-Zuidoost.

facts.text: Van Loon compared the Surinamese wood to De Kom, who was also brought to the Netherlands.
facts.sourceQuote: Van Loon zag een gelijkenis met De Kom, die (op bevel van het gouvernement) ook naar Nederland was gebracht en wees daarnaast op de uitdrukking “uit het goede hout gesneden”.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Van Loon saw a similarity with De Kom, who (at the orders of the government) had also been brought to the Netherlands and also pointed out the expression "cut from good wood".

facts.text: Opponents covered the statue with banners because they found it scandalous that De Kom was depicted naked.
facts.sourceQuote: Zij waren van mening dat het schandalig was dat De Kom naakt was afgebeeld, hetgeen voor zover bekend bij geen enkel ander beeld van een verzetsheld was gebeurd.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: They felt that it was scandalous that De Kom was depicted naked, which had not happened to any other image of a resistance hero to date as far as they knew.

facts.text: In 2007, the Amsterdam Zuidoost Neighborhood Council voted to let the controversial statue remain in place.
facts.sourceQuote: In 2007 stemde de Stadsdeelraad Amsterdam Zuidoost over de vraag of het beeld alsnog mocht blijven of verwijderd moest worden. Hieruit kwam dat het beeld mocht blijven.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 2007, the Amsterdam Zuidoost Neighborhood Council voted on whether the statue should remain or be removed. This meant that the image could remain.

features.name: Christelijke Gereformeerde Kerk - Amstelkerk
features.opening: The Amstelkerk (English: Amstel Church) is a Reformed church building in central Amsterdam, Netherlands.

facts.text: Plans to build the Dutch Mint next door were drawn up but never executed.
facts.sourceQuote: In the early 19th century, plans were drawn up, but never executed, to build the Dutch Mint in the square next to church.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In the early 19th century, plans were drawn up, but never executed, to build the Dutch Mint in the square next to church.

features.name: Uilenburger Synagoge
features.opening: The Uilenburger Synagoge or Uilenburgersjoel is a synagogue on the Nieuwe Uilenburgerstraat on the island of Uilenburg in the former Amsterdam Jewish Quarter.

facts.text: Ashkenazi Jews commissioned this Louis XV-style structure in 1766.
facts.sourceQuote: De synagoge werd in Lodewijk XV-stijl gebouwd in 1766 voor de Asjkenazische Joden.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The synagogue was built in Louis XV style in 1766 for the Ashkenazi Jews.

facts.text: For centuries, the synagogue was only accessible via corridors and stairs to rear buildings.
facts.sourceQuote: Het was eeuwenlang alleen bereikbaar via gangen (stegen naar achterliggende gebouwen).
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: For centuries it was only accessible via corridors (stairs to rear buildings).

features.name: Chinatown
features.opening: Chinatown is the Chinese quarter of Amsterdam.

facts.text: Dragon dances, lion dances, and fireworks are held annually for both New Year's Day and Chinese New Year.
facts.sourceQuote: Nieuwjaarsdag en Chinees nieuwjaar wordt in deze buurt jaarlijks gevierd met drakendans, leeuwendans en knalvuurwerk.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: New Year's Day and Chinese New Year are celebrated in this neighborhood annually with dragon dance, lion dance and fireworks.

features.name: AMHC Westerpark
features.opening: Amsterdamsche Mixed Hockey Club Westerpark is a hockey club from Amsterdam in the West district.

facts.text: The club operates five fields at Spieringhorn sports park.
facts.sourceQuote: AMHC Westerpark heeft vijf eigen velden op sportpark Spieringhorn, en sinds 2016 een eigen clubhuis.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: AMHC Westerpark has five own fields on sports park Spieringhorn, and since 2016 a own clubhouse.

facts.text: AMHC Westerpark opened its own clubhouse in 2016.
facts.sourceQuote: AMHC Westerpark heeft vijf eigen velden op sportpark Spieringhorn, en sinds 2016 een eigen clubhuis.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: AMHC Westerpark has five own fields on sports park Spieringhorn, and since 2016 a own clubhouse.

features.name: Museum Weesp
features.opening: Museum Weesp is located on the second floor of the Weesp Town Hall in the Dutch province of North Holland.

facts.text: A rare liturgical chalice used by priests for sacraments in the thirteenth or fourteenth century is a top exhibit.
facts.sourceQuote: Tot de topstukken behoort een liturgische schenkkan uit de 13e of 14e eeuw, een kannetje dat priesters gebruikten bij het toedienen van sacramenten.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The top pieces include a liturgical chalice from the 13th or 14th century, a chalice that priests used when administering sacraments.

facts.text: A porcelain donation from Baron F. van Heeckeren van Waliën's estate helped establish the collection.
facts.sourceQuote: In 1974 werd dit tot museum na een schenking porselein, die werd verkregen uit de nalatenschap van Baron F. van Heeckeren van Waliën.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 1974, this was turned into a museum after a donation of porcelain, which was obtained from the estate of Baron F. van Heeckeren van Waliën.

facts.text: Local history here covers three key industries: porcelain, cocoa, and bicycles.
facts.sourceQuote: Het belicht de geschiedenis van Weesp, waarvan de geschiedenis samenhangt met porselein, cacao en fietsen.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: It highlights the history of Weesp, whose history is related to porcelain, cocoa and bicycles.

features.name: Haarlemmerpoort
features.opening: The Haarlemmerpoort on the Haarlemmerplein in Amsterdam is officially called Willemspoort but is never called that in the city.

facts.text: Hendrick de Keyser designed the fourth gate built on Haarlemmerplein.
facts.sourceQuote: Met de Derde Uitleg, de uitbreiding tot de Singelgracht vanaf 1610, verrees er in 1615 een nieuwe, vierde, Haarlemmerpoort op het nieuw aangelegde Haarlemmerplein. Deze poort was ontworpen door Hendrick de Keyser.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: With the Third Explanation, the extension to the Singelgracht from 1610, a new, fourth, Haarlemmerpoort was built in 1615 on the newly constructed Haarlemmerplein. This gate was designed by Hendrick de Keyser.

facts.text: The first gate stood near Haringpakkerssteeg before a second appeared at the Old Haarlemmersluis.
facts.sourceQuote: De eerste 'Haarlemmerpoort' stond in de 14e eeuw ter hoogte van de Haringpakkerssteeg. Omstreeks 1397 verrees de tweede Haarlemmerpoort, deze stond op de (Oude) Haarlemmersluis in de Nieuwendijk (hier is nu de Martelaarsgracht).
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The first 'Haarlemmerpoort' stood in the 14th century near the Haringpakkerssteeg. Around 1397, the second Haarlemmerpoort was built, it stood at the (Old) Haarlemmersluis in the Nieuwendijk (this is now the Martelaarsgracht).

facts.text: Eight Corinthian columns made of Bentheimer sandstone line the passageway.
facts.sourceQuote: In de doorgang zijn acht Korinthische zuilen geplaatst, gemaakt van Bentheimer zandsteen.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Eight Corinthian columns are placed in the passageway, made of Bentheimer sandstone.

facts.text: The passageway ceiling features a cassette design decorated with rosettes.
facts.sourceQuote: Het cassetteplafond in de doorgang is voorzien van rozetten.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The cassette ceiling in the passageway is equipped with rosettes.

features.name: Rijksmuseum
features.opening: The Rijksmuseum (Dutch: [ˈrɛiksmyˌzeːjʏm] ) is the national museum of the Netherlands dedicated to Dutch arts and history, located at the Museum Square in the…

facts.text: Early holdings lacked works by Rembrandt, Vermeer, or Frans Hals despite their fame.
facts.sourceQuote: Although the seventeenth century was beginning to be recognised as the key period in Dutch art, the museum did not then hold paintings by Frans Hals, Rembrandt, Jan Steen, Johannes Vermeer, or Jacob van Ruisdael.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Although the seventeenth century was beginning to be recognised as the key period in Dutch art, the museum did not then hold paintings by Frans Hals, Rembrandt, Jan Steen, Johannes Vermeer, or Jacob van Ruisdael.

facts.text: Napoleon took the stadholder's collection to Paris before it returned in 1815.
facts.sourceQuote: Napoleon had carried off the stadholder's collection to Paris; the paintings were returned to The Netherlands in 1815 but housed in the Mauritshuis in The Hague rather than the Rijksmuseum.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Napoleon had carried off the stadholder's collection to Paris; the paintings were returned to The Netherlands in 1815 but housed in the Mauritshuis in The Hague rather than the Rijksmuseum.

facts.text: The exhibition featured marriage portraits of Marten Soolmans and Oopjen Coppit.
facts.sourceQuote: Principal features were the marriage portraits of Marten Soolmans and Oopjen Coppit along with the presentation of the Night Watch immediately before its planned restoration.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Principal features were the marriage portraits of Marten Soolmans and Oopjen Coppit along with the presentation of the Night Watch immediately before its planned restoration.

facts.text: Over 300 prints were shown alongside 22 paintings and 60 drawings in one collection.
facts.sourceQuote: Consisting of 22 paintings, 60 drawings and over 300 prints, this was the first time they had all been exhibited together.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Consisting of 22 paintings, 60 drawings and over 300 prints, this was the first time they had all been exhibited together.

features.name: Rozenoord
features.opening: Fusilladeplaats Rozenoord is a World War II memorial in the Dutch city of Amsterdam.

facts.text: The name Rozenoord comes from a 1930s teahouse built on the site of an old rose garden.
facts.sourceQuote: Fusilladeplaats Rozenoord is a World War II memorial in the Dutch city of Amsterdam. 'Fusilladeplaats' might be translated into English as 'firing squad place'. 'Rozenoord' was originally a rose garden, whose name was adopted during the 1930s by a teahouse by the Amsteldijk, a dyke in Amsterdam.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Fusilladeplaats Rozenoord is a World War II memorial in the Dutch city of Amsterdam. 'Fusilladeplaats' might be translated into English as 'firing squad place'. 'Rozenoord' was originally a rose garden, whose name was adopted during the 1930s by a teahouse by the Amsteldijk, a dyke in Amsterdam.

facts.text: German forces executed over one hundred Dutch civilians at this spot between January and April 1945.
facts.sourceQuote: Between 18 January and 14 April 1945, German occupation forces shot dead more than 100 Dutch civilians at Fusilladeplaats Rozenoord (at least that many have been identified, several of them resistance fighters).
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Between 18 January and 14 April 1945, German occupation forces shot dead more than 100 Dutch civilians at Fusilladeplaats Rozenoord (at least that many have been identified, several of them resistance fighters).

features.name: Monument voor gefusilleerde verzetstrijders
features.opening: The Resistance Monument Apollolaan is a work of art in Amsterdam-Zuid.

facts.text: On October 24, 1944, German occupiers executed 29 prisoners here as reprisal for resistance actions.
facts.sourceQuote: Op die plek werden op 24 oktober 1944 29 gevangenen uit het Huis van Bewaring aan de Weteringschans door de Duitse bezetter naar deze plek gebracht om vervolgens zonder vorm van proces gefusilleerd te worden. De bezettingsmacht deed dit als represaille voor plaatsgevonden actie van het verzet.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: On that place, on October 24, 1944, 29 prisoners from the Detention Center at the Weteringschans were brought to this place by the German occupiers to be then executed without any form of trial. The occupying force did this as a reprisal for actions taken by the resistance.

facts.text: Sculptor Jan Havermans designed the statue after receiving his final order in February 1951.
facts.sourceQuote: Het ontwerp van het beeld werd al in 1950 voorbestemd aan Jan Havermans. De definitieve opdracht volgde echter pas in februari 1951; opdrachtgever was het Initiatief Comité Amsterdam (ICA).
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The design of the statue was already destined for Jan Havermans in 1950. However, the final order was only issued in February 1951; the client was the Amsterdam Initiative Committee (ICA).

features.name: De Nieuwe Stad
features.opening: Kerkcentrum De Nieuwe Stad is a church in Amsterdam-Zuidoost (Bijlmermeer), built in 1992/1993 and designed by the architects Lafour and Wijk.

facts.text: Renovation of these faith centers began in the early 1990s.
facts.sourceQuote: Bij deze gebouwen begon echter de renovatie en sanering al in de vroege jaren negentig.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: However, renovation and rehabilitation began on these buildings in the early 1990s.

features.name: Amsterdam
features.opening: The Amsterdam of 1990 is a replica of the mirror return ship of the same name of the Dutch East India Company (VOC).

facts.text: Volunteers built the replica from iroko wood between 1982 and 1990.
facts.sourceQuote: Tussen 1982 en 1990 werd hiervan uit irokohout een replica gebouwd door 400 vrijwilligers van de Stichting Amsterdam Bouwt Oostindiëvaarder (SABO).
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Between 1982 and 1990, a replica was built from iroko wood by 400 volunteers of the Stichting Amsterdam Bouwt Oostindiëvaarder (SABO).

facts.text: The ship sailed from IJmuiden to Amsterdam on August 9, 1990, for the Sail event.
facts.sourceQuote: In de periode daarvoor werd tezamen met Sail Amsterdam 1990 besloten dat de Amsterdam zou meevaren voorop bij de Sail-intocht van IJmuiden naar Amsterdam op 9 augustus 1990.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In the period before that, together with Sail Amsterdam, it was decided in 1990 that the Amsterdam would sail ahead during the Sail entrance from IJmuiden to Amsterdam on August 9, 1990.

features.name: Het Huis met den Hoofden
features.opening: The House with the Heads (known as 'Huis met de Hoofden' in Dutch) is a large canal house on the Keizersgracht 123 in Amsterdam, named after the six ornaments…

facts.text: Wealthy stock trader Nicolaas Sohier commissioned the house in 1622.
facts.sourceQuote: The house was built in 1622 for Nicolaas Sohier, a wealthy stock trader and art lover.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The house was built in 1622 for Nicolaas Sohier, a wealthy stock trader and art lover.

facts.text: Pieter de Keyser likely executed the Renaissance façade after his father died.
facts.sourceQuote: The renaissance façade is attributed to architect Hendrick de Keyser, but was probably executed and completed by his son Pieter de Keyser, as Hendrick had already died in 1621.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The renaissance façade is attributed to architect Hendrick de Keyser, but was probably executed and completed by his son Pieter de Keyser, as Hendrick had already died in 1621.

facts.text: Legends claim a maid beheaded six thieves, inspiring the facade heads.
facts.sourceQuote: As for the heads in the façade, there is a legend that they refer to six thieves who had tried to break in the house and were then beheaded by the maid.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: As for the heads in the façade, there is a legend that they refer to six thieves who had tried to break in the house and were then beheaded by the maid.

facts.text: Sohier's wife and two daughters died shortly after he moved into the house.
facts.sourceQuote: Shortly after Sohier moved to the house, his wife and two daughters died.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Shortly after Sohier moved to the house, his wife and two daughters died.

facts.text: The De Geer family owned the property for four generations as a hub for trade and science.
facts.sourceQuote: Along four generations the house remained in possession of the family De Geer, who made it a nerve center of exchange for ideas in respect to trade, science, philosophy and culture.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Along four generations the house remained in possession of the family De Geer, who made it a nerve center of exchange for ideas in respect to trade, science, philosophy and culture.

facts.text: From 1909 to 1931, the building housed the Conservatorium van Amsterdam.
facts.sourceQuote: After a restoration in 1907 by the municipality, it served the Conservatorium van Amsterdam from 1909 to 1931.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: After a restoration in 1907 by the municipality, it served the Conservatorium van Amsterdam from 1909 to 1931.

features.name: Huis De Pinto
features.opening: Huis De Pinto is a former Amsterdam city mansion on the Sint Antoniesbreestraat near the Rembrandthuis.

facts.text: The double facade was designed by Elias Bouman after David de Pinto acquired the adjacent building.
facts.sourceQuote: In 1651 they were sold by the Burch heirs to Isaack de Pinto (who died 1681) Inherited by his only son David de Pinto, who bought the neighboring house in 1686 and ordered the double facade designed by Elias Bouman.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 1651 they were sold by the Burch heirs to Isaack de Pinto (who died 1681) Inherited by his only son David de Pinto, who bought the neighboring house in 1686 and ordered the double facade designed by Elias Bouman.

facts.text: From 1975 until 2012, the building served as a public library before becoming offices.
facts.sourceQuote: Sold in 1756 by Aron de David de Pinto Almost demolished during WWII Restored in 1975 Public library 1975-2012 Offices and community hall
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Sold in 1756 by Aron de David de Pinto Almost demolished during WWII Restored in 1975 Public library 1975-2012 Offices and community hall

facts.text: Huis De Pinto honors a dynasty of Portuguese-Jewish merchant bankers.
facts.sourceQuote: It was originally built in 1605 and is named after a leading Amsterdam family dynasty of Portuguese-Jewish merchant bankers.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: It was originally built in 1605 and is named after a leading Amsterdam family dynasty of Portuguese-Jewish merchant bankers.

facts.text: Grandson Isaac de Pinto grew up within these historic walls.
facts.sourceQuote: His son commissioned the unusual facade, and his grandson Isaac de Pinto grew up there.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: His son commissioned the unusual facade, and his grandson Isaac de Pinto grew up there.

features.name: De Hallen
features.opening: The Hallen is a cultural center in the Kinkerbuurt in Amsterdam-West, with more than two million visitors per year.

facts.text: The tram depot operated until 1996 before becoming a hub for various tenants.
facts.sourceQuote: Het centrum is gevestigd in de voormalige Remise Tollensstraat van de Gemeentetram Amsterdam, gebouwd in 1902-'05 en is tot 1996 in gebruik geweest bij het Gemeentevervoerbedrijf Amsterdam, daarna waren de gebouwen nog in gebruik bij diverse huurders, waaronder tot 2005 het Amsterdams Openbaar Vervoer Museum.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The center is located in the former Remise Tollensstraat of the Municipal Tramway Amsterdam, built in 1902-'05 and was in use until 1996 with the Municipal Transport Company Amsterdam, after which the buildings were still in use by various tenants, including until 2005 the Amsterdam Public Transport Museum.

facts.text: The Amsterdam Public Transport Museum occupied the site until 2005.
facts.sourceQuote: Het centrum is gevestigd in de voormalige Remise Tollensstraat van de Gemeentetram Amsterdam, gebouwd in 1902-'05 en is tot 1996 in gebruik geweest bij het Gemeentevervoerbedrijf Amsterdam, daarna waren de gebouwen nog in gebruik bij diverse huurders, waaronder tot 2005 het Amsterdams Openbaar Vervoer Museum.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The center is located in the former Remise Tollensstraat of the Municipal Tramway Amsterdam, built in 1902-'05 and was in use until 1996 with the Municipal Transport Company Amsterdam, after which the buildings were still in use by various tenants, including until 2005 the Amsterdam Public Transport Museum.

facts.text: One Filmhallen room recreates the interior of the former Cinema Parisien from Nieuwendijk.
facts.sourceQuote: In de Filmhallen is een zaal is ingericht met het interieur van de vroegere Cinema Parisien, die aan de Nieuwendijk stond.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In the Filmhallen, one room is decorated with the interior of the former Cinema Parisien, which stood on Nieuwendijk.

facts.text: A public passage runs parallel to Kinkerstraat, connecting all spaces except the hotel.
facts.sourceQuote: Met uitzondering van het hotel liggen alle organisaties en bedrijven in De Hallen aan de openbare Hannie Dankbaarpassage die evenwijdig aan de Kinkerstraat loopt. Deze passage verbindt alle ruimtes in het gebouwencomplex.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: With the exception of the hotel, all organizations and companies in De Hallen are located on the public Hannie Dankbaarpassage that runs parallel to Kinkerstraat. This passage connects all the spaces in the building complex.

features.name: Walloon Church
features.opening: The Walloon Church (Dutch: Waalse Kerk; French: Église Wallonne) is a Protestant church building in Amsterdam, along the southern stretch of the Oudezijds…

facts.text: A restoration revealed so many tombstones that the concrete floor was replaced with a new self-supporting structure.
facts.sourceQuote: During this restoration, so many tombstones were found that a decision was made to replace the concrete floor with a new, self-supporting floor with its own foundation.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: During this restoration, so many tombstones were found that a decision was made to replace the concrete floor with a new, self-supporting floor with its own foundation.

facts.text: Painter Bartholomeus van der Helst and scientist Jan Swammerdam are interred within its walls.
facts.sourceQuote: The painter Bartholomeus van der Helst (1613-1670) and the scientist Jan Swammerdam (1637-1680) are interred in the church.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The painter Bartholomeus van der Helst (1613-1670) and the scientist Jan Swammerdam (1637-1680) are interred in the church.

features.name: University of Amsterdam
features.opening: The University of Amsterdam (abbreviated as UvA; Dutch: Universiteit van Amsterdam) is a public research university located in Amsterdam, Netherlands.

facts.text: Mathematician Luitzen Brouwer and physicist Johannes van der Waals were former professors.
facts.sourceQuote: Notable former professors include winner of the Nobel Peace Prize in 1911 Tobias Asser, mathematician Luitzen Egbertus Jan Brouwer, winner of the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1901 Jacobus Henricus van 't Hoff, winner of the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1910 Johannes Diderik van der Waals, winner of the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1902 Pieter Zeeman, winner of the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1953 Frits Zernike, and scholar of religion, C.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Notable former professors include winner of the Nobel Peace Prize in 1911 Tobias Asser, mathematician Luitzen Egbertus Jan Brouwer, winner of the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1901 Jacobus Henricus van 't Hoff, winner of the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1910 Johannes Diderik van der Waals, winner of the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1902 Pieter Zeeman, winner of the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1953 Frits Zernike, and scholar of religion, C.

facts.text: Municipal authorities established the university in 1632.
facts.sourceQuote: Established in 1632 by municipal authorities, it is the fourth-oldest academic institution in the Netherlands still in operation.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Established in 1632 by municipal authorities, it is the fourth-oldest academic institution in the Netherlands still in operation.

features.name: Voormalige Schouwburgpoort
features.opening: The Theatre of Van Campen (Dutch: Schouwburg van Van Campen, pronounced [ˈsxʌubʏr(ə)x fɑɱ vɑŋ ˈkɑmpə(n)]) was a theatre located at Keizersgracht 384 in…

facts.text: Jacob van Campen coined the Dutch word Schouwburg when designing this theatre in 1637.
facts.sourceQuote: The theatre was built in 1637, by Jacob van Campen, who coined the word Schouwburg for it.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The theatre was built in 1637, by Jacob van Campen, who coined the word Schouwburg for it.

facts.text: The architrave above the surviving entrance bears Vondel's inscription about the world being a stage.
facts.sourceQuote: Vondel had also written the text in the architrave of the theatre's entrance: De weereld is een speeltoneel Elck speelt zijn rol en krijght zijn deel (The world is a theatre, Everyone plays his role and gets his part) This entrance still survives from the original building.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Vondel had also written the text in the architrave of the theatre's entrance: De weereld is een speeltoneel Elck speelt zijn rol en krijght zijn deel (The world is a theatre, Everyone plays his role and gets his part) This entrance still survives from the original building.

features.name: Anne Frank House
features.opening: The Anne Frank House (Dutch: Anne Frank Huis) is a writer's house and biographical museum dedicated to Jewish wartime diarist Anne Frank.

facts.text: The hiding space was just 450 square feet yet considered luxurious by its inhabitants.
facts.sourceQuote: Though the total amount of floor space in the inhabited rooms came to only about 450 square feet (42 m2), Anne Frank wrote in her diary that it was relatively luxurious compared to other hiding places they had heard about.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Though the total amount of floor space in the inhabited rooms came to only about 450 square feet (42 m2), Anne Frank wrote in her diary that it was relatively luxurious compared to other hiding places they had heard about.

facts.text: After the arrest, seized belongings were distributed to bombed-out families in Germany.
facts.sourceQuote: After those in hiding were arrested, the hiding place was cleared by order of the arresting officers and all the remaining contents (clothes, furniture, and personal belongings) of the Frank family and their friends were seized and distributed to bombed-out families in Germany.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: After those in hiding were arrested, the hiding place was cleared by order of the arresting officers and all the remaining contents (clothes, furniture, and personal belongings) of the Frank family and their friends were seized and distributed to bombed-out families in Germany.

facts.text: Anne Frank died during the war before her diary was published in 1947.
facts.sourceQuote: She did not survive the war but her wartime diary was published in 1947.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: She did not survive the war but her wartime diary was published in 1947.

facts.text: In 2017, the site welcomed 1.27 million visitors.
facts.sourceQuote: In 2017, the museum had 1.27 million visitors and was the third most visited museum in the Netherlands, after the Van Gogh Museum and the Rijksmuseum.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 2017, the museum had 1.27 million visitors and was the third most visited museum in the Netherlands, after the Van Gogh Museum and the Rijksmuseum.

features.name: Moskee El-Hijra
features.opening: The Olive Branch was built in 1956 as a Baptist church on Arthur van Schendelstraat in the garden city of Slotermeer in Amsterdam Nieuw-West.

facts.text: A 1955 sculpture called Flying Bird once hung outside but was moved to a central Amsterdam church entrance.
facts.sourceQuote: Een door Wessel Couzijn in 1955 gemaakte sculptuur, Vliegende vogel, die sinds 1956 buiten aan de linker zijmuur van deze kerk hing, is hier verwijderd en herplaatst naar boven de ingang aan de Herengracht van de Doopsgezinde Singelkerk in het centrum van Amsterdam.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: A sculpture by Wessel Couzijn made in 1955, Flying bird, which has hung outside on the left side wall of this church since 1956, has been removed here and relocated above the entrance on the Herengracht of the Baptist Singelkerk in the center of Amsterdam.

features.name: Concertgebouw
features.opening: The Royal Concertgebouw (Dutch: het Koninklijk Concertgebouw, pronounced [ət ˈkoːnɪŋklə kɔnˈsɛrtxəˌbʌu]) is a concert hall in Amsterdam, Netherlands.

facts.text: Construction started in a pasture outside Amsterdam that later became part of Amstelveen.
facts.sourceQuote: Construction began in 1883 in a pasture that was then outside the city, in Nieuwer-Amstel, a municipality that in 1964 became Amstelveen.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Construction began in 1883 in a pasture that was then outside the city, in Nieuwer-Amstel, a municipality that in 1964 became Amstelveen.

facts.text: A massive inaugural performance featured 120 musicians and 500 singers on stage.
facts.sourceQuote: The hall opened on 11 April 1888 with an inaugural concert, in which an orchestra of 120 musicians and a chorus of 500 singers participated, performing works of Wagner, Handel, Bach, and Beethoven.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The hall opened on 11 April 1888 with an inaugural concert, in which an orchestra of 120 musicians and a chorus of 500 singers participated, performing works of Wagner, Handel, Bach, and Beethoven.

facts.text: The Dutch term Concertgebouw translates directly to concert building.
facts.sourceQuote: The Dutch term "concertgebouw" translates into English as "concert building".
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Dutch term "concertgebouw" translates into English as "concert building".

facts.text: Queen Beatrix granted the royal title Koninklijk on April 11, 2013.
facts.sourceQuote: In celebration of the building's 125th anniversary, Queen Beatrix bestowed the royal title "Koninklijk" upon the building on 11 April 2013, as she had on the Royal Concertgebouw Orchestra upon its 100th in 1988.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In celebration of the building's 125th anniversary, Queen Beatrix bestowed the royal title "Koninklijk" upon the building on 11 April 2013, as she had on the Royal Concertgebouw Orchestra upon its 100th in 1988.

features.name: Dorpskerk Durgerdam
features.opening: The Dorpskerk Durgerdam, originally the Reformed church of Durgerdam, is the Protestant church of Durgerdam in Amsterdam-Noord.

facts.text: A bell cast by Pieter Hemony in 1672 hangs within the church alongside memorials to local captains.
facts.sourceQuote: Ook andere bouwelementen en voorwerpen stammen uit de oude kerk, dit zijn: De eikenhouten preekstoel, met knoppen van ebbenhout en met een koperen doopvont, uit 1646 Het doophek, eveneens van eikenhout en uit de 17e eeuw stammend, dat moest worden ingekort omdat de huidige kerk minder breed is Drie koperen kroonluchters, aangeschaft in 1666 en 1667, elk met zestien kaarshouders De luidklok van Pieter Hemony uit 1672 Een bord ter herinnering aan Gerrit Frederickszoon, een van de kapiteins in de Zeeslag bij Duins in 1639
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Other building elements and objects also come from the old church, these are: The oak pulpit, with ebony knobs and with a copper baptismal font, from 1646 The baptismal canopy, also made of oak and dating from the 17th century, which had to be shortened because the current church is less wide Three copper chandeliers, purchased in 1666 and 1667, each with sixteen candle holders Pieter Hemony's bell from 1672 A plaque in memory of Gerrit Frederickszoon, one of the captains in the Battle of the Sea at Duins in 1639

facts.text: Dorpskerk Durgerdam means Village Church of Durgerdam and was originally called the Reformed Church.
facts.sourceQuote: De Dorpskerk Durgerdam, oorspronkelijk de Hervormde kerk van Durgerdam, is de protestantse kerk in Durgerdam in Amsterdam-Noord.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Dorpskerk Durgerdam, originally the Reformed Church of Durgerdam, is the Protestant church in Durgerdam in Amsterdam-North.

features.name: Houten Huis
features.opening: Het Houten Huys is a building dating from 1528 or shortly thereafter on the Begijnhof in Amsterdam.

facts.text: Research in 2012 revised its age to 1528, disproving the long-held belief it dated to 1420.
facts.sourceQuote: Er werd voorheen dan ook altijd aangenomen dat het pand uit 1420 stamde. Nader onderzoek gaf echter in 2012 de bouwdatum van 1528 of kort daarna.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: It was therefore always assumed that the building dates back to 1420. However, further research in 2012 gave the construction date of 1528 or shortly thereafter.

facts.text: The house traditionally housed only single women, originally beguines living within the Begijnhof.
facts.sourceQuote: Het Houten Huys staat op het Begijnhof en is van oudsher alleen bewoond door alleenstaande vrouwen (aanvankelijk begijnen, tegenwoordig is religieuze affiliatie niet meer verplicht).
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Het Houten Huys is located on the Begijnhof and has traditionally been inhabited only by single women (originally beguines, today religious affiliation is no longer mandatory).

features.name: Elthetokerk
features.opening: The former Elthetokerk was a Reformed church building at the corner of Insulindeweg and Kramatweg in the Indische Buurt in Amsterdam-Oost.

facts.text: Architect Kruyswijk also designed three other Amsterdam churches still in use today.
facts.sourceQuote: Drie andere door Kruyswijk ontworpen kerken in Amsterdam zijn nog wel in gebruik, dit zijn de Willem de Zwijgerkerk in Amsterdam-Zuid en twee kerken van het Apostolisch Genootschap, één aan de Archimedesweg in Amsterdam-Oost (Watergraafsmeer) en één aan de Clematisstraat in Amsterdam-Noord.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Three other churches designed by Kruyswijk in Amsterdam are still in use, these are the Willem de Zwijgerkerk in Amsterdam-Zuid and two churches of the Apostolic Society, one on the Archimedesweg in Amsterdam-Oost (Watergraafsmeer) and one on the Clematisstraat in Amsterdam-North.

facts.text: Construction funding of 150,000 guilders was gathered between 1924 and 1929.
facts.sourceQuote: Voor de bouw was tussen 1924 en 1929 een bedrag van ƒ 150.000 bijeengebracht.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: An amount of ƒ 150,000 was raised between 1924 and 1929 for the construction.

facts.text: Architect Cornelis Kruyswijk designed the structure built in 1929.
facts.sourceQuote: De kerk is gebouwd in 1929 naar ontwerp van Cornelis Kruyswijk.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The church was built in 1929 to the design of Cornelis Kruyswijk.

features.name: Begijnhofkapel
features.opening: The Begijnhof Chapel, dedicated to Saint John and Saint Ursula, is a Roman Catholic chapel run by the Congregation of the Blessed Sacrament, in the St Nicholas…

facts.text: Unmarried women lived there without lifelong vows, free to leave and marry at any moment they chose.
facts.sourceQuote: They could renounce their vows at any moment and leave the Beguinage, for instance, to get married.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: They could renounce their vows at any moment and leave the Beguinage, for instance, to get married.

facts.text: A house was officially ceded to them on July 31, 1346, by a man named Cope van der Laene.
facts.sourceQuote: Another document, dated 31 July 1346, speaks of the Beghijnhuis (house of the Beguines) ceded to them by one Cope van der Laene on St Peter’s Eve.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Another document, dated 31 July 1346, speaks of the Beghijnhuis (house of the Beguines) ceded to them by one Cope van der Laene on St Peter’s Eve.

facts.text: The chapel honors Saint John and Saint Ursula as its patron saints.
facts.sourceQuote: The Begijnhof Chapel, dedicated to Saint John and Saint Ursula, is a Roman Catholic chapel run by the Congregation of the Blessed Sacrament, in the St Nicholas Parish of Amsterdam.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Begijnhof Chapel, dedicated to Saint John and Saint Ursula, is a Roman Catholic chapel run by the Congregation of the Blessed Sacrament, in the St Nicholas Parish of Amsterdam.

facts.text: A yearly procession for the Miracle of Amsterdam begins at this church.
facts.sourceQuote: The Miracle of Amsterdam is commemorated yearly with a procession starting from this church.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Miracle of Amsterdam is commemorated yearly with a procession starting from this church.

features.name: Pianola Museum
features.opening: The Pianola Museum in the Jordaan is a music museum in Amsterdam that offers an overview of the history and way of playing the pianola, a 'self-playing'…

facts.text: Theo de Boer and Kasper Janse founded the foundation that manages the collection in 1981.
facts.sourceQuote: Door Theo de Boer en Kasper Janse werd in 1981 de Stichting Nederlands Piano Museum opgericht.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 1981, Theo de Boer and Kasper Janse founded the Stichting Nederlands Piano Museum.

features.name: Lekstraatsynagoge
features.opening: The Lekstraat Synagogue stands at Lekstraat 63 in the Rivierenbuurt in Amsterdam.

facts.text: The synagogue was inaugurated on November 30, 1937 after plans were completed in 1932.
facts.sourceQuote: Omdat er steeds meer Joodse bewoners kwamen - van 4000 in 1930 tot rond de 17.000 in 1940 - wilde men een echte sjoel (synagoge) bouwen. De plannen ontstonden in het begin van de jaren 30, in 1932 was het ontwerp klaar en op 30 november 1937 werd de Lekstraatsynagoge ingewijd.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Because more and more Jewish residents were coming - from 4000 in 1930 to around 17,000 in 1940 - they wanted to build a real synagogue (synagogue). The plans were conceived in the early 1930s, the design was completed in 1932 and the Lekstraatsynagoge was inaugurated on November 30, 1937.

facts.text: During WWII, Jews could purchase Star of David symbols inside the Lekstraatsynagoge.
facts.sourceQuote: Tijdens de Tweede Wereldoorlog konden joden in de Lekstraatsynagoge gele Davidsterren kopen.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: During World War II, Jews could buy the Star of David in the Lekstraatsynagoge.

facts.text: From 1943, the building stored furniture belonging to deported Jews after closing its doors.
facts.sourceQuote: Later sloot de synagoge haar deuren, en vanaf 1943 deed het gebouw dienst als opslagplaats van meubels van weggevoerde joden.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Later, the synagogue closed its doors, and from 1943, the building served as a storage facility for furniture belonging to deported Jews.

features.name: Djame Masdjied Taibah
features.opening: The Taibah Mosque is a (Indo-Surinamese) mosque in Amsterdam, the Netherlands.

facts.text: Surinamese-born Muhammad Yunus Gaffar founded the mosque before passing away in 2020.
facts.sourceQuote: The mosque was founded by Surinam born Muhammad Yunus Gaffar (1940-2020) and designed by architect Paul Haffmans.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The mosque was founded by Surinam born Muhammad Yunus Gaffar (1940-2020) and designed by architect Paul Haffmans.

features.name: Eye Filmmuseum
features.opening: Eye Filmmuseum is a film archive, museum, and cinema in Amsterdam that preserves and presents both Dutch and foreign films screened in the Netherlands.

facts.text: Visitors can view roughly one hundred clips spanning silent eras and beyond within an immersive display.
facts.sourceQuote: The exhibit includes historical equipment drawn from the Museum's collection of approximately 1,500 cinematic apparatuses, as well as an immersive presentation of about one hundred film clips from the Museum's archive, including Dutch and international films dating from the silent era and beyond.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The exhibit includes historical equipment drawn from the Museum's collection of approximately 1,500 cinematic apparatuses, as well as an immersive presentation of about one hundred film clips from the Museum's archive, including Dutch and international films dating from the silent era and beyond.

facts.text: A focus on experimental cinema traces back to weekly screenings held at the Stedelijk Museum in the 1950s.
facts.sourceQuote: The second gallery space is dedicated to experimental cinema or expanded cinema, a commitment which dates back to the Filmmuseum's founding and the weekly screenings it organized at the Stedelijk Museum in the 1950s under the emerging aegis of cinema as a "seventh art." Past exhibitions in this space have focused on auteurs and cinematographers, as well as video artists and visual artists like Ryoji Ikeda and Anthony McCall.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The second gallery space is dedicated to experimental cinema or expanded cinema, a commitment which dates back to the Filmmuseum's founding and the weekly screenings it organized at the Stedelijk Museum in the 1950s under the emerging aegis of cinema as a "seventh art." Past exhibitions in this space have focused on auteurs and cinematographers, as well as video artists and visual artists like Ryoji Ikeda and Anthony McCall.

features.name: Zuiderkerk
features.opening: The Zuiderkerk (Dutch pronunciation: [ˈzœydərˌkɛr(ə)k], "southern church") is a 17th-century Reformed Protestant church in the Nieuwmarkt area of Amsterdam,…

facts.text: Architect Hendrick de Keyser, who designed the church, is buried inside it.
facts.sourceQuote: The design of the church in Amsterdam Renaissance style is by Hendrick de Keyser, who was also buried in the church in 1621.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The design of the church in Amsterdam Renaissance style is by Hendrick de Keyser, who was also buried in the church in 1621.

facts.text: During the 1944 hunger winter, the church served as a temporary morgue.
facts.sourceQuote: During the final (1944-1945) winter of World War II, known as the hongerwinter ("hunger winter") in the Netherlands because food was so scarce, the church was in use as a temporary morgue because people were dying faster than they could be buried.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: During the final (1944-1945) winter of World War II, known as the hongerwinter ("hunger winter") in the Netherlands because food was so scarce, the church was in use as a temporary morgue because people were dying faster than they could be buried.

facts.text: Three of Rembrandt's children were buried in this church near his home.
facts.sourceQuote: Three of Rembrandt's children were buried in the Zuiderkerk, which is very near to Rembrandt's house in the Jodenbreestraat.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Three of Rembrandt's children were buried in the Zuiderkerk, which is very near to Rembrandt's house in the Jodenbreestraat.

facts.text: Claude Monet painted the Zuiderkerk as a subject.
facts.sourceQuote: The church played an important part in the life of Rembrandt and was the subject of a painting by Claude Monet.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The church played an important part in the life of Rembrandt and was the subject of a painting by Claude Monet.

features.name: Allendemonument
features.opening: The Allendemonument is a statue/monument in Amsterdam Nieuw-West.

facts.text: Ton Blommerde stacked concrete parts without adhesive, inspired by the Incas.
facts.sourceQuote: Blommerde, die zich ook wel bediende van de naam Blommende, liet zich inspireren door de Inca's, hij stapelde de betonnen delen zonder voegmiddel.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Blommerde, who also used the name Blommende, was inspired by the Incas, he stacked the concrete parts without adhesive.

features.name: Theater Amsterdam
features.opening: Theater Amsterdam is a theater in Amsterdam.

facts.text: The venue opened on May 8, 2014 with a performance based on Anne Frank's diary.
facts.sourceQuote: Op 8 mei 2014 opende het theater met de voorstelling Anne, naar het dagboek van Anne Frank.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: On May 8, 2014, the theater opened with the performance Anne, based on the diary of Anne Frank.

facts.text: For now, it remains the only Amsterdam theater designed to run as long as the public is interested.
facts.sourceQuote: Het is voorlopig het enige theater in Amsterdam dat bedoeld is voor voorstellingen die doorspelen zolang het publiek belangstelling heeft.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: For the time being, it is the only theater in Amsterdam intended for performances that continue as long as the public is interested.

features.name: Koningin Emma
features.opening: Statue and memorial in Amsterdam, the Netherlands.

facts.text: Vandals severed the statue's head and shoulders in September 1987 before it was restored after the head was found.
facts.sourceQuote: In september 1987 werd het beeld door vandalen ontdaan van hoofd en schouders. Spoedig nadat het vorstelijk hoofd in de bosjes werd aangetroffen, werd het beeld hersteld.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In September 1987, the statue was stripped of its head and shoulders by vandals. Shortly after the princely head was found in the woods, the statue was restored.

facts.text: The monument was officially unveiled to the public in 1938.
facts.sourceQuote: Het beeld is ontworpen door beeldhouwer Lambertus Zijl (1866 - 1947) en werd onthuld in 1938.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The statue was designed by sculptor Lambertus Zijl (1866 - 1947) and was unveiled in 1938.

features.name: National Monument
features.opening: The National Monument on Dam Square (Dutch: Nationaal Monument op de Dam) is a 1956 cenotaph in Amsterdam, Netherlands.

facts.text: During a 1990s restoration, the brick interior of its central pillar was replaced with concrete.
facts.sourceQuote: During the restoration in the 1990s, the entire monument was disassembled, and the brick interior of the central pillar was replaced with concrete.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: During the restoration in the 1990s, the entire monument was disassembled, and the brick interior of the central pillar was replaced with concrete.

facts.text: Dutch architect Jacobus Oud designed the monument while sculptor John Rädecker created its main figures.
facts.sourceQuote: The monument was designed by Dutch architect Jacobus Oud; the monument's sculptures are by John Rädecker and his sons Han and Jan Willem Rädecker.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The monument was designed by Dutch architect Jacobus Oud; the monument's sculptures are by John Rädecker and his sons Han and Jan Willem Rädecker.

facts.text: A twenty-two-meter concrete pillar stands covered entirely in white travertine stone.
facts.sourceQuote: The central element of the monument is a concrete conical pillar 22 metres (72 ft) in height, covered entirely by white travertine stone.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The central element of the monument is a concrete conical pillar 22 metres (72 ft) in height, covered entirely by white travertine stone.

facts.text: Eleven urns hold soil from execution grounds across Dutch provinces plus one from Indonesia.
facts.sourceQuote: The wall contains eleven urns with soil from World War II execution grounds and war cemeteries in each of the Dutch provinces. and a twelfth urn with soil from the Dutch East Indies, present-day Indonesia.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The wall contains eleven urns with soil from World War II execution grounds and war cemeteries in each of the Dutch provinces. and a twelfth urn with soil from the Dutch East Indies, present-day Indonesia.

features.name: Agnietenkapel (UvA)
features.opening: The Agnietenkapel (Chapel of the Convent of Saint Agnes) is a 15th-century Gothic chapel in Amsterdam.

facts.text: Two side alleys were covered with glass and integrated into the structure during renovations.
facts.sourceQuote: Additionally, the alleys on each side of the chapel were covered with glass and incorporated into the building.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Additionally, the alleys on each side of the chapel were covered with glass and incorporated into the building.

facts.text: Willem Bogtman's original painted ceiling and stained-glass windows were restored to their former state.
facts.sourceQuote: During restoration and renovation in 2004–2007, the painted ceiling of the first-floor lecture hall by Willem Bogtman was restored to its original state, as were Bogtman's stained-glass windows.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: During restoration and renovation in 2004–2007, the painted ceiling of the first-floor lecture hall by Willem Bogtman was restored to its original state, as were Bogtman's stained-glass windows.

facts.text: The chapel became the birthplace of the University of Amsterdam and still hosts doctoral dissertations.
facts.sourceQuote: It is the birthplace of the University of Amsterdam and still in use for doctoral dissertations and other university ceremonies, as well as academic events such as lectures and symposiums.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: It is the birthplace of the University of Amsterdam and still in use for doctoral dissertations and other university ceremonies, as well as academic events such as lectures and symposiums.

facts.text: Agnietenkapel (UvA) has held rijksmonument status since 1970.
facts.sourceQuote: The building has held rijksmonument status since 1970.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The building has held rijksmonument status since 1970.

features.name: Sint-Agneskerk
features.opening: The Sint-Agneskerk in Amsterdam is a Catholic parish church, located at the corner of Amstelveenseweg 163 and Cornelis Krusemanstraat, on the…

facts.text: Sint-Agneskerk honors Agnes, a young Roman martyr.
facts.sourceQuote: De nieuwe kerk zou worden toegewijd aan de heilige Agnes, een jeugdige Romeinse martelares.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The new church would be dedicated to the saint Agnes, a young Roman martyr.

facts.text: Jan Stuyt modeled the church after ancient Christian basilicas in Rome.
facts.sourceQuote: Voor zijn ontwerp greep Stuyt daarom terug op "de prachtige hallen der oud-christelijke basilieken in Rome".
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: For his design, Stuyt therefore drew on "the beautiful halls of the ancient Christian basilicas in Rome".

facts.text: The tower was added during a second construction phase between 1930 and 1932.
facts.sourceQuote: Tijdens de tweede fase (1930-1932) is de kerk uitgebreid met het transept, het priesterkoor, de klokkentoren, de doopkapel, de pastorie en het winkelhuis aan de Cornelis Krusemanstraat.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: During the second phase (1930-1932), the church was expanded with the transept, the choir, the bell tower, the baptistry, the parish house and the shophouse on Cornelis Krusemanstraat.

facts.text: Construction of the building spanned from 1919 until its completion in 1932.
facts.sourceQuote: De kerk, die gewijd is aan de martelares Sint Agnes, werd tussen 1919 en 1932 gebouwd naar een ontwerp van architect Jan Stuyt en is in 1996 aangewezen als Rijksmonument.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The church, dedicated to the martyr Sint Agnes, was built between 1919 and 1932 according to a design by architect Jan Stuyt and was designated a Rijksmonument in 1996.

facts.text: Since 2006, the Sint-Pieter Priestly Brotherhood has been responsible for operating the parish.
facts.sourceQuote: De Sint Agneskerk wordt sinds 2006 bediend door de Priesterbroederschap van Sint-Pieter (FSSP)
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Sint Agneskerk has been operated by the Sint-Pieter Priestly Brotherhood (FSSP) since 2006

features.name: Embassy of the Free Mind
features.opening: The Embassy of the Free Mind is a museum, library and platform for free thinking inspired by the philosophy of the Bibliotheca Philosophica Hermetica…

facts.text: Amsterdam businessman Joost Ritman founded the collection as a private library in 1958.
facts.sourceQuote: It is a scientific research library with a collection of 25,000 books and its own publisher, and dates to 1958—when Amsterdam-based businessman Joost Ritman started it as a private library.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: It is a scientific research library with a collection of 25,000 books and its own publisher, and dates to 1958—when Amsterdam-based businessman Joost Ritman started it as a private library.

facts.text: The institution moved to Bloemstraat and opened to the public in 1984.
facts.sourceQuote: In 1984, the library was opened to the general public and moved within Amsterdam to the Bloemstraat.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 1984, the library was opened to the general public and moved within Amsterdam to the Bloemstraat.

facts.text: The collection features Hermetic, alchemical, astrological, magical, mystical, kabbalistic and Rosicrucian texts.
facts.sourceQuote: This connection is reflected in the Hermetic, alchemical, astrological, magical, mystical, kabbalistic and Rosicrucian texts and images in the collection.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: This connection is reflected in the Hermetic, alchemical, astrological, magical, mystical, kabbalistic and Rosicrucian texts and images in the collection.

features.name: Hash Marihuana & Hemp Museum
features.opening: The Hash, Marihuana & Hemp Museum is a museum located in De Wallen, Amsterdam, Netherlands.

facts.text: Over two million visitors have explored the exhibition since it opened in 1985.
facts.sourceQuote: According to the museum, more than two million visitors have visited the exhibition since it opened in 1985.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: According to the museum, more than two million visitors have visited the exhibition since it opened in 1985.

facts.text: Admission costs nine euros, though children under thirteen enter free with an adult.
facts.sourceQuote: The Hash, Marihuana & Hemp Museum is located at Oudezijds Achterburgwal 148, open daily, and costs €9 ($11.50) per adult (children under 13 are free when accompanied by an adult).
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Hash, Marihuana & Hemp Museum is located at Oudezijds Achterburgwal 148, open daily, and costs €9 ($11.50) per adult (children under 13 are free when accompanied by an adult).

facts.text: A 1660 painting by David Teniers the Younger depicts peasants smoking in a smoke house.
facts.sourceQuote: The museum also contains artwork, including David Teniers the Younger's painting, Hemp-Smoking Peasants in a Smoke House (1660), and one of the fake I.D's of the famous cannabis smuggler Howard Marks.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The museum also contains artwork, including David Teniers the Younger's painting, Hemp-Smoking Peasants in a Smoke House (1660), and one of the fake I.D's of the famous cannabis smuggler Howard Marks.

facts.text: One exhibit features a fake ID belonging to the famous cannabis smuggler Howard Marks.
facts.sourceQuote: The museum also contains artwork, including David Teniers the Younger's painting, Hemp-Smoking Peasants in a Smoke House (1660), and one of the fake I.D's of the famous cannabis smuggler Howard Marks.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The museum also contains artwork, including David Teniers the Younger's painting, Hemp-Smoking Peasants in a Smoke House (1660), and one of the fake I.D's of the famous cannabis smuggler Howard Marks.

features.name: Thomaskerk
features.opening: The Thomaskerk, or De Thomas, on the Prinses Irenestraat in Amsterdam-Zuid was built in 1966 and belongs to the Protestant Church of Amsterdam.

facts.text: Architect Karel Sijmons personally funded the 1967 crucifixion stained glass by Antonio Saura.
facts.sourceQuote: De kerk heeft een glas-in-loodraam dat in 1967 ontworpen is door de Spaanse kunstenaar Antonio Saura waarin de kruisiging van Jezus wordt afgebeeld. De architect heeft het zelf betaald omdat hij het stuk per se in de kerk wilde hebben.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The church has a stained glass window designed in 1967 by the Spanish artist Antonio Saura depicting the crucifixion of Jesus. The architect paid for it himself because he absolutely wanted to have the piece in the church.

facts.text: Originally built for wealthy residents in fur coats, it now serves as a resting spot for business workers.
facts.sourceQuote: Hun korte omschrijving grijpt terug op het veranderde gebruik. Het was eerst bestemd als geloofsuiting van de rijkere Amsterdammer in Buitenveldert (bontjassen, wellicht ook een verwijzing naar moeilijkheid dit soort gebouwen warm te krijgen), maar werd later opgeslokt door het zakencentrum Zuidas, waarin het een rustpunt is of zou moeten zijn (stropdassen): Van bontjassenkerk tot stropdassenkerk
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Their short description refers to the changed use. It was initially intended as a religious expression of the wealthier Amsterdammer in Buitenveldert (fur coats, perhaps also a reference to the difficulty of keeping such buildings warm), but was later swallowed up by the Zuidas business center, in which it is or should be a resting point (ties): From fur coat church to tie church

features.name: International Institute of Social History
features.opening: The International Institute of Social History (IISH/IISG) is one of the largest archives of labor and social history in the world.

facts.text: During WWII, Nazi agents stole archives to store them for an advanced party school rather than destroy them.
facts.sourceQuote: During the war, most remaining IISG archives were transported to Nazi Germany between June 1942 and September 1944 by agents of the Reichsleiter Rosenberg Taskforce led by Eberhard Kautter. They were not destroyed, but stored for eventual inclusion in the Advanced School of the NSDAP.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: During the war, most remaining IISG archives were transported to Nazi Germany between June 1942 and September 1944 by agents of the Reichsleiter Rosenberg Taskforce led by Eberhard Kautter. They were not destroyed, but stored for eventual inclusion in the Advanced School of the NSDAP.

facts.text: Lost papers were rediscovered in Hannover in 1946 and later found in Moscow before returning to Amsterdam.
facts.sourceQuote: Most of the papers were rediscovered in Hannover in 1946, and some other parts were later found in archives in Moscow in 1991, and returned to Amsterdam.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Most of the papers were rediscovered in Hannover in 1946, and some other parts were later found in archives in Moscow in 1991, and returned to Amsterdam.

facts.text: The institute hosts part of the IHLIA LGBT Heritage collection known as the LGBT Archives.
facts.sourceQuote: IISG hosts part of the IHLIA LGBT Heritage collection (LGBT Archives).
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: IISG hosts part of the IHLIA LGBT Heritage collection (LGBT Archives).

facts.text: Founder Nicolaas Posthumus established the institute in 1935 as an independent scientific body.
facts.sourceQuote: The IISH was founded in 1935 by Nicolaas Posthumus as an independent scientific institute.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The IISH was founded in 1935 by Nicolaas Posthumus as an independent scientific institute.

features.name: Boomkerk
features.opening: De Boom, or Boomkerk, is the usual name for the Roman Catholic Church of St Francis of Assisi in Amsterdam Bos en Lommer.

facts.text: An African community began holding Sunday afternoon services there.
facts.sourceQuote: Een Afrikaanse gemeenschap ging de kerk op zondagmiddag gebruiken voor haar erediensten.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: An African community went to use the church on Sunday afternoon for its services.

features.name: Amsterdam Public Library Oosterdok
features.opening: Oosterdokskade 143 in Amsterdam is a building on the Oosterdokseiland in Amsterdam-Centrum.

facts.text: New structures rose after 2003 featuring high buildings and narrow streets designed by Erick van Egeraat.
facts.sourceQuote: De PTT vertrok er na nog geen halve eeuw en de gemeente Amsterdam begon de terreinen te herontwikkelen. (Bijna) Alle bestaande gebouwen werden daarbij gesloopt en er kwam na 2003 nieuwbouw naar een stratenplan van Erick van Egeraat met relatief hoge gebouwen en nauwe straatjes daartussen.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The PTT left after less than half a century and the municipality of Amsterdam began redeveloping the sites. (Almost) All existing buildings were demolished and new buildings were built after 2003 according to a street plan by Erick van Egeraat with relatively high buildings and narrow streets between them.

features.name: Wereldmuseum Amsterdam
features.opening: The Wereldmuseum Amsterdam, previously known as Tropenmuseum between 1950 and 2023, is an ethnographic museum with its headquarters in Amsterdam, Netherlands.

facts.text: Researchers once tried to develop better methods for producing coffee beans, rattan, and paraffin to boost colonial profits.
facts.sourceQuote: In 1871 the institute began research to increase profits made off the colonies. This included attempting to develop improved means of producing coffee beans, rattan and paraffin.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 1871 the institute began research to increase profits made off the colonies. This included attempting to develop improved means of producing coffee beans, rattan and paraffin.

facts.text: The institution was renamed Wereldmuseum Amsterdam in 2023, having previously been called Tropenmuseum.
facts.sourceQuote: The Wereldmuseum Amsterdam, previously known as Tropenmuseum between 1950 and 2023, is an ethnographic museum with its headquarters in Amsterdam, Netherlands.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Wereldmuseum Amsterdam, previously known as Tropenmuseum between 1950 and 2023, is an ethnographic museum with its headquarters in Amsterdam, Netherlands.

features.name: Singelkerk
features.opening: The Singelkerk is a church of the Mennonite congregation in Amsterdam, lying between the Singel and the Herengracht.

facts.text: A major 1839 renovation replaced the roof and Herengracht facade with their current shapes.
facts.sourceQuote: In 1839 wordt bij een grote verbouwing door Martinus Gerardus Tétar van Elven het dak vervangen, waarmee het gebouw de vorm krijgt die het nu nog heeft. Ook de voorgevel aan de Herengracht dateert uit die tijd.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 1839, during a major renovation by Martinus Gerardus Tétar van Elven, the roof was replaced, giving the building the shape it still has today. The facade on the Herengracht also dates from that time.

facts.text: The original entrance consisted of semicircular doors located at Singel 454.
facts.sourceQuote: Aanvankelijk waren de halfronde deuren op Singel 454 de ingang tot de kerk.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Initially, the semicircular doors on Singel 454 were the entrance to the church.

features.name: Homomonument
features.opening: The Homomonument is a memorial in the centre of Amsterdam, the capital of the Netherlands.

facts.text: In 1970, police removed a wreath laid by activists at Dam Square, declaring it insulting to the dead.
facts.sourceQuote: In 1970, a year before the complete decriminalization of homosexuality in the Netherlands, a group of gay activists were arrested for trying to lay a wreath at the National Monument to the Victims of World War II on Dam Square, Amsterdam. The flowers were removed from the memorial by the police and declared insulting to the memory of the dead.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 1970, a year before the complete decriminalization of homosexuality in the Netherlands, a group of gay activists were arrested for trying to lay a wreath at the National Monument to the Victims of World War II on Dam Square, Amsterdam. The flowers were removed from the memorial by the police and declared insulting to the memory of the dead.

facts.text: Three pink granite triangles connect to form one large triangle with a 36-meter side.
facts.sourceQuote: The memorial is a composition of three equilateral triangles of pink granite with edge lengths of 10 meters, which are interconnected by thin lines of similar material, thus forming one large equilateral triangle with a side length of 36 meters.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The memorial is a composition of three equilateral triangles of pink granite with edge lengths of 10 meters, which are interconnected by thin lines of similar material, thus forming one large equilateral triangle with a side length of 36 meters.

facts.text: Designer Karin Daan created the structure to fit the historic landscape without disturbing it.
facts.sourceQuote: Karin Daan designed the monument to be as imposing as possible without disturbing the environment, fitting it as closely as possible into the historic urban landscape.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Karin Daan designed the monument to be as imposing as possible without disturbing the environment, fitting it as closely as possible into the historic urban landscape.

features.name: Nieuwendammerkerk
features.opening: The Nieuwendammerkerk is the village church of the dyke village of Nieuwendam in Amsterdam-Noord.

facts.text: Construction took place between 1848 and 1849 to replace an older, smaller church.
facts.sourceQuote: De Nieuwendammerkerk is een zaalkerk, gebouwd in 1848-1849, ter vervanging van een kleiner en ouder kerkgebouw.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Nieuwendammerkerk is a hall church, built in 1848-1849, to replace a smaller and older church building.

features.name: West Indian Warehouse
features.opening: The West Indian Warehouse in Amsterdam dates back to 1642 and is located on the western part of Rapenburg, where the Oudeschans flows into the Oosterdok.

facts.text: Between 1647 and 1674, the West Indian Warehouse served as the headquarters of the WIC.
facts.sourceQuote: Tussen 1647 en 1674 diende het pand als hoofdkwartier van de WIC.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Between 1647 and 1674, the building served as the headquarters of the WIC.

facts.text: Commanders based here managed trade in gold, sugar, and slaves alongside other goods.
facts.sourceQuote: Vanuit dit pand waren de bevelhebbers verantwoordelijk voor alle handelsactiviteiten, waaronder de handel in goud, suiker en slaven.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: From this building, the commanders were responsible for all trade activities, including the trade in gold, sugar and slaves.

facts.text: The facade letters GWC stand for the official name Geoctroyeerde West-Indische Compagnie.
facts.sourceQuote: De letters GWC op de gevel staan voor de officiële naam, 'Geoctroyeerde West-Indische Compagnie'.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The letters GWC on the facade stand for the official name, 'Geoctroyeerde West-Indische Compagnie'.

features.name: Ons' Lieve Heer op Solder
features.opening: Ons' Lieve Heer op Solder (OLHOS; English: Our Lord in the Attic) is a 17th-century canal house, house church, and museum in the city center of Amsterdam, The…

facts.text: Catholics built this clandestine church on the top three floors during the 1660s.
facts.sourceQuote: The Catholic church was built on the top three floors of the canal house during the 1660s.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Catholic church was built on the top three floors of the canal house during the 1660s.

features.name: Vredeskerk
features.opening: The Parish Church of Our Lady Queen of Peace or Vredeskerk is a Roman Catholic church between Pijnackerstraat and Van Hilligaertstraat in the southwest corner…

facts.text: Vredeskerk (Peace Church) was initially called the Stable of Bethlehem to mark its December 25, 1918 dedication.
facts.sourceQuote: Naar de datum van de inwijding van deze kerk (25 december 1918) werd zij de Stal van Bethlehem genoemd.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In honor of the date of the dedication of this church (December 25, 1918), it was called the Stable of Bethlehem.

features.name: Mozes en Aäronkerk
features.opening: The Moses and Aaron Church (Dutch: Mozes en Aäronkerk, pronounced [ˈmoːzəs ɛn aːˈʔaːrɔŋkɛr(ə)k]) in the Waterlooplein neighborhood of Amsterdam, the…

facts.text: The twin houses Mozes en Aäronkerk were named after the Old Testament brothers Moses and Aaron.
facts.sourceQuote: Named after the brothers from the Old Testament, the twin houses proved to be better known than their hidden church, Sint-Anthoniuskerk, which had been dedicated to the church's patron saint, St.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Named after the brothers from the Old Testament, the twin houses proved to be better known than their hidden church, Sint-Anthoniuskerk, which had been dedicated to the church's patron saint, St.

facts.text: A grander replacement building was constructed on this site between 1837 and 1841.
facts.sourceQuote: It was replaced between 1837 and 1841 by a bigger and grander building on the same site.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: It was replaced between 1837 and 1841 by a bigger and grander building on the same site.

facts.text: Belgian architect Tilman-François Suys designed this structure alongside Haarlem's Groenmarktkerk.
facts.sourceQuote: The present building was built as a "Water Management Church" (Dutch: Waterstaatskerk), between 1837 and 1841 from a design by Tilman-François Suys (1783–1861) in the style of neoclassicism, with three aisles and a recessed rectangular choir. Suys also designed the Groenmarktkerk ["Green Market Street"] in Haarlem.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The present building was built as a "Water Management Church" (Dutch: Waterstaatskerk), between 1837 and 1841 from a design by Tilman-François Suys (1783–1861) in the style of neoclassicism, with three aisles and a recessed rectangular choir. Suys also designed the Groenmarktkerk ["Green Market Street"] in Haarlem.

facts.text: Construction took place between 1837 and 1841 to serve as a Water Management Church.
facts.sourceQuote: The present building was built as a "Water Management Church" (Dutch: Waterstaatskerk), between 1837 and 1841 from a design by Tilman-François Suys (1783–1861) in the style of neoclassicism, with three aisles and a recessed rectangular choir.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The present building was built as a "Water Management Church" (Dutch: Waterstaatskerk), between 1837 and 1841 from a design by Tilman-François Suys (1783–1861) in the style of neoclassicism, with three aisles and a recessed rectangular choir.

features.name: Pathé City
features.opening: The Pathé City is a Pathé cinema at Kleine-Gartmanplantsoen 15-19 in Amsterdam, 40 meters from Leidseplein and diagonally opposite De Balie.

facts.text: The cinema hosted the 23rd Amsterdam Fantastic Film Festival in April 2007.
facts.sourceQuote: Op 31 januari 2007 vond de voorlopig laatste reguliere voorstelling plaats en van 18 tot 25 april 2007 was de bioscoop gastheer van het 23e Amsterdam Fantastic Film Festival.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: On January 31, 2007, the penultimate regular performance took place and from April 18 to 25, 2007, the cinema was the host of the 23rd Amsterdam Fantastic Film Festival.

facts.text: Conductor Lex van Weren led the City Theater Orchestra before films started.
facts.sourceQuote: De bioscoop had de beschikking over een orkestbak met het City Theater Orkest dat onder leiding van dirigent Lex van Weren voorafgaand aan de film muziek verzorgde.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The cinema had access to an orchestra pit with the City Theater Orchestra that provided music before the film under the direction of conductor Lex van Weren.

facts.text: An orchestra pit allowed live music to be played before screenings began.
facts.sourceQuote: De bioscoop had de beschikking over een orkestbak met het City Theater Orkest dat onder leiding van dirigent Lex van Weren voorafgaand aan de film muziek verzorgde.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The cinema had access to an orchestra pit with the City Theater Orchestra that provided music before the film under the direction of conductor Lex van Weren.

facts.text: The instrument underwent modifications in both 1938 and 1950 before later changes.
facts.sourceQuote: In 1938 en 1950 werd het instrument verbouwd.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 1938 and 1950 the instrument was modified.

facts.text: A lowered ceiling largely closed off the upper organ room during a 1970s renovation.
facts.sourceQuote: Bij de verbouwing van de zaal in het begin van de jaren zeventig werd de bovenste orgelkamer grotendeels afgesloten door een verlaagd plafond.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: During the renovation of the hall at the beginning of the 1970s, the upper organ room was largely closed off by a lowered ceiling.

features.name: Central Station
