facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The main "I AMsterdam" sign was also located here in front of the Rijksmuseum, until 4 December 2018, when it was removed at the behest of the city council.

facts.text: Visitors can explore the House of Bols and the Diamond Museum on this site.
facts.sourceQuote: Consulate General of Turkey Consulate General of the United States Concertgebouw Stedelijk Museum Van Gogh Museum House of Bols Diamond Museum Coster Diamonds Rijksmuseum Moco Museum (opened at the end of May 2016)
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Consulate General of Turkey Consulate General of the United States Concertgebouw Stedelijk Museum Van Gogh Museum House of Bols Diamond Museum Coster Diamonds Rijksmuseum Moco Museum (opened at the end of May 2016)

features.name: Zuiderkerkhof
features.opening: Zuiderkerkhof is an indoor square in Amsterdam-Centrum, Zuiderkerkbuurt.

facts.text: The name Zuiderkerkhof combines its past as a cemetery with its later role as a courtyard at the church's foot.
facts.sourceQuote: De naam is dus tweeledig, het was ooit een kerkhof, en later een hofje aan de voet van de Zuiderkerk.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The name is therefore two-part, it was once a cemetery, and later a courtyard at the foot of the Zuiderkerk.

facts.text: House numbers run from 1 to 72, yet more than half the intermediate numbers are missing.
facts.sourceQuote: De huisnummering loopt van 1 tot en met 72, maar meer dan de helft van de tussenliggende nummers ontbreekt.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The house numbering runs from 1 to 72, but more than half of the intermediate numbers are missing.

features.name: Leidseplein
features.opening: Leidseplein (English: Leiden Square) is a square in central Amsterdam, Netherlands.

facts.text: Leidseplein marks the historic terminus of the road leading from Leiden.
facts.sourceQuote: Historically, the square was the end of the road from Leiden; it served as a parking lot for horse-drawn traffic.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Historically, the square was the end of the road from Leiden; it served as a parking lot for horse-drawn traffic.

facts.text: Side streets surrounding the square are now packed with restaurants and nightclubs.
facts.sourceQuote: Today, modern traffic travels through the square and side streets are packed with restaurants and nightclubs.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Today, modern traffic travels through the square and side streets are packed with restaurants and nightclubs.

facts.text: The Stadsschouwburg stands as the most notable architectural landmark on the square.
facts.sourceQuote: The Stadsschouwburg, a national-renowned theatre, is the most notable architectural landmark on the square; the American Hotel is close by.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Stadsschouwburg, a national-renowned theatre, is the most notable architectural landmark on the square; the American Hotel is close by.

features.name: Frederiksplein
features.opening: The Frederiksplein is a square in Amsterdam-Centrum, named in 1870 after Prince Frederick, uncle of King William III.

facts.text: A hot air balloon launched by Charles-Henri Augustin took off from the square in 1806.
facts.sourceQuote: In 1806 steeg de luchtballon van Charles-Henri Augustin er op.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 1806, Charles-Henri Augustin's hot air balloon took off there.

facts.text: Traffic used the square as a roundabout until the year 1968.
facts.sourceQuote: Tot 1968 was het plein een rotonde voor het verkeer.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Until 1968, the square was a roundabout for traffic.

facts.text: De Nederlandsche Bank stands prominently on this Amsterdam square.
facts.sourceQuote: Aan het plein staat De Nederlandsche Bank.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: De Nederlandsche Bank is located on the square.

features.name: Krugerplein
features.opening: The Krugerplein is a square in the Transvaalbuurt in Amsterdam-Oost.

facts.text: During WWII raids, Jewish residents were gathered here before being transported by tram.
facts.sourceQuote: Het Krugerplein was de plaats waar de joodse buurtbewoners bij de razzia's door de Duitsers en de Nederlandse politie werden verzameld, om per tram te worden afgevoerd naar het station.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Krugerplein was the place where the Jewish neighborhood residents were gathered during the raids by the Germans and the Dutch police, to be transported by tram to the station.

facts.text: Urban renewal work in 1996 fitted new buildings into existing structures using an urban plinth design.
facts.sourceQuote: In het kader van stadsvernieuwing werd in 1996 gewerkt aan het complex 8 tot en met 16 en de nabijgelegen Majubastraat; ontwerp was afkomstig van Marge Architecten (Theo Steemers), die de nieuwbouw liet inpassen in de bestaande bouw door toepassing van een “stedelijke plint”.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: As part of urban renewal, work was carried out in 1996 on the complex 8 to 16 and the nearby Majubastraat; the design was by Marge Architecten (Theo Steemers), who had the new building fitted into the existing building by applying an "urban plinth".

features.name: Weesperplein
features.opening: The Weesperplein is a square in the center of Amsterdam, between the Singelgracht and the Nieuwe Achtergracht.

facts.text: The Weesperstaete building earned the grim nickname Death Chamber while housing a university psychology lab.
facts.sourceQuote: Op de hoek met de Sarphatistraat staat sinds 1971 het gebouw Weesperstaete, bijgenaamd de "Doodskist", dat jarenlang het psychologisch laboratorium van de Universiteit van Amsterdam huisvestte.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: On the corner of Sarphatistraat stands the Weesperstaete building, nicknamed the "Death Chamber", which has housed the psychological laboratory of the University of Amsterdam for many years since 1971.

facts.text: Trains to Utrecht departed from the nearby station between 1843 and 1939 after the original gate was demolished.
facts.sourceQuote: Ten zuiden van het Weesperplein stond de Weesperpoort. Nadat deze was gesloopt, werd zuidelijk van de Singelgracht in 1843 het Weesperpoortstation gebouwd. Tussen 1843 en 1939 vertrokken hier de treinen naar Utrecht.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: South of the Weesperplein stood the Weesperpoort. After this was demolished, the Weesperpoort station was built south of the Singelgracht in 1843. Between 1843 and 1939, trains left here for Utrecht.

facts.text: A monument honoring Jewish recognition returned to the square in 2021 after moving locations in 1968.
facts.sourceQuote: Het in 1947 door Jobs Wertheim ontworpen Monument van Joodse Erkentelijkheid, dat vanaf 1950 in een plantsoentje aan de westzijde van het plein stond, werd in 1968 verplaatst naar de Weesperstraat, tussen de Nieuwe Herengracht en Nieuwe Keizersgracht, maar is in 2021 op het plein teruggekeerd.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Monument of Jewish Recognition, designed by Jobs Wertheim in 1947 and standing in a courtyard on the west side of the square from 1950, was moved to Weesperstraat in 1968, between the Nieuwe Herengracht and Nieuwe Keizersgracht, but returned to the square in 2021.

facts.text: Hildo Krop's 1923 sculptures of a seagull and fish decorate the Dr. Meijer de Hondbrug over the canal.
facts.sourceQuote: Meijer de Hondbrug over de Nieuwe Achtergracht zijn beeldhouwwerken van Hildo Krop uit 1923/1924 te zien (Havik en vissen).
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Meijer de Hondbrug over the Nieuwe Achtergracht houses Hildo Krop's sculptures from 1923/1924 (Seagull and fish).

features.name: Jac. P. Thijsseplein
features.opening: Jac.P. Thijsseplein is a square in Volewijck, Amsterdam-North.

facts.text: German occupiers renamed the square Eschdoornplein in 1942 because its previous namesake Eli Heimans was Jewish.
facts.sourceQuote: De namen Heimansweg en het Heimansplein werden in 1942 tijdens de Tweede Wereldoorlog, in opdracht van de Duitse bezetter, door de foute burgemeester E.J. Voûte veranderd in Eschdoornweg/Esdoornweg en Eschdoornplein/Esdoornplein, vanwege dat Eli Heimans joods was.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The names Heimansweg and Heimansplein were given in 1942 during World War II, at the request of the German occupiers, by the wrong mayor E.J. Front changed to Eschdoornweg/Esdoornweg and Eschdoornplein/Esdoornplein, because Eli Heimans was Jewish.

facts.text: A road dividing the square is also named after biologist Eli Heimans, who described flowers to ordinary people.
facts.sourceQuote: Deze bioloog kreeg ook een weg naar zich vernoemd, die het plein in tweeën deelt, de Heimansweg. Heimans beschreef voor het “gewone volk” de bloemen, die hun namen terugvonden in de omringende straten zoals de sleutelbloem.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: This biologist also had a road named after him, which divides the square in two, the Heimansweg. Heimans described the flowers to the "ordinary people", whose names were found in the surrounding streets such as the daffodil.

facts.text: Before receiving its current name, the location was called Heimansplein from 1920 until 1946.
facts.sourceQuote: In het stratenplan heette het plein van 1920 tot 1946 het Heimansplein naar de eveneens natuurbechemer en -beschrijver Eli Heimans.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In the street plan, the square was called Heimansplein from 1920 to 1946 after the same nature conservationist and writer Eli Heimans.

facts.text: Architect Jan Ernst van der Pek designed the square's western and southeastern facades around 1926.
facts.sourceQuote: Jan Ernst van der Pek is hier ook de belangrijkste architect. De westelijke gevelwand en die in het zuidoosten zijn door hem ontworpen en rond 1926 afgebouwd.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Jan Ernst van der Pek is also the most important architect here. The western facade wall and the one in the southeast were designed by him and completed around 1926.

features.name: Albert Cuyp market
features.opening: The Albert Cuyp Market is a street market in Amsterdam, The Netherlands, on the Albert Cuypstraat between Ferdinand Bolstraat and Van Woustraat, in the De Pijp…

facts.text: The market honors Albert Cuyp, a painter from the 17th century.
facts.sourceQuote: The street and market are named for Albert Cuyp, a painter from the 17th century.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The street and market are named for Albert Cuyp, a painter from the 17th century.

facts.text: City officials formalized the chaotic stalls into an official market in 1905.
facts.sourceQuote: By the beginning of the 20th century, this had become so chaotic that in 1905, the city government decided to set up a market, at first only held on Saturday evenings.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: By the beginning of the 20th century, this had become so chaotic that in 1905, the city government decided to set up a market, at first only held on Saturday evenings.

features.name: Dam Square
features.opening: Dam Square, also known as the Dam (Dutch pronunciation: [dɑm]), is a town square in Amsterdam, the capital and most populous city of the Netherlands.

facts.text: The name Dam Square derives from the original dam on the Amstel River that gave Amsterdam its own name.
facts.sourceQuote: The Dam derives its name from its original function: a dam on the Amstel River, hence also the name of the city of Amsterdam.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Dam derives its name from its original function: a dam on the Amstel River, hence also the name of the city of Amsterdam.

facts.text: A war memorial known as De Eendracht was unveiled in 1856 before King William III.
facts.sourceQuote: In 1856, a war memorial named De Eendracht (The Unity) was unveiled inside the square before King William III.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 1856, a war memorial named De Eendracht (The Unity) was unveiled inside the square before King William III.

facts.text: The stone column monument earned the nickname Naatje of the Dam before being removed in 1914.
facts.sourceQuote: A stone column with a female statue on top, the monument acquired the nickname "Naatje of the Dam". It was taken down in 1914.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: A stone column with a female statue on top, the monument acquired the nickname "Naatje of the Dam". It was taken down in 1914.

features.name: Bijlmermonument
features.opening: The growing monument (Bijlmer disaster) or Bijlmermonument is an artistic work of art in Amsterdam-Zuidoost.

facts.text: Every October 4, the monument serves as the focal point for commemorating the Bijlmer disaster.
facts.sourceQuote: Bij het monument wordt jaarlijks op 4 oktober stilgestaan bij de Bijlmerramp.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: On October 4 every year, the Bijlmer disaster is commemorated at the monument.

facts.text: Management of the site shifted from a dedicated foundation to joint neighbors starting in 2023.
facts.sourceQuote: Tot 2023 was een apart in het leven geroepen "Stichting Beheer Het Groeiend Monument" verantwoordelijk voor het monument. Sindsdien zijn de gezamenlijke buurtbewoners verantwoordelijk.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Until 2023, a separate "Stichting Beheer Het Groeiend Monument" was responsible for the monument. Since then, the joint neighbors have been responsible.

facts.text: Survivors initially gathered beneath this tree to share their stories of the tragedy.
facts.sourceQuote: Die boom werd binnen korte tijd na de ramp de verzamelplaats van personen die de ramp hadden meegemaakt en er verhaal over wilden doen.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: That tree became the gathering place of people who had experienced the disaster and wanted to tell stories about it shortly after the disaster.

features.name: Wibautstraat
features.opening: The Wibautstraat is a street in Amsterdam-Oost, between the Rhijnspoorplein and the Prins Bernhardplein and named after former alderman Floor Wibaut.

facts.text: German occupiers renamed it Weesperpoortstraat from 1942 to 1945 due to his socialist politics.
facts.sourceQuote: Tijdens de Tweede Wereldoorlog, van 13 februari 1942 tot 18 mei 1945, was de naam van deze straat in opdracht van de Duitse bezetter — afkerig van dit eerbetoon aan de linkse socialistische politicus — gewijzigd in Weesperpoortstraat.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: During World War II, from February 13, 1942 to May 18, 1945, the name of this street was changed at the request of the German occupiers - disgusted by this tribute to the left-wing socialist politician - to Weesperpoortstraat.

facts.text: A statue of Floor Wibaut once stood directly in front of the municipal urban planning services housed there.
facts.sourceQuote: Voor het gebouw, waarin tussen 1963 en 1990 de stedelijke bouwkundige diensten waren ondergebracht, stond een standbeeld van Floor Wibaut.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In front of the building, in which the urban planning services were housed between 1963 and 1990, stood a statue of Floor Wibaut.

features.name: Entrepotdok
features.opening: The Entrepotdok (Warehouse Dock), formerly Nieuwe Rapenburgergracht, is a canal in Amsterdam, and a street and row of former warehouses with the same name…

facts.text: The Entrepotdok (Warehouse Dock) was formerly known as Nieuwe Rapenburgergracht.
facts.sourceQuote: The Entrepotdok (Warehouse Dock), formerly Nieuwe Rapenburgergracht, is a canal in Amsterdam, and a street and row of former warehouses with the same name along the northeast side of the canal.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Entrepotdok (Warehouse Dock), formerly Nieuwe Rapenburgergracht, is a canal in Amsterdam, and a street and row of former warehouses with the same name along the northeast side of the canal.

facts.text: Construction of these warehouses spanned from 1708 until 1829.
facts.sourceQuote: They were constructed between 1708 and 1829, used for storage, squatted in the 1990s and are now converted into apartments.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: They were constructed between 1708 and 1829, used for storage, squatted in the 1990s and are now converted into apartments.

facts.text: Squatters occupied the complex during the 1990s before conversion to apartments.
facts.sourceQuote: They were constructed between 1708 and 1829, used for storage, squatted in the 1990s and are now converted into apartments.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: They were constructed between 1708 and 1829, used for storage, squatted in the 1990s and are now converted into apartments.

features.name: Slotermeerlaan
features.opening: The Slotermeerlaan is a street in Amsterdam Nieuw-West.

facts.text: While starting as a narrow residential road, it transforms into a major main route further along.
facts.sourceQuote: Het eerste gedeelte van de straat in een smalle woonstraat terwijl de straat daarna een belangrijke doorgaande route wordt.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The first part of the street is in a narrow residential street while the street becomes an important main route after that.

features.name: Scharrebiersluis
features.opening: The Scharrebiersluis (bridge 278) is a lift bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum.

facts.text: Electricity from a tram line allowed the bridge to operate automatically starting in 1913.
facts.sourceQuote: De brug moest nog met de hand bediend worden tot 1913; toen kwam de elektrische tram hier en kwam elektriciteit beschikbaar om de brug te openen en sluiten.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The bridge had to be operated manually until 1913; then the electric tram came here and electricity became available to open and close the bridge.

facts.text: A major renovation in 1986 finally fixed a long-standing defect while preserving original features.
facts.sourceQuote: In 1986/1987 kreeg de brug een flinke opknapbeurt, waarbij ook het oorspronkelijk mankement eindelijk verholpen kon worden. Bij die opknapbeurt werd getracht de brug zoveel mogelijk in de originele staat te houden.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 1986/1987, the bridge underwent a major renovation, during which the original defect could finally be remedied. During that renovation, efforts were made to keep the bridge as close to its original condition as possible.

facts.text: Original iron fencing was kept during renovations while new red-white barricades were hidden away.
facts.sourceQuote: De ijzeren hekwerken, al uit dienst, werden gehandhaafd en de nieuwe rood-witte slagbomen werden in staande stand weggewerkt en aan het zicht onttrokken.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The iron fencing, already in use, was maintained and the new red-white barricades were removed in standing order and hidden from view.

features.name: Burgemeester Stramanweg
features.opening: The Burgemeester Stramanweg is an important main road in the municipality of Ouder-Amstel and the municipality of Amsterdam, Zuidoost district.

facts.text: Until 1976, a railway viaduct crossed this route before the tracks were raised and the road ran underneath instead.
facts.sourceQuote: Tot 1976 werd de spoorlijn Amsterdam - Utrecht met een viaduct gekruist. Na het omhoog brengen van deze spoorlijn liep de weg onder het spoorviaduct door.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Until 1976, the Amsterdam - Utrecht railway line was crossed by a viaduct. After raising this railway line, the road ran under the railway viaduct.

facts.text: A free bus lane once operated here between the A2 intersection and the Amstel bridge before the South Tangent arrived in 2002.
facts.sourceQuote: Voor de komst van de Zuidtangent in 2002 verscheen er een vrije busbaan tussen de kruising met de A2 en de brug over de Amstel in Ouderkerk.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Before the arrival of the South Tangent in 2002, a free bus lane appeared between the intersection with the A2 and the bridge over the Amstel in Ouderkerk.

features.name: Waterlinie
features.opening: Defensive works surrounded by inundated areas.

facts.text: Water was raised just 40 cm to block infantry while remaining too shallow for swimming.
facts.sourceQuote: De bedoeling van inundatie is dat het water circa 40 cm boven het bewuste terrein komt, waarmee het voor infanterie onbegaanbaar wordt, doch te ondiep is om erdoorheen te varen.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The purpose of inundation is that the water comes about 40 cm above the intended terrain, making it impassable for infantry, but too shallow to be able to swim through.

facts.text: The Fortress Act protected the line from sabotage by angry farmers whose land would flood.
facts.sourceQuote: De boeren wier grond in de onder water te zetten gebieden lag, waren natuurlijk niet blij met deze actie. De linie moest daarom niet alleen beschermd worden tegen aanvallen van de vijand, maar ook tegen boze boeren die de linie zouden kunnen willen saboteren (in de Vestingwet was hiertoe in een schadeloosstelling voorzien).
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Of course, the farmers whose land was in the underwater areas to be flooded were not happy with this action. The line therefore had to be protected not only from attacks by the enemy, but also from angry farmers who might want to sabotage the line (this was provided for in the Fortress Act).

features.name: Bijlmerdreef
features.opening: The Bijlmerdreef is the first and also the most important promenade in the Bijlmermeer in Amsterdam-Southeast.

facts.text: House numbers only appeared after renovation, reaching a surprisingly high number of 1477.
facts.sourceQuote: Pas na de vernieuwing en verlaging kwamen er aan de dreef wel huisnummers, het hoogste nummer is 1477.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: It was only after the renovation and lowering that house numbers appeared on the drive, the highest number is 1477.

features.name: Karspeldreef
features.opening: The Karspeldreef is a dreef in the Bijlmermeer in Amsterdam-Zuidoost and runs from west to east just like the Bijlmerdreef and Daalwijkdreef.

facts.text: The middle section opened in 1969 as an exclusive fast-traffic road.
facts.sourceQuote: Het middelste gedeelte van de oorspronkelijk grotendeels halfhoog gelegen dreef, uitsluitend voor snelverkeer, werd geopend in 1969 tussen de Flierbosdreef en de Groesbeekdreef die toen nog werd aangegeven als "verbindingsweg Gooioord".
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The middle section of the originally mostly half-high dreef, exclusively for fast traffic, was opened in 1969 between the Flierbosdreef and the Groesbeekdreef, which was then still indicated as "connection road Gooioord".

facts.text: Originally mostly half-high, the dreef was lowered to street level in the early 2000s.
facts.sourceQuote: In de eerste helft van de jaren nul werd de Karspeldreef in het kader van de vernieuwing van de Bijlmermeer tussen de 's-Gravendijkdreef en Gooiseweg verlaagd en veranderd in een stadsstraat.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In the first half of the 2000s, the Karspeldreef was lowered and converted into a city street as part of the renewal of the Bijlmermeer between the 's-Gravendijkdreef and Gooiseweg.

features.name: Transformatorweg
features.opening: The Transformatorweg is an important thoroughfare in Amsterdam, in the Westpoort district.

facts.text: No houses exist along this busy freight route, only companies, hotels, and a swimming pool.
facts.sourceQuote: Aan de weg, die intensief wordt gebruikt door het (vracht)verkeer, bevinden zich geen woningen maar zijn uitsluitend bedrijven gevestigd met onder meer het "Coengebouw" met daar tegenover de "Kolonel Six kazerne", een tweetal hotels, een zwembad (Brediusbad) en het Mediacollege Amsterdam (voorheen Grafische school).
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: On the road, which is intensively used by (freight) traffic, there are no houses but only companies are located, including the "Coengebouw" with opposite the "Kolonel Six barracks", two hotels, a swimming pool (Brediusbad) and the Mediacollege Amsterdam (formerly Graphic School).

features.name: Oude Haagseweg
features.opening: The Oude Haagseweg is a road in Sloten in the municipality of Amsterdam, formed by the remaining part of the first highway from Amsterdam to The Hague.

facts.text: Since 1975, the route has extended westward through the Riekerpolder to Schiphol-Noord.
facts.sourceQuote: De weg loopt sinds 1975 vanaf de Johan Huizingalaan in Amsterdam Nieuw-West door de Riekerpolder, in westelijke en zuidwestelijke richting over de Ringvaart van de Haarlemmermeerpolder en vervolgens door de gemeente Haarlemmermeer (buurtschap Nieuwe Meer) tot aan de rijksweg 9 bij Schiphol-Noord.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Since 1975, the road has run from Johan Huizingalaan in Amsterdam Nieuw-West through the Riekerpolder, in a westerly and southwestly direction over the Ringvaart of the Haarlemmermeerpolder and then through the municipality of Haarlemmermeer (neighbourhood Nieuwe Meer) to the national highway 9 near Schiphol-Noord.

facts.text: A dedicated bus lane for high-quality public transport runs along the southwestern section near the Oude Haagsebrug.
facts.sourceQuote: Op het zuidwestelijke deel, waaronder de Oude Haagsebrug over de Ringvaart, is een vrije busbaan ingericht voor het R-net en GVB, een vorm van hoogwaardig openbaar vervoer.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: On the southwestern part, including the Oude Haagsebrug over the Ringvaart, a free bus lane has been set up for the R-net and GVB, a form of high-quality public transport.

facts.text: The entrance to De Oeverlanden features a large artwork of pink glasses created by Daniella Rubinovitz.
facts.sourceQuote: Bij een ingang van De Oeverlanden staat het kunstwerk Giant pink glasses van Daniella Rubinovitz en aan de gebouwen van de voormalige Rijksluchtvaartdienst op nummer 50 hangt een reliëf van Hans Verhulst.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: At the entrance of De Oeverlanden stands the work of art Giant pink glasses by Daniella Rubinovitz and on the buildings of the former Rijksluchtvaartdienst at number 50 hangs a relief by Hans Verhulst.

features.name: Europaplein
features.opening: The Europaplein is a square in Amsterdam-Zuid.

facts.text: Tram line 4 operated its terminus here starting in 1948, replacing an earlier route from 1936.
facts.sourceQuote: Tramlijn 4 had hier sinds 1948 zijn eindpunt (daarvoor lijn 8 van 1936 tot 1942).
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Tram line 4 had its terminus here since 1948 (before that, line 8 from 1936 to 1942).

facts.text: After reopening in 2011, the square features the Festive series of sculptures by Guillaume Bijl.
facts.sourceQuote: Nadat de werkzaamheden klaar waren werd het gehele plein opnieuw ingericht en voorzien van de Feestelijke beeldenreeks van beeldhouwer Guillaume Bijl. Op 15 mei 2011 werd het Europaplein officieel heropend.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: After the work was finished, the entire square was redesigned again and provided with the Festive series of sculptures by sculptor Guillaume Bijl. On May 15, 2011, the Europaplein was officially reopened.

features.name: Valkenburgerstraat
features.opening: The Valkenburgerstraat is a street in the Nieuwmarkt neighborhood in Amsterdam-Centrum.

facts.text: A map from 1599 already showed this island, though it had almost no settlement at that time.
facts.sourceQuote: Het eiland staat al vermeld op de kaart van Pieter Bast uit 1599 al was er toen nauwelijks bebouwing aanwezig.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The island is already mentioned on Pieter Bast's map from 1599, although there was hardly any settlement present at that time.

facts.text: After the war ended, Interior Forces troops stationed here to maintain order until Allies arrived.
facts.sourceQuote: Na de Duitse capitulatie aan het einde van de oorlog werden hier troepen van de Binnenlandse Strijdkrachten ondergebracht om de orde in de stad handhaven totdat de geallieerden de stad konden bereiken.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: After the German capitulation at the end of the war, troops of the Interior Forces were stationed here to maintain order in the city until the Allies could reach the city.

features.name: Hugo de Vrieslaan
features.opening: The Hugo de Vrieslaan is a street in the Watergraafsmeer neighborhood Jerusalem in Amsterdam-Oost.

facts.text: Hugo de Vrieslaan follows the extension of Wethouder Frankeweg from its start at Middenweg.
facts.sourceQuote: De straat begint bij de Middenweg en ligt in het verlengde van de Wethouder Frankeweg.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The street begins at the Middenweg and runs along the extension of the Wethouder Frankeweg.

features.name: Jan van Galenstraat
features.opening: The Jan van Galenstraat is a street in the Amsterdam neighborhoods of West and Nieuw-West.

facts.text: A viaduct with ramps opened for northbound traffic in 1969 and southbound traffic in 1972.
facts.sourceQuote: In 1969 werd de straat bij de kruising met de Einsteinweg (Ringweg-West) verhoogd en kruist met een viaduct met op- en afritten, in gebruik genomen in 1969 in noordelijke richting en in 1972 in zuidelijke richting.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 1969, the street near the intersection with Einsteinweg (Ringweg-West) was raised and crosses with a viaduct with on- and off-ramps, opened to traffic in 1969 in the northbound direction and in 1972 in the southbound direction.

facts.text: Tram line 13 has been running through this street since 1989 between Jan Tooropstraat and the subway station.
facts.sourceQuote: Tussen de Jan Tooropstraat en het metrostation rijdt sinds 1989 tramlijn 13 door de straat.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Since 1989, tram line 13 has been running through the street between Jan Tooropstraat and the subway station.

features.name: Rhijnspoorplein
features.opening: The Rhijnspoorplein is a square in Amsterdam-East and -Center.

facts.text: Construction of the Amsterdam subway began here in August 1970.
facts.sourceQuote: De bouw van de Amsterdamse metro startte in augustus 1970 op het Rhijnspoorplein.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Construction of the Amsterdam subway began in August 1970 at the Rhijnspoorplein.

facts.text: Foundations of a former train station turntable were demolished during this work.
facts.sourceQuote: Toen werden ook de nog aanwezige fundamenten van de draaischijf van het voormalige treinstation gesloopt.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Then the still present foundations of the turntable of the former train station were also demolished.

facts.text: The tunnel for the East Line opened to traffic in October 1977.
facts.sourceQuote: De tunnel van de Oostlijn werd in oktober 1977 in gebruik genomen.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The tunnel of the East Line was put into use in October 1977.

features.name: Jaargetijden
features.opening: Brug Driemond is a lift bridge over the Weespertrekvaart in the North Holland village of Driemond.

facts.text: Until 1966, the village and its bridge belonged to the separate municipality of Weesperkarspel.
facts.sourceQuote: Tot 1966 lagen brug en dorp in de gemeente Weesperkarspel.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Until 1966, bridge and village were in the municipality of Weesperkarspel.

facts.text: Ships must wait at a lock here before entering the Amsterdam-Rhine Canal due to narrow waters.
facts.sourceQuote: De Weespertrekvaart is dit laatste gedeelte voorbij de brug smaller dan de rest van de vaart en er bevindt zich een sluis waar de schepen moeten wachten tot ze veilig op het Amsterdam Rijnkanaal kunnen invoegen tussen de binnenvaartschepen of kunnen oversteken naar het Smal Weesp aan de overzijde van het kanaal.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Weesper Canal is narrower than the rest of the canal beyond the bridge in this last section, and there is a lock where the ships must wait until they can safely enter the Amsterdam Rhine Canal between the inland vessels or cross to the Narrow Weesp on the other side of the canal.

features.name: Tasmanstraat
features.opening: The Tasmanstraat is a residential street in the Amsterdam Spaarndammer neighborhood.

facts.text: The Spaarndammertunnel connecting to Van Diemenstraat opened for traffic in February 2018.
facts.sourceQuote: De gemeente Amsterdam had in 2013 de opdracht verstrekt aan de firma Max Bögl om naast de Tasmanstraat de Spaarndammertunnel te bouwen, die aansluiting geeft op de Van Diemenstraat/Westerkeersluis. De tunnel is op 5 februari 2018 officieel in gebruik genomen.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 2013, the municipality of Amsterdam had entrusted the company Max Bögl with the task of building the Spaarndammertunnel in addition to the Tasmanstraat, which connects to the Van Diemenstraat/Westerkeersluis. The tunnel was officially put into use on February 5, 2018.

facts.text: Ferry wings returned to the Tasmanstraat pier in June 2018 after a temporary relocation in 2015.
facts.sourceQuote: Deze steiger was in 2015 voor enige tijd verplaatst naar de Westerdoksdijk in verband met bouwwerkzaamheden. Sinds 18 juni 2018 varen de veren weer naar de Tasmanstraat.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: This pier was temporarily moved to the Westerdoksdijk in 2015 due to construction work. Since June 18, 2018, the wings have been sailing to the Tasmanstraat again.

facts.text: Red asphalt bike paths run on both sides of the tunnel, separated from vehicle traffic.
facts.sourceQuote: Ook de fietspaden liggen aan weerszijden van de tunnel. Beide fietspaden zijn gescheiden van de wegen, rood geasfalteerd met dubbele rijrichting.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The bike paths are also on either side of the tunnel. Both bike paths are separated from the roads, red asphalted with double direction.

facts.text: Through traffic uses the tunnel, leaving the street surface primarily for local destinations.
facts.sourceQuote: Doordat de tunnel het doorgaande verkeer afhandelt, wordt de Tasmanstraat voornamelijk gebruikt door verkeer met lokale bestemming.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Because the tunnel handles through traffic, the Tasmanstraat is primarily used by traffic with local destinations.

features.name: Spaarndammerdijk
features.opening: The Spaarndammerdijk is a dike that was built from the first half of the 13th century to protect the peatland grazing area south of the still not drained IJ.

facts.text: The dike was significantly shortened after the Saint Elizabeth flood of 1421.
facts.sourceQuote: Na de Sint-Elisabethsvloed van 1421 werd de lengte van de dijk aanmerkelijk verkort door het leggen van een inlaagdijk dwars door de ambachten Spaarnwoude en Hofambacht, de huidige Hoge Spaarndammerdijk.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: After the Saint Elizabeth flood of 1421, the length of the dike was significantly shortened by the construction of a causeway dike across the municipalities of Spaarnwoude and Hofambacht, the current Hoge Spaarndammerdijk.

facts.text: Residents from Houtrijk, Polanen, Osdorp, and Sloten were originally liable for keeping the dike secure.
facts.sourceQuote: Ten oosten van Spaarndam waren de bewoners van de ambachten Houtrijk en Polanen, Osdorp en Sloten verantwoordelijk voor het onderhoud.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: To the east of Spaarndam, the inhabitants of the crafts of Houtrijk and Polanen, Osdorp and Sloten were responsible for maintenance.

features.name: Haparandadam
features.opening: The Haparandadam is a dam in Amsterdam-West.

facts.text: The road on the dam connects to the south side of Haparandaweg, a name established in 1940.
facts.sourceQuote: De weg op de dam sluit aan de zuidkant aan op de Haparandaweg (naam sinds 1940).
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The road on the dam connects to the south side of the Haparandaweg (name since 1940).

facts.text: Haparandadam honors Haparanda, a Swedish port on the Gulf of Bothnia bordering Finland.
facts.sourceQuote: De dam is vernoemd naar de Zweedse havenstad Haparanda aan de Botnische Golf, op de grens met Finland, waar veel hout vandaan naar Amsterdam kwam.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The dam is named after the Swedish port city of Haparanda on the Gulf of Bothnia, on the border with Finland, where much wood came from to Amsterdam.

features.name: Petemayenbrug
features.opening: The Petemayenbrug is a double pickup bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum.

facts.text: The name Petemayenbrug derives from petemoeien, meaning stepmother or old women.
facts.sourceQuote: De naam zou afgeleid zijn van petemoeien (peetmoeder), tevens aanduiding van oude vrouwtjes.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The name would be derived from petemoeien (stepmother), also indicating old women.

facts.text: Queen Wilhelmina crossed the bridge in 1910 with her entourage and Princess Juliana.
facts.sourceQuote: In 1910 kreeg de brug een koninklijk tintje toen koningin Wilhelmina met haar gevolg de brug overtrok en de toen eenjarige prinses Juliana aan de Oranjevereniging uit de wijk toonde.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 1910, the bridge received a royal touch when Queen Wilhelmina crossed the bridge with her entourage and showed the then one-year-old Princess Juliana to the Orange Society from the neighborhood.

facts.text: Artist Jacob Olie captured the new iron bridge just months after it opened.
facts.sourceQuote: Men had toen het idee dat het toepassen van ijzer voor hameipoort, de balans en liggers een besparing zou opleveren (ten opzichte van een houten brug), de brug werd enkele maanden na opening vastgelegd door Jacob Olie.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: At that time, the idea was that applying iron to the hameipoort, the balance and struts would result in a savings (compared to a wooden bridge), the bridge was captured a few months after opening by Jacob Olie.

features.name: Texelweg
features.opening: Texel (Dutch pronunciation: [ˈtɛsəl] ; Texels dialect: Tessel) is a municipality and an island with a population of 13,846 in North Holland, Netherlands.

facts.text: The name Texel is Frisian, though Dutch sound changes make it typically pronounced Tessel.
facts.sourceQuote: The name Texel is Frisian, but because of historical sound-changes in Dutch, where all -x- sounds have been replaced with -s- sounds (compare for instance English fox, Frisian fokse, German Fuchs with Dutch vos), the name is typically pronounced Tessel in Dutch.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The name Texel is Frisian, but because of historical sound-changes in Dutch, where all -x- sounds have been replaced with -s- sounds (compare for instance English fox, Frisian fokse, German Fuchs with Dutch vos), the name is typically pronounced Tessel in Dutch.

facts.text: In 1594, the first Dutch expedition to the Northeast Passage departed from the island that shares its name.
facts.sourceQuote: The first Dutch expedition to the Northeast Passage departed from the island on 5 June 1594.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The first Dutch expedition to the Northeast Passage departed from the island on 5 June 1594.

features.name: Dolingadreef
features.opening: The Dolingadreef is a dike in the Bijlmermeer in Amsterdam-Zuidoost.

facts.text: The first elevated section for fast traffic opened in 1971.
facts.sourceQuote: Het eerste gedeelte van de verhoogde dreef, uitsluitend voor snelverkeer, werd geopend in 1971.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The first section of the elevated causeway, exclusively for fast traffic, was opened in 1971.

facts.text: Unlike nearby roads, it remains mostly half-high as originally planned.
facts.sourceQuote: In tegenstelling tot bijvoorbeeld de Bijlmerdreef is de dreef nog voor het grootse deel half hooggelegen conform de uitgangspunten van het stedenbouwkundig plan van de Bijlmermeer.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Unlike, for example, the Bijlmerdreef, the dreef is still mostly half-high according to the starting points of the Bijlmermeer urban planning plan.

features.name: Pieter Calandlaan
features.opening: The Pieter Calandlaan is a street in Amsterdam Nieuw-West.

facts.text: The south side originally held addresses up to 1377, while the north side only reached 258 due to far fewer buildings.
facts.sourceQuote: Opvallend is dat de huisnummering aan de zuidzijde gaat tot 1377 maar aan de noordzijde oorspronkelijk slechts tot 258 omdat aan de noordzijde zich veel minder adressen bevinden dan aan de zuidzijde.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: It is striking that the house numbering on the south side goes up to 1377 but on the north side originally only up to 258 because there are much fewer addresses on the north side than on the south side.

facts.text: An extension toward Ecuplein added north-side addresses, pushing the maximum number to 822.
facts.sourceQuote: Sinds de verlenging naar het Ecuplein, waarbij alleen adressen aan de noordzijde bestaan, gaat de nummering echter tot 822.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: However, since the extension to the Ecuplein, where only addresses on the north side exist, the numbering goes up to 822.

facts.text: The south side bears the name Pieter Calandplantsoen due to a shortage of house numbers.
facts.sourceQuote: De straat kreeg hier echter aan de zuidzijde de naam "Pieter Calandplantsoen", dit omdat er onvoldoende huisnummers beschikbaar waren binnen de oorspronkelijke huisnummering.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: However, the street was named "Pieter Calandplantsoen" on the south side here, because there were not enough house numbers available within the original house numbering.

facts.text: Paul Vendel's Swarm sculpture was installed at the intersection with Baden Powellweg in 2006.
facts.sourceQuote: Op de kruising met de Baden Powellweg werd in 2006 het beeld Zwerm van Paul Vendel geplaatst.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 2006, the Swarm sculpture by Paul Vendel was placed at the intersection with Baden Powellweg.

features.name: James Rosskade
features.opening: The James Rosskade is a street in the Bos en Lommer district in the Amsterdam municipality of West.

facts.text: All three residential blocks were constructed for the Catholic Housing Cooperative Dr. Shepherd.
facts.sourceQuote: Alle drie deze woonblokken zijn gebouwd voor de Katholieke Woningcooperatie Dr. Schaepman.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: All three of these residential blocks were built for the Catholic Housing Cooperative Dr. Shepherd.

facts.text: Architect Johannes Martinus van Hardeveld designed the houses in two of the three residential blocks.
facts.sourceQuote: Een groot deel van de woningen in deze buurt is ontworpen door architect Johannes Martinus van Hardeveld (van de blokken 2 en 3 is bekend, dat ze van zijn hand zijn).
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: A large part of the houses in this neighborhood was designed by architect Johannes Martinus van Hardeveld (it is known that they were designed by him for blocks 2 and 3).

facts.text: Only the east side of James Rosskade features buildings, which are medium-rise structures.
facts.sourceQuote: De straat is een woonstraat met alleen aan de oostzijde bebouwing, bestaande uit middelhoogbouw.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The street is a residential street with only buildings on the east side, consisting of medium-rise buildings.

features.name: Burgemeester De Vlugtlaan
features.opening: The Burgemeester De Vlugtlaan is a street in Amsterdam Nieuw-West.

facts.text: Queen Juliana officially opened the Slotermeer garden city expansion here on October 7, 1952.
facts.sourceQuote: Aan de brug over de sloot langs de spoordijk is een plaquette bevestigd die herinnert aan de opening op 7 oktober 1952 door Koningin Juliana van de tuinstad Slotermeer als eerste stadsuitbreiding buiten de Ringspoordijk.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: On the bridge over the ditch along the railway embankment, a plaque has been attached that commemorates the opening on October 7, 1952 by Queen Juliana of the garden city Slotermeer as the first urban expansion outside the Ringspoordijk.

features.name: Buitenveldertselaan
features.opening: The Buitenveldertselaan is a street in Amsterdam by Buitenveldert that connects the Zuid district with Amstelveen.

facts.text: Construction occurred during the 1960s along the Parnassusweg near a former dike body.
facts.sourceQuote: De weg werd in de jaren zestig aangelegd. De weg kwam in het verlengde van de Parnassusweg en begon oorspronkelijk ten zuiden van het toenmalige dijklichaam waar later de rijksweg 10 en station Zuid op zouden worden aangelegd.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The road was built in the 1960s. The road ran along the Parnassusweg and originally began south of the then-existing dike body where the national highway 10 and Zuid station would later be built.

facts.text: Zuidas development shortened the street's northern end in 2015 to start south of De Boelelaan.
facts.sourceQuote: In verband met de ontwikkeling van de Zuidas werd de straat in 2015 aan de noordzijde ingekort; ze begint vanaf dan ten zuiden van de De Boelelaan.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In connection with the development of the Zuidas, the street was shortened on the north side in 2015; it begins from there south of the De Boelelaan.

facts.text: Crossing the municipal boundary near Kalfjeslaan, the road continues as Beneluxbaan in Amstelveen.
facts.sourceQuote: Vanaf de gemeentegrens bij de Kalfjeslaan wordt de weg op Amstelveens grondgebied voortgezet als Beneluxbaan.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: From the municipal boundary near Kalfjeslaan, the road continues on Amstelveen territory as Beneluxbaan.

facts.text: Architects Zeeger Gulden and Ger Husslage created the buildings at house numbers 78 through 84.
facts.sourceQuote: Daaronder bevindt zich werk van Zeeger Gulden, Ger Husslage (huisnummers 78-84) en Piet Zanstra (bij Cannenburg/Assumburg) en Zanstra, Ab Gmelig Meyling en Peter de Clercq Zubli (102-120).
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Among them are works by Zeeger Gulden, Ger Husslage (house numbers 78-84) and Piet Zanstra (near Cannenburg/Assumburg) and Zanstra, Ab Gmelig Meyling and Peter de Clercq Zubli (102-120).

facts.text: House numbers run from 1 to 184, yet many specific numbers are missing along the route.
facts.sourceQuote: Huisnummers lopen op van 1 tot en met 184, al missen er hier en daar een flink aantal huisnummers.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: House numbers run from 1 to 184, although there are a fair number of house numbers missing here and there.

features.name: Michiel de Ruijtertunnel
features.opening: The Michiel de Ruijtertunnel is a tunnel for car traffic in Amsterdam-Centrum.

facts.text: The Michiel de Ruijtertunnel honors the famous Dutch admiral Michiel de Ruyter, who lived from 1607 to 1676.
facts.sourceQuote: De tunnel is vernoemd naar Michiel de Ruyter (1607-1676).
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The tunnel is named after Michiel de Ruyter (1607-1676).

facts.text: Construction began in 2003 and the tunnel finally opened to traffic on July 13, 2015.
facts.sourceQuote: De bouw van de tunnel startte in 2003, de ruwbouw kwam gereed in mei 2013. Op 13 juli 2015 werd de tunnel opengesteld voor het autoverkeer.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Construction of the tunnel began in 2003, the rough construction was ready in May 2013. On July 13, 2015, the tunnel was opened to vehicular traffic.

features.name: Noordzijde
features.opening: The Noordzijde is a street in Amsterdam Slotermeer.

facts.text: A bay once called Varkensbaai was renamed Sloterstrand after a beach opened in 2017.
facts.sourceQuote: Aan de andere kant van de jachthaven bevindt zich een baai die in de jaren zestig Varkensbaai werd genoemd maar na de aanleg van een recreatiestrand in mei 2017 'Sloterstrand' werd gedoopt.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: On the other side of the marina is a bay that was called Varkensbaai in the 1960s but was renamed 'Sloterstrand' after a recreational beach was built in May 2017.

facts.text: A wide green strip with elm trees and paths runs alongside the traffic road.
facts.sourceQuote: Naast de verkeersweg is een brede groenstrook met iepenlanen met voet- en fietspaden.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In addition to the traffic road, there is a wide green strip with row of elm trees with footpaths and cycling paths.

facts.text: Noordzijde means "north side," describing its location along the northern bank of Sloterplas.
facts.sourceQuote: Deze is tevens de noordoever van de Sloterplas.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: This is also the north bank of the Sloterplas.

facts.text: In 2017, this street and the adjacent lake bank received official municipal protection status.
facts.sourceQuote: Sinds 2017 is de Noordzijde met de noordelijke oever van de Sloterplas aangewezen als Gemeentelijk beschermd stadsgezicht.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Since 2017, the Noordzijde with the northern bank of the Sloterplas has been designated as a Municipal protected urban landscape.

features.name: Oostoever
features.opening: Oostoever is a street in Amsterdam Nieuw-West, located mostly in the Oostoever Sloterplas neighborhood.

facts.text: Oostoever means "eastern bank" and was named for forming the eastern shore of the Sloterplas.
facts.sourceQuote: Ze is vernoemd naar wat zij is; zij vormt deels de oostoever van de Sloterplas.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: It is named after what it is; it partly forms the eastern bank of the Sloterplas.

facts.text: A street called Westoever existed from 1948 until it became President Allendelaan in 1974.
facts.sourceQuote: Er was sinds 1948 ook een straat met de naam Westoever, maar die kreeg op 27 februari 1974 een nieuwe naam: President Allendelaan.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: There had also been a street called Westoever since 1948, but it was renamed President Allendelaan on February 27, 1974.

facts.text: The sewage plant on the east side gave way to a new residential area in the 1990s.
facts.sourceQuote: Aan de oostzijde was sinds 1926 / 1954 de rioolwaterzuiveringsinstallatie Amsterdam-West. In de jaren negentig van de 20e eeuw maakte die plaats voor de nieuwe woonwijk Oostoever Sloterplas.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: On the east side, since 1926 / 1954, the Amsterdam-West sewage treatment plant has been located there. In the 1990s of the 20th century, that place gave way to the new residential area Oostoever Sloterplas.

facts.text: A planned observation tower was never built because funding ran out before construction could begin.
facts.sourceQuote: Slebos kwam overigens met het totaalontwerp voor de noordelijke oevers van de Sloterplas, met daarin: het paviljoen (gezien als stuurhut); de specifieke lantaarnpalen (gezien als masten); het grote terras met panorama over de plas (gezien als dek); een terras geplaveid met witte ronde tegels (het 'stippenterras'); hoge kademuren met daarop een brede wandelboulevard; de witte betonnen kaderand (gezien als romp van het schip) vormt tevens de balustrade van een trap naar een boventerras; onder die trap bevindt zich een trap naar aanlegsteigers aan het water; een kiosk; later uitgebouwd tot horecagelegenheid; uitkijktoren; de jachthaven aan de Noordzijde; een openluchtzwembad (Sloterparkbad) De uitkijktoren is echter nooit gebouwd; het geld was op. Hiervoor is wel een zware onderbouw gemaakt met stevige fundering die als sokkel voor de toren zou dienen.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: By the way, Slebos came up with the overall design for the northern shores of the Sloterplas, which included: the pavilion (seen as the steering hut); the specific lampposts (seen as masts); the large terrace with panoramic view of the pond (seen as the deck); a terrace paved with white round tiles (the 'stippler terrace'); high retaining walls with a wide promenade on top; the white concrete frame edge (seen as the hull of the ship) also forms the balustrade of a staircase to an upper terrace; under that staircase isa staircase to construction jetties by the water; a kiosk; later expanded into a catering establishment; observation tower; the marina on the north side; an outdoor swimming pool (Sloterparkbad). The observation tower was never built; the money ran out. For this, a heavy base has been made with a solid foundation that would serve as a base for the tower.

features.name: Havenstraat
features.opening: The Havenstraat is a street in the Schinkel neighborhood, Amsterdam-Zuid.

facts.text: Havenstraat means harbor street, named for a ship mooring place.
facts.sourceQuote: De straat kreeg op 3 april 1912 per raadsbesluit haar naam; een vernoeming naar haven, een ligplaats voor schepen.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The street was given its name on April 3, 1912 by a council decision; a name after the harbor, a mooring place for ships.

facts.text: Nearby streets share shipping names like Vaartstraat and Zeilstraat.
facts.sourceQuote: Meerdere straten in de buurt zijn vernoemd naar begrippen uit de scheepvaart (Vaartstraat, Vlietstraat, Zeilstraat).
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Several streets in the neighborhood are named after concepts from shipping (Vaartstraat, Vlietstraat, Zeilstraat).

facts.text: Until 2024, the street contained only two odd house numbers: 3 and 5.
facts.sourceQuote: De straat kende (tot 2024) slechts twee oneven huisnummers 3 en 5, bestaande uit Romneyloodsen op het terrein achter het Haarlemmermeerstation.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The street only had two odd house numbers 3 and 5 (until 2024), consisting of Romney sheds on the site behind the Haarlemmermeer station.

facts.text: The prison at number 6 was renovated from 2019 to become the British School of Amsterdam.
facts.sourceQuote: De straat kent drie opvallende gebouwen: het Huis van Bewaring (II) met huisnummer 6, een ontwerp van architect Willem Metzelaar (werkend voor Justitie), een gevangenis uit 1890, die, nadat er vluchtelingen en dak- en thuislozen waren opgevangen, vanaf 2019 werd verbouwd ten behoeve van de British School of Amsterdam die hier van start is gegaan vanaf het schooljaar 2021-2022.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The street has three striking buildings: the Huis van Bewaring (II) with house number 6, a design by architect Willem Metzelaar (working for the Justice Department), a prison from 1890, which, after refugees and homeless people were accommodated, was renovated from 2019 for the British School of Amsterdam, which started here from the 2021-2022 school year.

features.name: Burgemeester Fockstraat
features.opening: The Burgemeester Fockstraat is a street in Slotermeer, Amsterdam Nieuw-West.

facts.text: Burgemeester Fockstraat was officially named on July 9, 1952.
facts.sourceQuote: De straat kreeg zijn naam op 9 juli 1952 en werd vernoemd naar Cornelis Fock (1828-1910), burgemeester van Amsterdam van 1866 tot 1868, daarna Commissaris des Konings voor Zuid-Holland.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The street was named on July 9, 1952 and was named after Cornelis Fock (1828-1910), mayor of Amsterdam from 1866 to 1868, then Commissioner of the King for South Holland.

facts.text: Cornelis Fock later became Commissioner of the King for South Holland after his mayoral term.
facts.sourceQuote: De straat kreeg zijn naam op 9 juli 1952 en werd vernoemd naar Cornelis Fock (1828-1910), burgemeester van Amsterdam van 1866 tot 1868, daarna Commissaris des Konings voor Zuid-Holland.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The street was named on July 9, 1952 and was named after Cornelis Fock (1828-1910), mayor of Amsterdam from 1866 to 1868, then Commissioner of the King for South Holland.

facts.text: A temporary bus barrier appeared in 2001 during A10 renovation work.
facts.sourceQuote: Wel verscheen in 2001 gedurende de renovatie werkzaamheden op de A10 een tijdelijke busdam.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: However, a temporary bus barrier appeared in 2001 during the renovation work on the A10.

features.name: IJdoornlaan
features.opening: The IJdoornlaan is an important east-west through route in Amsterdam-North.

facts.text: An elevated section featuring uneven floor crossings and pedestrian stairs was completed in 1969.
facts.sourceQuote: Het verhoogd liggende gedeelte met ongelijkvloerse kruisingen en trappen voor voetgangers naar maaiveldniveau na de Jisperveldstraat en langs de Th.Weeversweg, J.Drijverweg en het Buikslotermeerplein kwam in 1969 gereed, aangelegd op de plaats van ongeveer de vroegere Kruisweg.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The elevated section with uneven floor crossings and pedestrian stairs to meadow level after Jisperveldstraat and along Th.Weeversweg, J.Drijverweg and Buikslotermeerplein was completed in 1969, built on the site of approximately the former Kruisweg.

facts.text: In 1983, the road extended to Banne Buiksloot after a new bridge over the North Holland Canal opened.
facts.sourceQuote: In 1983, na de opening van de brug 970 (destijds IJdoornlaanbrug genoemd) over het Noord-Hollandsch Kanaal, werd de straat verlengd naar Banne Buiksloot.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 1983, after the opening of bridge 970 (then called IJdoornlaanbrug) over the North Holland Canal, the street was extended to Banne Buiksloot.

facts.text: A branch called Vorticellaweg replaced the narrow Kadoelerweg specifically for the opening of Kadoelen.
facts.sourceQuote: Voor de ontsluiting van Kadoelen kwam een aftakking, de Vorticellaweg ter vervanging van de route over de smalle Kadoelerweg.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: For the opening of Kadoelen, a branch was created, the Vorticellaweg in place of the route over the narrow Kadoelerweg.

features.name: Hoofddorpweg
features.opening: The Hoofddorpweg in the Hoofddorpplein neighborhood of Amsterdam-Zuid was built in the 1920s on the territory of the municipality of Sloten, which was annexed…

facts.text: Hoofddorpweg takes its name from the town of Hoofddorp in the Haarlemmermeer.
facts.sourceQuote: De Hoofddorpweg is vernoemd naar Hoofddorp in de Haarlemmermeer.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Hoofddorpweg is named after Hoofddorp in the Haarlemmermeer.

facts.text: Before district divisions, this road belonged to the Overtoomse Veld neighborhood.
facts.sourceQuote: Tot de indeling in stadsdelen maakte de Hoofddorpweg onderdeel uit van het Overtoomse Veld.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Until it was divided into districts, Hoofddorpweg was part of the Overtoomse Veld.

features.name: De Boelelaan
features.opening: The De Boelelaan in Amsterdam-Buitenveldert was named on January 15, 1958 and was named after Gerrit de Boele, bailiff of Amstelland and Waterland (1354/55).

facts.text: The road gained importance after the VU medical center arrived on its south side in 1957 or 1958.
facts.sourceQuote: De weg begon eigenlijk als een veredelde zandweg, maar won aan importantie door de komst van het VU medisch centrum in 1957/1958 aan de zuidkant van de laan.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The road actually began as an improved dirt road, but gained importance due to the arrival of the VU medical center in 1957/1958 on the south side of the lane.

facts.text: Garden town Buitenveldert was constructed along the southern stretch during the 1960s.
facts.sourceQuote: Aan de zuidzijde verrees tuinstad Buitenveldert, gebouwd in de jaren zestig.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: On the south side, garden town Buitenveldert was built in the 1960s.

facts.text: A connection called Lex van Deldenbrug linked De Boelelaan to George Gershwinplein between 2012 and 2013.
facts.sourceQuote: In het kader van het project Zuidas werd vanuit de Boelelaan in de jaren 2012/2013 in de vorm van de Lex van Deldenbrug een verbinding gelegd vanuit De Boelelaan als deel van het "oude" Buitenveldert naar het George Gershwinplein als deel van het grote project.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: As part of the Zuidas project, a connection was laid from De Boelelaan in the form of the Lex van Deldenbrug from the Boelelaan in the years 2012/2013 as part of the "old" Buitenveldert to the George Gershwinplein as part of the large project.

facts.text: The tower at number 2 opened as the Esso Motor Hotel in 1969 before becoming a refugee shelter in 2022.
facts.sourceQuote: Op huisnummer 2 staat een voormalige hoteltoren die in 1969 geopend werd onder de naam Esso Motor Hotel. In 1975 werd het verkocht aan Crest Hotels en in 1990 aan Holiday Inn dat in 2020 sloot. In 2022 kwam in de toren een opvang voor vluchtelingen.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: At house number 2 stands a former hotel tower that was opened in 1969 under the name Esso Motor Hotel. In 1975 it was sold to Crest Hotels and in 1990 to Holiday Inn that closed in 2020. In 2022, a shelter for refugees was opened in the tower.

facts.text: A 160-meter-long flat from the 1960s occupies much of the southern facade and was later renamed De Boel.
facts.sourceQuote: Een groot deel van de zuidelijke gevelwand wordt in beslag genomen door een 160 meter lange flat uit de jaren 60; zij kreeg begin 21e eeuw een opknapbeurt en kreeg de naam "De Boel".
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: A large part of the southern facade wall is occupied by a 160-meter-long flat from the 1960s; it underwent a renovation at the beginning of the 21st century and was renamed "De Boel".

facts.text: The VU Medical Center received an overpass crossing De Boelelaan during construction in 1984 or 1985.
facts.sourceQuote: Soms voor de universiteit zelf, maar ook voor het VU Medisch Centrum, dat in 1984/1985 een overkluizing over de De Boelelaan kreeg.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Sometimes for the university itself, but also for the VU Medical Center, which received an overpass over the De Boelelaan in 1984/1985.

features.name: Nassaukade
features.opening: The Nassaukade is a street in Amsterdam-West, on the banks of the Singelgracht, between Nassauplein and the Overtoom.

facts.text: Nearby Nassauplein and two Nassau streets share the same royal namesake origin.
facts.sourceQuote: Ook het Nassauplein en de Eerste en Tweede Nassaustraat in de Staatsliedenbuurt zijn naar het huis Oranje-Nassau vernoemd.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Nassauplein and the Eerste and Tweede Nassaustraat in the Staatsliedenbuurt are also named after the house Oranje-Nassau.

facts.text: A movable bridge over the Kattensloot was renovated in 1954.
facts.sourceQuote: Over de Kattensloot ligt een beweegbare brug, de Kattenslootbrug, die in 1954 werd vernieuwd.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Over the Kattensloot lies a movable bridge, the Kattenslootbrug, which was renovated in 1954.

facts.text: Eight municipal monuments line this street, including numbers 17 and 18.
facts.sourceQuote: De straat telt een achttal gemeentelijke monumenten, waaronder Nassaukade 17 en Nassaukade 18.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The street has eight municipal monuments, including Nassaukade 17 and Nassaukade 18.

features.name: Stadionplein
features.opening: The Stadionplein is a square in Amsterdam-Zuid, which was built in the 1920s at the intersection of Stadionweg and Amstelveenseweg to better control car…

facts.text: Architects designed six new closed blocks using styles based on the Amsterdam School and Berlage.
facts.sourceQuote: Het stedenbouwkundige plan en de architectuur zijn gebaseerd op de Amsterdamse School en de ideeën van Berlage. De zes nieuwe gesloten bouwblokken zijn ontworpen door architectenbureaus als Mulleners & Mulleners (langs de Afroditekade), Lafour en Wijk (langs de binnenstraten) en Rudy Uytenhaak (langs de Laan der Hesperiden).
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The urban planning plan and architecture are based on the Amsterdam School and the ideas of Berlage. The six new closed building blocks were designed by architectural firms such as Mulleners & Mulleners (along the Afroditekade), Lafour and Wijk (along the inner streets) and Rudy Uytenhaak (along the Laan der Hesperiden).

facts.text: Part of Stadionplein was renamed Laan der Hesperiden due to the district's construction.
facts.sourceQuote: In verband met de bouw van deze wijk is een deel van het Stadionplein hernoemd tot Laan der Hesperiden.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Due to the construction of this district, part of Stadionplein has been renamed Laan der Hesperiden.

facts.text: Architect Berlage did not design this square despite common belief.
facts.sourceQuote: In tegenstelling tot wat vaak wordt gedacht, heeft Berlage zelf dit gedeelte niet ontworpen; dit heeft te maken met de komst van de Olympische Spelen.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Contrary to what is often thought, Berlage himself did not design this part; this has to do with the coming of the Olympic Games.

facts.text: Two Febo snack bars stood in former ticket offices from 1971 until 2013.
facts.sourceQuote: Midden op het plein waren van 1971 tot 2013 een tweetal filialen van Febo gevestigd in een tweetal voormalige kaartverkoophuisjes van het Olympisch Stadion. Door de herontwikkeling van het plein moesten ze na 42 jaar verdwijnen.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In the middle of the square, from 1971 to 2013, two branches of Febo were located in two former ticket offices of the Olympic Stadium. Due to the redevelopment of the square, they had to disappear after 42 years.

features.name: Bos en Lommerweg
features.opening: The Bos en Lommerweg is a street in Amsterdam-West.

facts.text: The New Kit apartment complex has stood at the end of the road since 2012.
facts.sourceQuote: Aan het eind van de weg staat sinds 2012 het appartementencomplex New Kit.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: At the end of the road stands the New Kit apartment complex since 2012.

facts.text: A Wednesday and Saturday market operated on a side street here until the municipality abolished it in November 2023.
facts.sourceQuote: Ter vervanging van de markt op het Gulden Winckelplantsoen / Bos en Lommerplein was er van 2021 tot 2023 op woensdag en zaterdag een markt op de ventweg aan de noordkant tussen het Bos en Lommerplein en de Egidiusstraat. Omdat de markt steeds slechter functioneerde, besloot de gemeente de markt op te heffen per 1 november 2023.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In place of the market on the Gulden Winckelplantsoen / Bos en Lommerplein, there was a market on the ventweg on the north side between the Bos en Lommerplein and the Egidiusstraat on Wednesdays and Saturdays from 2021 to 2023. Because the market was functioning increasingly poorly, the municipality decided to abolish the market as of November 1, 2023.

facts.text: A local building known as Theelichtje since 2005 is now called Podium Mozaïek.
facts.sourceQuote: Boeyinga, beter bekend als het 'Theelichtje' (sinds 2005 'Podium Mozaïek') en de Opstandingskerk van M.F.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Boeyinga, better known as the 'Theelichtje' (since 2005 'Podium Mozaïek') and the Resurrection Church of M.F.

features.name: Linnaeusstraat
features.opening: The Linnaeusstraat in Amsterdam-Oost runs between the Mauritskade and the Ringdijk, located around the Watergraafsmeer.

facts.text: A storm surge in March 1651 nearly washed away the village of Oetewaal that once stood nearby.
facts.sourceQuote: In maart 1651 werd Oetewaal bij een stormvloed bijkans weggevaagd.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In March 1651, Oetewaal was almost washed away by a storm surge.

facts.text: Film director Theo van Gogh was murdered near the district office on this street in November 2004.
facts.sourceQuote: Op 2 november 2004 werd filmregisseur Theo van Gogh ter hoogte van het toenmalige stadsdeelkantoor Oost/Watergraafsmeer aan de Linnaeusstraat vermoord.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: On November 2, 2004, film director Theo van Gogh was murdered near the then-Oost/Watergraafsmeer district office on the Linnaeusstraat.

facts.text: Carl Linnaeus, the namesake of this Amsterdam avenue, lived from 1707 to 1778.
facts.sourceQuote: De Linnaeusstraat is in 1878 vernoemd naar de beroemde natuuronderzoeker Carl Linnaeus (1707–1778).
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Linnaeusstraat was named in 1878 after the famous natural scientist Carl Linnaeus (1707–1778).

features.name: Ookmeerweg
features.opening: The Ookmeerweg is a continuous road in Amsterdam-Nieuw-West.

facts.text: The Ookmeerweg takes its name from the Ookmeer drainage works, now the site of Sportpark Ookmeer.
facts.sourceQuote: De weg is vernoemd naar het Ookmeer, een droogmakerij ten oosten van de oude buurtschap Osdorp, op (ongeveer) de plek van het huidige Sportpark Ookmeer.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The road is named after the Ookmeer, a drainage works east of the old village of Osdorp, on (approximately) the site of the current Sportpark Ookmeer.

facts.text: A massive Theo Jansen artwork titled Animaris rhinoceros transport hangs suspended before a local business park.
facts.sourceQuote: Voor dat laatste bedrijvenpark staat het massieve kunstwerk Animaris rhinoceros transport van Theo Jansen gekooid opgesteld.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In front of that last business park is the massive artwork Animaris rhinoceros transport by Theo Jansen suspended on display.

features.name: Sint Antoniesbreestraat
features.opening: The Sint Antoniesbreestraat ("St. Anthony's Broad Street") is a street in the centre of Amsterdam in the Netherlands.

facts.text: Originally a medieval dike called Sint Antoniesdijk, it protected the city from flooding before becoming a street.
facts.sourceQuote: The street was originally a dike, the Sint Antoniesdijk, constructed during the Middle Ages. It protected the city and its surroundings from flooding.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The street was originally a dike, the Sint Antoniesdijk, constructed during the Middle Ages. It protected the city and its surroundings from flooding.

facts.text: Rembrandt lived here from 1631 to 1635 at the home of art dealer Hendrick van Uylenburgh.
facts.sourceQuote: In the early 17th century, the street was popular with immigrants and artists such as the painter Rembrandt, who lived there from 1631 to 1635, at the home of art dealer Hendrick van Uylenburgh. (From 1639 to 1656 he lived in his own home, now the Rembrandt House Museum.) Other painters who lived in the street, near the Guild of Saint Luke in the former Sint Anthoniespoort, include Pieter Isaacsz, Esaias Boursse, who lived next door to Rembrandt, Nicolaes Eliaszoon Pickenoy, Cornelis van der Voort, Roelant Savery, Pieter Lastman (in whose workshop Rembrandt served as apprentice), Adriaen van Nieulandt, Pieter Codde, Willem Kick, Justus and Johannes Vingboons, and their father David Vinckboons.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In the early 17th century, the street was popular with immigrants and artists such as the painter Rembrandt, who lived there from 1631 to 1635, at the home of art dealer Hendrick van Uylenburgh. (From 1639 to 1656 he lived in his own home, now the Rembrandt House Museum.) Other painters who lived in the street, near the Guild of Saint Luke in the former Sint Anthoniespoort, include Pieter Isaacsz, Esaias Boursse, who lived next door to Rembrandt, Nicolaes Eliaszoon Pickenoy, Cornelis van der Voort, Roelant Savery, Pieter Lastman (in whose workshop Rembrandt served as apprentice), Adriaen van Nieulandt, Pieter Codde, Willem Kick, Justus and Johannes Vingboons, and their father David Vinckboons.

facts.text: Sint Antoniesbreestraat translates to "St. Anthony's Broad Street".
facts.sourceQuote: The Sint Antoniesbreestraat ("St. Anthony's Broad Street") is a street in the centre of Amsterdam in the Netherlands.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Sint Antoniesbreestraat ("St. Anthony's Broad Street") is a street in the centre of Amsterdam in the Netherlands.

features.name: Frederiksstraat
features.opening: The Frederiksstraat is a relatively short street in Amsterdam Oud-West.

facts.text: Amsterdam annexed the area in 1896 but allowed the name to remain since no other Frederiksstraat existed.
facts.sourceQuote: In 1896 annexeerde de gemeente Amsterdam dit gebied. Aangezien Amsterdam nog geen Frederiksstraat had, mocht de straat haar naam behouden.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 1896, the municipality of Amsterdam annexed this area. Since Amsterdam did not yet have a Frederiksstraat, the street was allowed to retain its name.

facts.text: For a time, this street served as a reference point for defining the boundary of Zocherstraat.
facts.sourceQuote: De straat diende enige tijd als aanduiding van de Zocherstraat. Bij de rooilijnbepaling voor die straat werd die straat aangeduid als de "zijstraat van de Overtoom ten westen van de Frederiksstraat".
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The street served as an indication of the Zocherstraat for a while. When determining the boundary line for that street, that street was designated as the "side street of the Overtoom west of the Frederiksstraat".

facts.text: Revolutionary construction methods created a striking uniformity across almost all buildings on the street.
facts.sourceQuote: Er kwam hier revolutiebouw, waardoor alle panden grote gelijkenis vertonen.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: There was revolutionary construction here, which caused all the buildings to have great similarity.

facts.text: The largest building at this address is actually located on an internal site behind structures on the opposite side.
facts.sourceQuote: Het grootste gebouw met het adres Frederiksstraat staat niet aan de straat zelf; het ligt achter de bebouwing aan de even zijde op een binnenterrein. Het is gebouw Frederiksstraat 18a.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The largest building with the address Frederiksstraat is not on the street itself; it is located behind the buildings on the opposite side on an internal site. It is building Frederiksstraat 18a.

features.name: Meerkerkdreef
features.opening: The Meerkerkdreef is a dreef in the Gaasperdam district in Amsterdam-Zuidoost.

facts.text: The first section opened in 1977, replacing the closed Rijksstraatweg.
facts.sourceQuote: Het eerste gedeelte, uitsluitend voor snelverkeer, werd geopend in 1977 en ligt in het verlengde van de Huntumdreef en loopt zuidwaarts, na passage boven de Gaasperdammertunnel met Brasapark. Samen met de Huntumdreef en Holendrechtdreef verving de weg op dat gedeelte de toen gesloten Rijksstraatweg.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The first section, exclusively for fast traffic, was opened in 1977 and runs along the Huntumdreef and southwards, after passing above the Gaasperdammertunnel with Brasapark. Together with the Huntumdreef and Holendrechtdreef, the road replaced the then closed Rijksstraatweg on that section.

facts.text: A planned extension to Veenendaaldreef was never built due to a cancelled project.
facts.sourceQuote: Oorspronkelijk zou de Meerkerkdreef hier eindigen en overgaan in de Veenendaaldreef. Door het niet doorgaan van de verlenging van de Gooiseweg zuidwaarts van de Gaasperdammerweg is de Veenendaaldreef echter nooit gerealiseerd.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Originally, the Meerkerkdreef was supposed to end here and transition into the Veenendaaldreef. However, because the extension of the Gooiseweg southwards from the Gaasperdammerweg was not carried out, the Veenendaaldreef was never realized.

features.name: Ringweg-West
features.opening: The Second Coen Tunnel is a tunnel under the North Sea Canal, next to the Coen Tunnel in Amsterdam.

facts.text: Two lanes reverse direction based on whether morning or evening traffic is heaviest.
facts.sourceQuote: The tunnel consists of three fixed lanes and two reversible lanes, which are opened in the direction where traffic is the heaviest.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The tunnel consists of three fixed lanes and two reversible lanes, which are opened in the direction where traffic is the heaviest.

facts.text: Construction began in September 2009 and the tunnel opened in July 2014.
facts.sourceQuote: Total costs of the project are estimated at 1.2 billion euros and construction started on September 7, 2009. The tunnel was officially opened on July 21, 2014.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Total costs of the project are estimated at 1.2 billion euros and construction started on September 7, 2009. The tunnel was officially opened on July 21, 2014.

facts.text: A consortium including French group Vinci Concessions built the project under a public-private partnership.
facts.sourceQuote: The Second Coen Tunnel was procured under a public-private partnership model under a DBFM structure (design, build, finance, and maintain). The project was awarded to a consortium consisting of French group Vinci Concessions, CFE, Dredging International, Besix, Dura Vermeer, TBI Bouwgroep and Arcadis.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Second Coen Tunnel was procured under a public-private partnership model under a DBFM structure (design, build, finance, and maintain). The project was awarded to a consortium consisting of French group Vinci Concessions, CFE, Dredging International, Besix, Dura Vermeer, TBI Bouwgroep and Arcadis.

features.name: Nieuwe Leeuwarderweg
features.opening: The Nieuwe Leeuwarderweg is a motorway that lies partly parallel to the North Holland Canal in Amsterdam-Noord.

facts.text: Only five house numbers exist along this major thoroughfare, including a former gas station.
facts.sourceQuote: Hisgenpad brug 2109 en brug 2112 bij kruispunt IJdoornlaan brug 2246 over een gracht kruispunt Rijksweg 10 brug 1714 over de weg Buikslotermeerdijk Slochterbrug, brug 45P (provinciale brug) De Nieuwe Leeuwarderweg kent slechts vijf huisnummers: 15 (Cultureel centrum De tanker in voormalig benzinestation), 16 (café De gele pomp, een voormalige benzinestation tegenover De tanker), 25 (P+R), 26 (onbestemd gebouwtje bij kruising IJdoornlaan) en 30 (Aannemingsbedrijf).
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Hisgenpad bridge 2109 and bridge 2112 at the intersection of IJdoornlaan bridge 2246 over a canal intersection of Rijksweg 10 bridge 1714 over the road Buikslotermeerdijk Slochterbrug, bridge 45P (provincial bridge) The Nieuwe Leeuwarderweg has only five house numbers: 15 (Cultural center De tanker in former gas station), 16 (café De gele pomp, a former gas station opposite De tanker), 25 (P+R), 26 (unspecified building at the intersection of IJdoornlaan) and 30 (Construction company).

features.name: Noordzeeweg
features.opening: The Noordzeeweg is a connecting road in Amsterdam Westpoort and connects the Basisweg at the T-intersection with the Hornweg with the Westpoortweg and Luvernes.

facts.text: The council named Noordzeeweg (North Sea Road) after the North Sea in April 1978.
facts.sourceQuote: De weg is bij een raadsbesluit van 26 april 1978 vernoemd naar de Noordzee.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The road was named after the North Sea by a council decision of April 26, 1978.

facts.text: A railway viaduct was constructed on this road around 1980.
facts.sourceQuote: Over de weg kwam rond 1980 een viaduct ten behoeve van de Nederlandse Spoorwegen.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Around 1980, a viaduct was built on the road for the Dutch Railways.

features.name: Molukkenstraat
features.opening: The Molukkenstraat is a street in the Indian Quarter in Amsterdam-Oost.

facts.text: After its final definition, the street measures approximately one kilometer.
facts.sourceQuote: Na die laatste definiëring is zij ongeveer een kilometer lang.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: After that last definition, it is about one kilometer long.

facts.text: Large-scale redevelopment transformed the Indian Quarter including this street during the 1980s.
facts.sourceQuote: In de jaren tachtig van de 20e eeuw vond er grootscheepse sanering plaats in de Indische Buurt, waaronder de Molukkenstraat.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In the 1980s of the 20th century, large-scale redevelopment took place in the Indian Quarter, including the Molukkenstraat.

facts.text: Since 1932, the street has extended past Valentijnkade via a bridge over the Ringvaart.
facts.sourceQuote: Aan de zuidzijde loopt de Molukkenstraat sinds 1932 voorbij de Valentijnkade (haar oorspronkelijk eind) door met een brug over de Ringvaart, en sinds 1939 (na het gereedkomen van de Spoorwegwerken Oost) tot onder het spoorwegviaduct door, waar de straat uitkomt op de Archimedesweg in de wijk Watergraafsmeer.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: On the south side, the Molukkenstraat has been running past Valentijnkade (its original end) since 1932 through with a bridge over the Ringvaart, and since 1939 (after the completion of the Spoorwegwerken Oost) under the railway viaduct, where the street leads to Archimedesweg in the Watergraafsmeer district.

features.name: Van Diemenstraat
features.opening: The Van Diemenstraat is a street in the Zeeheldenbuurt of Amsterdam-Centrum.

facts.text: A railway line once ran through the street to serve grain wagons loading at a nearby warehouse.
facts.sourceQuote: Voorheen liep ook een spoorlijn door de straat, vanaf de Westerdoksdijk tot aan de brug, voor de spoorwagons die bij het veempakhuis geladen en gelost werden.
