facts.sourceQuote: Hoofdwatergangen worden daarom vaak door een waterschap onderhouden, dat wil dus zoveel zeggen als dat het op afmetingen wordt gehouden door ze regelmatig te schonen (maaien van gras en riet) en te baggeren.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Main water channels are therefore often maintained by a water board, which means that they are kept within dimensions by regularly cleaning them (cutting grass and reeds) and dredging them.

features.name: Seranggracht
features.opening: The Serangracht is a canal with associated embankments in Amsterdam-Oost, classified under the Indian Quarter.

facts.text: The canal was excavated in the late 1990s after the island of Java shifted from a shipyard to housing.
facts.sourceQuote: De gracht werd eind jaren negentig gegraven op het Java-eiland dat toen werd omgebouwd van aanlegplaats voor schepen tot woongebied.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The canal was dug in the late 1990s on the island of Java, which was then converted from a shipbuilding yard to a residential area.

facts.text: Odd-numbered houses stop at number 19, even though the full range of house numbers extends to 58.
facts.sourceQuote: De huisnummers lopen op van 1 tot en met 58, terwijl de oneven huisnummers ophouden bij 19.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The house numbers run from 1 to 58, while the odd house numbers stop at 19.

features.name: Smallepadsgracht
features.opening: The Smallepadsgracht (Narrow path canal in Dutch) is a short and narrow canal in the Amsterdam-Centrum district of Amsterdam.

facts.text: Unusually, no bridges cross this canal and no quay runs along its banks.
facts.sourceQuote: Unusually, there are no bridges over this canal, nor is there a quay that runs along the canal.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Unusually, there are no bridges over this canal, nor is there a quay that runs along the canal.

features.name: Brantasgracht
features.opening: The Brantasgracht is a canal with associated embankments in Amsterdam-Oost, classified under the Indian Quarter.

facts.text: The name Brantasgracht honors the Indonesian river Brantas on Java.
facts.sourceQuote: De gracht kreeg al op 23 maart 1994 haar naam (op de tekentafel), een vernoeming naar de Indonesische rivier Brantas op Java.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The canal already received its name (on the drawing board) on March 23, 1994, a name derived from the Indonesian river Brantas on Java.

facts.text: Sjoerd Soeters designed the entire neighborhood surrounding this canal.
facts.sourceQuote: De inrichting van de gehele wijk was in handen van Sjoerd Soeters.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The design of the entire neighborhood was in the hands of Sjoerd Soeters.

facts.text: House numbers run from one to twenty-one, yet number twenty is completely missing.
facts.sourceQuote: De huisnummers lopen op van 1 tot en met 21, terwijl huisnummer 20 ontbreekt (gegevens juli 2019).
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The house numbers run from 1 to 21, while house number 20 is missing (data July 2019).

facts.text: The corner complex at Brantasgracht three to five was designed by the firm Cruz y Ortiz.
facts.sourceQuote: Een van die complexen (Brantasgracht 3-5/hoek Sumatrakade) is ontworpen door Cruz y Ortiz.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: One of those complexes (Brantasgracht 3-5/corner Sumatrakade) was designed by Cruz y Ortiz.

features.name: Nieuwe Meersluis
features.opening: The Nieuwe Meersluis, also known as Schinkelsluis, is a sluice gate in the Dutch municipality of Amsterdam.

facts.text: The current lock opened on July 1, 1942 to replace the older Overtoomse Sluis.
facts.sourceQuote: De huidige Nieuwe Meersluis werd op 1 juli 1942 in gebruik genomen ter vervanging van de Overtoomse Sluis.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The current Nieuwe Meersluis was put into use on July 1, 1942 to replace the Overtoomse Sluis.

facts.text: A new control center was later built directly halfway over the old lock keeper's post.
facts.sourceQuote: Eind 20e eeuw was er een nieuwe bedieningscentrale nodig; deze werd half over de oude sluiswachterpost heen gebouwd.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: At the end of the 20th century, a new control center was needed; this was built halfway over the old lock keeper's post.

facts.text: Sliding sluice doors on rails also serve as the carriers for bridge decks.
facts.sourceQuote: De sluisdeuren zijn schuifdeuren op rails, de sluisdeuren zijn tevens de dragers van brugdekken.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The sluice doors are sliding doors on rails, the sluice doors are also the carriers of bridge decks.

features.name: Gein
features.opening: Gein is a residential area in Amsterdam-Zuidoost in the Gaasperdam district.

facts.text: The district takes its name from the Gein river that flows just to its east.
facts.sourceQuote: De naam van de wijk is ontleend aan het ten oosten van de wijk lopende riviertje Gein.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The name of the district is derived from the Gein river running east of the district.

facts.text: Gaasperpark was built for the 1982 Floriade before being simplified into a city park.
facts.sourceQuote: Het nabijgelegen Gaasperpark werd aangelegd tussen 1977 en 1982 voor de in dat laatste jaar gehouden Floriade. Na afloop van de Floriade werden bijna alle toevoegingen verwijderd, zodat een eenvoudiger stadspark overbleef.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The nearby Gaasperpark was built between 1977 and 1982 for the Floriade held in that last year. After the end of the Floriade, almost all additions were removed, leaving behind a simpler city park.

facts.text: Low-rise housing in Gein III and IV was created by former alderman Jan Schaefer.
facts.sourceQuote: In Gein III (ook wel Gein3dorp genoemd) en Gein IV bevindt zich vrijwel uitsluitend laagbouw die tot stand kwam door toedoen van de vroegere wethouder Jan Schaefer.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In Gein III (also known as Gein3dorp) and Gein IV, there is almost exclusively low-rise housing that was created by the former alderman Jan Schaefer.

features.name: Schippersgracht
features.opening: The Schippersgracht (Dutch pronunciation: [ˈsxɪpərsˌxrɑxt]) is a canal and street in the Centrum district of Amsterdam that runs from the Rapenburgerplein to…

facts.text: Drinking water installation began here in April 1854.
facts.sourceQuote: In April 1854 the Amsterdamsche Duinwater-Maatschappij started installation of drinking water on the Schippersgracht.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In April 1854 the Amsterdamsche Duinwater-Maatschappij started installation of drinking water on the Schippersgracht.

facts.text: Tram line 2 ended at this canal around 1906 before being cut short.
facts.sourceQuote: Around 1906 the end of tram line 2 was on the Schippersgracht. This was canceled after six months and shortened to Central Station.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Around 1906 the end of tram line 2 was on the Schippersgracht. This was canceled after six months and shortened to Central Station.

facts.text: Architect Herman Hendrik Baanders designed number 5 in 1897.
facts.sourceQuote: The Amsterdam architect Herman Hendrik Baanders (1849–1905) designed Schippersgracht 5 (1897).
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Amsterdam architect Herman Hendrik Baanders (1849–1905) designed Schippersgracht 5 (1897).

facts.text: Monumental buildings from the seventeenth century stand at numbers 14 and 15.
facts.sourceQuote: There are a number of monumental buildings from the 17th century on Schippersgracht, including numbers 14 and 15.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: There are a number of monumental buildings from the 17th century on Schippersgracht, including numbers 14 and 15.

features.name: Schellingwouderbreek
features.opening: The Schellingwouderbreek is a lake in Amsterdam-North.

facts.text: A plaque with a bursting 'IJ' was placed in 2020 to highlight the crack's formation history.
facts.sourceQuote: In 2020 hebben de 'Vrienden van het Schellingwouderbreekpark' aan de kant van de Volendammerweg een gedenkplaat met een barstend 'IJ' geplaatst om te attenderen op de ontstaansgeschiedenis van de breek.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 2020, the 'Friends of the Schellingwouderbreekpark' on the side of the Volendammerweg placed a plaque with a bursting 'IJ' to draw attention to the history of the formation of the crack.

facts.text: Two small islands on the north side connect to each other and the mainland via a path.
facts.sourceQuote: In de waterpartij bevinden zich aan de noordzijde een tweetal eilandjes die onderling en met de vaste wal zijn verbonden met een pad.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: On the north side of the water area there are two small islands connected to each other and to the mainland by a path.

features.name: Mercuriushaven
features.opening: The Mercuriushaven is a port in the Amsterdam port area.

facts.text: Mercuriushaven honors Mercury, the god and personification of trade.
facts.sourceQuote: De Mercuriushaven is gegraven in het laatste deel van de 19e eeuw en is genoemd naar Mercurius als god/personificatie van de handel.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Mercuriushaven was dug in the latter part of the 19th century and is named after Mercury as god/personification of trade.

facts.text: After tropical hardwood imports fell in the late 1970s, the port shifted to shipping cocoa, food, and fertilizer.
facts.sourceQuote: Maar toen de import van tropisch hardhout eind jaren-1970 terugliep, werd overgeschakeld naar andere producten. Er wordt nu vooral cacao, voedsel en kunstmest verscheept.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: But when the import of tropical hardwood declined in the late 1970s, it was switched to other products. Cocoa, food and fertilizer are now mainly shipped.

features.name: Houthaven
features.opening: Houthaven is a neighbourhood of Amsterdam, Netherlands situated in the West borough.

facts.text: Houthaven was the first Amsterdam port dug from scratch, unlike earlier ones using existing waters.
facts.sourceQuote: It was the first port in Amsterdam to be dug out (the earlier ones using existing waters).
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: It was the first port in Amsterdam to be dug out (the earlier ones using existing waters).

facts.text: Parts of Houthaven were filled with sand in 1945 as lumber transport shifted to road vehicles.
facts.sourceQuote: As lumber was increasingly transported by road, parts of the port were filled up with sand to be used for other purposes in 1945.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: As lumber was increasingly transported by road, parts of the port were filled up with sand to be used for other purposes in 1945.

facts.text: The name Houthaven literally translates to 'lumber port'.
facts.sourceQuote: Literally meaning "lumber port", Houthaven is a port situated along the IJ in Amsterdam's western port.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Literally meaning "lumber port", Houthaven is a port situated along the IJ in Amsterdam's western port.

facts.text: The harbour consists of four distinct parts arranged from east to west.
facts.sourceQuote: The harbour is made up out of four parts (from east to west): Oude Houthaven (Old Lumber Port), Houthaven, Nieuwe Houthaven (New Lumber Port) and Minervahaven (Minerva Port).
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The harbour is made up out of four parts (from east to west): Oude Houthaven (Old Lumber Port), Houthaven, Nieuwe Houthaven (New Lumber Port) and Minervahaven (Minerva Port).

features.name: Stadiongracht
features.opening: The Stadiongracht is a canal in Amsterdam-Zuid; dug around 1928.

facts.text: The northern section now runs dry because it lost its direct water connection to the Noorder Amstel Canal.
facts.sourceQuote: Er is geen rechtstreekse waterverbinding meer met het Noorder Amstelkanaal, zodat het noordelijk deel van de Stadiongracht doodloopt op de Amstelveenseweg.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: There is no direct water connection anymore with the Noorder Amstel Canal, so the northern part of the Stadiongracht runs dry on the Amstelveenseweg.

facts.text: A small lock exists here but no longer functions as one since water levels are identical on both sides.
facts.sourceQuote: Er is daarnaast een kleine sluis aanwezig, die niet meer als zodanig dienstdoet omdat het waterpeil aan beide kanten even hoog is.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: There is also a small lock present, which no longer serves as such because the water level is the same on both sides.

facts.text: The canal's name does not appear in postal codes, while its quays carry distinct names like Afroditekade.
facts.sourceQuote: In postcodegidsen ontbreekt de naam; de kades van de gracht hebben een andere naam, waaronder de Afroditekade.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The name is missing in postal codes; the quays of the canal have a different name, including the Afroditekade.

features.name: Nieuwe Prinsengracht
features.opening: The Nieuwe Prinsengracht is a canal in the Plantage neighborhood of Amsterdam, an extension of the Prinsengracht in the eastern Grachtengordel (canal belt).

facts.text: Until 1866, the canal extended east of the Muidergracht all the way to the Entrepotdok.
facts.sourceQuote: Until 1866 the Nieuwe Prinsengracht ran east of the Muidergracht to the Entrepotdok.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Until 1866 the Nieuwe Prinsengracht ran east of the Muidergracht to the Entrepotdok.

facts.text: Three ponds within the Artis zoo site remain from the section of this canal that was later filled in.
facts.sourceQuote: The three ponds within the Artis zoo site still remain from the filled-in section of the canal.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The three ponds within the Artis zoo site still remain from the filled-in section of the canal.

facts.text: A plate bridge built in 1924 crosses the water at Roetersstraat.
facts.sourceQuote: 258, a so-called plate bridge from 1924) spans the Nieuwe Prinsengracht at the Roetersstraat.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: 258, a so-called plate bridge from 1924) spans the Nieuwe Prinsengracht at the Roetersstraat.

features.name: Oostelijk Marktkanaal
features.opening: The Oostelijk Marktkanaal is a canal in Amsterdam-West.

facts.text: The canal opened in 1934 specifically to supply the Central Market Halls.
facts.sourceQuote: Het kanaal is in 1934 in gebruik genomen voor de ontsluiting en bevoorrading van de Centrale Markthallen.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The canal was put into use in 1934 for the opening and supply of the Central Market Halls.

features.name: Smal Weesp
features.opening: Smal Weesp is a channeled stream between the Vecht River and the Amsterdam-Rhine Canal.

facts.text: Canal construction later cut off the Driemond section of Smal Weesp, causing it to visually disappear.
facts.sourceQuote: Sinds de aanleg van het Amsterdam-Rijnkanaal is het deel van het Smal Weesp dat in Driemond ligt er als het ware afgehakt. En toen door de verbreding van dit kanaal het Driemondse deel werd omgelegd ten behoeve van de aanleg van een sluis, ging de verbinding ook visueel verloren.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Since the construction of the Amsterdam-Rhine Canal, the part of the Smal Weesp that is located in Driemond has been cut off as it were. And then, due to the widening of this channel, the Three-Months section was diverted for the construction of a lock, and the connection also visually disappeared.

features.name: Hans Snoekfontein
features.opening: The Hans Snoekfontein is a work of art in Amsterdam-Centrum.

facts.text: The fountain honors Hans Snoek, founder of the Scapino Ballet, who funded its creation via a legacy.
facts.sourceQuote: De fontein is vernoemd naar Hans Snoek, oprichtster van het Scapino Ballet, die via een legaat financieel bijdroeg aan de bouw van de fontein en het opknappen van het plein.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The fountain is named after Hans Snoek, founder of the Scapino Ballet, who financially contributed to the construction of the fountain and the renovation of the square through a legacy.

features.name: Betonsluis
features.opening: Sluis 124, also known as the Concrete Lock, is a sluice lock in the IJburg district of Amsterdam.

facts.text: Betonsluis earned its concrete lock nickname from its pioneering concrete doors, a first in the Netherlands.
facts.sourceQuote: De bijnaam "betonnen sluis" kreeg dit bouwwerk vanwege de betonnen sluisdeuren; dit was een primeur in Nederland.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: This building was nicknamed "concrete lock" because of its concrete lock doors; this was a first in the Netherlands.

facts.text: The flat bridge is firmly mounted on both lock sides, blocking high boats from passing underneath.
facts.sourceQuote: De brug is vlak en vast gemonteerd op de beide kades van de sluis; Hoge boten kunnen daardoor niet onder de brug door.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The bridge is flat and firmly mounted on both sides of the lock; high boats cannot therefore pass under the bridge.

features.name: Afrikahaven
features.opening: The Afrikahaven is a port in the Amsterdam port area.

facts.text: A mammoth molar tooth fragment found here is the oldest discovery in the area.
facts.sourceQuote: In 2001 werd een fragment van een mammoetslagtand gevonden in dit gebied en is daarmee de oudste vondst in dit gebied.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 2001, a fragment of a mammoth molar tooth was found in this area and is therefore the oldest find in this area.

facts.text: Construction of this port took place between 1997 and 2001.
facts.sourceQuote: De haven werd gegraven in 1997-2001 en ligt aan de zuidkant van het Noordzeekanaal, in de Houtrakpolder, ten westen van het vroegere Zijkanaal F.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The port was dug in 1997-2001 and is located on the south side of the North Sea Canal, in the Houtrakpolder, west of the former Zijkanaal F.

facts.text: The harbor sits within the Houtrakpolder area west of former Zijkanaal F.
facts.sourceQuote: De haven werd gegraven in 1997-2001 en ligt aan de zuidkant van het Noordzeekanaal, in de Houtrakpolder, ten westen van het vroegere Zijkanaal F.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The port was dug in 1997-2001 and is located on the south side of the North Sea Canal, in the Houtrakpolder, west of the former Zijkanaal F.

features.name: Keizersgracht
features.opening: The Keizersgracht (Dutch pronunciation: [ˈkɛizərsˌxrɑxt]; "Emperor's canal") is a canal in Amsterdam, the Netherlands.

facts.text: Mayor Frans Hendricksz Oetgens and surveyor Lucas Jansz Sinck initiated its first section in 1615.
facts.sourceQuote: The first part of the Keizersgracht, between Brouwersgracht and (approximately) the current Leidsegracht, was dug in the summer of 1615 at the initiative of mayor Frans Hendricksz Oetgens, city carpenter Hendrick Jacobsz Staets and city surveyor Lucas Jansz Sinck.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The first part of the Keizersgracht, between Brouwersgracht and (approximately) the current Leidsegracht, was dug in the summer of 1615 at the initiative of mayor Frans Hendricksz Oetgens, city carpenter Hendrick Jacobsz Staets and city surveyor Lucas Jansz Sinck.

facts.text: City planners briefly considered turning this waterway into a dry boulevard like The Hague's Lange Voorhout.
facts.sourceQuote: In September 1614 there arose an intention to turn the Keizersgracht into a chic boulevard without water, following the example of Lange Voorhout in The Hague.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In September 1614 there arose an intention to turn the Keizersgracht into a chic boulevard without water, following the example of Lange Voorhout in The Hague.

facts.text: The first Italian opera was performed on the site in 1680 by Dirck Strijcker.
facts.sourceQuote: The first Italian opera was performed on the site in 1680 by Dirck Strijcker.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The first Italian opera was performed on the site in 1680 by Dirck Strijcker.

facts.text: Hendrik Carloff and Jan Valckenburgh, residents of the canal, were both involved in the slave trade between the Gold Coast and South America.
facts.sourceQuote: 71, 73, and 127: Cornelis Trip 111 and 113: Hendrik Carloff and Jan Valckenburgh. They were both involved in the slave trade between the Gold Coast and South America.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: 71, 73, and 127: Cornelis Trip 111 and 113: Hendrik Carloff and Jan Valckenburgh. They were both involved in the slave trade between the Gold Coast and South America.

features.name: Bijleveldschesluis
features.opening: The Bijleveldschesluis (bridge 495) is a structural work of art in Amsterdam-Centrum.

facts.text: The name Bijleveldschesluis honors the Bijleveld Water Board, which once held land east of the city.
facts.sourceQuote: De naam voert terug op het Waterschap Bijleveld dat toen terreinen had ten oosten van de stad.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The name refers to the Bijleveld Water Board, which at that time had land east of the city.

facts.text: Amsterdam took over management of this lock in July 1492 after it had been run by the Bijleveld board.
facts.sourceQuote: De sluis onder de Sint-Anthoniespoort (Waag) viel aanvankelijk onder het beheer van Bijleveld, maar ging in juli 1492 over naar Amsterdam.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The lock under the Sint-Anthoniespoort (Waag) initially fell under the management of Bijleveld, but was transferred to Amsterdam in July 1492.

features.name: Da Costagracht
features.opening: The Da Costagracht is a canal in Amsterdam-West.

facts.text: German occupiers forced a street name change on August 14, 1942, targeting names of Jews and royalty.
facts.sourceQuote: Op 14 augustus 1942 werd, op aandrang van de Duitse bezetters, bij besluit van burgemeester Edward Voûte een aantal Amsterdamse straatnamen veranderd. Het ging om straten die naar het Nederlandse koningshuis of naar Joden genoemd waren.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: On August 14, 1942, at the urging of the German occupiers, a number of Amsterdam street names were changed by decision of Mayor Edward Voûte. It was about streets that were named after the Dutch royal family or after Jews.

facts.text: Four bridges span the water at De Clercqstraat, Potgieterstraat, Kinkerstraat, and Jacob van Lennepstraat.
facts.sourceQuote: De gracht wordt overspannen/gekruist door vier bruggen/straten: De Clercqstraat (brug 108) Potgieterstraat (brug 138) Kinkerstraat (brug 183) Jacob van Lennepstraat (brug 180).
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The canal is spanned/crossed by four bridges/streets: De Clercqstraat (bridge 108) Potgieterstraat (bridge 138) Kinkerstraat (bridge 183) Jacob van Lennepstraat (bridge 180).

features.name: Bloemgracht
features.opening: The Bloemgracht (Dutch pronunciation: [ˈblumˌɣrɑxt]) is a canal in the Jordaan district of Amsterdam, the Netherlands.

facts.text: Cartographer Willem Blaeu established his workshop here in 1635, producing the famous Atlas Maior.
facts.sourceQuote: Willem Blaeu started his cartography workshop here in 1635, and it was continued by his son Joan Blaeu and his grandson Joan Junior until 1698. The Atlas Maior or Grooten Atlas by Blaeu was made on the Bloemgracht.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Willem Blaeu started his cartography workshop here in 1635, and it was continued by his son Joan Blaeu and his grandson Joan Junior until 1698. The Atlas Maior or Grooten Atlas by Blaeu was made on the Bloemgracht.

facts.text: Fourteen sugar factories operated along this canal during the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries.
facts.sourceQuote: Fourteen sugar factories were active on the canal in the 18th and 19th century.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Fourteen sugar factories were active on the canal in the 18th and 19th century.

facts.text: Bridge number 120 at Derde Leliedwarsstraat bears the name Atlas Bridge.
facts.sourceQuote: Bridge no. 120 across the Bloemgracht at the corner of the Derde Leliedwarsstraat was given the name Atlas Bridge.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Bridge no. 120 across the Bloemgracht at the corner of the Derde Leliedwarsstraat was given the name Atlas Bridge.

facts.text: The trio known as De Drie Hendricken at numbers 87, 89 and 91 was built in 1642.
facts.sourceQuote: Bloemgracht 87, 89 and 91, also called "De Drie Hendricken", with their typical stepped gables and frequent use of glass, were built in 1642.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Bloemgracht 87, 89 and 91, also called "De Drie Hendricken", with their typical stepped gables and frequent use of glass, were built in 1642.

features.name: Lauriergracht
features.opening: The Lauriergracht (Dutch pronunciation: [lʌuˈriːrˌɣrɑxt]; literally "Laurel Canal") is one of the canals of Amsterdam, located in the Jordaan, west of the…

facts.text: Painter George Hendrik Breitner ran a studio at number 8 from 1893 to 1898.
facts.sourceQuote: It was painted and photographed by George Hendrik Breitner who set up a studio on the canal, at number 8, in 1893 and stayed there until 1898.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: It was painted and photographed by George Hendrik Breitner who set up a studio on the canal, at number 8, in 1893 and stayed there until 1898.

facts.text: Fictional coffee broker Batavus Droogstoppel famously claimed to live at number 37 in Max Havelaar.
facts.sourceQuote: One of the famous residents of the Lauriergracht is the fictional Batavus Droogstoppel, the unreliable narrator in Max Havelaar who is introduced in the first line of the book "Ik ben makelaar in koffie, en woon op de Lauriergracht nº 37". ("I am a coffee broker and I live at Number 37 Lauriergracht") which the character repeats over and over. In Dutch literature the address Lauriergracht 37 is as well known as James Joyce's 7 Eccles Street; in reality, it was an alley in the time of the author Dekker.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: One of the famous residents of the Lauriergracht is the fictional Batavus Droogstoppel, the unreliable narrator in Max Havelaar who is introduced in the first line of the book "Ik ben makelaar in koffie, en woon op de Lauriergracht nº 37". ("I am a coffee broker and I live at Number 37 Lauriergracht") which the character repeats over and over. In Dutch literature the address Lauriergracht 37 is as well known as James Joyce's 7 Eccles Street; in reality, it was an alley in the time of the author Dekker.

features.name: Groene Tunnel
features.opening: The Groene Tunnel is a 35-meter-wide canal between Haveneiland and the Grote Rieteiland, and between the northern and southern part of Haveneiland-Oost, in the…

facts.text: Six bridges crossing the canal were all designed by architect Jeroen van Schooten.
facts.sourceQuote: De volgende straten en bruggen kruisen de Groene Tunnel: Westelijk Haveneiland Vennepluimstraat (sluis 2008) Diemerparklaan (brug 2003) Ruisrietstraat (brug 2010) Oostelijk Haveneiland Max de Haasstraat (brug 2045) Jaap Speyerstraat (brug 2046) Fritz Dietrich Kahlenbergstraat (brug 2047) De zes bruggen werden alle zes ontworpen door architect Jeroen van Schooten van Meyer en Van Schooten (MVSA).
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The following streets and bridges cross the Groene Tunnel: Western Harbor Island Vennepluimstraat (lock 2008) Diemerparklaan (bridge 2003) Ruisrietstraat (bridge 2010) Eastern Harbor Island Max de Haasstraat (bridge 2045) Jaap Speyerstraat (bridge 2046) Fritz Dietrich Kahlenbergstraat (bridge 2047) The six bridges were all designed by architect Jeroen van Schooten van Meyer and Van Schooten (MVSA).

facts.text: Construction of the first bridge on this route was completed in 2003.
facts.sourceQuote: De volgende straten en bruggen kruisen de Groene Tunnel: Westelijk Haveneiland Vennepluimstraat (sluis 2008) Diemerparklaan (brug 2003) Ruisrietstraat (brug 2010) Oostelijk Haveneiland Max de Haasstraat (brug 2045) Jaap Speyerstraat (brug 2046) Fritz Dietrich Kahlenbergstraat (brug 2047) De zes bruggen werden alle zes ontworpen door architect Jeroen van Schooten van Meyer en Van Schooten (MVSA).
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The following streets and bridges cross the Groene Tunnel: Western Harbor Island Vennepluimstraat (lock 2008) Diemerparklaan (bridge 2003) Ruisrietstraat (bridge 2010) Eastern Harbor Island Max de Haasstraat (bridge 2045) Jaap Speyerstraat (bridge 2046) Fritz Dietrich Kahlenbergstraat (bridge 2047) The six bridges were all designed by architect Jeroen van Schooten van Meyer and Van Schooten (MVSA).

features.name: Singelgracht
features.opening: The Singelgracht (Dutch pronunciation: [ˈsɪŋəlˌɣrɑxt]) is a semi-circular waterway that borders the entire city centre of Amsterdam, Netherlands.

facts.text: The name Singelgracht derives from the Dutch word omsingelen, meaning to surround.
facts.sourceQuote: The name is related to the Dutch word omsingelen, "to surround", and comes ultimately from Latin cingulum, meaning "belt". "Gracht" means canal.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The name is related to the Dutch word omsingelen, "to surround", and comes ultimately from Latin cingulum, meaning "belt". "Gracht" means canal.

facts.text: Streets like Marnixkade line the inside while Nassaukade runs along the outside.
facts.sourceQuote: The names of the streets on the 'inside' of the semi-circular canal are: Marnixkade, Leidsekade, Nicolaas Witsenkade, Sarphatikade, Huddekade, Spinozastraat and Alexanderkade. On the 'outside' are three major roads: Nassaukade (west), Stadhouderskade (south) and Mauritskade (east).
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The names of the streets on the 'inside' of the semi-circular canal are: Marnixkade, Leidsekade, Nicolaas Witsenkade, Sarphatikade, Huddekade, Spinozastraat and Alexanderkade. On the 'outside' are three major roads: Nassaukade (west), Stadhouderskade (south) and Mauritskade (east).

features.name: Nieuwe Achtergracht
features.opening: The Nieuwe Achtergracht is a canal in Amsterdam in the east of the Grachtengordel (canal belt) in the Amsterdam-Centrum district.

facts.text: Construction took place within the prosperous Jewish quarter known as Jodenbuurt.
facts.sourceQuote: This extension was in the prosperous part of Amsterdam's Jodenbuurt (Jewish quarter).
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: This extension was in the prosperous part of Amsterdam's Jodenbuurt (Jewish quarter).

facts.text: Rabbi Dr. Meijer de Hond lends his name to bridge no. 257 crossing the canal.
facts.sourceQuote: Meijer de Hondbrug (Bridge No. 257) (Nieuwe Achtergracht / Weesperstraat) bears the name of Rabbi Dr. Meijer de Hond.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Meijer de Hondbrug (Bridge No. 257) (Nieuwe Achtergracht / Weesperstraat) bears the name of Rabbi Dr. Meijer de Hond.

facts.text: The former main barracks of the Amsterdam fire brigade stand at numbers 26-34.
facts.sourceQuote: The former main barracks of the Amsterdam fire brigade are located on Nieuwe Achtergracht 26-34.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The former main barracks of the Amsterdam fire brigade are located on Nieuwe Achtergracht 26-34.

features.name: Westerkanaalschutsluis
features.opening: The Westerkanaalschutsluis is a lock in the Westerkanaal, Amsterdam-West.

facts.text: Renovations likely added hiding cells capable of sheltering four hundred people within the landheads.
facts.sourceQuote: Vermoedelijk zijn bij die verbouwing zijn ook schuilkelders aangebracht in de vier landhoofden; er zou plaats zijn voor 4 x 100 personen (vier landhoofden).
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: It is likely that hiding cellars were also installed during that renovation in the four landheads; there would be space for 4 x 100 people (four landheads).

features.name: IJhaven
features.opening: The Eastern Docklands (Dutch: Oostelijk Havengebied) is a neighborhood of Amsterdam, Netherlands, located between the IJ and the Nieuwe Vaart in the borough of…

facts.text: The IJhaven was created in 1904 when the western IJkade was lengthened to form a new peninsula.
facts.sourceQuote: When the western part of the IJkade was lengthened in 1904, a new peninsula was created, as well as two harbors: the water between the Java Island and the Oostelijke Handelskade is called the IJhaven, the water south of the KNSM Island is called the Ertshaven, both also being connected by rail.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: When the western part of the IJkade was lengthened in 1904, a new peninsula was created, as well as two harbors: the water between the Java Island and the Oostelijke Handelskade is called the IJhaven, the water south of the KNSM Island is called the Ertshaven, both also being connected by rail.

facts.text: Late nineteenth-century construction replaced old quays to boost trade with the Dutch East Indies.
facts.sourceQuote: The harbor area was constructed in the late nineteenth century to allow for increasing trade with the Dutch East Indies; a new location was necessitated by the construction of the Amsterdam Centraal railway station, which replaced the old quays.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The harbor area was constructed in the late nineteenth century to allow for increasing trade with the Dutch East Indies; a new location was necessitated by the construction of the Amsterdam Centraal railway station, which replaced the old quays.

facts.text: Early 2000s redevelopment transformed former industrial zones into homes for 17,000 residents.
facts.sourceQuote: In the early 2000s, after a large-scale reorganization, the city's biggest post-World War II building project, the Eastern Docklands was de-industrialized and became home to some 17,000 people living in some the highest population densities in the Netherlands.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In the early 2000s, after a large-scale reorganization, the city's biggest post-World War II building project, the Eastern Docklands was de-industrialized and became home to some 17,000 people living in some the highest population densities in the Netherlands.

features.name: Groenburgwal
features.opening: The Groenburgwal (Dutch pronunciation: [ˈɣrumˌbʏr(ə)xʋɑl]) is a canal in Amsterdam that connects the Raamgracht with the Amstel.

facts.text: Impressionist Claude Monet painted the canal in 1874 as The Zuiderkerk, Amsterdam.
facts.sourceQuote: 1874, the impressionist Claude Monet painted the canvas The Zuiderkerk, Amsterdam (Looking up the Groenburgwal).
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: 1874, the impressionist Claude Monet painted the canvas The Zuiderkerk, Amsterdam (Looking up the Groenburgwal).

facts.text: A section served as a temporary Red Light District for an Amsterdamned film scene in 1987.
facts.sourceQuote: In 1987, a part of the Groenburgwal was converted into Rosse Buurt for two days for the recording of a scene from the Amsterdamned film , because it was not allowed to film on the Red Light District.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 1987, a part of the Groenburgwal was converted into Rosse Buurt for two days for the recording of a scene from the Amsterdamned film , because it was not allowed to film on the Red Light District.

facts.text: Cloth weavers once processed wool here, washing and spinning it before weaving fabric.
facts.sourceQuote: Cloth weavers worked here. The wool was washed, carded and spun, then cloth was woven from it.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Cloth weavers worked here. The wool was washed, carded and spun, then cloth was woven from it.

facts.text: Finished cloth was stretched on wooden frames to dry and stretch after fulling and dyeing.
facts.sourceQuote: After fulling and dyeing the cloth was tensioned on wooden frames to dry and stretch.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: After fulling and dyeing the cloth was tensioned on wooden frames to dry and stretch.

features.name: Oostertocht
features.opening: Oostertocht is a district, located in the town of Heerhugowaard in the Netherlands.

facts.text: Construction started in 1994 and the district was fully completed by 2001.
facts.sourceQuote: In de wijk werd begonnen met bouwen rond 1994 en rond 2001 was de wijk in zijn geheel voltooid.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Construction began in the district around 1994 and around 2001 the district was completed as a whole.

facts.text: A crane fell from a construction shed during building, killing one worker.
facts.sourceQuote: Dit herinnert aan een ongeval bij het bouwen van de huizen, waarbij een kraan boven op een bouwkeet viel. Hierbij is een bouwvakker om het leven gekomen.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: This reminds us of an accident during the construction of the houses, where a crane fell from the top of a construction shed. A construction worker has died in the process.

features.name: Oude Houthaven
features.opening: Houthaven is a neighbourhood of Amsterdam, Netherlands situated in the West borough.

facts.text: Oude Houthaven was excavated in 1876 alongside the North Sea Canal.
facts.sourceQuote: The Houthaven was dug out in 1876, together with the North Sea Canal.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Houthaven was dug out in 1876, together with the North Sea Canal.

facts.text: Parts of the harbor were filled with sand in 1945 as lumber transport shifted to roads.
facts.sourceQuote: As lumber was increasingly transported by road, parts of the port were filled up with sand to be used for other purposes in 1945.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: As lumber was increasingly transported by road, parts of the port were filled up with sand to be used for other purposes in 1945.

features.name: Ertshaven
features.opening: The Ertshaven is a port in the Eastern Port Area of Amsterdam.

facts.text: The name Ertshaven reflects the heavy silt overflow that once characterized this water.
facts.sourceQuote: De naam van de haven is ontleend aan het feit dat hier veel ertsoverslag was.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The name of the port is derived from the fact that there was a lot of silt overflow here.

facts.text: The Blauwehoofdbrug spans the port while it discharges into the Amsterdam-Rhine Canal.
facts.sourceQuote: De haven ligt ten oosten van de Verbindingsdam, met daarin de Blauwehoofdbrug, en mondt uit in het Amsterdam-Rijnkanaal.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The port is located east of the Connecting Dam, with the Blauwehoofdbrug in it, and discharges into the Amsterdam-Rhine Canal.

features.name: Westerkanaal
features.opening: The Westerkanaal is a canal in Amsterdam that connects the Singelgracht and the Haarlemmertrekvaart to the IJ, where the ships on the north side of the canal…

facts.text: Sailing ships often moor here by day to wait for the Singelgrachtbrug to open at night.
facts.sourceQuote: Hierdoor liggen overdag doorgaans veel zeilschepen aangemeerd in het Westerkanaal om te wachten op de nachtopening van de Singelgrachtbrug.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: As a result, many sailing ships are usually moored in the Westerkanaal during the day to wait for the night opening of the Singelgrachtbrug.

facts.text: The western quay is interrupted by the Le Mairegracht and Van Noordtgracht canals.
facts.sourceQuote: De westelijke kaai wordt onderbroken door de Le Mairegracht en de Van Noordtgracht, de oostelijke kaai door de Zoutkeetsgracht.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The western quay is interrupted by the Le Mairegracht and the Van Noordtgracht, the eastern quay by the Zoutkeetsgracht.

facts.text: The original Westerplantsoen park was excavated to make way for the new canal route.
facts.sourceQuote: Hiervoor diende een nieuw kanaal te worden gegraven, dat rechter liep dan de bochtige Singelgracht op deze plek, tussen het Haarlemmerplein en de latere Zeeheldenbuurt, waarbij de bolwerken en het Westerplantsoen zouden worden afgegraven.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: For this, a new canal had to be dug, which would then run up the winding Singelgracht at this location, between the Haarlemmerplein and the later Zeeheldenbuurt, with the fortifications and Westerplantsoen being excavated.

facts.text: Amsterdam's first housing association built worker homes here in 1856 as a hygiene model.
facts.sourceQuote: Niet voor niets bouwde de Vereeniging ten behoeve der Arbeidersklasse te Amsterdam, de eerste woningbouwvereniging van Nederland, hier in 1856 haar eerste grote complex in de huidige Planciusstraat en Houtmanstraat met arbeiderswoningen. Dit blok in deze groene omgeving moest daarmee model staan voor betere huisvesting van de arbeidersklasse met veel licht, schone lucht en hygiëne in elke woning.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Not for nothing did the Association for the Benefit of the Working Class in Amsterdam, the first housing association in the Netherlands, build its first large complex here in 1856 in the current Planciusstraat and Houtmanstraat with worker's homes. This block in this green environment was therefore meant to serve as a model for better housing for the working class with plenty of light, clean air and hygiene in every home.

features.name: Jacob van Lennepkanaal
features.opening: The Jacob van Lennepkanaal is a canal in Amsterdam-West, named after the Dutch writer Jacob van Lennep (1802-1868).

facts.text: The name Jacob van Lennepkanaal was officially established by council resolutions in 1892 and 1896.
facts.sourceQuote: The name Jacob van Lennepkanaal was established by council resolution of both the municipalities of Nieuwer-Amstel (1892) and Amsterdam (1896).
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The name Jacob van Lennepkanaal was established by council resolution of both the municipalities of Nieuwer-Amstel (1892) and Amsterdam (1896).

facts.text: A never-built metro line to Osdorp was once planned to run directly underneath this canal.
facts.sourceQuote: In the 1968 metro plan, the (never constructed) route of the underground metro line to Osdorp was planned to run under the Jacob van Lennep Canal.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In the 1968 metro plan, the (never constructed) route of the underground metro line to Osdorp was planned to run under the Jacob van Lennep Canal.

facts.text: Houseboats are moored along quays officially named Jacob van Lennepkade.
facts.sourceQuote: The quays, along which houseboats are moored, are called Jacob van Lennepkade.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The quays, along which houseboats are moored, are called Jacob van Lennepkade.

features.name: Erasmusgracht
features.opening: The Erasmusgracht in Amsterdam-West was built in the 1940s as part of the new Bos en Lommer district.

facts.text: A helophyte filter near a pumping building features a mural named Zuiver since 2021.
facts.sourceQuote: In dat doodlopende stukje gracht ligt een helofytenfilter in de nabijheid van een bemalingsgebouwtje, dat sinds 2021 voorzien is van de muurschildering Zuiver.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In that dead-end canal section, there is a helophyte filter near a pumping building, which has been equipped with the mural Zuiver since 2021.

facts.text: Seven distinct bridges span the waterway, including a railway and metro bridge over the Ringspoorbaan.
facts.sourceQuote: Over de gracht liggen zeven bruggen: Wil de Graaffbrug (brug 393, voetgangersbrug Wachterliedplantsoen), Saïdja en Adindabrug (brug 162, in Hoofdweg), Erasmusgrachtbrug (142P, in Einsteinweg), Voet- en fietsbrug Erasmusgracht (nabij Jacob van Arteveldestraat), Camera Obscurabrug (brug 322, fietsbrug in Leeuwendalersweg) en de spoor- en metrobrug in de Ringspoorbaan.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: There are seven bridges over the canal: Wil de Graaffbrug (bridge 393, pedestrian bridge Wachterliedplantsoen), Saïdja and Adindabrug (bridge 162, in Hoofdweg), Erasmusgrachtbrug (142P, in Einsteinweg), Erasmusgracht foot and bicycle bridge (near Jacob van Arteveldestraat), Camera Obscurabrug (bridge 322, bicycle bridge in Leeuwendalersweg) and the railway and metro bridge in the Ringspoorbaan.

features.name: Prinsengracht
features.opening: The Prinsengracht is a 3.2-kilometer (2.0 mi)-long canal that runs parallel to the Keizersgracht in the center of Amsterdam.

facts.text: Mayor Frans Hendricksz Oetgens initiated construction in 1612.
facts.sourceQuote: Construction started in 1612 on the initiative of Mayor Frans Hendricksz Oetgens, after a design by city carpenter Hendrick Jacobsz Staets and city surveyor Lucas Jansz Sinck.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Construction started in 1612 on the initiative of Mayor Frans Hendricksz Oetgens, after a design by city carpenter Hendrick Jacobsz Staets and city surveyor Lucas Jansz Sinck.

facts.text: The eastern section was built later and named Nieuwe Prinsengracht.
facts.sourceQuote: The section to the east of the Amstel was constructed during the last expansion. This part was named Nieuwe Prinsengracht.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The section to the east of the Amstel was constructed during the last expansion. This part was named Nieuwe Prinsengracht.

facts.text: St. Van Brienens founded the Star at Prinsengracht 89–133.
facts.sourceQuote: St Van Brienens Founded The Star at Prinsengracht 89–133.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: St Van Brienens Founded The Star at Prinsengracht 89–133.

facts.text: Prinsengracht 849 holds the best-preserved copy of five identical neck gables from 1701.
facts.sourceQuote: The best-preserved copy of five identical neck gables from 1701 at Prinsengracht 849.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The best-preserved copy of five identical neck gables from 1701 at Prinsengracht 849.

features.name: Boerenwetering
features.opening: The Boerenwetering is a canal in Amsterdam-Zuid.

facts.text: The ditch was widened after the Amsteldijk was built to drain sinking polder land further north.
facts.sourceQuote: Na de aanleg van de Amsteldijk langs de rivier, die het lager gelegen polderland moest beschermen tegen overstromingen vanuit de rivier, werd de bestaande dwarswetering, ongeveer halverwege de Amstel en de Amstelveenseweg, verbreed tot de latere Boerenwetering om het inklinkende polderland verder in het noorden af te wateren op de Amstel.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: After the construction of the Amsteldijk along the river, which was intended to protect the lower polder land from flooding from the river, the existing cross-drainage ditch, about halfway between the Amstel and the Amstelveenseweg, was widened to the later Boerenwetering to further drain the sinking polder land further north on the Amstel.

features.name: Entrepotdok
features.opening: The Entrepotdok (Warehouse Dock), formerly Nieuwe Rapenburgergracht, is a canal in Amsterdam, and a street and row of former warehouses with the same name…

facts.text: The Entrepotdok (Warehouse Dock) was formerly known as Nieuwe Rapenburgergracht.
facts.sourceQuote: The Entrepotdok (Warehouse Dock), formerly Nieuwe Rapenburgergracht, is a canal in Amsterdam, and a street and row of former warehouses with the same name along the northeast side of the canal.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Entrepotdok (Warehouse Dock), formerly Nieuwe Rapenburgergracht, is a canal in Amsterdam, and a street and row of former warehouses with the same name along the northeast side of the canal.

facts.text: Construction of these warehouses spanned from 1708 until 1829.
facts.sourceQuote: They were constructed between 1708 and 1829, used for storage, squatted in the 1990s and are now converted into apartments.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: They were constructed between 1708 and 1829, used for storage, squatted in the 1990s and are now converted into apartments.

facts.text: Squatters occupied the complex during the 1990s before conversion to apartments.
facts.sourceQuote: They were constructed between 1708 and 1829, used for storage, squatted in the 1990s and are now converted into apartments.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: They were constructed between 1708 and 1829, used for storage, squatted in the 1990s and are now converted into apartments.

features.name: Westlandgracht
features.opening: The Westlandgracht is a surface water, a street and until 1962 the name of a district and is named after the Westland, the area west of Delft and south of The…

facts.text: Amsterdam built this waterway in the 1920s on land annexed from Sloten in 1921.
facts.sourceQuote: De gracht kreeg zijn naam in 1933 en werd aangelegd in de jaren 1920 op het grondgebied van de in 1921 geannexeerde gemeente Sloten. Deze gemeente had al plannen voor een nieuwbouwwijk ten westen van de Sloterkade, deze werden in gewijzigde vorm uitgevoerd door de gemeente Amsterdam als onderdeel van Plan West.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The canal was named in 1933 and was built in the 1920s on the territory of the municipality of Sloten, which was annexed in 1921. This municipality already had plans for a new residential area west of the Sloterkade, these were carried out in a modified form by the municipality of Amsterdam as part of Plan West.

facts.text: A nearby sluice separates the urban basin level from the lower polder level of the Slotervaart.
facts.sourceQuote: Nabij de Heemstedestraat en de Delflandlaan ligt de Westlandgrachtschutsluis, die de peilscheiding vormt tussen het stadsboezempeil van de Westlandgracht (NAP -0.40) en de Slotervaart op polderpeil (NAP -2.10).
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Near Heemstedestraat and Delflandlaan is the Westlandgrachtschutsluis, which forms the water level separation between the urban basin water level of the Westlandgracht (NAP -0.40) and the Slotervaart at polder level (NAP -2.10).

features.name: Eilandsgracht
features.opening: The Eilandsgracht (Dutch pronunciation: [ˈɛilɑntsˌxrɑxt]) is a canal in Amsterdam between the Westelijke Eilanden (Western Islands) and the mainland.

facts.text: The soil used to build the nearby islands was mostly dug up rather than dredged.
facts.sourceQuote: The new islands were made of soil that was mostly dug up rather than dredged up.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The new islands were made of soil that was mostly dug up rather than dredged up.

facts.text: The section along Bickerseiland was filled in during 1928.
facts.sourceQuote: In 1928 the section along Bickerseiland was filled in.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 1928 the section along Bickerseiland was filled in.

facts.text: Eilandsgracht originally connected the mainland to Prinseneiland and Bickerseiland.
facts.sourceQuote: It originally ran between the mainland and two of the islands, Prinseneiland and Bickerseiland.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: It originally ran between the mainland and two of the islands, Prinseneiland and Bickerseiland.

features.name: Grimburgwal
features.opening: The Grimburgwal is a small canal and street in the center of Amsterdam.

facts.text: The name Grimburgwal combines 'Grim', meaning muddy ditch, with 'burgwal' for the earthen wall.
facts.sourceQuote: The Grimburgwal was originally a tributary of the Amstel, the Grim (meaning "muddy ditch"). In the 14th century it was dug into a moat with an earthen wall ("burgwal") to protect the medieval city.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Grimburgwal was originally a tributary of the Amstel, the Grim (meaning "muddy ditch"). In the 14th century it was dug into a moat with an earthen wall ("burgwal") to protect the medieval city.

facts.text: A bridge over the Grimburgwal was constructed seven years before the nearby lock's demolition in 1868.
facts.sourceQuote: This lock, sketched by Rembrandt, remained until it was demolished in 1868. Seven years earlier a bridge was built over the Grimburgwal, now part of the Oude Turfmarkt, near the statue of Wilhelmina.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: This lock, sketched by Rembrandt, remained until it was demolished in 1868. Seven years earlier a bridge was built over the Grimburgwal, now part of the Oude Turfmarkt, near the statue of Wilhelmina.

facts.text: The House on the Three Canals features a stepped gable facing each of its three surrounding canals.
facts.sourceQuote: This building from 1610 owes its name to the fact that it is surrounded on three sides by canals: the Grimburgwal on the south side, the Oudezijds Voorburgwal on the west side and the Oudezijds Achterburgwal on the east side. It is a double house with a stepped gable on each canal .
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: This building from 1610 owes its name to the fact that it is surrounded on three sides by canals: the Grimburgwal on the south side, the Oudezijds Voorburgwal on the west side and the Oudezijds Achterburgwal on the east side. It is a double house with a stepped gable on each canal .

facts.text: During World War II, a bookstore here secretly published illegal literature.
facts.sourceQuote: During World War II the August Aimé Balkema bookstore in the House on the Three Canals was a clandestine publisher of illegal literature.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: During World War II the August Aimé Balkema bookstore in the House on the Three Canals was a clandestine publisher of illegal literature.

facts.text: In the 1980s and 1990s, drug addicts sold stolen bicycles along this canal.
facts.sourceQuote: In the 1980s and 1990s, the Grimburgwal was primarily known as a place where drug addicts offered stolen bicycles for sale.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In the 1980s and 1990s, the Grimburgwal was primarily known as a place where drug addicts offered stolen bicycles for sale.

features.name: Prinseneilandsgracht
features.opening: The Prinseneilandsgracht is a canal in the Centrum district of Amsterdam.

facts.text: Building plots on the adjacent island began in 1623 after a dispute with land speculators.
facts.sourceQuote: After a dispute with land speculators, building plots on Prinseneiland began in 1623.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: After a dispute with land speculators, building plots on Prinseneiland began in 1623.

facts.text: In 1643, tar works relocated to both sides of this canal from their previous site.
facts.sourceQuote: In 1643 the tar works moved from Oude Teertuinen to both sides of Prinseneilandsgracht.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 1643 the tar works moved from Oude Teertuinen to both sides of Prinseneilandsgracht.

facts.text: Hardly anyone lived on the island until after World War II despite over one hundred warehouses here.
facts.sourceQuote: Hardly anyone lived on Prinseneiland until after World War II. Of the 900 warehouses in Amsterdam, more than one hundred were on Prinseneiland.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Hardly anyone lived on Prinseneiland until after World War II. Of the 900 warehouses in Amsterdam, more than one hundred were on Prinseneiland.

facts.text: Until after World War II, the canal was bordered almost exclusively by warehouses and factories.
facts.sourceQuote: Until after World War II (1939–45) the canal was bordered almost exclusively by warehouses and factories.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Until after World War II (1939–45) the canal was bordered almost exclusively by warehouses and factories.

features.name: Kloveniersburgwal
features.opening: Kloveniersburgwal is an Amsterdam canal flowing south from Nieuwmarkt to the Amstel River on the edge of the medieval city, lying east of the dam in the centre…

facts.text: The name Kloveniersburgwal comes from the 'kloveniers', a civic guard division armed with a specific gun.
facts.sourceQuote: The name 'Kloveniersburgwal' comes from a division of the civic guards, the 'kloveniers', named after the gun the guards were armed with.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The name 'Kloveniersburgwal' comes from a division of the civic guards, the 'kloveniers', named after the gun the guards were armed with.

facts.text: Starting in February 1941, this canal formed the border of the Jewish quarter segregated by German occupiers.
facts.sourceQuote: During the Second World War, starting in February 1941, Kloveniersburgwal was the border of the Jewish quarter, segregated by the Germans.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: During the Second World War, starting in February 1941, Kloveniersburgwal was the border of the Jewish quarter, segregated by the Germans.

facts.text: The Trippenhuis was constructed in 1662 at number 29.
facts.sourceQuote: There are some historically important monuments located at Kloveniersburgwal, for example: 'The Trippenhuis' (1662), KLoveniersburgwal 29; The former church from the 'Evangelisch-Lutherse Gemeente ', Kloveniersburwal 50; 'The Bushuis' (1890) between 'The Compagnietheater' and Oude Hoogstraat; 'The Huis Joan Poppen' (1642), which is also called 'The Gulden Steur', Kloveniersburgwal 95; A part of the former Binnengasthuis; The entrance of Oudemanhuispoort.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: There are some historically important monuments located at Kloveniersburgwal, for example: 'The Trippenhuis' (1662), KLoveniersburgwal 29; The former church from the 'Evangelisch-Lutherse Gemeente ', Kloveniersburwal 50; 'The Bushuis' (1890) between 'The Compagnietheater' and Oude Hoogstraat; 'The Huis Joan Poppen' (1642), which is also called 'The Gulden Steur', Kloveniersburgwal 95; A part of the former Binnengasthuis; The entrance of Oudemanhuispoort.

facts.text: Huis Joan Poppen, also known as Gulden Steur, dates to 1642.
facts.sourceQuote: There are some historically important monuments located at Kloveniersburgwal, for example: 'The Trippenhuis' (1662), KLoveniersburgwal 29; The former church from the 'Evangelisch-Lutherse Gemeente ', Kloveniersburwal 50; 'The Bushuis' (1890) between 'The Compagnietheater' and Oude Hoogstraat; 'The Huis Joan Poppen' (1642), which is also called 'The Gulden Steur', Kloveniersburgwal 95; A part of the former Binnengasthuis; The entrance of Oudemanhuispoort.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: There are some historically important monuments located at Kloveniersburgwal, for example: 'The Trippenhuis' (1662), KLoveniersburgwal 29; The former church from the 'Evangelisch-Lutherse Gemeente ', Kloveniersburwal 50; 'The Bushuis' (1890) between 'The Compagnietheater' and Oude Hoogstraat; 'The Huis Joan Poppen' (1642), which is also called 'The Gulden Steur', Kloveniersburgwal 95; A part of the former Binnengasthuis; The entrance of Oudemanhuispoort.

facts.text: The Bushuis building appeared in 1890 between the Compagnietheater and Oude Hoogstraat.
facts.sourceQuote: There are some historically important monuments located at Kloveniersburgwal, for example: 'The Trippenhuis' (1662), KLoveniersburgwal 29; The former church from the 'Evangelisch-Lutherse Gemeente ', Kloveniersburwal 50; 'The Bushuis' (1890) between 'The Compagnietheater' and Oude Hoogstraat; 'The Huis Joan Poppen' (1642), which is also called 'The Gulden Steur', Kloveniersburgwal 95; A part of the former Binnengasthuis; The entrance of Oudemanhuispoort.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: There are some historically important monuments located at Kloveniersburgwal, for example: 'The Trippenhuis' (1662), KLoveniersburgwal 29; The former church from the 'Evangelisch-Lutherse Gemeente ', Kloveniersburwal 50; 'The Bushuis' (1890) between 'The Compagnietheater' and Oude Hoogstraat; 'The Huis Joan Poppen' (1642), which is also called 'The Gulden Steur', Kloveniersburgwal 95; A part of the former Binnengasthuis; The entrance of Oudemanhuispoort.

features.name: Plantage Muidergracht
features.opening: The Plantage Muidergracht is a canal and street in the Plantage neighborhood of Amsterdam.

facts.text: The section along Sarphatistraat was once named Plantage Lijnbaansgracht before 1915.
facts.sourceQuote: The part of the current Plantage Muidergracht that runs along Sarphatistraat, was an extension of the Lijnbaansgracht and was called the Plantage Lijnbaansgracht before 1915.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The part of the current Plantage Muidergracht that runs along Sarphatistraat, was an extension of the Lijnbaansgracht and was called the Plantage Lijnbaansgracht before 1915.

facts.text: Poet Adriaan Morriën lived at number three and titled a memoir after the street.
facts.sourceQuote: The Dutch poet and essayist Adriaan Morriën (1912–2002) lived at Plantage Muidergracht 3 and also named part one of his memoirs: Plantage Muidergracht.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Dutch poet and essayist Adriaan Morriën (1912–2002) lived at Plantage Muidergracht 3 and also named part one of his memoirs: Plantage Muidergracht.

facts.text: Journalist Milo Anstadt described his family home at number eighty-nine in De verdachte oorboog.
facts.sourceQuote: The Dutch journalist, writer and director Milo Anstadt (1920–2011) lived with his family at Plantage Muidergracht 89. Their house is described in Anstadt's book De verdachte oorboog.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Dutch journalist, writer and director Milo Anstadt (1920–2011) lived with his family at Plantage Muidergracht 89. Their house is described in Anstadt's book De verdachte oorboog.

facts.text: Buildings along this canal originally hosted physics, chemistry, and biology courses before shifting to other faculties.
facts.sourceQuote: On and along the Plantage Muidergracht, near Roeterseiland, are some of the buildings of the University of Amsterdam, originally built for courses or subfaculties of physics, chemistry, biology, environmental science and mathematics, but now used by other faculties.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: On and along the Plantage Muidergracht, near Roeterseiland, are some of the buildings of the University of Amsterdam, originally built for courses or subfaculties of physics, chemistry, biology, environmental science and mathematics, but now used by other faculties.

facts.text: The University of Amsterdam occupies structures near Roeterseiland that once specialized in environmental science studies.
facts.sourceQuote: On and along the Plantage Muidergracht, near Roeterseiland, are some of the buildings of the University of Amsterdam, originally built for courses or subfaculties of physics, chemistry, biology, environmental science and mathematics, but now used by other faculties.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: On and along the Plantage Muidergracht, near Roeterseiland, are some of the buildings of the University of Amsterdam, originally built for courses or subfaculties of physics, chemistry, biology, environmental science and mathematics, but now used by other faculties.

features.name: Realengracht
features.opening: The Realengracht is a canal in Amsterdam, in the Centrum district.

facts.text: Bickersgracht flows directly into the center of this waterway from the south side.
facts.sourceQuote: Bickersgracht enters the center of the canal from the south.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Bickersgracht enters the center of the canal from the south.

features.name: Zanzibarhaven
features.opening: The Zanzibarhaven is a port in the Amsterdam Western Port Area east of the Westpoortweg and west of the Afrikahaven.

facts.text: Zanzibarhaven takes its name from the Tanzanian island of Zanzibar.
facts.sourceQuote: De haven is vernoemd naar het tot het Tanzania behorende eiland Zanzibar.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The port is named after the island of Zanzibar, which belongs to Tanzania.

features.name: Rokin
features.opening: The Rokin is a canal and major street in the centre of Amsterdam.

facts.text: A tobacco shop at Rokin has served as a royal purveyor of cigars since 1826.
facts.sourceQuote: Tobacco shop Hajenius at Rokin 92-96, royal purveyor of cigars and other tobacco goods since 1826.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Tobacco shop Hajenius at Rokin 92-96, royal purveyor of cigars and other tobacco goods since 1826.

facts.text: One rooftop displays a statue of a monkey holding binoculars.
facts.sourceQuote: There is a statue of a monkey with binoculars on the rooftop.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: There is a statue of a monkey with binoculars on the rooftop.

features.name: Grote Haven
features.opening: Natural harbour in Valetta, Malta.

facts.text: A tornado struck the harbour in the 1550s, killing 600 people and destroying a shipping armada.
facts.sourceQuote: Later on in the 1550s, a tornado struck the Grand Harbour, killing 600 people and destroying a shipping armada.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Later on in the 1550s, a tornado struck the Grand Harbour, killing 600 people and destroying a shipping armada.

facts.text: The Order of Saint John used this harbour as their base for 268 years starting in 1530.
facts.sourceQuote: The Grand Harbour was the base for the Order of Saint John for 268 years, from 1530 to 1798.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Grand Harbour was the base for the Order of Saint John for 268 years, from 1530 to 1798.

facts.text: Megalithic remains from around 3700 BC once overlooked the waters from nearby Corradino Heights.
facts.sourceQuote: The Kordin Temples, the earliest of which date back to around 3700 BC, overlooked the harbour from Corradino Heights.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Kordin Temples, the earliest of which date back to around 3700 BC, overlooked the harbour from Corradino Heights.

features.name: Vecht
features.opening: Vecht may refer to: Vecht (Utrecht), a Rhine branch in the Netherlands from Utrecht to the IJmeer (Lake IJ) near Muiden, sometimes called Utrechtse Vecht…

facts.text: The Utrecht branch is sometimes called Utrechtse Vecht to distinguish it from the Overijsselse Vecht.
facts.sourceQuote: Vecht may refer to: Vecht (Utrecht), a Rhine branch in the Netherlands from Utrecht to the IJmeer (Lake IJ) near Muiden, sometimes called Utrechtse Vecht Vechtstreek, the region along the above river Vecht Vechte, a river that originates in the German state of North Rhine-Westphalia and ends in confluence with river Zwarte Water in the Netherlands province of Overijssel; often called Overijsselse Vecht in Dutch Stichtse Vecht, a municipality of the Netherlands in the province of Utrecht Rosa Vecht (1881–1915), Dutch nurse
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Vecht may refer to: Vecht (Utrecht), a Rhine branch in the Netherlands from Utrecht to the IJmeer (Lake IJ) near Muiden, sometimes called Utrechtse Vecht Vechtstreek, the region along the above river Vecht Vechte, a river that originates in the German state of North Rhine-Westphalia and ends in confluence with river Zwarte Water in the Netherlands province of Overijssel; often called Overijsselse Vecht in Dutch Stichtse Vecht, a municipality of the Netherlands in the province of Utrecht Rosa Vecht (1881–1915), Dutch nurse

features.name: Haarlemmervaart
features.opening: The Haarlemmertrekvaart [ˌhaːrlɛmərˈtrɛkfaːrt] (Haarlem's Tow-Canal) is a canal between Amsterdam and Haarlem in the province of North Holland, the Netherlands.

facts.text: A railway built in 1839 rendered passenger transport on the canal obsolete.
facts.sourceQuote: A railway parallel to the canal was built in 1839 which rendered passenger transport on the Haarlemmertrekvaart obsolete.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: A railway parallel to the canal was built in 1839 which rendered passenger transport on the Haarlemmertrekvaart obsolete.

facts.text: Dug in 1631, it holds the title of Holland's oldest tow-canal.
facts.sourceQuote: It was dug in 1631, making it the oldest tow-canal in Holland.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: It was dug in 1631, making it the oldest tow-canal in Holland.

features.name: Raamgracht
features.opening: The Raamgracht (Frame Canal) is a canal in central Amsterdam that runs from the Kloveniersburgwal to the Zwanenburgwal.

facts.text: Journalist Igor Cornelissen wrote a book titled Raamgracht 4 about his editorship there in the 1960s.
facts.sourceQuote: Journalist Igor Cornelissen wrote the book Raamgracht 4 about his time as editor of Vrij Nederland in the 1960s.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Journalist Igor Cornelissen wrote the book Raamgracht 4 about his time as editor of Vrij Nederland in the 1960s.

facts.text: Poet Hugo Claus and actress Sylvia Kristel lived together at Raamgracht 5-7 in the early 1970s.
facts.sourceQuote: In the early 1970s, the poet and writer Hugo Claus, together with his then muse, the actress Sylvia Kristel, occupied the Raamgracht 5-7 building.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In the early 1970s, the poet and writer Hugo Claus, together with his then muse, the actress Sylvia Kristel, occupied the Raamgracht 5-7 building.

facts.text: Sal Meijer painted Raamgracht, and the government bought this artwork in 1957 for its 80th birthday.
facts.sourceQuote: Sal Meijer painted the Raamgracht. This painting was purchased by the government in 1957 on the occasion of its 80th birthday.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Sal Meijer painted the Raamgracht. This painting was purchased by the government in 1957 on the occasion of its 80th birthday.

facts.text: Raamgracht recalls weaving mills where wool was stretched on wooden frames (raamen) to dry.
facts.sourceQuote: At that time there were weaving mills in the area, where after washing, carding, spinning, weaving and dying the woolen fabric was stretched on wooden frames (raamen) to dry and stretch.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: At that time there were weaving mills in the area, where after washing, carding, spinning, weaving and dying the woolen fabric was stretched on wooden frames (raamen) to dry and stretch.

facts.text: A 1625 map once labeled this waterway the Verwers Graft, or Dyers Canal.
facts.sourceQuote: On a map from 1625 by Balthasar Florisz. van Berckenrode the canal is called the "Verwers Graft" (Dyers Canal).
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: On a map from 1625 by Balthasar Florisz. van Berckenrode the canal is called the "Verwers Graft" (Dyers Canal).

features.name: Bickersgracht
features.opening: The Bickersgracht (Dutch pronunciation: [ˈbɪkərsˌxrɑxt]) is a canal in the center of Amsterdam at Westelijke Eilanden (Western Islands), but also a street.

facts.text: Bickersgracht honors Jan Bicker, who purchased the adjacent island in 1631.
facts.sourceQuote: The canal is named after Jan Bicker, who bought Bickerseiland in 1631.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The canal is named after Jan Bicker, who bought Bickerseiland in 1631.

facts.text: A towered house was constructed on the island specifically for shipping magnate Bicker.
facts.sourceQuote: In the middle of the island a house with a tower was built for the shipping magnate Bicker.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In the middle of the island a house with a tower was built for the shipping magnate Bicker.

facts.text: The original towered house vanished around 1700 to allow space for new residential buildings.
facts.sourceQuote: This building was demolished around 1700 to make way for more houses.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: This building was demolished around 1700 to make way for more houses.

facts.text: The Galgenbrug was originally a bascule bridge before being converted to a fixed structure.
facts.sourceQuote: 315) was constructed between Galgenstraat on Prinseneiland and Kleine Bickersstraat on Bickerseiland. From the street and the bridge, originally a bascule bridge, now a fixed bridge, one had a good view of the gallows of the Volewijck, north of the IJ.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: 315) was constructed between Galgenstraat on Prinseneiland and Kleine Bickersstraat on Bickerseiland. From the street and the bridge, originally a bascule bridge, now a fixed bridge, one had a good view of the gallows of the Volewijck, north of the IJ.

facts.text: A cobblestone road runs between the houses and gardens east of the canal.
facts.sourceQuote: East of the canal and the former location of the shipyards runs a public road. This street, between the houses and the "overtuinen" is paved with cobblestones.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: East of the canal and the former location of the shipyards runs a public road. This street, between the houses and the "overtuinen" is paved with cobblestones.

features.name: Westelijk Marktkanaal
features.opening: The Westelijk Marktkanaal is a canal in Amsterdam-West.

facts.text: The canal opened in 1934 specifically to supply the Central Market Halls.
facts.sourceQuote: Het kanaal is in 1934 in gebruik genomen voor de ontsluiting en bevoorrading van de Centrale Markthallen.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The canal was put into use in 1934 for the opening and supply of the Central Market Halls.

facts.text: Unlike the Lost Fleet, this waterway is not a continuous route.
facts.sourceQuote: In tegenstelling tot de Kostverlorenvaart is het kanaal geen doorgaande vaarroute.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Unlike the Lost Fleet, the canal is not a continuous waterway.

facts.text: A bascule bridge named Jan van Galen Bridge crosses the canal here.
facts.sourceQuote: In de Jan van Galenstraat ligt de basculebrug Jan van Galenbrug over het kanaal.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In the Jan van Galenstraat is the Jan van Galen Bridge, a bascule bridge over the canal.

features.name: Oostenburgervaart
features.opening: The Oostenburgervaart is a canal in the center of Oostenburg island, one of the Oostelijke Eilanden (Eastern Islands) in Amsterdam.

facts.text: Both original ends of the canal were later filled in, leaving only a short channel to the Wittenburgervaart.
facts.sourceQuote: Later both ends of the Oostenburgervaart were filled in leaving only the channel to the Wittenburgervaart.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Later both ends of the Oostenburgervaart were filled in leaving only the channel to the Wittenburgervaart.

facts.text: A warehouse completed in 1721 collapsed in 1822 and was replaced by a smaller structure.
facts.sourceQuote: To the south of the Oostenburgerdwarsvaart, down to the end of the canal, the canal bank is occupied by former East Indian warehouse of the Dutch East India Company, completed in 1721. The warehouse collapsed in 1822 and a new, smaller warehouse was built on the same site.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: To the south of the Oostenburgerdwarsvaart, down to the end of the canal, the canal bank is occupied by former East Indian warehouse of the Dutch East India Company, completed in 1721. The warehouse collapsed in 1822 and a new, smaller warehouse was built on the same site.

facts.text: Four-story apartment buildings along Conradstraat face away from the canal's southeast bank.
facts.sourceQuote: A series of four-story apartment buildings along Conradstraat have their backs on the southeast bank.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: A series of four-story apartment buildings along Conradstraat have their backs on the southeast bank.

features.name: Gaasperplas
features.opening: Gaasperplas is an artificial lake used for recreational purposes south-east of Amsterdam in the Netherlands.

facts.text: The lake hosted the 1982 Floriade landscape and flower show.
facts.sourceQuote: It was the setting for the 1982 Floriade landscape and flower show, and the Eastern end of the lake is surrounded by parks and woodlands that once formed part of the event.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: It was the setting for the 1982 Floriade landscape and flower show, and the Eastern end of the lake is surrounded by parks and woodlands that once formed part of the event.

features.name: Zijkanaal I
features.opening: The Zijkanaal I (with the letter "I") is a waterway in Amsterdam-North.

facts.text: The waterway is a remnant of the original IJ left behind when the Noorder IJpolder was drained in 1872.
facts.sourceQuote: Het is geen gegraven kanaal, maar een deel van het oorspronkelijke IJ dat bij de droogmaking van de Noorder IJpolder (toen bekend als Polder VIII) in 1872 werd overgelaten zodat de Oostzaner Overtoom, waar tot 1986 een scheepsbouwwerf was, over water verbonden bleef.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: It is not a dug canal, but part of the original IJ that was left over when the Noorder IJpolder (then known as Polder VIII) was drained in 1872 so that the Oostzaner Overtoom, where a shipyard was until 1986, could remain connected to the water.

facts.text: Three new bridges for bicycles and pedestrians were added between 2012 and 2013 to cross this canal.
facts.sourceQuote: Er is één brug voor gemotoriseerd verkeer: Brug 356 in de Klaprozenweg (in renovatie, 2016-2018) en er zijn drie nieuwe bruggen voor fietsen en voetgangers: de Theo Fransmanbrug (nr 1788) van 2013 tussen de Papaverweg en het NDSM-terrein en de Kadoelenbrug (nr 1787) van 2012 tussen de Landsmeerderdijk en de nieuwbouwbuurt De Bongerd.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: There is one bridge for motorized traffic: Bridge 356 in the Klaprozenweg (under renovation, 2016-2018) and there are three new bridges for bicycles and pedestrians: the Theo Fransmanbrug (no. 1788) of 2013 between the Papaverweg and the NDSM site and the Kadoelenbrug (no. 1787) of 2012 between the Landsmeerderdijk and the new housing area De Bongerd.

facts.text: A shipyard operated at the Oostzaner Overtoom end of the canal until 1986.
facts.sourceQuote: Het is geen gegraven kanaal, maar een deel van het oorspronkelijke IJ dat bij de droogmaking van de Noorder IJpolder (toen bekend als Polder VIII) in 1872 werd overgelaten zodat de Oostzaner Overtoom, waar tot 1986 een scheepsbouwwerf was, over water verbonden bleef.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: It is not a dug canal, but part of the original IJ that was left over when the Noorder IJpolder (then known as Polder VIII) was drained in 1872 so that the Oostzaner Overtoom, where a shipyard was until 1986, could remain connected to the water.

features.name: Zijkanaal H
features.opening: The Zijkanaal H is a side channel of the North Sea Canal and connects the Barndegat on the border of Amsterdam and Zaandam to the North Sea Canal.

facts.text: The canal opened in 1876 alongside the North Sea Canal.
facts.sourceQuote: Het kanaal is in 1876 gelijktijdig met het Noordzeekanaal in gebruik genomen.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The canal was put into use in 1876 simultaneously with the North Sea Canal.

facts.text: A 1960 dike burst flooded Tuindorp Oostzaan, forcing residents to flee.
facts.sourceQuote: Op 14 januari 1960 brak een dijk van het zijkanaal door, waardoor de Amsterdamse wijk Tuindorp Oostzaan geheel onder water kwam te staan en de bewoners tijdelijk hun huizen moesten verlaten.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: On January 14, 1960, a dike of the side canal burst, causing the Amsterdam district of Tuindorp Oostzaan to become completely underwater and the residents to have to temporarily leave their homes.

features.name: Zijkanaal F
features.opening: Zijkanaal F has been a canal in the Dutch province of North Holland since 1873.

facts.text: Most of the canal was dammed in the 1960s during Western Port Area construction.
facts.sourceQuote: Als gevolg van de aanleg van het Westelijk Havengebied van Amsterdam is het grootste deel van het kanaal in de jaren zestig gedempt.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: As a result of the construction of the Western Port Area of Amsterdam, most of the canal was dammed in the 1960s.

features.name: Westerdok
features.opening: Westerdok (Western Dock) is a former wet dock in Amsterdam.

facts.text: The Westerdok's water level stayed constant, unaffected by tides.
facts.section: Early significance as a harbor and wet dock
facts.sourceQuote: It meant that inside the area closed off by the Westerdok Lock, the water level remained more or less constant. I.e. it was not influenced by the tides.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: It meant that inside the area closed off by the Westerdok Lock, the water level remained more or less constant. I.e. it was not influenced by the tides.

facts.text: Floating dry docks provided a special service within the Westerdok area.
facts.section: Early significance as a harbor and wet dock
facts.sourceQuote: A special feature of the Westerdok was Drydock II of the Rederij der Drijvende Droogdokken, a company that provided service by floating dry docks.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: A special feature of the Westerdok was Drydock II of the Rederij der Drijvende Droogdokken, a company that provided service by floating dry docks.

facts.text: The dyke protecting the dock stretched 2,010 meters across the IJ.
facts.sourceQuote: The Westerdoksdam was a 2,010 m long dyke constructed through the IJ from the west bank of the Haarlemmersluis in the Martelaarsgracht to the Spaarndammerdijk.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Westerdoksdam was a 2,010 m long dyke constructed through the IJ from the west bank of the Haarlemmersluis in the Martelaarsgracht to the Spaarndammerdijk.

facts.text: The Westerdok officially opened when its lock was first used in September 1834.
facts.sourceQuote: The commemorative stone of the lock was set on 19 September 1832. The lock was first used on 19 September 1834, opening the Westerdok.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The commemorative stone of the lock was set on 19 September 1832. The lock was first used on 19 September 1834, opening the Westerdok.

features.name: Dijksgracht
