features.opening: The Dijksgracht (Dutch pronunciation: [ˈdɛiksˌxrɑxt]; Dike Canal) is a canal in the center of Amsterdam, north of the three Oostelijke Eilanden (Eastern…

facts.text: The protective dike was built in the late 19th century to stop silting on the Eastern Islands.
facts.sourceQuote: The dike, after which the canal and street are named, was created at the end of the 19th century as protection for the Oostelijke Eilanden (Eastern Islands) against silting up from the IJ.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The dike, after which the canal and street are named, was created at the end of the 19th century as protection for the Oostelijke Eilanden (Eastern Islands) against silting up from the IJ.

facts.text: Singer Ramses Shaffy lived on a houseboat here during the 1970s.
facts.sourceQuote: One of the most famous residents of Dijksgracht was singer Ramses Shaffy, who lived in one of these houseboats in the 1970s.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: One of the most famous residents of Dijksgracht was singer Ramses Shaffy, who lived in one of these houseboats in the 1970s.

facts.text: A railway line runs directly atop the dike structure itself.
facts.sourceQuote: The railway line from Amsterdam Centraal station to Utrecht and Hilversum is located on the dike body itself.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The railway line from Amsterdam Centraal station to Utrecht and Hilversum is located on the dike body itself.

facts.text: The name Dijksgracht translates to Dike Canal.
facts.sourceQuote: The Dijksgracht (Dutch pronunciation: [ˈdɛiksˌxrɑxt]; Dike Canal) is a canal in the center of Amsterdam, north of the three Oostelijke Eilanden (Eastern Islands).
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Dijksgracht (Dutch pronunciation: [ˈdɛiksˌxrɑxt]; Dike Canal) is a canal in the center of Amsterdam, north of the three Oostelijke Eilanden (Eastern Islands).

facts.text: The adjacent street shares the exact same name as the canal itself.
facts.sourceQuote: It is also the name of the adjacent street.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: It is also the name of the adjacent street.

features.name: Nieuwendammersluis
features.opening: The Nieuwendammersluis is a historic lock in the Nieuwendammerdijk in Amsterdam-North.

facts.text: A Sunday boat ferry called Nieuwendammerbootje stops at the lock during summer months.
facts.sourceQuote: In de zomermaanden is er op zondag een bootverbinding, het IJ-buurtveer, ook bekend als het Nieuwendammerbootje, met een halte bij de sluis.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In the summer months, there is a boat connection on Sundays, the IJ neighborhood ferry, also known as the Nieuwendammerbootje, with a stop at the lock.

facts.text: Until 1974, a bakery in a nearby stone house specialized in making duivekater sweet bread.
facts.sourceQuote: Rond de sluis staan vier gebouwen: een houten huis op Nieuwendammerdijk 297, rijksmonument, sinds 1904 is hier het café 't Sluisje gevestigd; een stenen huis op 301, waarin tot 1974 een bakkerij was gevestigd van de familie Kroese, gespecialiseerd in duivekater, een traditioneel soort zoet brood uit de regio; een houten huis op 303, rijksmonument; het stenen sluiswachtershuis op 270, aan de "Grote Haven".
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Around the lock there are four buildings: a wooden house on Nieuwendammerdijk 297, a national monument, since 1904 the café 't Sluisje has been located here; a stone house on 301, in which until 1974 a bakery was located of the Kroese family, specializing in duivekater, a traditional type of sweet bread from the region; a wooden house on 303, a national monument; the stone lock keeper's house on 270, on the "Grote Haven".

facts.text: A fixed bridge within the Nieuwendammerdijk forms part of this lock structure.
facts.sourceQuote: Onderdeel van de sluis is een vaste brug in de Nieuwendammerdijk.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Part of the lock is a fixed bridge in the Nieuwendammerdijk.

features.name: Recht Boomssloot
features.opening: The Rechtboomssloot, or Recht Boomssloot, is a canal in the Lastage (Nieuwmarktbuurt) neighborhood in the center of Amsterdam.

facts.text: The Fa Yin Chinese Association has taught language and hosted activities for seniors at number 5 since 1978.
facts.sourceQuote: The Fa Yin Chinese Association in the Netherlands has been located at Rechtboomssloot 5 since 1978. The association organizes Chinese language education and socio-cultural activities for Chinese elderly people.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Fa Yin Chinese Association in the Netherlands has been located at Rechtboomssloot 5 since 1978. The association organizes Chinese language education and socio-cultural activities for Chinese elderly people.

facts.text: De Rode Leeuw dates back to 1726 among several national monuments lining this stretch.
facts.sourceQuote: There are a number of national monuments along the Rechtboomssloot such as De Rode Leeuw (1726), Recht Boomssloot 36-40 (18th century) and De Mouterij (19th century) at Recht Boomssloot 28 / Zakslootje 16.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: There are a number of national monuments along the Rechtboomssloot such as De Rode Leeuw (1726), Recht Boomssloot 36-40 (18th century) and De Mouterij (19th century) at Recht Boomssloot 28 / Zakslootje 16.

features.name: Buiksloterkanaal
features.opening: The Buiksloterkanaal in Amsterdam-North is the connection between the (western part of the) Johan van Hasselt Canal and the IJ.

facts.text: The canal was excavated in 1926 within the Buiksloterham polder.
facts.sourceQuote: Het kanaal werd in 1926 gegraven in de polder Buiksloterham.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The canal was dug in 1926 in the polder Buiksloterham.

facts.text: Six distinct bridges span the waterway, including the Van der Pekbrug and Galgenveldbrug.
facts.sourceQuote: De Wasknijper (brug 177 in de Distelweg), de Leeuwenputbrug (371) (Grasweg), de Van der Pekbrug (995), de Elsje Christiaensbrug (2474) (Tolhuisweg), de Galgenveldbrug (188) en de Volewijckbrug (2475) overspannen het kanaal.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Wasknijper (bridge 177 in the Distelweg), the Leeuwenputbrug (371) (Grasweg), the Van der Pekbrug (995), the Elsje Christiaensbrug (2474) (Tolhuisweg), the Galgenveldbrug (188) and the Volewijckbrug (2475) span the canal.

features.name: Colakreek
features.opening: Cola Creek (Dutch: Colakreek) is a blackwater creek in Suriname's Para District.

facts.text: Colakreek takes its name from the Coca-Cola-like color of its blackwater.
facts.sourceQuote: The name refers to the colour of the water, which resembles that of Coca-Cola.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The name refers to the colour of the water, which resembles that of Coca-Cola.

facts.text: A resort on the creek was constructed during World War II for American soldiers.
facts.sourceQuote: The resort on the creek was built during World War II for the American soldiers stationed at Zanderij.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The resort on the creek was built during World War II for the American soldiers stationed at Zanderij.

facts.text: Weekend tourists frequently travel from Paramaribo to visit this nearby creek.
facts.sourceQuote: On weekends many tourists visit the creek from Paramaribo as it is only a short drive away.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: On weekends many tourists visit the creek from Paramaribo as it is only a short drive away.

features.name: Burgemeester van Tienhovengracht
features.opening: The Burgemeester Van Tienhovengracht in Amsterdam Nieuw-West was built in the 1950s as part of the Western Garden Cities.

facts.text: Burgemeester van Tienhovengracht honors Gijsbert van Tienhoven, who served as Amsterdam's mayor between 1880 and 1891.
facts.sourceQuote: De gracht kreeg zijn naam in 1952 en werd genoemd naar Gijsbert van Tienhoven (1841-1914), burgemeester van Amsterdam van 1880 tot 1891.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The canal was named in 1952 and was named after Gijsbert van Tienhoven (1841-1914), mayor of Amsterdam from 1880 to 1891.

features.name: Barnegat
features.opening: Barnegat can refer to:

facts.text: A seaplane tender named Barnegat served from 1941 until 1946.
facts.sourceQuote: USS Barnegat (AVP-10), a United States Navy seaplane tender in commission from 1941 to 1946 Barnegat-class seaplane tender, commissioned into the United States Navy between 1941 and 1946 United States lightship Barnegat (LV-79), built in 1904
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: USS Barnegat (AVP-10), a United States Navy seaplane tender in commission from 1941 to 1946 Barnegat-class seaplane tender, commissioned into the United States Navy between 1941 and 1946 United States lightship Barnegat (LV-79), built in 1904

features.name: Entrepothaven
features.opening: The Entrepothaven in Amsterdam is a trumpet-shaped body of water in the Eastern Harbor Area of Amsterdam.

facts.text: The harbor was excavated directly into a swamp area known as the City Reedlands.
facts.sourceQuote: De haven is gegraven in een moerasgebied dat de Stads Rietlanden heette.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The harbor was dug into a swamp area that was called the City Reedlands.

facts.text: Security relied on a wall along Cruquiusweg, railway gates, and a barrier of wooden stakes in the water.
facts.sourceQuote: Beveiliging werd verzekerd door een muur langs de Cruquiusweg, poorten over de spoorlijnen die vanuit het oosten binnenkwamen en een barrière van houten palen in het water.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Security was ensured by a wall along Cruquiusweg, gates over the railway lines that came in from the east and a barrier of wooden stakes in the water.

facts.text: Entrepothaven connects to the Nieuwe Vaart via a sluice gate crossed by Bridge 352.
facts.sourceQuote: Ook in 1899 werd het dok verbonden met de in 1675 gegraven Nieuwe Vaart door de Nieuwe Entrepotdokschutsluis, die door Brug 352 wordt overgestoken.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 1899, the dock was also connected to the Nieuwe Vaart, which was dug in 1675, by the Nieuwe Entrepotdok sluice gate, which is crossed by Bridge 352.

facts.text: Construction of this eastern port took place between 1898 and 1900.
facts.sourceQuote: De haven werd in 1898-1900 ingericht en is 1,2 km lang, maximaal 200 meter breed maar taps toelopend naar het westen.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The harbor was built in 1898-1900 and is 1.2 km long, maximum 200 meters wide but tapering to the west.

facts.text: The water depth here ranges from five to seven meters.
facts.sourceQuote: De diepte is gemeten tussen de 5 en 7 meter.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The depth was measured between 5 and 7 meters.

features.name: Oudezijds Voorburgwal
features.opening: The Oudezijds Voorburgwal, often abbreviated to OZ Voorburgwal, is a street and canal in De Wallen in the center of Amsterdam.

facts.text: The name Oudezijds Voorburgwal reflects its origin as the inner rampart behind the original moat.
facts.sourceQuote: To protect the city, a moat was dug on each side with a burgwal behind it, an earthen wall, with a wooden palisade for protection. When new ramparts were constructed behind these ramparts around 1385, on both the old and new sides the existing rampart became the Voorburgwal and the new rampart became the Achterburgwal.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: To protect the city, a moat was dug on each side with a burgwal behind it, an earthen wall, with a wooden palisade for protection. When new ramparts were constructed behind these ramparts around 1385, on both the old and new sides the existing rampart became the Voorburgwal and the new rampart became the Achterburgwal.

facts.text: During the 17th and 18th centuries, this canal was commonly known by the nickname Fluwelenburgwal.
facts.sourceQuote: In the 17th and 18th centuries the canal was usually called the Fluwelenburgwal.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In the 17th and 18th centuries the canal was usually called the Fluwelenburgwal.

facts.text: A local proverb about fighting a hopeless cause originates from the spirited residents of the Bierkaai.
facts.sourceQuote: The Bierkaai (beer quay) was the quay on the Oudezijds Voorburgwal, near the Oude Kerk, where barrels of beer arrived and porters loaded and unloaded the heavy barrels. The residents of this part of Amsterdam were known as invincible fighters. The proverbial "fight against the beer quay" is derived from this: dedication to a hopeless cause.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Bierkaai (beer quay) was the quay on the Oudezijds Voorburgwal, near the Oude Kerk, where barrels of beer arrived and porters loaded and unloaded the heavy barrels. The residents of this part of Amsterdam were known as invincible fighters. The proverbial "fight against the beer quay" is derived from this: dedication to a hopeless cause.

features.name: Majanggracht
features.opening: The Majanggracht is a canal with associated embankments in Amsterdam-Oost, classified under the Indian Quarter.

facts.text: The name Majanggracht honors the Indonesian river Majang on Java, chosen in 1994.
facts.sourceQuote: De gracht kreeg al op 23 maart 1994 haar naam (op de tekentafel), een vernoeming naar de Indonesische rivier Majang op Java.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The canal already received its name on March 23, 1994 (at the drawing table), a name derived from the Indonesian river Majang on Java.

facts.text: Architect Sjoerd Soeters designed the entire neighborhood surrounding this canal.
facts.sourceQuote: De inrichting van de gehele wijk was in handen van Sjoerd Soeters.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The design of the entire neighborhood was in the hands of Sjoerd Soeters.

facts.text: House number 19 is missing from the sequence that runs from one to twenty.
facts.sourceQuote: De huisnummers lopen op van 1 tot en met 20, terwijl huisnummer 19 ontbreekt (gegevens juli 2019).
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The house numbers run from 1 to 20, while house number 19 is missing (data July 2019).

facts.text: Houses twelve and fifteen share identical veranda crosses, yet their placement prevents a perfect mirror image.
facts.sourceQuote: Daarbij staan sommige soortgelijke panden tegenover elkaar, maar niet in de juiste volgorde, waardoor een spiegelbeeld wordt voorkomen. Zo hebben huisnummers 12 en 15 een veranda met eenzelfde kruis in de afscheiding.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Some similar buildings are opposite each other, but not in the correct order, which prevents a mirror image from being created. For example, house numbers 12 and 15 have a veranda with the same cross in the partition.

features.name: Lamonggracht
features.opening: The Lamonggracht is a canal with associated embankments in Amsterdam-Oost, classified under the Indian Quarter.

facts.text: The name Lamonggracht honors the Indonesian river Lamong on Java, chosen in 1994.
facts.sourceQuote: De gracht kreeg al op 23 maart 1994 haar naam (op de tekentafel), een vernoeming naar de Indonesische rivier Lamong op Java.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The canal already received its name on March 23, 1994 (at the drawing table), a name derived from the Indonesian river Lamong on Java.

facts.text: Construction occurred in the late 1990s as a shipyard transformed into a residential zone.
facts.sourceQuote: De gracht werd eind jaren negentig gegraven op het Java-eiland dat toen werd opgebouwd van aanlegplaats voor schepen tot woongebied.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The canal was dug in the late 1990s on the island of Java, which was then built from a shipbuilding yard to a residential area.

facts.text: Architect Sjoerd Soeters designed the entire neighborhood surrounding this canal.
facts.sourceQuote: De inrichting van de gehele wijk was in handen van Sjoerd Soeters.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The design of the entire neighborhood was in the hands of Sjoerd Soeters.

facts.text: Architects mimicked centuries-old canal belt styles when designing these buildings around 1995.
facts.sourceQuote: De bouwstijl van de panden is van rond 1995, waarbij architecten als Art Zaaijer inspiratie haalden uit de eeuwenoude bebouwing binnen de grachtengordel.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The architectural style of the buildings dates back to around 1995, with architects such as Art Zaaijer drawing inspiration from the centuries-old buildings within the canal belt.

features.name: Oesjesduiker
features.opening: The Oesjesduiker is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum.

facts.text: The Oesjesduiker is named after a butcher who once operated in this location.
facts.sourceQuote: Het plan tot verbreding en verhoging ging niet door (gegevens 2017) De Oesjesduiker dankt haar naam aan een ossenslager, die hier gevestigd was.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The plan to expand and increase did not go through (data 2017) The Oesjesduiker owes its name to an butcher, who was based here.

facts.text: A wooden bridge at this spot was reinforced in 1905 when the tram arrived.
facts.sourceQuote: Er zou hier een houten brug hebben gelegen, die in 1905 verstevigd werd in verband met de komst van de tram..
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: There would have been a wooden bridge here, which was reinforced in 1905 in connection with the arrival of the tram..

features.name: Damrak
features.opening: The Damrak is an avenue and partially filled in canal at the centre of Amsterdam, Netherlands, running between Amsterdam Centraal in the north and Dam Square…

facts.text: The name Damrak combines 'dam' with 'rak', a straight river reach of the Amstel.
facts.sourceQuote: The street was located on a rak (reach), a straight part of the Amstel river near a dam; hence the name.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The street was located on a rak (reach), a straight part of the Amstel river near a dam; hence the name.

facts.text: A section of this avenue was filled in during the nineteenth century.
facts.sourceQuote: In the 19th century, a section of it was filled in.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In the 19th century, a section of it was filled in.

facts.text: The name Damrak became a synonym for the Amsterdam Stock Exchange, similar to how Wall Street represents New York.
facts.sourceQuote: Because of the former stock exchange building, the monumental Beurs van Berlage, and several other buildings related to financial activities erected there in the early 20th century, the term "Damrak" has come to be a synonym for the Amsterdam Stock Exchange in the same way "Wall Street" is synonymous with the New York Stock Exchange and NASDAQ.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Because of the former stock exchange building, the monumental Beurs van Berlage, and several other buildings related to financial activities erected there in the early 20th century, the term "Damrak" has come to be a synonym for the Amsterdam Stock Exchange in the same way "Wall Street" is synonymous with the New York Stock Exchange and NASDAQ.

facts.text: The monumental Beurs van Berlage building now functions as a concert and exhibition hall.
facts.sourceQuote: The Beurs van Berlage now serves as a concert and exhibition hall.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Beurs van Berlage now serves as a concert and exhibition hall.

features.name: De Rijpgracht
features.opening: The De Rijpgracht is a canal in the Amsterdam neighborhood of Landlust.

facts.text: Seawalls along the canal were constructed between 1935 and 1936.
facts.sourceQuote: De kades werden in 1935-1936 aangelegd, maar riolering was al in 1931 gepland.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The seawalls were built in 1935-1936, but sewerage had already been planned in 1931.

facts.text: A deep steel pipe with a pumping station connects to the canal below the water surface.
facts.sourceQuote: Er werd wel een verbinding met een stalen buis gelegd met gemaalhuis, die buis ligt echter diep onder het wateroppervlak en wegdek.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: A connection was made with a steel pipe with pumping station, but that pipe is very deep below the water surface and road surface.

facts.text: Jan Corneliszoon Rijp lived between 1570 and 1630 before the waterway was named after him.
facts.sourceQuote: De gracht is per raadsbesluit van 27 april 1933 vernoemd naar de ontdekkingsreiziger Jan Corneliszoon Rijp (1570-1630), met dien verstande dat de gracht en bijbehorende straat een lidwoord hebben (de De Rijpgracht).
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The canal was named after the explorer Jan Corneliszoon Rijp (1570-1630) by a council decision of April 27, 1933, with the understanding that the canal and associated street have an article (the De Rijpgracht).

features.name: Kattensloot
features.opening: The Kattensloot is a canal in Amsterdam-West, between the Singelgracht and the Kostverlorenvaart.

facts.text: A bridge spanning the water at the Singelgracht sits directly on Nassaukade.
facts.sourceQuote: De Kattenslootbrug in de Nassaukade overspant dit kanaal bij de Singelgracht.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Kattensloot Bridge in the Nassaukade spans this canal at the Singelgracht.

facts.text: While the Kostverlorenvaart translates to Lost Cost River, this specific stretch bears the name Kattensloot.
facts.sourceQuote: Hier volgt het niet de relatief smalle Kostverlorenvaart door de Staatsliedenbuurt maar de verbrede Kattensloot.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Here follows not the relatively narrow Lost Cost River through the Staatsliedenbuurt but the widened Kattensloot.

features.name: Scharrebiersluis
features.opening: The Scharrebiersluis is a pick-up bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum.

facts.text: Electricity from a tram line allowed the bridge to operate automatically starting in 1913.
facts.sourceQuote: De brug moest nog met de hand bediend worden tot 1913; toen kwam de elektrische tram hier en kwam elektriciteit beschikbaar om de brug te openen en sluiten.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The bridge had to be operated manually until 1913; then the electric tram came here and electricity became available to open and close the bridge.

facts.text: A major renovation in 1986 finally fixed a long-standing defect while preserving original features.
facts.sourceQuote: In 1986/1987 kreeg de brug een flinke opknapbeurt, waarbij ook het oorspronkelijk mankement eindelijk verholpen kon worden. Bij die opknapbeurt werd getracht de brug zoveel mogelijk in de originele staat te houden.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 1986/1987, the bridge underwent a major renovation, during which the original defect could finally be remedied. During that renovation, efforts were made to keep the bridge as close to its original condition as possible.

facts.text: Original iron fencing was kept during renovations while new red-white barricades were hidden away.
facts.sourceQuote: De ijzeren hekwerken, al uit dienst, werden gehandhaafd en de nieuwe rood-witte slagbomen werden in staande stand weggewerkt en aan het zicht onttrokken.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The iron fencing, already in use, was maintained and the new red-white barricades were removed in standing order and hidden from view.

features.name: Oudezijds Kolk
features.opening: The Oudezijds Kolk is a short and narrow canal/lock in Amsterdam between the Oudezijds Voorburgwal and the Oosterdok.

facts.text: The Oudezijds Kolk is traditionally known by the nickname Het Kolkje.
facts.sourceQuote: The Oudezijds Kolk, often abbreviated to: OZ Kolk, has traditionally been called "Het Kolkje".
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Oudezijds Kolk, often abbreviated to: OZ Kolk, has traditionally been called "Het Kolkje".

facts.text: Only one quay exists on the southeast side, reserved exclusively for pedestrians.
facts.sourceQuote: There is only one quay, on the southeast side, which is only for pedestrians.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: There is only one quay, on the southeast side, which is only for pedestrians.

facts.text: The 1617 wine warehouse at number five now contains privately owned apartments.
facts.sourceQuote: The national monument Oudezijds Kolk 5, “Het wijnpakhuis Malaga” (Malaga wine warehouse), was built in 1617. It now holds privately owned apartments.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The national monument Oudezijds Kolk 5, “Het wijnpakhuis Malaga” (Malaga wine warehouse), was built in 1617. It now holds privately owned apartments.

features.name: Spoorwegbassin
features.opening: The Spoorwegbassin is a port in the Eastern Port Area of Amsterdam.

facts.text: The eastern Python Bridge rises about 10 meters high to let pleasure boats pass beneath it.
facts.sourceQuote: De oostelijke Pythonbrug is opvallend hoog en heeft een hoogte van circa 10 meter, zodat pleziervaartuigen er makkelijk onderdoor kunnen.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The eastern Python Bridge is remarkably high and has a height of about 10 meters, so pleasure boats can easily pass under it.

facts.text: Since the early 1990s, this historic port area has transformed into a neighborhood of houses.
facts.sourceQuote: Het gebied rondom het Spoorwegbassin was van oudsher havengebied waar zich veel loodsen en werkplaatsen bevonden, maar sinds begin jaren negentig van de 20e eeuw bestaat het Oostelijk Havengebied overwegend uit woningen.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The area around the Spoorwegbassin has historically been a port area where there were many sheds and workshops, but since the early 1990s, the Eastern Harbor Area consists predominantly of houses.

facts.text: A tunnel connecting Amsterdam to IJburg runs directly underneath the Spoorwegbassin waterway.
facts.sourceQuote: Onder het Spoorwegbassin loopt de Piet Heintunnel, de verbinding tussen het centrum van Amsterdam en de nieuwe wijk IJburg.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Under the Spoorwegbassin runs the Piet Heintunnel, the connection between the center of Amsterdam and the new district IJburg.

features.name: Achtergracht
features.opening: The Achtergracht (Dutch pronunciation: [ˈɑxtərˌɣrɑxt]) is a short canal in Amsterdam, located between Frederiksplein and the Amstel, parallel to the…

facts.text: A skipper captured a mischievous elf who promised twenty gold pieces in exchange for freedom.
facts.sourceQuote: He lay down on guard and saw that this was being done by elves playing. He captured one and the elf then promised the skipper that she would give him 20 gold pieces if he let her go.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: He lay down on guard and saw that this was being done by elves playing. He captured one and the elf then promised the skipper that she would give him 20 gold pieces if he let her go.

facts.text: Three bridges originally spanned the canal at the Reguliersgracht, Utrechtsestraat, and Amstel quays.
facts.sourceQuote: Three bridges were laid over the canal. The first was in the eastern quay of the Reguliersgracht, a second in Utrechtsestraat and a third in the western quay of the Amstel.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Three bridges were laid over the canal. The first was in the eastern quay of the Reguliersgracht, a second in Utrechtsestraat and a third in the western quay of the Amstel.

facts.text: Most of the canal was filled in 1870 to create Falckstraat and part of Frederiksplein.
facts.sourceQuote: In 1870 most of the canal was filled in, with the first two bridges becoming redundant. The filled-in part now forms the Falckstraat and the north side of the Frederiksplein.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 1870 most of the canal was filled in, with the first two bridges becoming redundant. The filled-in part now forms the Falckstraat and the north side of the Frederiksplein.

facts.text: The Nieuwe Achtergracht later extended the original line eastward toward the IJ river.
facts.sourceQuote: At the last extension of the canal belt east of the Amstel in the direction of the IJ, the Nieuwe Achtergracht was constructed as an extension of the Achtergracht.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: At the last extension of the canal belt east of the Amstel in the direction of the IJ, the Nieuwe Achtergracht was constructed as an extension of the Achtergracht.

features.name: Open Havenfront
features.opening: The Open Havenfront is the water between the Prins Hendrikkade and the Stationseiland in Amsterdam.

facts.text: A building called Nieuwe Stadsherberg once stood on stilts directly in this water from 1660 to 1870.
facts.sourceQuote: Van 1660 tot 1870 stond hier de Nieuwe Stadsherberg op palen in het water bij de oude monding van de Amstel.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: From 1660 to 1870, the Nieuwe Stadsherberg stood here on stilts in the water near the old mouth of the Amstel.

facts.text: The project cost an estimated 90 million euros to complete.
facts.sourceQuote: De kosten van het hele project zijn begroot op 90 miljoen euro.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The costs of the entire project are estimated at 90 million euros.

features.name: Noorder Amstelkanaal
features.opening: The Noorder Amstelkanaal is a canal in Amsterdam-Zuid.

facts.text: The canal is absent from street name and postal code books because its banks have different names.
facts.sourceQuote: In straatnamen- en postcodeboeken ontbreekt deze gracht omdat de kades er langs andere namen hebben.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: This canal is missing in street name and postal code books because the embankments have other names along it.

facts.text: Tram line 5 crosses the canal on the Timo Smeehuijzenbrug.
facts.sourceQuote: Coenenstraat - Beethovenstraat (Timo Smeehuijzenbrug (brug 407), hier rijdt tramlijn 5 overheen.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Coenenstraat - Beethovenstraat (Timo Smeehuijzenbrug (bridge 407), tram line 5 runs over here.

facts.text: The Lyceumbrug connects the Amsterdam Lyceum to Olympiaplein.
facts.sourceQuote: Cornelis Schuytstraat - Breitnerstraat (brug 408) Emmastraat - Willem Witsenstraat (brug 409) Lyceumbrug tussen het Amsterdams Lyceum en het Olympiaplein (brug 410) Bernard Kochstraat - Marathonweg (brug 411)
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Cornelis Schuytstraat - Breitnerstraat (bridge 408) Emmastraat - Willem Witsenstraat (bridge 409) Lyceumbrug between the Amsterdam Lyceum and the Olympiaplein (bridge 410) Bernard Kochstraat - Marathonweg (bridge 411)

features.name: Twiske
features.opening: Twiske can refer to: The Twiske, water in North Holland The Twiske (recreation area), recreation and nature area in North Holland Twiske (school), public…

facts.text: The name Twiske appears in a list of related nature areas including Ilperveld and Varkensland.
facts.sourceQuote: Twiske kan verwijzen naar: De Twiske, water in Noord-Holland Het Twiske (recreatiegebied), recreatie- en natuurgebied in Noord-Holland (gemeenten Oostzaan en Landsmeer) Twiske (school), openbare basisschool in Amsterdam Zie ookː Ilperveld, Varkensland, Oostzanerveld & Twiske, natuurgebied (Natura2000) in Noord-Holland Twisk, plaats in Noord-Holland (gemeente Medemblik)
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Twiske can refer to: The Twiske, water in North Holland The Twiske (recreation area), recreation and nature area in North Holland (municipalities of Oostzaan and Landsmeer) Twiske (school), public elementary school in Amsterdam See alsoː Ilperveld, Varkensland, Oostzanerveld & Twiske, nature area (Natura2000) in North Holland Twisk, town in North Holland (municipality of Medemblik)

facts.text: A public elementary school named Twiske operates within the city of Amsterdam.
facts.sourceQuote: Twiske kan verwijzen naar: De Twiske, water in Noord-Holland Het Twiske (recreatiegebied), recreatie- en natuurgebied in Noord-Holland (gemeenten Oostzaan en Landsmeer) Twiske (school), openbare basisschool in Amsterdam Zie ookː Ilperveld, Varkensland, Oostzanerveld & Twiske, natuurgebied (Natura2000) in Noord-Holland Twisk, plaats in Noord-Holland (gemeente Medemblik)

features.name: Amstel
features.opening: The Amstel (Dutch: [ˈɑmstəl] ) is a river in the province of North Holland in the Netherlands.

facts.text: Amstel combines 'aam' (water) and 'stelle' (solid ground), meaning water on dry land.
facts.sourceQuote: The name Amstel and the older form Aemstel are derived from Amestelle, which is a compound of the words aam or ame meaning water and stelle meaning solid, high, and dry ground.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The name Amstel and the older form Aemstel are derived from Amestelle, which is a compound of the words aam or ame meaning water and stelle meaning solid, high, and dry ground.

facts.text: The Van Amstel family ruled the region between the twelfth and fourteenth centuries.
facts.sourceQuote: Between the 12th and 14th centuries, the area was developed and ruled by the Van Amstel family.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Between the 12th and 14th centuries, the area was developed and ruled by the Van Amstel family.

facts.text: Each year the water hosts a Liberation Day concert and a rowing match.
facts.sourceQuote: Annually, the river is the location of the Liberation Day concert, Head of the River Amstel rowing match, and the Amsterdam Gay Pride boat parade.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Annually, the river is the location of the Liberation Day concert, Head of the River Amstel rowing match, and the Amsterdam Gay Pride boat parade.

features.name: Holysloter Die
features.opening: The Holysloter Die is a creek, called "Die", located mostly in the municipality of Amsterdam and a small one in the municipality of Waterland.

facts.text: The name Holysloter Die means 'low-lying area next to a ditch', typical for Waterland.
facts.sourceQuote: De naam Holysloot betekent zoiets als 'laaggelegen gebied aan een sloot' - een omschrijving die typerend is voor vrijwel geheel Waterland.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The name Holysloot means something like 'low-lying area next to a ditch' - a description that is typical of almost all of Waterland.

facts.text: A summer ferry connects the church path and Holysloot for those who ring a bell to summon it.
facts.sourceQuote: In de zomer vaart er een veerpontje tussen dit kerkepad en Holysloot voor fietsers en voetgangers die door middel van het luiden van een bel de schipper kunnen waarschuwen overgezet te willen worden.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In the summer, a ferry operates between this church path and Holysloot for cyclists and pedestrians who can warn the skipper by ringing a bell if they want to be ferried over.

facts.text: Since 2018, the nearby small forest has been designated as a bee forest for wild insects.
facts.sourceQuote: Sinds 2018 wordt het bosje in samenwerking met Nederland Zoemt ingericht als bijenbos voor de wilde bij en andere insecten.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Since 2018, the small forest has been set up as a bee forest for the wild bee and other insects in cooperation with Nederland Zoemt.

features.name: Goudriaankanaal
features.opening: The Goudriaankanaal is an unfinished canal through Waterland, between IJdoorn (Durgerdam) and the east coast of Marken.

facts.text: Construction started in 1826 but halted just two years later.
facts.sourceQuote: De werkzaamheden vingen aan in 1826 en werden in 1828 gestaakt.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Construction began in 1826 and was stopped in 1828.

facts.text: The canal honors Adrianus François Goudriaan, an inspector-general who proposed damming the IJ in 1824.
facts.sourceQuote: Diens collega (en rivaal) Adrianus François Goudriaan (1768-1829), inspecteur-generaal van 's Rijks Waterstaat, ontwikkelde een ander concept voor de bereikbaarheid van Amsterdam over zee. Hij presenteerde met hoofdingenieur Dirk Mentz in 1824 een voorstel voor de afdamming van het IJ.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: His colleague (and rival) Adrianus François Goudriaan (1768-1829), inspector-general of the Dutch Water Management, developed another concept for the accessibility of Amsterdam by sea. In 1824, he presented a proposal for the damming of the IJ with chief engineer Dirk Mentz.

facts.text: King William I ordered the design for this massive hydraulic project just months after the 1825 flood disaster.
facts.sourceQuote: De (inter)nationale watersnoodramp van 1825 die ook in Waterland grote schade opleverde maakte het voorstel van Goudriaan en Mentz actueel. Koning Willem I gaf Goudriaan enkele maanden later, in april 1825, opdracht een ontwerp te maken voor de afdamming van het IJ en een nieuwe waterweg door Waterland en Marken.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The (inter)national flood disaster of 1825, which also caused great damage in Waterland, made the proposal of Goudriaan and Mentz timely. King William I gave Goudriaan an order a few months later, in April 1825, to make a design for the damming of the IJ and a new waterway through Waterland and Marken.

features.name: Krom Boomssloot
features.opening: The Kromboomssloot, or Krom Boomssloot, is a canal in the Lastage (Nieuwmarktbuurt) neighborhood in the center of Amsterdam.

facts.text: The canal honors Cornelis Boom, a 16th-century shipbuilder who commissioned its creation.
facts.sourceQuote: The canal is named after the 16th-century landowner and shipbuilder Cornelis Boom. Both the Kromboomssloot and Rechtboomssloot were originally ditches that were commissioned by Cornelis Boom to be widened into canals to connect his shipyard on the Lastage with the IJ.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The canal is named after the 16th-century landowner and shipbuilder Cornelis Boom. Both the Kromboomssloot and Rechtboomssloot were originally ditches that were commissioned by Cornelis Boom to be widened into canals to connect his shipyard on the Lastage with the IJ.

facts.text: Residents successfully stopped a 1994 plan to remove the trees lining this waterway.
facts.sourceQuote: In 1994 the municipality proposed a plan to dig up the trees on the Kromboomssloot and Rechtboomssloot. However, this plan was canceled after protests by residents.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 1994 the municipality proposed a plan to dig up the trees on the Kromboomssloot and Rechtboomssloot. However, this plan was canceled after protests by residents.

facts.text: Architect Emanuel Marcus Rood designed the former coffee roasting factory in the early 20th century.
facts.sourceQuote: The Branderij, the former coffee roasting factory of Alex Meijer & Co., was designed in the early 20th century by architect Emanuel Marcus Rood (1851-1929).
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Branderij, the former coffee roasting factory of Alex Meijer & Co., was designed in the early 20th century by architect Emanuel Marcus Rood (1851-1929).

facts.text: The sober art nouveau structure is now recognized as a municipal monument.
facts.sourceQuote: The sober art nouveau style building is now a municipal monument.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The sober art nouveau style building is now a municipal monument.

features.name: Noordzeekanaal
features.opening: The North Sea Canal (Dutch: Noordzeekanaal) is a Dutch ship canal from Amsterdam to the North Sea at IJmuiden, constructed between 1865 and 1876 to enable…

facts.text: An English contractor built the canal because no Dutch company would take on the task.
facts.sourceQuote: Since no Dutch company was willing to take on this task, the project was awarded to an English contractor.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Since no Dutch company was willing to take on this task, the project was awarded to an English contractor.

facts.text: Workers lived in huts made of twigs and straw where disease and fights were rampant.
facts.sourceQuote: The workers lived in horrid conditions, being housed in huts built from twigs, driftwood, sod, and straw, where disease, fights, and alcohol abuse were rampant.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The workers lived in horrid conditions, being housed in huts built from twigs, driftwood, sod, and straw, where disease, fights, and alcohol abuse were rampant.

facts.text: The new town at the canal's mouth was named IJmuiden, meaning IJ Mouth.
facts.sourceQuote: A small set of locks (Zuidersluis) were built at the mouth in 1876 where the new town of IJmuiden (Dutch for "IJ Mouth") formed.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: A small set of locks (Zuidersluis) were built at the mouth in 1876 where the new town of IJmuiden (Dutch for "IJ Mouth") formed.

facts.text: King William III officially opened the North Sea Canal on November 1, 1876.
facts.sourceQuote: On 1 November 1876, the North Sea Canal was officially opened by King William III of the Netherlands.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: On 1 November 1876, the North Sea Canal was officially opened by King William III of the Netherlands.

facts.text: Construction of the canal took place between 1865 and 1876 to allow ships to reach Amsterdam.
facts.sourceQuote: The North Sea Canal (Dutch: Noordzeekanaal) is a Dutch ship canal from Amsterdam to the North Sea at IJmuiden, constructed between 1865 and 1876 to enable seafaring vessels to reach the port of Amsterdam.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The North Sea Canal (Dutch: Noordzeekanaal) is a Dutch ship canal from Amsterdam to the North Sea at IJmuiden, constructed between 1865 and 1876 to enable seafaring vessels to reach the port of Amsterdam.

features.name: Vlothaven
features.opening: The Vlothaven is a port in the Amsterdam Western Port Area south of the Coenhaven, north of the Nieuwe Hemweg, east of the Einsteinweg and north of the…

facts.text: Diggers created this port in 1931 to relocate unwanted ships and activities from the Eastern Harbor Area.
facts.sourceQuote: De haven is gegraven in 1931 bij de Mercuriushaven en bood ruimte aan schepen en activiteiten die in het Oostelijk Havengebied niet meer gewenst waren.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The port was dug in 1931 near the Mercuriushaven and provided space for ships and activities that were no longer desired in the Eastern Harbor Area.

facts.text: Dredging allowed ships up to 100,000 tons to dock at a depth of fifteen meters.
facts.sourceQuote: De Vlothaven werd tot 15 meter diep uitgebaggerd waardoor schepen tot 100.000 ton konden aan- en afmeren.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Vlothaven was dredged to a depth of up to 15 meters, allowing ships up to 100,000 tons to dock and unload.

facts.text: Equipment once enabled the uninterrupted transfer of twelve hundred tons of grain per hour.
facts.sourceQuote: De losapparatuur maakte een onafgebroken overslag van 1200 ton graan per uur mogelijk.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The loose equipment made an uninterrupted transfer of 1200 tons of grain per hour possible.

facts.text: In mid-2021, OBA Bulk Terminal Amsterdam acquired all assets including cranes and weighing towers.
facts.sourceQuote: Medio 2021 kreeg OBA Bulk Terminal Amsterdam (OBA) IGMA in handen. OBA koopt alle activa, met inbegrip van alle laad- en losapparatuur zoals kranen, weegtorens, grijpers en transportsystemen.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In mid-2021, OBA Bulk Terminal Amsterdam (OBA) acquired IGMA. OBA purchases all assets, including all loading and unloading equipment such as cranes, weighing towers, grippers and transport systems.

features.name: Syphonsluis
features.opening: The Merwedekanaal siphon is a feeder tunnel, or water transport tunnel, that connects two branches of the Merwedekanaal on the south side of the city of…

facts.text: The current structure replaced an older steel passage in 1973.
facts.sourceQuote: De huidige sifon bestaat sinds 1973 en is in de plaats gekomen voor een oudere, stalen doorgang.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The current siphon has existed since 1973 and has replaced an older, steel passage.

facts.text: The tunnel uses prefabricated concrete sections measuring 8.89 meters wide and weighing 70 tons each.
facts.sourceQuote: De tunnel bestaat uit geprefabriceerde betonnen elementen van 3 meter lang, 2,85 meter hoog en 8,89 meter breed. Met deze elementen, die elk 70 ton wegen, is een tunnel gemaakt van 138 meter lengte.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The tunnel consists of prefabricated concrete elements 3 meters long, 2.85 meters high and 8.89 meters wide. With these elements, each weighing 70 tons, a tunnel 138 meters long has been made.

facts.text: Factory-built segments were assembled inside a temporarily dried-up sluice canal near Jutphaas.
facts.sourceQuote: De tunnelsegmenten zijn gebouwd bij de betonfabriek Kats Prefab Beton in Kats op het eiland Noord-Beveland, waarna ze naar de bouwlocatie vervoerd zijn en geassembleerd in de tijdelijk drooggelegde sluiskolk van de Noordersluis bij Jutphaas.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The tunnel sections were built at the Kats Prefab Beton concrete factory in Kats on the island of Noord-Beveland, after which they were transported to the construction site and assembled in the temporarily dried-up sluice canal of the Noordersluis near Jutphaas.

features.name: Passeerdersgracht
features.opening: The Passeerdersgracht is a short canal in Amsterdam, the Netherlands, that connects the Prinsengracht with the Lijnbaansgracht.

facts.text: The Walengang alley between numbers 15 and 17 was demolished in 1850 to build a shelter for the needy.
facts.sourceQuote: For example, in the "Walenhoek" on the Passeerdersgracht there was the "Walengang" between numbers 15 and 17. This corridor was demolished in 1850 for construction of the former Toevlugt voor Behoeftigen on Passeerdersgracht 9–19.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: For example, in the "Walenhoek" on the Passeerdersgracht there was the "Walengang" between numbers 15 and 17. This corridor was demolished in 1850 for construction of the former Toevlugt voor Behoeftigen on Passeerdersgracht 9–19.

facts.text: Architects Joan van der Mey and Piet Kramer designed the former Arbeidsbeurs around 1915 at number 28.
facts.sourceQuote: The building of the former Arbeidsbeurs on Passeerdersgracht 28-32, at the corner of Tweede Passeerdersdwarsstraat, was designed around 1915 by architects Joan van der Mey and Piet Kramer.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The building of the former Arbeidsbeurs on Passeerdersgracht 28-32, at the corner of Tweede Passeerdersdwarsstraat, was designed around 1915 by architects Joan van der Mey and Piet Kramer.

facts.text: Circus Elleboog performed in this building until moving to Amsterdam-West in the summer of 2012.
facts.sourceQuote: Until the summer of 2012, this monumental building housed one of the two branches of the Amsterdam youth circus Circus Elleboog. Elleboog then moved to a new location, Laan van Spartaan in Amsterdam-West.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Until the summer of 2012, this monumental building housed one of the two branches of the Amsterdam youth circus Circus Elleboog. Elleboog then moved to a new location, Laan van Spartaan in Amsterdam-West.

features.name: Alaskahaven
features.opening: The Alaskahaven is one of the harbor basins in the port of Amsterdam that together form the Amerikahaven.

facts.text: The harbor features a quay length of 1,500 meters and reaches a depth of 15.5 meters.
facts.sourceQuote: De beschikbare kadelengte is 1.500 meter, de haven is 15,5 meter diep.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The available quay length is 1,500 meters, the harbor is 15.5 meters deep.

facts.text: Among the Amerikahaven basins, this one sits closest to the North Sea Canal.
facts.sourceQuote: De Alaskahaven is van de insteekhavens in de Amerikahaven degene die het dichtst bij het Noordzeekanaal ligt.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Alaskahaven is from the ports of call in the Amerikahaven the one that is closest to the North Sea Canal.

features.name: Coenhaven
features.opening: The Coenhaven is a port in the Amsterdam Western Port Area north of the Vlothaven, south of the North Sea Canal near the Coentunnel named after the port, east…

facts.text: The port honors Jan Pieterszoon Coen, a historical colonizer.
facts.sourceQuote: De haven is vernoemd naar de kolonisator Jan Pieterszoon Coen.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The port is named after the colonizer Jan Pieterszoon Coen.

features.name: Ransdorper Die
features.opening: The Ransdorper Die is a creek, named, in Waterland in North Holland.

facts.text: Ransdorper Die is a remnant of the former Waterlandse Die, once a peat river.
facts.sourceQuote: Het is een restant van het vroegere Waterlandse Die, een veenriviertje in Waterland.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: It is a remnant of the former Waterlandse Die, a peat river in Waterland.

facts.text: The Uitdammer Die no longer connects to the Markermeer but drains at the Uitdammerdijk.
facts.sourceQuote: Tegenwoordig is het Uitdammer Die niet meer rechtstreeks verbonden met het huidige Markermeer maar loopt dood op de Uitdammerdijk.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Today, the Uitdammer Die is no longer directly connected to the current Markermeer but runs out at the Uitdammerdijk.

features.name: Van Noordtgracht
features.opening: The Van Noordtgracht is a canal in the West district of Amsterdam.

facts.text: The waterway once formed part of an inner harbor along the Westerkanaal.
facts.sourceQuote: Samen met de aan de noordzijde liggende Le Mairegracht was het een binnenhaven aan het Westerkanaal.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Together with the Le Mairegracht on the north side, it was an inner harbor on the Westerkanaal.

features.name: Le Mairegracht
features.opening: The Le Mairegracht is a canal in the West district of Amsterdam.

facts.text: Both banks of this waterway are officially designated as Le Mairekade.
facts.sourceQuote: De beide kaden van de gracht heten Le Mairekade.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The two banks of the canal are called Le Mairekade.

facts.text: One crossing was delivered in 1964 and served as Noordpoolbrug until 2016.
facts.sourceQuote: Er zijn twee oeververbindingen over de Le Mairegracht: brug 349, een basculebrug (opgeleverd in 1964 en tot 2016 bekend als Noordpoolbrug; in april 2020 officieel vernoemd naar Cor Thesing) in de Houtmankade; brug 1908, vaste brug tussen de Henk Curièrekade en de Noordkaapstraat.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: There are two river crossings over the Le Mairegracht: bridge 349, a bascule bridge (delivered in 1964 and known as Noordpoolbrug until 2016; officially renamed after Cor Thesing in April 2020) in the Houtmankade; bridge 1908, fixed bridge between the Henk Curièrekade and the Noordkaapstraat.

features.name: Achter Twiske
features.opening: The Twiske is an original tributary of the IJ and runs northwest of Amsterdam.

facts.text: The name Twiske derives from West Frisian and translates to "between".
facts.sourceQuote: De naam Twiske komt uit het West-Fries en betekent "tussen".
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The name Twiske comes from West Frisian and means "between".

facts.text: A map from 1288 already indicated this bog river flowing from Wormermeer to the IJ.
facts.sourceQuote: Het veenriviertje staat al aangegeven op een kaart van 1288 en liep oorspronkelijk van het toenmalige Wormermeer tot aan de noordelijke oever van het IJ.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The bog river is already indicated on a map of 1288 and originally ran from the then-Wormermeer to the northern bank of the IJ.

facts.text: Bridge 2091 carries a bicycle path across the water near the Kinselmeer.
facts.sourceQuote: Nabij het Kinselmeer kruist een fietspad over brug 2091 de waterloop.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Near the Kinselmeer, a bicycle path crosses the watercourse over bridge 2091.

features.name: Zwanenburgwal
features.opening: The Zwanenburgwal is a canal and street in the center of Amsterdam.

facts.text: Rembrandt could move his giant Night Watch canvas out of his studio via a hidden exit running under the corner house onto this street.
facts.sourceQuote: Rembrandt was able to leave his house via an exit onto the Zwanenburgwal, running underneath the adjacent corner house, which enabled him to move the giant canvas of the Night Watch out of his studio.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Rembrandt was able to leave his house via an exit onto the Zwanenburgwal, running underneath the adjacent corner house, which enabled him to move the giant canvas of the Night Watch out of his studio.

facts.text: In 1602 a breach in the Sint Antoniesdike allowed construction of the Sint Antoniessluis gate that defined the canal's inner section.
facts.sourceQuote: In 1602 the Sint Antoniesdijk, a dike along the eastern edge of the city, was breached to construct a sluice gate, the Sint Antoniessluis. The inner section came to be known as the Zwanenburgwal and the outer section, beyond the sluice gate, became known as the Oude Schans.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 1602 the Sint Antoniesdijk, a dike along the eastern edge of the city, was breached to construct a sluice gate, the Sint Antoniessluis. The inner section came to be known as the Zwanenburgwal and the outer section, beyond the sluice gate, became known as the Oude Schans.

features.name: Uitdammer Die
features.opening: The Uitdammer Die is a creek, called "die", in Waterland in North Holland.

facts.text: Originally a sea arm of the North Sea, it now ends dead on the Uitdammerdijk.
facts.sourceQuote: Oorspronkelijk was het een zeearm van de Zuiderzee. Tegenwoordig is het Uitdammer Die niet meer rechtstreeks verbonden met het huidige Markermeer maar loopt dood op de Uitdammerdijk.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Originally it was a sea arm of the North Sea. Today, Uitdammer Die is no longer directly connected to the current Markermeer but ends up dead on the Uitdammerdijk.

features.name: Schutsluis
features.opening: Fall structure with a fixed chamber in which the water level changes.

facts.text: Unlike caisson locks where the chamber rises, this structure features a fixed chamber where only the water level varies to move boats.
facts.sourceQuote: The distinguishing feature of a lock is a chamber in a permanently fixed position in which the water level can be varied. In a caisson lock, a boat lift, or on a canal inclined plane, it is the chamber itself (usually then called a caisson) that rises and falls.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The distinguishing feature of a lock is a chamber in a permanently fixed position in which the water level can be varied. In a caisson lock, a boat lift, or on a canal inclined plane, it is the chamber itself (usually then called a caisson) that rises and falls.

facts.text: Engineers added larger locks over time to canals so ships could follow more direct routes across uneven terrain.
facts.sourceQuote: Locks are used to make a river more easily navigable, or to allow a canal to cross land that is not level. Over time, more and larger locks have been used in canals to allow a more direct route to be taken.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Locks are used to make a river more easily navigable, or to allow a canal to cross land that is not level. Over time, more and larger locks have been used in canals to allow a more direct route to be taken.

facts.text: Ancient Egyptian engineers solved the Nile's saltwater problem around 274–273 BC.
facts.sourceQuote: Engineers of Ptolemy II are credited by Diodorus Siculus with being the first to solve the problem of keeping the Nile free of salt water when they invented the lock around 274–273 BC.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Engineers of Ptolemy II are credited by Diodorus Siculus with being the first to solve the problem of keeping the Nile free of salt water when they invented the lock around 274–273 BC.

features.name: Herengracht
features.opening: The Herengracht (Dutch pronunciation: [ˈɦeːrə(ŋ)ˌɣrɑxt]) is the second of four Amsterdam canals belonging to the canal belt and lies between the Singel and the…

facts.text: The canal received its name Herengracht in 1612 after the city's Gentlemen Governors.
facts.sourceQuote: When the ditch was widened into the present canal it was given the name Herengracht in 1612, after the Heren Regeerders van de stad Amsterdam (Gentlemen Governors of the city of Amsterdam).
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: When the ditch was widened into the present canal it was given the name Herengracht in 1612, after the Heren Regeerders van de stad Amsterdam (Gentlemen Governors of the city of Amsterdam).

facts.text: Before becoming a canal, this waterway served as a defensive moat dug in 1585.
facts.sourceQuote: Before that it was a moat (dug in 1585) for the companies located behind the Singel.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Before that it was a moat (dug in 1585) for the companies located behind the Singel.

facts.text: A distinct kink at Driekoningenstraat remains from the original outer moat's route around a stronghold.
facts.sourceQuote: The Herengracht therefore still has a kink at Driekoningenstraat, where the outer moat was routed around a stronghold at that height.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Herengracht therefore still has a kink at Driekoningenstraat, where the outer moat was routed around a stronghold at that height.

facts.text: The Gouden Bocht, or Golden Bend, features the canal's most magnificent houses.
facts.sourceQuote: The Gouden Bocht (Golden Bend) in particular is known for its large and beautiful canal houses.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Gouden Bocht (Golden Bend) in particular is known for its large and beautiful canal houses.

features.name: Kinselmeer
features.opening: The Kinselmeer is a Dutch lake in the province of North Holland north of Durgerdam and east of Ransdorp (Amsterdam municipality).

facts.text: A massive 1825 storm expanded the lake when Stenen Beer collapsed into the sea.
facts.sourceQuote: Bij de dijkdoorbraak van 1825 werd het Kinselmeer sterk vergroot, toen tijdens een zware storm het in de Waterlandse Zeedijk gelegen verdedigingswerk de Stenen Beer in de Zuiderzee verdween.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: During a severe storm in 1825, the Kinselmeer was significantly expanded when the defensive structure Stenen Beer, located on the Waterlandse Zeedijk, disappeared into the North Sea.

features.name: Snoekjesgracht
features.opening: The Snoekjesgracht (Pike Canal) is a small canal in Amsterdam, in the Lastage neighborhood.

facts.text: The name Snoekjesgracht honors Jan Pieters Snoeck, who displayed a pike on his 1595 house facade.
facts.sourceQuote: The Snoekjesgracht, originally called Snoeksgracht, was named after a 16th-century resident, Jan Pieters Snoeck, who had a house built on this canal in 1595 and depicted a pike (fish) on the facade.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Snoekjesgracht, originally called Snoeksgracht, was named after a 16th-century resident, Jan Pieters Snoeck, who had a house built on this canal in 1595 and depicted a pike (fish) on the facade.

facts.text: Plans to dig out the buried Rotterdammersloot were abandoned in 2003 due to existing buildings and lack of space.
facts.sourceQuote: In 2003, the Amsterdam-Centrum district investigated whether the filled-in Rotterdammersloot was suitable for being dug out again, but abandoned this because of the existing buildings and lack of space.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 2003, the Amsterdam-Centrum district investigated whether the filled-in Rotterdammersloot was suitable for being dug out again, but abandoned this because of the existing buildings and lack of space.

facts.text: Bridge number 289 crosses the water where Snoekjessteeg meets the canal.
facts.sourceQuote: 289) crosses the Snoekjesgracht at the Snoekjessteeg.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: 289) crosses the Snoekjesgracht at the Snoekjessteeg.

features.name: IJmeer
features.opening: The IJmeer is a 'bordering lake' (Randmeer) in the Netherlands straddling the provinces of North Holland and Flevoland.

facts.text: A straight line from Uitdam to Almere-Pampus marks its northeastern border.
facts.sourceQuote: The IJmeer is bordered, and separated from the IJ, by the Oranje Locks to the east, a straight line extending from Uitdam to the Almere-Pampus to the northeast, and the Hollandse Brug to the southeast, where it connects with the Gooimeer.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The IJmeer is bordered, and separated from the IJ, by the Oranje Locks to the east, a straight line extending from Uitdam to the Almere-Pampus to the northeast, and the Hollandse Brug to the southeast, where it connects with the Gooimeer.

facts.text: The Hollandse Brug connects the IJmeer to the Gooimeer in the southeast.
facts.sourceQuote: The IJmeer is bordered, and separated from the IJ, by the Oranje Locks to the east, a straight line extending from Uitdam to the Almere-Pampus to the northeast, and the Hollandse Brug to the southeast, where it connects with the Gooimeer.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The IJmeer is bordered, and separated from the IJ, by the Oranje Locks to the east, a straight line extending from Uitdam to the Almere-Pampus to the northeast, and the Hollandse Brug to the southeast, where it connects with the Gooimeer.

features.name: Sisyfusgemaal
features.opening: The Sisyfusgemaal is both a structural and artistic work of art (applied art) in Amsterdam Nieuw-West.

facts.text: A predecessor mill stood here from 1874 until an electric station replaced it in 1921.
facts.sourceQuote: Een voorganger van dit gemaal, de Akermolen, staat er sinds 1874, maar is in 1921 buiten werking gesteld door de komst van een elektrisch gemaal.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: A predecessor of this pumping station, the Akermolen, has been there since 1874, but was decommissioned in 1921 due to the arrival of an electric pumping station.

facts.text: A concrete gutter was laid into an excavated dike section to drain water from the aqueduct.
facts.sourceQuote: Om het water vanuit het aquaduct te kunnen lozen moest een stukje dijk uitgegraven worden waarin de betonnen goot werd gelegd.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In order to drain the water from the aqueduct, a section of dike had to be excavated into which the concrete gutter was laid.

features.name: Hoekenesgracht
features.opening: Hoekenes in a street in Amsterdam Nieuw-West.

facts.text: A dam crossing this canal was removed in 1965 after a street ran over it.
facts.sourceQuote: Tot 1965 was er een dam in de Hoekenesgracht waarover de verlengde Van Suchtelen van de Haarestraat tussen Hoekenes en Wolbrantskerkweg liep.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Until 1965, there was a dam in the Hoekenesgracht over which the extended Van Suchtelen van de Haarestraat ran between Hoekenes and Wolbrantskerkweg.

facts.text: The stretch between Tussen Meer and Pieter Calandlaan is nicknamed the golden coast of Osdorp.
facts.sourceQuote: Zo is er sociale woningbouw te vinden uit de jaren vijftig, maar tussen Tussen Meer en de Pieter Calandlaan straat en gracht staat een aantal bungalows, ook wel aangeduid als “de goudkust van Osdorp”.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: For example, there are social housing buildings from the 1950s, but between Tussen Meer and the Pieter Calandlaan street and canal there are a number of bungalows, also known as "the golden coast of Osdorp".

features.name: Brouwersgracht
features.opening: The Brouwersgracht is a canal in Amsterdam that connects the Singel with the Singelgracht.

facts.text: Brouwersgracht earned its name in 1594 from the many beer breweries found here.
facts.sourceQuote: The canal took its name in 1594 from the many beer breweries that were to be found in this neighborhood in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The canal took its name in 1594 from the many beer breweries that were to be found in this neighborhood in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

facts.text: The canal belt was dug southward from this waterway starting in 1612.
facts.sourceQuote: Starting in 1612 the canal belt was dug in southern direction from the Brouwersgracht.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Starting in 1612 the canal belt was dug in southern direction from the Brouwersgracht.

facts.text: Most warehouses built for goods storage were later converted into residential houses.
facts.sourceQuote: Most warehouses, built for the storage of goods, have been converted into residential houses.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Most warehouses, built for the storage of goods, have been converted into residential houses.

facts.text: Only the 'Faith' remains of a former trio that also included Hope and Love.
facts.sourceQuote: Originally Brouwersgracht 218, 220 and 222 formed the 'triplets', 'Faith', 'Hope' and 'Love'. Only the "Faith" still exists. (Brouwersgracht 220 received a clock gable in the 18th century, Brouwersgracht 222 was demolished.) Between Brouwersgracht 130 and 134, the narrow passage gives access to the Johannes en Willibrordus old Catholic clandestine church in the interior.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Originally Brouwersgracht 218, 220 and 222 formed the 'triplets', 'Faith', 'Hope' and 'Love'. Only the "Faith" still exists. (Brouwersgracht 220 received a clock gable in the 18th century, Brouwersgracht 222 was demolished.) Between Brouwersgracht 130 and 134, the narrow passage gives access to the Johannes en Willibrordus old Catholic clandestine church in the interior.

facts.text: A narrow passage between numbers 130 and 134 leads to an old Catholic clandestine church.
facts.sourceQuote: Only the "Faith" still exists. (Brouwersgracht 220 received a clock gable in the 18th century, Brouwersgracht 222 was demolished.) Between Brouwersgracht 130 and 134, the narrow passage gives access to the Johannes en Willibrordus old Catholic clandestine church in the interior.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Only the "Faith" still exists. (Brouwersgracht 220 received a clock gable in the 18th century, Brouwersgracht 222 was demolished.) Between Brouwersgracht 130 and 134, the narrow passage gives access to the Johannes en Willibrordus old Catholic clandestine church in the interior.

features.name: Sloterplas
features.opening: The Sloterplas is located in the center of the Western Garden Cities in Amsterdam Nieuw-West.

facts.text: The lake was deepened to 38 meters by pouring in debris between 1948 and 1956.
facts.sourceQuote: Voor ophoging van de nieuw te bouwen tuinsteden Slotermeer, Geuzenveld, Slotervaart en Osdorp werd de plas tussen 1948 en 1956 tientallen meters uitgediept tot een zandgat van 45 meter diep. Door het storten van puin werd de uiteindelijke diepte 38 meter.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: For the elevation of the newly to be built garden towns Slotermeer, Geuzenveld, Slotervaart and Osdorp, the pond was deepened by dozens of meters between 1948 and 1956 to a sand pit 45 meters deep. By pouring in debris, the final depth was 38 meters.

facts.text: An outdoor swimming pool opened on the northwest bank in 1957.
facts.sourceQuote: In 1957 werd aan de noordwestkant van de plas het openlucht-Sloterparkbad geopend, in 1973 verrees hier tevens een overdekt zwembad (50 meterbad), met in 1974 ook buitenbaden, dat in 2001 werd vervangen door een nieuw gebouw voor de (wedstrijd-)zwemsport.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 1957, the outdoor Sloterparkbad was opened on the northwest side of the pond, in 1973 a covered swimming pool (50-meter pool) was also built here, with outdoor pools in 1974, which was replaced in 2001 by a new building for (competitive) swimming.

facts.text: The northern bank became a protected landscape on October 18, 2017.
facts.sourceQuote: Het noordelijk deel bij de noordoever van de Sloterplas werd op 18 oktober 2017 aangewezen als gemeentelijk beschermd stadsgezicht.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The northern part near the northern bank of the Sloterplas was designated as a municipal protected urban landscape on October 18, 2017.

facts.text: In 2024, protection expanded to cover the entire lake and all its banks.
facts.sourceQuote: Naar aanleiding van een aanvraag van Heemschut heeft de gemeenteraad van Amsterdam op 28 maart 2024 de gehele Sloterplas en oevers aangewezen als gemeentelijk beschermd stadsgezicht.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Following a request from Heemschut, the municipal council of Amsterdam designated the entire Sloterplas and banks as a municipal protected urban landscape on March 28, 2024.

features.name: Looiersgracht
features.opening: The Looiersgracht (Dutch pronunciation: [ˈloːi.ərsˌxrɑxt]; Tanners' Canal) is a short canal in Amsterdam, between Prinsengracht (at no. 334) and…

facts.text: Bridge 102 on Eerste Looiersdwarsstraat is a pedestrian municipal monument.
facts.sourceQuote: Bridge 100 is located on the Lijnbaansgracht and at Eerste Looiersdwarsstraat there is (pedestrian) bridge 102, they are both municipal monuments.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Bridge 100 is located on the Lijnbaansgracht and at Eerste Looiersdwarsstraat there is (pedestrian) bridge 102, they are both municipal monuments.

facts.text: A cargo ship named MV Looiersgracht operates under the Spliethoff charter office.
facts.sourceQuote: The MV Looiersgracht is a cargo ship from the Spliethoff charter office .
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The MV Looiersgracht is a cargo ship from the Spliethoff charter office .

facts.text: A mechanical gallery called The Old Maze displayed rolling-eyed images of David and Goliath until 1862.
facts.sourceQuote: From the early 17th century the "Maze Garden" and image gallery: "The Old Maze" were located on the corner of the Looiersgracht / Prinsengracht. The amusement park with a maze of green hedges, a water feature and a gallery with mechanically moving images was in operation from before 1625 to 1862. Here, among other things, one saw images of David and Goliath which could roll their eyes.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: From the early 17th century the "Maze Garden" and image gallery: "The Old Maze" were located on the corner of the Looiersgracht / Prinsengracht. The amusement park with a maze of green hedges, a water feature and a gallery with mechanically moving images was in operation from before 1625 to 1862. Here, among other things, one saw images of David and Goliath which could roll their eyes.

facts.text: Silver smelter Anthoni Grill established his gold-testing facility here between 1651 and 1661.
facts.sourceQuote: The smelter of silversmith Anthoni Grill (1607–75) for "investigating the content of gold or silver" was established between 1651 and 1661 on the Looiersgracht.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The smelter of silversmith Anthoni Grill (1607–75) for "investigating the content of gold or silver" was established between 1651 and 1661 on the Looiersgracht.

features.name: Nieuwe Houthaven
features.opening: Houthaven is a neighbourhood of Amsterdam, Netherlands situated in the West borough.

facts.text: The port was excavated in 1876 alongside the North Sea Canal.
facts.sourceQuote: The Houthaven was dug out in 1876, together with the North Sea Canal.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Houthaven was dug out in 1876, together with the North Sea Canal.

facts.text: The name Nieuwe Houthaven translates to "New Lumber Port," distinguishing it from its older neighbor.
facts.sourceQuote: The harbour is made up out of four parts (from east to west): Oude Houthaven (Old Lumber Port), Houthaven, Nieuwe Houthaven (New Lumber Port) and Minervahaven (Minerva Port).
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The harbour is made up out of four parts (from east to west): Oude Houthaven (Old Lumber Port), Houthaven, Nieuwe Houthaven (New Lumber Port) and Minervahaven (Minerva Port).

facts.text: The entire harbor complex consists of four distinct sections arranged from east to west.
facts.sourceQuote: The harbour is made up out of four parts (from east to west): Oude Houthaven (Old Lumber Port), Houthaven, Nieuwe Houthaven (New Lumber Port) and Minervahaven (Minerva Port).
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The harbour is made up out of four parts (from east to west): Oude Houthaven (Old Lumber Port), Houthaven, Nieuwe Houthaven (New Lumber Port) and Minervahaven (Minerva Port).

features.name: Amstelkanaal
features.opening: The Amstelkanaal is a canal in Amsterdam-Zuid that was dug as part of H.P. Berlage's Plan Zuid.

facts.text: A planned sixth bridge at De Kom was never built.
facts.sourceQuote: 404) Een zesde brug bij De Kom kwam er nooit.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: 404) A sixth bridge at De Kom never came to be.

facts.text: Gerard Reve wrote and set his novel The Nights in a house on the Jozef Israëlskade.
facts.sourceQuote: Aan het Amstelkanaal liggen: Berlage Lyceum Okura Hotel Het huis waar Gerard Reve De avonden schreef en situeerde (aan de Jozef Israëlskade, in De avonden de Schilderskade geheten).
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: On the Amstelkanaal are: Berlage Lyceum Okura Hotel The house where Gerard Reve wrote and set The Nights (on the Jozef Israëlskade, in The Nights called Schilderskade).

facts.text: The northern quay is named Jozef Israëlskade while the southern side bears the name Amstelkade.
facts.sourceQuote: De kades langs het Amstelkanaal heten Jozef Israëlskade (de noordelijke zijde van het kanaal, in De Pijp) en Amstelkade (de zuidelijke zijde van het kanaal, in de Rivierenbuurt).
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The quays along the Amstelkanaal are called Jozef Israëlskade (the northern side of the canal, in De Pijp) and Amstelkade (the southern side of the canal, in the Rivierenbuurt).

features.name: Zorgvliedsluis
features.opening: The Zorgvliedsluis or Zorgvliedschutsluis is a lock in the Nieuwe Wetering near the Zuidelijke Wandelweg in Amsterdam.

facts.text: Construction occurred in 1921 alongside the Stadwijck pumping station.
facts.sourceQuote: De sluis is in 1921 gebouwd, in dezelfde tijd als het gemaal Stadwijck en de Zorgvliedbrug.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The lock was built in 1921, at the same time as the Stadwijck pumping station and the Zorgvliedbrug.

facts.text: Amstel water rarely refills the polder here because it is saltier.
facts.sourceQuote: De schutsluis, beheerd door de gemeente Amsterdam, wordt soms gebruikt voor het verversen van het water in de Binnendijkse Buitenveldertse polder met water uit de Amstel, dit gebeurt echter alleen bij uitzondering, omdat het Amstelwater zouter is.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The sluice gate, managed by the municipality of Amsterdam, is sometimes used to refill the water in the Binnendijkse Buitenveldertse polder with water from the Amstel, however, this only happens on an exceptional basis, because the Amstel water is saltier.

features.name: Duivendrechtsevaart
features.opening: The Duivendrechtsevaart is a canal in Amsterdam and Duivendrecht (Ouder-Amstel municipality).

facts.text: The Duivendrechtsevaart takes its name from the nearby village of Duivendrecht.
facts.sourceQuote: De vaart is vernoemd naar het nabij gelegen dorp Duivendrecht.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The canal is named after the nearby village of Duivendrecht.

facts.text: A dam once allowed east-west traffic until Van der Madeweg opened in 1963.
facts.sourceQuote: Tot de openstelling van de Van der Madeweg in 1963 bleef er ter hoogte van de Paul van Vlissingenstraat een dam aanwezig om het verkeer de mogelijkheid te geven van oost naar west te rijden.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Until the opening of the Van der Madeweg in 1963, there was a dam at the level of Paul van Vlissingenstraat to give traffic the opportunity to drive east to west.

features.name: Wittenburgervaart
features.opening: The Wittenburgervaart is a short canal in Amsterdam, between the Oostelijke Eilanden (Eastern Islands).

facts.text: Robert Jasper Grootveld's Tire Boat artwork was placed on stilts in the water in 2012.
facts.sourceQuote: In 2012, the artwork Tire Boat (1972) by Robert Jasper Grootveld, was placed on stilts in the water on the south side at the Oostenburgerdwarsstraat next to the Ezelsbrug.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 2012, the artwork Tire Boat (1972) by Robert Jasper Grootveld, was placed on stilts in the water on the south side at the Oostenburgerdwarsstraat next to the Ezelsbrug.

facts.text: Water sports clubs Albatros and De Oostvaarders maintain a marina on the north bank.
facts.sourceQuote: On the north side on the banks of Wittenburg at the Fortuinstraat is a marina of the water sports clubs Albatros and De Oostvaarders.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: On the north side on the banks of Wittenburg at the Fortuinstraat is a marina of the water sports clubs Albatros and De Oostvaarders.

features.name: Kostverlorenvaart
features.opening: The Kostverlorenvaart in Amsterdam-West is the connection between the Schinkel and the IJ.

facts.text: The name Kostverlorenvaart (Lost Cost) arose because the sluice gates became unusable, wasting money.
facts.sourceQuote: Omdat daardoor de wetering en de sluizen onbruikbaar werden, was dit verspilling van geld ofwel verloren cost. Zo is de naam Kostverloren te verklaren.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Because as a result the sluice gates and locks became unusable, this was either a waste of money or lost cost. This is how the name Lost Cost can be explained.

facts.text: Amsterdam fiercely opposed a 1413 plan to dig locks that might let enemies flood the city.
facts.sourceQuote: Toen in 1413 Graaf Willem VI toestemming verleende om vanaf de Nieuwe Meer en de Schinkel een wetering met spuisluizen naar het IJ te graven, protesteerde Amsterdam hevig. Er bestond namelijk het gevaar dat in die roerige tijden een vijand de stad onder water kon zetten via die sluizen.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: When in 1413 Count William VI granted permission to dig a sluice gate with sluice gates from the Nieuwe Meer and the Schinkel to the IJ, Amsterdam protested fiercely. There was a danger that in those turbulent times an enemy could flood the city through those locks.

facts.text: A turnaround path called an overtoom was laid on a dam in 1515 to allow small ships to pass.
facts.sourceQuote: Om toch nog (klein) scheepvaartverkeer tussen Amsterdam en het Haarlemmermeer mogelijk te maken werd in 1515 op de dam een overhaal ('overtoom') gelegd.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In order to still make (small) shipping traffic between Amsterdam and the Haarlemmermeer possible, a turnaround ('overtoom') was laid on the dam in 1515.

features.name: Admiralengracht
features.opening: The Admiralengracht is a canal and street name in Amsterdam-West, the canal was dug in the 1920s as part of the Plan West.

facts.text: Admiralengracht honors Dutch and Zeelandish admirals from the 16th to 19th centuries.
facts.sourceQuote: De gracht kreeg zijn naam in 1924, naar de Hollandse en Zeeuwse admiraals uit de 16e, 17e, 18e en 19e eeuw, waarnaar in de omliggende wijk, de Admiralenbuurt, vele straten zijn genoemd.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The canal was named in 1924, after the Dutch and Zeelandish admirals from the 16th, 17th, 18th and 19th centuries, after which many streets in the surrounding district, the Admiralenbuurt, are named.

facts.text: Three bridges crossing this canal were built in the distinctive Amsterdam School style.
facts.sourceQuote: 381) De drie bruggen zijn alle gebouwd in de stijl van de Amsterdamse School.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: 381) The three bridges were all built in the style of the Amsterdam School.

features.name: Prins Willem-Alexandersluis
features.opening: The Oranje Locks are a group of locks and other water management facilities just east of Amsterdam.

facts.text: In 1971, eighty thousand vessels passed through while still being operated by hand.
facts.sourceQuote: In 1971 80,000 vessels passed the locks, but they were still operated by hand, requiring 42 employees.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 1971 80,000 vessels passed the locks, but they were still operated by hand, requiring 42 employees.

facts.text: The facility required forty-two employees to manually operate the gates in 1971.
facts.sourceQuote: In 1971 80,000 vessels passed the locks, but they were still operated by hand, requiring 42 employees.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 1971 80,000 vessels passed the locks, but they were still operated by hand, requiring 42 employees.

facts.text: The dam's top sat 3.5 meters above AOD, with a base width of 45 meters tapering to just 4 meters at the summit.
facts.sourceQuote: The dam through the IJ was 45 m wide at the base, and 4 m at the top. The top was 3.5 m above AOD.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The dam through the IJ was 45 m wide at the base, and 4 m at the top. The top was 3.5 m above AOD.

facts.text: Two sections of the foundational ground pieces broke later, causing considerable sinkage in the structure.
facts.sourceQuote: The first of these zinkstukken was called grondstuk, because it reposed on the bottom or ground. In two places these grondstukken would later break, causing considerable sinkage.
