facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The first of these zinkstukken was called grondstuk, because it reposed on the bottom or ground. In two places these grondstukken would later break, causing considerable sinkage.

features.name: Sint Antoniesluis
features.opening: Sint Antoniesluis or Sint Anthoniesluis can refer to: old name for the Sint Antoniessluishoogwaterkering, a lock in Amsterdam-Centrum Sint Antoniesluis…

facts.text: The name Sint Antoniesluis also appears as Sint Anthoniesluis in historical records.
facts.sourceQuote: Sint Antoniesluis of Sint Anthoniesluis kan verwijzen naar: oude naam voor de Sint Antoniessluishoogwaterkering, een sluis in Amsterdam-Centrum Sint Antoniesluis (straat), een straat op de kade van de kolk van genoemde sluis Sint Anthoniesluis (brug), een verkeersbrug over genoemde sluis Verwant zijn ook Sint Antoniesbreestraat en Sint Anthoniesdijk
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Sint Antoniesluis or Sint Anthoniesluis can refer to: old name for the Sint Antoniessluishoogwaterkering, a lock in Amsterdam-Centrum Sint Antoniesluis (street), a street on the quay of the pool of the aforementioned lock Sint Anthoniesluis (bridge), a traffic bridge over the aforementioned lock Related are also Sint Antoniesbreestraat and Sint Anthoniesdijk

features.name: Onbekendegracht
features.opening: The Onbekendegracht (Unknown Canal) is a short canal in Amsterdam, in the eastern part of the Grachtengordel (canal belt).

facts.text: The name Onbekendegracht means 'unknown canal' and was once also called Korte Amstelgrachtje.
facts.sourceQuote: The name Korte Amstelgrachtje was also in vogue. The name means 'unknown canal'.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The name Korte Amstelgrachtje was also in vogue. The name means 'unknown canal'.

facts.text: Residents requested a name change in 1948 because the current title caused confusion.
facts.sourceQuote: In 1948, residents of the Onbekendegracht asked the municipality of Amsterdam to change the name of the canal because they found it too confusing.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 1948, residents of the Onbekendegracht asked the municipality of Amsterdam to change the name of the canal because they found it too confusing.

facts.text: Buildings numbered one through five were constructed in 1906.
facts.sourceQuote: The buildings at Onbekendegracht 1–5, built in 1906 and designed by AJ Tymensen, became a monument in 2006.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The buildings at Onbekendegracht 1–5, built in 1906 and designed by AJ Tymensen, became a monument in 2006.

features.name: Ringvaart
features.opening: The Ringvaart in Amsterdam-Oost is the name of the northern and eastern part of the ring canal around the Watergraafsmeer polder, which was reclaimed in 1629.

facts.text: A section of the canal vanished in the 1980s to make way for a major highway extension.
facts.sourceQuote: Aan de oostkant is een klein deel van de ringvaart verdwenen in de jaren 80 voor de verlenging van het oostelijk deel van de Amsterdamse Ringweg (A10) naar de Zeeburgerbrug en voor het Knooppunt Watergraafsmeer, die beide in 1990 zijn gereed gekomen.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: On the east side, a small part of the ring road disappeared in the 1980s for the extension of the eastern part of the Amsterdam Ring Road (A10) to the Zeeburgerbrug and for the Watergraafsmeer Junction, which both came into operation in 1990.

features.name: Holendrecht
features.opening: Holendrecht is a residential area (neighborhood) in Gaasperdam in the Amsterdam district Amsterdam-Zuidoost.

facts.text: The district takes its name from the Holendrecht river that marks the border between North Holland and Utrecht.
facts.sourceQuote: De wijk ontleent zijn naam aan het gelijknamige riviertje op de grens van de provincies Noord-Holland en Utrecht.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The district derives its name from the river of the same name on the border of the provinces of North Holland and Utrecht.

facts.text: Relocation of families from the Bijlmermeer to Holendrecht-West began in 2004, leading to local impoverishment.
facts.sourceQuote: De sloop van de hoogbouwflats in de Bijlmermeer en de uitplaatsing van probleemgezinnen vandaar naar Holendrecht-West leidde vanaf 2004 tot een verpaupering van de wijk.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The demolition of the high-rise flats in the Bijlmermeer and the relocation of problem families from there to Holendrecht-West led from 2004 to a impoverishment of the district.

features.name: Christoffel Plantijngracht
features.opening: The Christoffel Plantijnpad (and the Christoffel Plantijngracht) in Amsterdam-Slotervaart have been named after the South Dutch printer and lexicographer…

facts.text: The namesake was a South Dutch printer and lexicographer who ran a famous publishing house in Antwerp.
facts.sourceQuote: Het Christoffel Plantijnpad (en de Christoffel Plantijngracht) in Amsterdam-Slotervaart zijn vanaf 1955 vernoemd naar de Zuid-Nederlandse boekdrukker en lexicograaf Christoffel Plantijn (1514-1589), die in Antwerpen een beroemde drukkerij en uitgeverij bezat.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Christoffel Plantijnpad (and the Christoffel Plantijngracht) in Amsterdam-Slotervaart have been named after the South Dutch printer and lexicographer Christoffel Plantijn (1514-1589), who owned a famous printing house and publishing house in Antwerp.

facts.text: A tunnel under the A4 motorway serves as both a path crossing and a wildlife passage.
facts.sourceQuote: De tunnel van het pad tussen Riekerpolder en Oude Haagseweg onder de Rijksweg A4 dient tevens als faunapassage.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The tunnel of the path between Riekerpolder and Oude Haagseweg under the A4 motorway also serves as a wildlife passage.

facts.text: The Piet Römer Bridge at the Plesmanlaan intersection became a municipal monument in 2008.
facts.sourceQuote: De Piet Römerbrug bij de kruising met de Plesmanlaan is sinds 2008 een gemeentelijk monument.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Piet Römer Bridge at the intersection with the Plesmanlaan has been a municipal monument since 2008.

facts.text: Small boats can navigate this waterway along its path.
facts.sourceQuote: Dit, voor kleine boten bevaarbare, kanaal begint in het Sloterpark aan de zuidkant van de Sloterplas, bij het "Watersporteiland", en loopt van daar in zuidelijke richting naar de waterweg Slotervaart.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: This, navigable for small boats, canal begins in the Sloterpark on the south side of the Sloterplas, near the "Water Sports Island", and runs from there in a southerly direction to the Slotervaart waterway.

facts.text: The canal runs south from the Sloterpark to meet the Slotervaart waterway.
facts.sourceQuote: Dit, voor kleine boten bevaarbare, kanaal begint in het Sloterpark aan de zuidkant van de Sloterplas, bij het "Watersporteiland", en loopt van daar in zuidelijke richting naar de waterweg Slotervaart.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: This, navigable for small boats, canal begins in the Sloterpark on the south side of the Sloterplas, near the "Water Sports Island", and runs from there in a southerly direction to the Slotervaart waterway.

features.name: Oostertoegang
features.opening: The Oostertoegang is a short canal in Amsterdam-Centrum, directly east of Central Station, that connects the IJ to the Geldersekade and the Open Havenfront…

facts.text: The canal dates to the Station Island construction between 1870 and 1880.
facts.sourceQuote: De Oostertoegang bestaat sinds de aanleg van het Stationseiland tussen 1870 en 1880.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Oostertoegang has existed since the construction of the Station Island between 1870 and 1880.

facts.text: A wide traffic bridge replaced a historic drawbridge that could no longer handle traffic.
facts.sourceQuote: Over de Oostertoegang ligt een complex aan bruggen, van noord naar zuid: Brug 2274, een fiets- en voetgangersbrug Brug 486, een brede verkeersbrug die in plaats kwam van de brug 276, een historische hefbrug die het verkeer niet meer aan kon Trambrug voor lijn 26, in eerste instantie een aparte brug, maar in de 21e eeuw geïntegreerd in brug 486 Een complex van spoorbruggen Brug 228, een fiets- en voetgangersbrug tussen de Oosterdokskade en het Stationseiland.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Over the Oostertoegang lies a complex of bridges, from north to south: Bridge 2274, a bicycle and pedestrian bridge Bridge 486, a wide traffic bridge that replaced bridge 276, a historic drawbridge that could no longer handle traffic Tram bridge for line 26, initially a separate bridge, but integrated into bridge 486 in the 21st century A complex of railway bridges Bridge 228, a bicycle and pedestrian bridge between the Oosterdokskade and the Stationseiland.

facts.text: Tram line 26 originally used a separate bridge before integrating into the main traffic structure in the 21st century.
facts.sourceQuote: Over de Oostertoegang ligt een complex aan bruggen, van noord naar zuid: Brug 2274, een fiets- en voetgangersbrug Brug 486, een brede verkeersbrug die in plaats kwam van de brug 276, een historische hefbrug die het verkeer niet meer aan kon Trambrug voor lijn 26, in eerste instantie een aparte brug, maar in de 21e eeuw geïntegreerd in brug 486 Een complex van spoorbruggen Brug 228, een fiets- en voetgangersbrug tussen de Oosterdokskade en het Stationseiland.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Over the Oostertoegang lies a complex of bridges, from north to south: Bridge 2274, a bicycle and pedestrian bridge Bridge 486, a wide traffic bridge that replaced bridge 276, a historic drawbridge that could no longer handle traffic Tram bridge for line 26, initially a separate bridge, but integrated into bridge 486 in the 21st century A complex of railway bridges Bridge 228, a bicycle and pedestrian bridge between the Oosterdokskade and the Stationseiland.

features.name: Reguliersgracht
features.opening: Reguliersgracht is a canal in Amsterdam, Netherlands.

facts.text: The canal was established in 1658 within Amsterdam's historic Grachtengordel.
facts.sourceQuote: Established in 1658, it is located in the Grachtengordel, in the Centrum borough.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Established in 1658, it is located in the Grachtengordel, in the Centrum borough.

facts.text: During WWII, the illegal paper Het Parool operated from house number 111 there.
facts.sourceQuote: During World War II the "nerve center" of the illegal paper Het Parool was housed there, in a house (number 111) occupied by Simon Carmiggelt, Max Nord, Wim van Norden and their families.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: During World War II the "nerve center" of the illegal paper Het Parool was housed there, in a house (number 111) occupied by Simon Carmiggelt, Max Nord, Wim van Norden and their families.

facts.text: Writer Simon Carmiggelt and his family occupied that specific house during the war.
facts.sourceQuote: During World War II the "nerve center" of the illegal paper Het Parool was housed there, in a house (number 111) occupied by Simon Carmiggelt, Max Nord, Wim van Norden and their families.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: During World War II the "nerve center" of the illegal paper Het Parool was housed there, in a house (number 111) occupied by Simon Carmiggelt, Max Nord, Wim van Norden and their families.

features.name: Spiegelgracht
features.opening: The Spiegelgracht (Dutch: [ˈspi.ɣəlɣrɑxt], mirror canal) is a canal in the centre of Amsterdam, located near the Prinsengracht.

facts.text: The Dutch name Spiegelgracht translates to mirror canal.
facts.sourceQuote: The Spiegelgracht (Dutch: [ˈspi.ɣəlɣrɑxt], mirror canal) is a canal in the centre of Amsterdam, located near the Prinsengracht.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Spiegelgracht (Dutch: [ˈspi.ɣəlɣrɑxt], mirror canal) is a canal in the centre of Amsterdam, located near the Prinsengracht.

facts.text: Construction of this waterway began during the sixteenth century.
facts.sourceQuote: Built in the 16th century, it is a part of the Canals of Amsterdam which have been designated as UNESCO World Heritage Sites.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Built in the 16th century, it is a part of the Canals of Amsterdam which have been designated as UNESCO World Heritage Sites.

features.name: Marinehaven
features.opening: A naval harbour is a seaport the armed forces use to station warships or submarines.

facts.text: Strict guards protect the site due to stored ammunition and potential attack threats.
facts.sourceQuote: Deze haven wordt dan ook streng bewaakt, omdat hier munitie ligt voor schepen, maar ook voor een mogelijke aanval of een terroristische aanslag.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: This port is therefore strictly guarded, because there is ammunition here for ships, but also for a possible attack or terrorist attack.

facts.text: Facilities often include administrative buildings, helicopter platforms, or an associated airport.
facts.sourceQuote: Meestal hebben deze havens ook administratieve gebouwen, helikopterplatforms of een bijhorend vliegveld.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Most of the time, these ports also have administrative buildings, helicopter platforms or an associated airport.

facts.text: Unlike Zeebrugge, Marinehaven is a dedicated naval harbor used exclusively by military ships.
facts.sourceQuote: Een gewone marinehaven, deze wordt alleen gebruikt voor marineschepen.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: A regular naval harbor, this is only used for naval ships.

features.name: Kattenburgervaart
features.opening: The Kattenburgervaart is a short canal in Amsterdam that runs through the Oostelijke Eilanden (Eastern Islands).

facts.text: The Kattenburgervaart separates Wittenburg, an island built in the 17th century.
facts.sourceQuote: The canal separates the island of Wittenburg, which was built in the 17th century, from the island of Kattenburg.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The canal separates the island of Wittenburg, which was built in the 17th century, from the island of Kattenburg.

facts.text: The Kippebrug is a fixed bridge for cyclists dating to 1923.
facts.sourceQuote: Four bridges cross the canal: the Paerlduiker (bridge number 91) at the Nieuwe Vaart, between the Wittenburgergracht and Kattenburgergracht streets, which form part of the so-called Eilandboulevard. the Kippebrug (bridge number 270), a fixed bridge for cyclists from 1923 in the Wittenburgerkade. the Witte Katbrug (bridge number 1914), an arched bridge for pedestrians and cyclists in the Jacob Burggraafstraat. the Zebrabrug (bridge number 389), in the Derde Wittenburgerdwarsstraat.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Four bridges cross the canal: the Paerlduiker (bridge number 91) at the Nieuwe Vaart, between the Wittenburgergracht and Kattenburgergracht streets, which form part of the so-called Eilandboulevard. the Kippebrug (bridge number 270), a fixed bridge for cyclists from 1923 in the Wittenburgerkade. the Witte Katbrug (bridge number 1914), an arched bridge for pedestrians and cyclists in the Jacob Burggraafstraat. the Zebrabrug (bridge number 389), in the Derde Wittenburgerdwarsstraat.

facts.text: One missing bridge was historically known as the Worm bridge.
facts.sourceQuote: The missing bridges are numbers 268 and 269, the last of which was also known as the Worm bridge .
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The missing bridges are numbers 268 and 269, the last of which was also known as the Worm bridge .

features.name: Westerdoksluis
features.opening: The Westerdoksluis is a bascule bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum.

facts.text: Engineer Dick Slebos designed the new structure while working for the Department of Public Works.
facts.sourceQuote: Het ontwerp daarvan kwam van Dick Slebos werkend bij de Dienst der Publieke Werken.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The design of it came from Dick Slebos working at the Department of Public Works.

facts.text: The massive 285-ton steel vessel was manufactured by Constructiewerkplaats NV on Valkenweg.
facts.sourceQuote: Het (voor die tijd) enorme stalen gevaarte van 285 ton werd vervaardigd door Constructiewerkplaats NV, die gevestigd was aan de Valkenweg in Amsterdam-Noord.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The (at that time) enormous steel vessel of 285 tons was manufactured by Constructiewerkplaats NV, which was located on Valkenweg in Amsterdam-North.

features.name: Ringvaart van de Haarlemmermeerpolder
features.opening: The Ringvaart (known in full as Ringvaart of the Haarlemmermeer Polder) is a canal in the province of North Holland, the Netherlands.

facts.text: Ringvaart van de Haarlemmermeerpolder means "ring canal" in Dutch.
facts.sourceQuote: The Ringvaart (Dutch meaning "ring canal") is a true circular canal surrounding the Haarlemmermeer polder and forms the boundary of the Haarlemmermeer municipality.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Ringvaart (Dutch meaning "ring canal") is a true circular canal surrounding the Haarlemmermeer polder and forms the boundary of the Haarlemmermeer municipality.

facts.text: Construction began in 1839 to reclaim land from the lake known as Haarlem's Lake.
facts.sourceQuote: Construction of the canal began in 1839 as the first step to reclaim land from Haarlemmermeer (Dutch for Haarlem's Lake). Thousands of laborers dug a canal through the existing land, as much as possible closely following the lake's contour.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Construction of the canal began in 1839 as the first step to reclaim land from Haarlemmermeer (Dutch for Haarlem's Lake). Thousands of laborers dug a canal through the existing land, as much as possible closely following the lake's contour.

facts.text: Three sections of the canal were dug through peninsulas that later became part of the polder.
facts.sourceQuote: But at three locations (Vijfhuizen, Lisserbroek, and Huigsloot), the Ringvaart was dug through peninsulas which thereafter became part of Haarlemmermeer.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: But at three locations (Vijfhuizen, Lisserbroek, and Huigsloot), the Ringvaart was dug through peninsulas which thereafter became part of Haarlemmermeer.

facts.text: The main dike of Amsterdam's defense line runs diagonally across the polder, crossing the Ringvaart van de Haarlemmermeerpolder twice.
facts.sourceQuote: The main dike of the Stelling van Amsterdam runs diagonally across the Haarlemmermeer polder and crosses the Ringvaart twice.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The main dike of the Stelling van Amsterdam runs diagonally across the Haarlemmermeer polder and crosses the Ringvaart twice.

facts.text: Fort Vijfhuizen sits directly on the Ringvaart van de Haarlemmermeerpolder and now hosts art exhibitions.
facts.sourceQuote: Fort Vijfhuizen located on the Ringvaart is used for art exhibitions.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Fort Vijfhuizen located on the Ringvaart is used for art exhibitions.

features.name: Beulingsloot
features.opening: The Beulingsloot is one of the oldest and shortest canals in Amsterdam-Centrum.

facts.text: Gerrit Jansz Beulinck lived here around 1660 and displayed a signboard with his name.
facts.sourceQuote: Wiersma stelt dat de naam afkomstig is van een voormalige bewoner, Gerrit Jansz Beulinck, die hier rond 1660 gewoond heeft. Hij zou zijn aanwezigheid kenbaar hebben gemaakt door een uithangbord waar "de Beuling uithing".
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Wiersma states that the name comes from an former resident, Gerrit Jansz Beulinck, who lived here around 1660. He would have made his presence known by a signboard where "the Beuling was hanging".

facts.text: Unlike most Amsterdam canals, this waterway has no guard gates.
facts.sourceQuote: De Beulingsloot is atypisch voor Amsterdam daar het een kadeloze gracht is.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Beulingsloot is atypical for Amsterdam because it is an unguarded canal.

features.name: Oosterdok
features.opening: The Oosterdok ('Eastern Dock') is a former wet dock in Amsterdam.

facts.text: Prince Willem laid the first stone for the lock on June 11, 1830.
facts.sourceQuote: Foundation work for the lock started before the first stone was laid by on 11 June 1830 by Prince Willem, the later King William III.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Foundation work for the lock started before the first stone was laid by on 11 June 1830 by Prince Willem, the later King William III.

facts.text: The double lock featured a small chamber finished before the large ocean-going one opened in 1832.
facts.sourceQuote: It was a double lock, the small lock was finished early. The big lock for ocean-going ships was opened with solemn festivities in 1832.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: It was a double lock, the small lock was finished early. The big lock for ocean-going ships was opened with solemn festivities in 1832.

facts.text: The western dyke end called Oosterdam was removed in the late 2010s to improve views.
facts.sourceQuote: The western end of this dyke was until recently called Oosterdam. It was removed in the late 2010s in order to improve the visual quality of the area.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The western end of this dyke was until recently called Oosterdam. It was removed in the late 2010s in order to improve the visual quality of the area.

facts.text: Construction of this deep port occurred between 1831 and 1832.
facts.sourceQuote: It was created in 1831–1832 by constructing the Oosterdoksdam and the Oosterdoksluis, forming a reliable deep port closed off from the tidal IJ.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: It was created in 1831–1832 by constructing the Oosterdoksdam and the Oosterdoksluis, forming a reliable deep port closed off from the tidal IJ.

facts.text: Engineers built the Oosterdoksdam and Oosterdoksluis to close the dock from tidal waters.
facts.sourceQuote: It was created in 1831–1832 by constructing the Oosterdoksdam and the Oosterdoksluis, forming a reliable deep port closed off from the tidal IJ.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: It was created in 1831–1832 by constructing the Oosterdoksdam and the Oosterdoksluis, forming a reliable deep port closed off from the tidal IJ.

features.name: Zuider Amstelkanaal
features.opening: The Zuider Amstelkanaal is a canal in Amsterdam-Zuid.

facts.text: The canal is absent from postcode books because its quays and streets have mismatched names.
facts.sourceQuote: Doordat de kades en de daarop liggende straten afwijkende namen heeft komt het kanaal niet voor in postcodeboeken.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Because the quays and the streets on them have different names, the canal does not appear in postcode books.

facts.text: Tram lines 5 and 24 cross the canal on two of its eight bridges.
facts.sourceQuote: Over het Zuider Amstelkanaal liggen acht bruggen: Apollolaan/Muzenplein -Hildo Kropbrug (brug 419) Diepenbrockstraat - brug 418 Beethovenstraat - Joep Langebrug, hier rijdt tramlijn 5 overheen Minervalaan - brug 416, voetgangers- en fietsersbrug Parnassusweg - brug 415 Achillesstraat - Locatellikade - brug 414, voetgangers- en fietsersbrug Stadionkade bij Jasonstraat - brug 421, voetgangersbrug Amstelveenseweg - Aldo van Eyckbrug (brug 413), hier rijdt tramlijn 24 overheen
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: There are eight bridges over the Zuider Amstelkanaal: Apollolaan/Muzenplein -Hildo Kropbrug (bridge 419) Diepenbrockstraat - bridge 418 Beethovenstraat - Joep Langebrug, tram line 5 runs over here Minervalaan - bridge 416, pedestrian and cyclist bridge Parnassusweg - bridge 415 Achillesstraat - Locatellikade - bridge 414, pedestrian and cyclist bridge Stadionkade near Jasonstraat - bridge 421, pedestrian bridge Amstelveenseweg - Aldo van Eyckbrug (bridge 413), tram line 24 runs over here

features.name: Oudezijds Achterburgwal
features.opening: The Oudezijds Achterburgwal, often abbreviated to OZ Achterburgwal, is a street and canal in De Wallen, the red light district in the center of Amsterdam.

facts.text: Before 1578, this street hosted nineteen monasteries, including sixteen for women and three for men.
facts.sourceQuote: Before the Alteratie (Alteration) in 1578 there were many monasteries in this neighborhood. There were 16 women's monasteries and three male monasteries in Amsterdam, most of them on Oudezijds Achterburgwal.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Before the Alteratie (Alteration) in 1578 there were many monasteries in this neighborhood. There were 16 women's monasteries and three male monasteries in Amsterdam, most of them on Oudezijds Achterburgwal.

facts.text: A book market has been held along this canal for centuries.
facts.sourceQuote: A book market has been held in this for centuries .
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: A book market has been held in this for centuries .

facts.text: The Walloon Church was consecrated in 1496 after replacing a chapel destroyed in 1452.
facts.sourceQuote: The Walloon Church, originally the chapel of the Paulusbroedersklooster. This chapel, consecrated in 1496, replaced an earlier chapel that was probably destroyed in the town fire of 1452.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Walloon Church, originally the chapel of the Paulusbroedersklooster. This chapel, consecrated in 1496, replaced an earlier chapel that was probably destroyed in the town fire of 1452.

features.name: Amerikahaven
features.opening: The Amerikahaven is a port in the Amsterdam port area.

facts.text: Construction of this port basin began during the 1960s.
facts.sourceQuote: De haven werd gegraven in de jaren zestig en ligt aan de zuidkant van het Noordzeekanaal, in de vroegere Groote IJpolder, ten oosten van het vroegere Zijkanaal F.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The port was dug in the 1960s and is located on the south side of the North Sea Canal, in the former Groote IJpolder, east of the former Zijkanaal F.

facts.text: The complex includes distinct basins named Australia, Asia, Tasmania, Texas, Cocoa, and Alaska.
facts.sourceQuote: De haven in Westpoort bestaat uit verschillende havenbekkens: de Australiëhaven, de Aziëhaven, de Tasmaniëhaven, de Texashaven, de Cacaohaven en de Alaskahaven.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The port in Westpoort consists of several port basins: the Australia port, the Asia port, the Tasmania port, the Texas port, the Cocoa port and the Alaska port.

facts.text: Cargo processing here handles everything from oil and coal to vegetable oils and food products.
facts.sourceQuote: Verder worden in de haven olie, kolen, voedselproducten en plantaardige oliën verwerkt.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In addition, oil, coal, food products and vegetable oils are processed in the port.

facts.text: Cranes on both sides allowed ships to be loaded and unloaded extra quickly.
facts.sourceQuote: De plannen bestonden uit een insteekhaven, de huidige Alaskahaven, met containerkranen aan beide zijden. Schepen konden extra snel worden gelost en geladen omdat aan beide zijden de kranen hun werk konden doen.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The plans consisted of a terminal port, the current Alaska Harbor, with container cranes on both sides. Ships could be unloaded and loaded extra quickly because the cranes could work on both sides.

facts.text: In its first three years, only one ship with empty containers ever tested the facility.
facts.sourceQuote: De hooggespannen verwachtingen kwamen niet uit. In de eerste drie jaar dat de terminal in bedrijf was, kwam er slechts een containerschip met lege containers om de terminal te testen.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The high expectations did not come true. In the first three years that the terminal was in operation, only one container ship with empty containers came to test the terminal.

facts.text: The company dissolved in 2012 after attempts to use it for inland waterways failed.
facts.sourceQuote: Pogingen om er een overslagterminal voor de binnenvaart van te maken, liepen op niets uit. In 2012 werd het bedrijf opgeheven en sindsdien wordt het terrein niet gebruikt.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Attempts to turn it into a transhipment terminal for inland waterways failed. The company was dissolved in 2012 and since then the premises have not been used.

features.name: Postjeswetering
features.opening: The Postjeswetering in Amsterdam-West was built in its current form in the 1920s as part of Plan West.

facts.text: In 1954, the canal was raised from polder level to city center height after connecting to the Kostverlorenvaart.
facts.sourceQuote: Tot 1954 lag de gracht op het polderpeil van de Sloterpolder (NAP -2,10 m). Daarna werd de gracht verbonden met de Kostverlorenvaart en verhoogd naar het stadsboezempeil (NAP -0,40 m).
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Until 1954, the canal was at the polder level of the Sloterpolder (NAP -2.10 m). After that, the canal was connected to the Kostverlorenvaart and raised to the city center level (NAP -0.40 m).

facts.text: Amsterdam's thousandth bridge, installed in 1973, spans this waterway near Rembrandtpark.
facts.sourceQuote: De duizendste brug van Amsterdam (brug nr. 684; in gebruik genomen in 1973) ligt over de Postjeswetering bij het Rembrandtpark.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The thousandth bridge of Amsterdam (bridge no. 684; put into use in 1973) is located over the Postjeswetering near the Rembrandtpark.

features.name: Nieuwe Vaart
features.opening: The Nieuwe Vaart or Nieuwevaart is a 17th-century canal in Amsterdam that runs from the center to Amsterdam-Oost (Amsterdam East).

facts.text: Residents could isolate the island by lifting the Kattenburger bridge during the 1787 Bijltjesoproer riot.
facts.sourceQuote: By lifting this Kattenburger bridge, the residents could shut themselves off from the outside world. This came in handy with the Bijltjesoproer, a riot in 1787 by Orangist ship carpenters in Kattenburg against the patriot city council.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: By lifting this Kattenburger bridge, the residents could shut themselves off from the outside world. This came in handy with the Bijltjesoproer, a riot in 1787 by Orangist ship carpenters in Kattenburg against the patriot city council.

facts.text: In 1917, stone-throwing women followed a potato barge through the canal before police fired into the air.
facts.sourceQuote: The Nieuwe Vaart also played a role in the 1917 Potato riots. A barge with potatoes was sent via the Nieuwe Vaart to the Entrepotdok on 30 June. A group of women followed the barge and started throwing stones, at which mounted police started shooting in the air.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Nieuwe Vaart also played a role in the 1917 Potato riots. A barge with potatoes was sent via the Nieuwe Vaart to the Entrepotdok on 30 June. A group of women followed the barge and started throwing stones, at which mounted police started shooting in the air.

facts.text: The canal was dug in 1649 to fix silting problems caused by the island crossing much of the IJ.
facts.sourceQuote: The island crossed so much of the IJ that silting problems arose. The Nieuwe Vaart canal was dug in 1649 to ensure a good flow of water.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The island crossed so much of the IJ that silting problems arose. The Nieuwe Vaart canal was dug in 1649 to ensure a good flow of water.

facts.text: A houseboat association formed in 2011 after city plans threatened to remove most berths from the western section.
facts.sourceQuote: The Nieuwe Vaart Association was established in January 2011. This association represents the interests of the residents of houseboats in the western part of the Nieuwe Vaart. The association was founded by houseboat residents as a result of redevelopment plans by the Centrum district, where most of the berths for houseboats in the Nieuwe Vaart would disappear.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Nieuwe Vaart Association was established in January 2011. This association represents the interests of the residents of houseboats in the western part of the Nieuwe Vaart. The association was founded by houseboat residents as a result of redevelopment plans by the Centrum district, where most of the berths for houseboats in the Nieuwe Vaart would disappear.

facts.text: The Kromhout Museum sits directly on the Nieuwe Vaart canal.
facts.sourceQuote: Kromhout Museum is located on the Nieuwe Vaart.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Kromhout Museum is located on the Nieuwe Vaart.

facts.text: The Westkap shipyard remains active while its Oosthal now serves as a museum.
facts.sourceQuote: On this site, the Westkap is still used as a shipyard, but the Oosthal is furnished as a museum.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: On this site, the Westkap is still used as a shipyard, but the Oosthal is furnished as a museum.

features.name: Lijnbaansgracht
features.opening: Lijnbaansgracht (Dutch pronunciation: [ˈlɛimbaːnsˌxrɑxt]) is a partly filled-in canal in Amsterdam which bends beyond the boundary of the center,…

facts.text: Construction began in 1612 during the initial phase of building the canal belt.
facts.sourceQuote: Construction of the canal started in 1612 during the first stages of the construction of the canal belt.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Construction of the canal started in 1612 during the first stages of the construction of the canal belt.

facts.text: The canal runs parallel to the Singelgracht between the Brouwersgracht and Reguliersgracht.
facts.sourceQuote: The canal runs parallel to the Singelgracht, between the Brouwersgracht and the Reguliersgracht.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The canal runs parallel to the Singelgracht, between the Brouwersgracht and the Reguliersgracht.

facts.text: A portion of this waterway has been filled in over time.
facts.sourceQuote: Lijnbaansgracht (Dutch pronunciation: [ˈlɛimbaːnsˌxrɑxt]) is a partly filled-in canal in Amsterdam which bends beyond the boundary of the center, Amsterdam-Centrum.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Lijnbaansgracht (Dutch pronunciation: [ˈlɛimbaːnsˌxrɑxt]) is a partly filled-in canal in Amsterdam which bends beyond the boundary of the center, Amsterdam-Centrum.

features.name: Geldersekade
features.opening: The Geldersekade is a canal and a street in Amsterdam that connects the Nieuwmarkt with the Prins Hendrikkade.

facts.text: A stone fish hall replaced wooden sheds on the water in 1862 before being demolished in 1938.
facts.sourceQuote: A fish market was built after 1840 in the water of the Geldersekade, on the north side of the Nieuwmarkt. It replaced the fish market on Dam Square, which had to make way for the Beurs van Zocher. The scaffolding and wooden sheds were replaced in 1862 by the stone Gemeentelijke Vishal, which was demolished in 1938.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: A fish market was built after 1840 in the water of the Geldersekade, on the north side of the Nieuwmarkt. It replaced the fish market on Dam Square, which had to make way for the Beurs van Zocher. The scaffolding and wooden sheds were replaced in 1862 by the stone Gemeentelijke Vishal, which was demolished in 1938.

features.name: Oudeschans
features.opening: The Oudeschans, or Oude Schans (Old Rampart), originally the Nieuwe Gracht, is a wide canal in the eastern part of the inner city of Amsterdam.

facts.text: The Oudeschans was originally named Nieuwe Gracht when an arm of the Amstel was dug out between 1515 and 1518.
facts.sourceQuote: Between 1515 and 1518 an armof the Amstel was dug out, the Zwanenburgwal, leading to the Nieuwe Gracht, as the Oudeschans was then called.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Between 1515 and 1518 an armof the Amstel was dug out, the Zwanenburgwal, leading to the Nieuwe Gracht, as the Oudeschans was then called.

facts.text: In 1602 a lock was built to allow ships to sail from the Oudeschans to the Amstel via the Zwanenburgwal.
facts.sourceQuote: In 1602 a channel was cut through the Sint Antoniesdijk on the south side of the Oudeschans, and the Sint Antoniesluis (a lock) was built so that ships could sail to the Amstel via the Zwanenburgwal.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 1602 a channel was cut through the Sint Antoniesdijk on the south side of the Oudeschans, and the Sint Antoniesluis (a lock) was built so that ships could sail to the Amstel via the Zwanenburgwal.

facts.text: A rumor of ghosts in 1833 earned the Oudeschans the nickname the ghost quay.
facts.sourceQuote: In 1833, after a rumor that ghosts had been seen, the Oudeschans was nicknamed the ghost quay.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 1833, after a rumor that ghosts had been seen, the Oudeschans was nicknamed the ghost quay.

facts.text: Naturalist Jan Swammerdam lived at number 18, where his father ran a pharmacy with a natural history collection.
facts.sourceQuote: Jan Swammerdam lived at Oudeschans 18, where his father, who was known for his natural history collection, had a pharmacy .
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Jan Swammerdam lived at Oudeschans 18, where his father, who was known for his natural history collection, had a pharmacy .

facts.text: Painter Willem Witsen rented the studio at number 5 between 1887 and 1888, previously occupied by George Hendrik Breitner.
facts.sourceQuote: Between 1887 and 1888, the painter Willem Witsen rented the studio in Oudeschans 5 formerly used by George Hendrik Breitner.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Between 1887 and 1888, the painter Willem Witsen rented the studio in Oudeschans 5 formerly used by George Hendrik Breitner.

features.name: Bilderdijkgracht
features.opening: The Bilderdijkgracht is a canal in Amsterdam-West, named after poet and historian Willem Bilderdijk.

facts.text: Catholics once bought bread at the Assumptio bakery complex opposite a warehouse entrance.
facts.sourceQuote: Tegenover de ingang van de remise lag het complex van Bakkerijfabriek Assumptio, alwaar katholieken hun brood konden kopen (in plaats bij de socialistische bakkers in de buurt).
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Opposite the entrance to the warehouse was the complex of Bakkerijfabriek Assumptio, where Catholics could buy their bread (instead of from the socialist bakers nearby).

facts.text: The canal honors Willem Bilderdijk, a noted poet and historian.
facts.sourceQuote: De Bilderdijkgracht is een gracht in Amsterdam-West, vernoemd naar dichter en geschiedschrijver Willem Bilderdijk.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Bilderdijkgracht is a canal in Amsterdam-West, named after poet and historian Willem Bilderdijk.

features.name: Rapenburgwal
features.opening: The Rapenburgwal (Dutch pronunciation: [ˈraːpə(m)ˌbʏr(ə)xʋɑl]) is a canal in Amsterdam in the east of the Amsterdam-Centrum district, in the Lastage…

facts.text: Bridge 281, known as Peperbrug, crosses the canal's center section.
facts.sourceQuote: It is crossed in its center section by Bridge 281, Peperbrug, which connects Nieuwe Uilenburgerstraat on Uilenburg island to Peperstraat on Marken (Valkenburg) island.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: It is crossed in its center section by Bridge 281, Peperbrug, which connects Nieuwe Uilenburgerstraat on Uilenburg island to Peperstraat on Marken (Valkenburg) island.

facts.text: A 1737 map shows the waterway once extended further east to Markengracht.
facts.sourceQuote: A 1737 map shows that the canal once ran further east to the Markengracht, which was back-filled in 1968 during construction of the IJtunnel.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: A 1737 map shows that the canal once ran further east to the Markengracht, which was back-filled in 1968 during construction of the IJtunnel.

facts.text: The eastern extension of this canal was back-filled in 1968 during tunnel construction.
facts.sourceQuote: A 1737 map shows that the canal once ran further east to the Markengracht, which was back-filled in 1968 during construction of the IJtunnel.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: A 1737 map shows that the canal once ran further east to the Markengracht, which was back-filled in 1968 during construction of the IJtunnel.

features.name: Nieuwe Diep
features.opening: The Nieuwe Diep is a lake in Amsterdam-Oost, between the IJ and the Watergraafsmeer.

facts.text: The Amsterdam-Rhine Canal splits the lake into two distinct sections.
facts.sourceQuote: Door het Amsterdam-Rijnkanaal, wordt het meer in twee stukken gedeeld: het westelijke Benedendiep ligt tegen het Flevopark aan, het oostelijke Bovendiep ligt tegen de Diemerzeedijk aan.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Due to the Amsterdam-Rhine Canal, the lake is divided into two parts: the western Benedendiep lies against the Flevopark, the eastern Bovendiep lies against the Diemerzeedijk.

facts.text: A 1422 breakthrough of the Zuiderzee created this lake through the Diemerzeedijk.
facts.sourceQuote: Door een doorbraak van de Zuiderzee door de Diemerzeedijk in 1422 ontstond het meer.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The lake was created by a breakthrough of the Zuiderzee through the Diemerzeedijk in 1422.

facts.text: The 1651 Saint Peter's Flood caused new flooding in what is now Flevopark via Nieuwe Diep.
facts.sourceQuote: In 1651 bij de Sint-Pietersvloed was er een nieuwe doorbraak, waardoor via het Nieuwe Diep een deel van wat nu het Flevopark en de Indische buurt is, overstroomde.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 1651 during the Saint Peter's Flood there was a new breakthrough, causing part of what is now the Flevopark and the Indian neighborhood to flood through the Nieuwe Diep.

facts.text: Completion of the Merwedekanaal in 1892 split the lake into two distinct parts.
facts.sourceQuote: Door de aanleg van het toenmalige Merwedekanaal, dat 1892 klaar was, is het meer in twee stukken gedeeld.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Due to the construction of the then-existing Merwedekanaal, which was completed in 1892, the lake was divided into two parts.

facts.text: Since 1952, this waterway has served as a section of the Amsterdam-Rhine Canal.
facts.sourceQuote: Dit deel van het kanaal maakt sinds 1952 deel uit van het Amsterdam-Rijnkanaal.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: This part of the canal has been part of the Amsterdam-Rhine Canal since 1952.

features.name: Nieuwe Meer
features.opening: The Nieuwe Meer (or 'the' Nieuwe Meer) is a narrow lake southwest of Amsterdam.

facts.text: A motorboat ferry named Helena connects the north and south banks on Sundays from April to October.
facts.sourceQuote: Op zondagen tussen april en oktober is er een veerverbinding met motorschip 'Helena' tussen de noord- en zuidoever.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: On Sundays between April and October there is a ferry connection with motorboat 'Helena' between the north and south banks.

features.name: Schinkel
features.opening: The Schinkel is a small canalized river in Amsterdam, in the Dutch province of North Holland.

facts.text: A dam blocked the river in 1434 to stop shipping, forcing vessels to take a long detour via Spaarndam.
facts.sourceQuote: Op last van de Graaf van Holland, werd echter in 1434 al een dam in de Schinkel gemaakt, zodat er geen scheepvaart plaats kon vinden. Schepen moesten, volgens de door graaf verleende rechten, de voorgeschreven route via Spaarndam volgen om bij het IJ te komen.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: However, at the request of the Count of Holland, a dam was already built in the Schinkel in 1434, so that no shipping could take place. According to the rights granted by the count, ships had to follow the prescribed route via Spaarndam to reach the IJ.

facts.text: In 1515, a drawbridge called an overtoom was built where only small ships could be pulled across manually.
facts.sourceQuote: Over deze dam werd in 1515 een overhaal of overtoom gemaakt, waar alleen kleine schepen overheen getrokken mochten worden.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 1515, a drawbridge or overtoom was built over this dam, where only small ships were allowed to be pulled over it.

facts.text: Unlike city canals, the Schinkel still actively transports goods today.
facts.sourceQuote: De Schinkel wordt nog steeds gebruikt voor goederenvervoer over het water, een functie die de stadsgrachten verloren hebben.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Schinkel is still used for goods transport over the water, a function that the city canals have lost.

facts.text: A large community of living boats has settled near the lock on this waterway.
facts.sourceQuote: Nabij de schutsluis ligt een 'woonbotendorp', een grote concentratie woonboten.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Near the lock is a 'living boat village', a large concentration of living boats.

facts.text: Since 1958, a statue honoring Jan Meefout has stood on the riverbank.
facts.sourceQuote: Op de oever ter hoogte van het IJsbaanpad staat sinds 1958 een beeld van Jan Meefout.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Since 1958, a statue of Jan Meefout has stood on the bank near the Ice Skating Path.

features.name: Minervahaven
features.opening: The Minervahaven is a harbor basin in the port of Amsterdam.

facts.text: In May 1941, two English deserters and two others fled to England using a seaplane moored here.
facts.sourceQuote: In mei 1941 vluchtten Jan Beelaerts van Blokland, Govert Steen en nog twee Engelandvaarders naar Engeland met een Fokker T.VIIIw watervliegtuig dat in de Minervahaven lag afgemeerd.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In May 1941, Jan Beelaerts van Blokland, Govert Steen and two more English deserters fled to England with an Fokker T.VIII seaplane that was moored in the Minervahaven.

facts.text: For a long time this basin served as a dumping ground for wood alongside a processing industry.
facts.sourceQuote: De haven werd lange tijd gebruikt voor houtoverslag en er was houtverwerkende industrie gevestigd.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The port was used for wood dumping for a long time and there was a wood processing industry established.

features.name: Leidsegracht
features.opening: The Leidsegracht (Dutch pronunciation: [ˈlɛitsəˌɣrɑxt]) is a canal in Amsterdam, Netherlands.

facts.text: The canal received its name, Leidsegracht, in 1658 after the city of Leiden.
facts.sourceQuote: The canal got its name in 1658 and is named after the city of Leiden.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The canal got its name in 1658 and is named after the city of Leiden.

facts.text: Hydraulic engineer Cornelis Lely was born at number 39 on this canal.
facts.sourceQuote: Cornelis Lely (1854–1929), the hydraulic engineer, governor and minister who made the original plans for the reclamation of the Zuiderzee, was born on Leidsegracht no. 39.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Cornelis Lely (1854–1929), the hydraulic engineer, governor and minister who made the original plans for the reclamation of the Zuiderzee, was born on Leidsegracht no. 39.

features.name: Petroleumhaven
features.opening: The Petroleumhaven is a port in the Amsterdam port area.

facts.text: Amsterdam women refused to store petroleum in the city due to fire risks in 1862.
facts.sourceQuote: De aanleiding was de weigering van de Amsterdamse vemen in 1862 om petroleum op te slaan vanwege het brandgevaar.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The reason was the refusal of the Amsterdam women in 1862 to store petroleum due to the fire risk.

facts.text: The harbor was built in a horseshoe shape so its entrance could be quickly closed during accidents.
facts.sourceQuote: De haven werd aangelegd in een hoefijzervorm, zodat bij een ongeval de ingang snel kon worden afgesloten.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The harbor was built in a horseshoe shape, so that in the event of an accident, the entrance could be quickly closed.

facts.text: British forces set fuel tanks on fire in 1940 to prevent supplies from falling into German hands.
facts.sourceQuote: Op 14 mei 1940 werden de brandstoftanks aan de Petroleumhaven door de Britten in brand gestoken. De Duitse inval noodzaakte de Britten vernietigingsploegen te sturen naar de Amsterdamse en Rotterdamse havens om te voorkomen dat de benzinevoorraden in Duitse handen zouden vallen.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: On May 14, 1940, the fuel tanks at Petroleumhaven were set on fire by the British. The German invasion forced the British to send destruction teams to the Amsterdam and Rotterdam harbors to prevent the gasoline supplies from falling into German hands.

facts.text: Ships drawing up to 10.5 meters can dock at this terminal for loading or unloading operations.
facts.sourceQuote: Zeeschepen met een diepgang van maximaal 10,5 meter kunnen bij de terminal aanleggen.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Seagoing ships with a maximum draft of 10.5 meters can dock at the terminal.

facts.text: Vopak operated the facility until mid-2013 before ownership transferred to FinCo.
facts.sourceQuote: De terminal was tot medio 2013 in handen van Vopak en is nu in handen van FinCo.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The terminal was in the hands of Vopak until mid-2013 and is now in the hands of FinCo.

facts.text: Maritime Waste Collection Netherlands processes bilge water leaking from ship engine rooms here.
facts.sourceQuote: Verder wordt in de haven bilgewater en afgewerkte olie verwerkt door Maritieme Afvalstoffen Inzameling Nederland (MAIN). Bilgewater is met olie verontreinigd water dat onder in de machinekamer van binnenvaart- en zeeschepen lekt.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In addition, bilge water and finished oil are processed in the port by Maritime Waste Collection Netherlands (MAIN). Bilgewater is oil-contaminated water that leaks from the bottom of the engine room of inland and sea vessels.

features.name: Zoutkeetsgracht
features.opening: The Zoutkeetsgracht (Salt sheds canal) is a canal to the west of the center of Amsterdam.

facts.text: Zoutkeetsgracht means salt-kiln canal, named for the salt factories that once lined its banks.
facts.sourceQuote: The canal is named after the salt factories that stood on both sides of the canal in the 17th and 18th centuries.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The canal is named after the salt factories that stood on both sides of the canal in the 17th and 18th centuries.

facts.text: A flour and bread factory called Holland operated here before being demolished to make way for new homes.
facts.sourceQuote: The flour and bread factory "Holland" was also there for some time, but after the demolition of the factory new homes were built on the site.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The flour and bread factory "Holland" was also there for some time, but after the demolition of the factory new homes were built on the site.

facts.text: Smallepadsgracht joins this waterway from the south just prior to the Zoutkeetsbrug crossing.
facts.sourceQuote: Smallepadsgracht enters Zoutkeetsgracht from the south just before Zoutkeetsbrug.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Smallepadsgracht enters Zoutkeetsgracht from the south just before Zoutkeetsbrug.
